item.title: Co-CEO (Maternity Cover)
item.description: Job description Responsibilities People and Team Leadership Line manage the Fundraising Manager, providing regular supervision, support, and performance development Lead the planning and delivery of all-hands meetings and team development programmes, fostering a collaborative and high-performing team culture Maintain oversight of team resource mapping, ensuring capacity is well-managed across the organisation Impact and Evaluation Lead the design and ongoing development of Routes' impact evaluation framework, ensuring it captures meaningful data about the difference our work makes Oversee the collection, analysis, and interpretation of impact data throughout the year, using findings to inform programme development and organisational decision-making Write and produce Routes' annual impact report, communicating our work and outcomes compellingly to funders, partners, and the wider sector Income Generation Support the Fundraising Manager with grant applications, funder relationships, and income generation activity as needed Manage the sales pipeline for the mentoring programme, including prospecting, relationship development, and conversion of corporate and organisational clients Source and manage CSR partnerships, building relationships with corporate partners and ensuring existing partnerships are well-stewarded Operations Lead on the creation, review, and approval of organisational policies, ensuring Routes' policies are up to date, legally compliant, and reflective of our values Oversee day-to-day office administration and organisational housekeeping Manage organisational insurance, ensuring appropriate cover is maintained and reviewed annually Oversee staff IT, laptops, phones, and software subscriptions, including troubleshooting and managing supplier relationships Draft and manage organisational contracts, including supplier, partner, and service agreements Lead on the conversion of Routes from a CIC to a CIO, working with legal advisors, the board, and relevant statutory bodies to manage the process Strategy Contribute to the development and delivery of Routes' organisational strategy, bringing insight from your areas of responsibility Lead on the development and implementation of Routes' income generation strategy, working closely with the Fundraising Manager and Co-CEO Communications Leadership Development and Learning Take ownership of your own professional development, using the annual training budget to attend relevant training, events, and sector learning opportunities that strengthen your contribution to Routes and the wider sector There are some areas of responsibility that sit under the other Co-CEO, but we would expect the person in this role to maintain some oversight or involvement in to enable smooth co-working between the roles. These are: Safeguarding: Act as Designated Safeguarding Lead (DSL) when required, ensuring Routes meets its safeguarding obligations and that staff and volunteers are appropriately supported Finance: Attend and contribute to monthly finance meetings, planned by other Co-CEO, maintaining a clear understanding of the organisation's financial position and flagging any concerns to the Co-CEO and board Person Specification Experience Experience in a senior leadership role within the charity, social enterprise, or public sector Demonstrable experience of managing and developing staff, with a coaching and supportive leadership style Experience of income generation in a charity or social enterprise context, including either grant fundraising, corporate partnerships, or programme sales Experience of designing or overseeing monitoring, evaluation, and learning frameworks and producing reports that communicate impact clearly Experience of managing operational and governance responsibilities, including policy development and working with a board Experience leading teams in challenging, fast-changing and resource-constrained environments Experience of working with or for communities facing marginalisation, discrimination, or structural disadvantage, and a deep understanding of the barriers refugee and asylum seeking women face in the UK Skills and Knowledge Ability to balance day to day operational oversight with long term strategic planning, ensuring that Routes’ work remains in line with values and objectives whilst responding to the changing needs of participants and the external landscape Strong written communication skills, with the ability to write compellingly for different audiences Financially literate, with the ability to read and engage meaningfully with management accounts and budgets Highly organised, with the ability to manage a broad and varied portfolio without dropping the ball Comfortable working with data, both quantitative and qualitative, and using it to draw meaningful conclusions Strong relationship-building skills, with the ability to build trust quickly with a wide range of stakeholders including funders, corporate partners, board members, and colleagues Sound understanding of CIC/charity governance and good practice, and the ability to make confident decisions independently while knowing when to consult Values and Approach Deep personal commitment to gender equality, racial justice, and the rights of refugees and asylum seeking people Understanding of the importance of implementing trauma informed practices and a commitment to accessible working practices for all A collaborative leadership style that builds trust, shares power, and brings out the best in others Comfortable with ambiguity and change, able to hold complexity without becoming overwhelmed by it Honest, transparent, and accountable, someone who says what they mean and follows through on commitments Energised by working in a small, values-led organisation where everyone mucks in Additionally, it would be desirable for you to be trained as a Designated Safeguarding Lead, but training on this can be provided. A Note on Experience We know that leadership experience takes many forms, and that people from marginalised communities, including those with lived experience of the asylum system, are often underrepresented at senior levels in the charity sector despite having exactly the qualities and understanding this role requires. We warmly encourage applications from people who may not follow a conventional career trajectory but who can demonstrate the skills, values, and commitment we are looking for. If you are unsure whether your experience is the right fit, please do get in touch before applying, we would rather have that conversation than miss out on the right person. item.title: Helpline Care Navigator - South and South West Region
item.description: Job Purpose This role offers an opportunity to play a vital part in sustaining our Helpline service, which sits at the heart of the support we provide to people living with PSP & CBD. As Helpline Care Navigator (HCN), you will act as the first point of contact for individuals, families and health professionals across the West and South West. You will deliver compassionate, person-centred support and clear, practical information via telephone and email, ensuring people affected by PSP & CBD feel heard, informed and supported at every stage of their journey. Alongside direct support, you will actively engage with health and social care professionals, neurology clinics and wider partners to strengthen local awareness of PSP & CBD and enhance referral pathways across the region. This is a key role in maintaining continuity, quality and momentum within our Helpline service and you will be reporting to the Helpline and Support Services Manager. Contract Type Full Time – permanent contract (6 month probationary period) Salary £27,500 per annum Hours of Work & Annual Leave 35 hours per week - this may include working some unsociable hours, including evenings and weekends. 28 days plus bank holidays. Pro-rated for part time role. The main office is in Milton Keynes, and we have a hybrid working policy with staff expected to spend one day a week in the office and the remainder can be worked from home. HCN’s currently work from the office on a Wednesday. There is flexibility in the arrangements that need to be agreed upon with the line manager. Key Responsibilities To be ‘first point of call’ for people with PSP & CBD and their families living in the West and South West Region including Shropshire, Herefordshire, Warwickshire, Gloucestershire, Wiltshire, Hampshire, West Sussex, East Sussex, Dorset, Somerset, Devon, Cornwall, Avon, Isle of Wight. Providing people with support and information over the phone and via email. To raise awareness of PSP & CBD across all health and social care disciplines in he region by engaging with HSCP’s and neurology clinics. To provide accurate information in all aspects of PSP & CBD in response to enquiries and signpost onto other organisations where appropriate. Ensure a maximum response to all helpline calls, emails and enquires. To keep clear and accurate records and statistics of enquires received and actions taken. To carry out a maximum number of proactive calls to people affected by PSP & CBD within the region as directed by the Helpline Manager. Develop and maintain the existing database of key health and social care professionals and regional services. Attend outreach events to build the profile of PSPA services amongst health and social care professionals. To deliver awareness and learning sessions to HSCP’s within your region Work with the Director of Policy and Influencing to identify ways in which services and care can be improved for families affected by PSP & CBD in the region. To signpost to PSPA Support Groups and services. Liaise with external services to signpost to local support. Take an active part in the delivery and planning of information and support events, which may include the possibility of overnight stays and weekends. Liaise with the fundraising team to signpost to fundraising activities. Liaise with the Volunteer Coordinator to maintain and build volunteering in the region. To attend and contribute constructively to team and other meetings as required. To ensure the implementation of policies, procedures and quality standards as defined by PSPA. Contribute to the development of literature and articles for PSPA Matters. To undertake any other tasks, by agreement as required, in support of the work of PSPA. The duties may be changed and/or varied to meet changing circumstances at the discretion of the CEO and Board of Trustees. Person Specification Essential Criteria: Experience in delivering helpline and/or information and support services Excellent listening and interpersonal skills, with the capacity to listen actively understanding different points of view Ability to keep accurate records Willingness to undertake training and continuing personal development Experience of and sensitivity to communicating with audiences from a range of backgrounds Strong IT skills, with experience in MS Office products and customer relationship management software Flexible and reliable attitude and the ability to self-organise and to work without direct supervision Good communication skills, both oral and written and excellent telephone manner Ability to manage difficulty questions, emotions and situations in a calm and confident way. Desirable Criteria: Knowledge of PSP & CBD or other neurodegenerative diseases and/or experience of working in the NHS An understanding of Safeguarding and an ability to follow relevant policies and procedures Knowledge of healthcare or social care systems. item.title: Therapeutic Community Caseworker
item.description: Job description The Baobab Centre is a non-residential therapeutic community supporting unaccompanied minors who have experienced human rights abuses and are seeking asylum, refugee status and settlement in the United Kingdom. The role of a Therapeutic Community Caseworker at the Baobab Centre is to support unaccompanied asylum seeking and refugee adolescents and young adults to access care, basic rights and entitlements and to support their social development and rehabilitation. This role involves working closely with the clinical key worker of each young person and with our wider multidisciplinary team. As a Caseworker you will aim to empower individuals to build stable, independent lives in the UK, including by supporting them to communicate their views, needs and experiences in decision-making processes, and supporting them to make challenges when necessary. Caseworkers assist young people to make effective choices about what happens in their lives and encourage them to speak up and build agency. Baobab aims to be a non-residential therapeutic community with a holistic and integrated perspective. As a Caseworker, you will play a key role within our multidisciplinary team. We aim to be a thinking organisation and place a high value on shared thinking time and shared responsibilities. Our team work together with each other and with agencies and key individuals in young people’s lives, both within and outside of Baobab. A key aspect of the role is communicating with members of the clinical and admin staff team within the Baobab Centre and with other workers in the network around each young person including social workers, teachers, foster carers, lawyers, hospital consultants, housing and benefits workers. etc. You will strive to develop relationships across networks and advocate access to rights and entitlements for our community members. It is critical that as a Caseworker: you have an insight to the backgrounds and experiences of both the internal and external factors impacting on the lives of unaccompanied young people attending our centre and an understanding of the broader context in our society as it impacts on young asylum seekers (including invisibility, marginalisation, discrimination and the fact of waiting in uncertainty for a long time. You have an insight in how current immigration rules and social care system procedures act as barriers to rehabilitation, including by restricting access to education, adequate benefits, housing and healthcare provision. Posted on: 26 August 2026 Closing date: 24 September 2026 at 23:30 Tags: Advice / Information, Social Care / Development, Advocacy, Housing, Care Management, Child Protection, Health / Medical, Human Rights, Justice, Mental Health, Modern Slavery / Human Trafficking, Refugee / Immigration, Safeguarding, Substance Misuse, Victim Support, Wellbeing, Youth / Children, Social / Support Work

item.title: Legacy and In Memory Manager
item.description: A fantastic opportunity has arisen within our award-winning fundraising team, to join us in an exciting new role of Legacy and In Memory Manager (Lead). At Birmingham Women’s and Children’s Hospital Charity, we believe there’s always more we can do for our sick kids and women, and that’s why we will always strive to do more for our patients and families. It’s our mission to raise the vital funds needed to make a real difference to all who use our hospitals, and to make our hospital feel just like home. This role requires someone with experience in legacy administration and promotion and/or in memory fundraising, as well as excellent communication skills and a strategic mindset. We need someone with previous experience in relationship management and income generation - ideally within a legacy and/or in memory setting - who is able to lead and inspire our supporters and staff in order to generate long term income and awareness for the charity. To be successful in this role you will: Lead the development and delivery of legacy marketing and in-memory fundraising strategies to drive sustained income growth and supporter retention Be self-motivated, independent and target-driven Act as the subject matter expert on legacy administration and in-memory giving, providing guidance, training, and mentoring while promoting a strong culture of philanthropy Manage all aspects of legacy casework, including complex and contentious cases, ensuring effective stakeholder relationships and full compliance with legal, regulatory, and best practice standards Oversee data management, reporting, and analysis to generate insights, improve processes, and support accurate forecasting and long-term financial planning Collaborate across teams to maximise fundraising opportunities, enhance donor engagement across channels, and deliver impactful events and integrated giving initiatives Posses a natural confidence in talking to people with high emotional intelligence and resilience due to the sensitive nature of the role, with excellent communication and relationship building skills. What we offer: Flexible and hybrid working to support work-life balance Generous annual leave entitlement with additional leave for long service Enhanced sick pay Enhanced Maternity and Paternity Pay Employee Assistance Program and Lifestyle Savings Free flu jabs Cycle to work scheme Charity events throughout the year Employer enhanced auto-enrolment pension scheme with 8% employer contribution Ongoing commitment to education and professional development The Charity is committed to equal opportunities and welcomes applications from all suitably qualified persons regardless of their race, sex, disability, religion/belief, sexual orientation or age. Successful candidates will have access to vulnerable beneficiaries therefore the role is subject to Disclosure and Barring Service (DBS) clearance. If you think you have the qualities we are looking for and the desire to contribute, please download the Job Vacancy Pack and then send us a CV and covering letter explaining how you meet the criteria for the role and making clear why you would like to be considered for it. PLEASE NOTE: Within our organisation, this role is titled Legacy and In Memory Lead . This reflects our internal structure and does not change the scope or responsibilities described in this advert. We will conduct interviews as suitable candidates apply and we're ready to hire if we find the right person before the job ad closes.
item.dc:creator: Birmingham Women's and Children's Hospital Charity

item.title: Community Action Coordinator (Manchester)
item.description: Job description Join a passionate and committed team driving forward social justice through women-led community organising! The successful candidate will support Community Savers groups and networks in North Manchester and Wythenshawe achieve their goals for financial and social inclusion, mental wellbeing, community led development, participatory decision-making, and housing and climate justice. You will work through a community-led process to: build strong community associations develop common visions and area action plans build membership and support capacity building among young women aged 18-30 raise small grants funding identify priorities for skills development and learning exchange help coordinate evidence-based advocacy projects keep appropriate records of meetings and events capture and communicate learning, progress, and impacts. You are: Experienced in working in neighbourhoods with long term health inequalities. Good at building trusting relationships while maintaining boundaries and being mindful of your own levels of resilience. Passionate about social justice and championing community expertise. Compassionate and non-judgemental. Please download the application pack for further information and a full job description. Note that Community Savers is a majority women-led and transinclusive movement that works in alliance with Community Led Action and Savings Support (CLASS). Membership is open to anyone of any gender identity and community action aims to benefit all people in the areas where we work. Leadership and governance structures seek to celebrate and amplify the voices of working class women as those most disadvantaged by the intersecting cost of living, housing and climate crises. Posted on: 26 August 2026 Closing date: 25 September 2026 at 17:00 Tags: Campaigns, Finance, Advocacy, Housing, Engagement / Outreach, Mental Health, Safeguarding, Women's Rights, Youth / Children, Community Fundraising, Events / Activities The client requests no contact from agencies or media sales.

item.title: Operations Coordinator
item.description: Job Purpose: Still in its original Fleet Street location, our historic building retains much of its 1890s character, reflecting over a hundred years of history while providing 21st century facilities. With six floors, St Bride Foundation is a unique and memorable setting for a range of events - lectures, workshops, board meetings, conferences, weddings and other celebrations. The Operations Coordinator plays a key role in supporting the day-to-day operation of St Bride Foundation, helping to ensure our historic building is safe, compliant, well maintained and welcoming. Working closely with the Operations Manager and Facilities Coordinator, you'll provide support across facilities management while also acting as a welcoming first point of contact for visitors, tenants and contractors. We're looking for an organised, approachable and proactive individual who enjoys a varied role and is equally comfortable managing administrative tasks behind the scenes as delivering excellent front of house service. Key Responsibilities: Operational Administration Provide administrative support to the Operations Manager and Facilities Coordinator across all aspects of facilities management including planned preventative maintenance programmes and reactive maintenance requests. Liaise with Facilities Coordinator to ascertain what jobs can be completed in-house and what needs an external contractor. Obtain quotations for maintenance, repairs and improvement works from contractors and suppliers. Arrange contractor visits, coordinate access and ensure works are completed to the required standard. Ensure contractors provide appropriate documentation, including risk assessments, method statements and insurance certificates where required. Maintain records of maintenance schedules, servicing, warranties and contractor documentation. Check and process invoices relating to facilities expenditure. Maintain accurate records of maintenance logs and supplier information. Health & Safety Administration Support the Facilities Coordinator and Operations Manager in maintaining Health & Safety records and ensure documentation is up to date. Support Health & Safety compliance appropriate to a Grade II listed heritage building and its public, commercial and performance spaces. Support the administration of statutory inspections, testing and servicing, including fire safety systems, emergency lighting, lifts, electrical testing and water hygiene. Assist with the administration of risk assessments, inspections and audits. Monitor compliance dates and ensure inspections and certifications are completed on time. Assist with emergency procedures, fire safety administration and business continuity documentation. Front of House & Building Support Provide Front of House support, covering reception desk during core hours, welcoming visitors and providing excellent customer service. Assist with general queries on email and drop-in enquiries. Receive deliveries, distribute post and manage courier collections. Act as a point of contact for building tenants, responding to queries and coordinating facilities requests. Assist with room access, keys and general building administration. Help ensure shared spaces remain safe, presentable and welcoming. Digital & Administrative Support Support the Learning team with updating of event listings across ticketing platforms and the organisation's website as required. Manage the administration of the organisation's online bookshop, including processing orders, maintaining stock records and liaising with customers where required. General Act as an ambassador for St Bride Foundation, upholding its mission to preserve and promote print and design heritage. Engage with stakeholders, including donors, volunteers, and beneficiaries, to strengthen community and fundraising efforts. Support and contribute to initiatives that enhance the Foundation’s impact, such as public engagement events, educational programmes, and collaborative partnerships. Complete ongoing staff training to include Health & Safety, compliance and other related topics as required by the organisation. Contribute to the smooth running of the organisation by supporting colleagues across departments. Undertake any other duties appropriate to the role. Essential Qualifications & Experience: Excellent administrative and organisational skills with strong attention to detail. Experience coordinating contractors, suppliers or facilities-related services. Confident obtaining quotations, scheduling works and maintaining accurate records. Good understanding of Health & Safety administration within a workplace environment. Strong IT skills, including Microsoft Office 365 and experience using databases or online management systems. Experience in the charitable, cultural, or heritage sector preferred. Key Skills & Competencies: Good team-working and interpersonal skills, with ability to build effective relationships with a wide range of people. Good time-management and organisational skills, with ability to multitask, prioritise and problem-solve. Good written and verbal communication skills, with ability to present well in person and on the phone with a polite, professional and approachable manner, and an outgoing approach to customer service. Ability to self-motivate, use own initiative and maintain attention to detail while working under pressure. A positive, proactive and professional attitude, with a willingness to adopt a flexible and adaptable approach to day-to-day workload. A passion for the arts, heritage, and education, with a strong commitment to the Foundation’s vision and values. Organisational Values & Expectations: Promote and uphold St Bride Foundation’s commitment to cultural preservation, lifelong learning, and community engagement. Work collaboratively with colleagues, volunteers, and external partners to support the Foundation’s charitable objectives. Uphold ethical standards and best practices in charity governance and operations. Health & Safety Responsibilities: Promote a safe and inclusive environment for colleagues, volunteers, and visitors. Act as a Fire Marshal and Emergency First Aider. Terms & Conditions: Working Hours: 8 hours per day (including one hour unpaid lunchbreak), five days per week. The role requires you to work at Front of House reception during core hours.
item.dc:creator: St Bride Foundation

item.title: Business Development and Events Manager
item.description: Job description Job Purpose: To oversee the management and growth of Venue Hire for our historic spaces covering meetings, conferences, talks, weddings and community activities. This is our primary source of income and key to supporting our library and learning programme, alongside our theatre income and fundraising. The role will also lead on identifying and developing new business opportunities for other commercial income streams, building relationships with clients and partners, and ensuring that commercial activity supports the Foundation’s charitable purpose and long-term sustainability. Optimising the use of space to ensure that St Bride Foundation (SBF) operates profitably as well as meeting the needs of our communities is a key part of the role. The Business Development and Events Manager will oversee the Venue Hire activity and promote the venue’s room resources, as well as supporting the Library and Workshop in the organisation of in-house courses, seminars and events. Key Responsibilities: Events Management Manage the Events Team activity of promoting and selling the venue’s event spaces, ensuring SBF has good visibility on all relevant venue hire websites. Responding to and converting enquiries and monitoring conversion effectiveness. Managing clients’ needs for booked events. Negotiating contracts for both short and long-term use; and ensuring that all aspects of the venue are fit for purpose. Identify new networks and online promotions to promote the SBF offer Be responsible, along with the Operations Manager and Foundation Manager, to the Board for: Setting and achieving yearly and monthly income budgets, including quarterly forecasting and planning. All aspects of pricing and contract negotiation for areas of responsibility including catering, furniture hire, keyholding and cleaning. Ensure service, pricing and contracts are regularly reviewed. Working “hands-on” within a small team, getting involved in all aspects of delivering a quality service, monitoring and reviewing customer experience and satisfaction. Assisting the Operations Manager with Health & Safety and compliance issues relating to your area of responsibility. Line management responsibility for Event Coordinators and Venue Assistant. Overseeing and supporting the Events Team with smooth running of SBF and external events. Ensure time management and priorities are managed for line reports. Support SBF marketing efforts working with the Events team on social media content and website updates. Act as an ambassador for St Bride Foundation, upholding its mission to preserve and promote print and design heritage. Actively contribute to SBF redevelopment plans in terms of future planning for events and building operations. Engage with stakeholders, including donors, volunteers, and beneficiaries, to strengthen community and fundraising efforts. Support and contribute to initiatives that enhance the Foundation’s impact, such as public engagement events, educational programmes, and collaborative partnerships. Complete ongoing staff training to include Health & Safety, compliance and other related topics as required by the organisation. Business Development & Commercial Growth Develop and implement a proactive business development strategy for Venue Hire, identifying new clients, partners and commercial opportunities, as well as additional marketing/outreach activities to boost income during quieter periods. Build and maintain a pipeline of prospective clients and strategic partners, converting opportunities into new and repeat business. Develop relationships with event agencies, corporate organisations, professional bodies, cultural and educational organisations and other relevant networks. Identify opportunities to increase revenue through repeat bookings, new event formats, longer-term agreements, partnerships and additional services. Monitor market trends, competitor activity, customer feedback and venue performance to inform pricing, product development and sales activity. Establish and report on business development KPIs, including pipeline value, enquiry-to-booking conversion, repeat business, occupancy, average booking value and revenue growth. Work collaboratively with Marketing, Fundraising, Learning, Library and Workshop teams to develop opportunities that support both the Foundation's commercial and charitable objectives. Work with fundraising to develop incentives and cross promotions between sponsorship/membership and venue hire and identify other synergies between the physical SBF assets and the fundraising function Essential Qualifications & Experience: Proven experience of business development, sales, partnership-building or income generation, ideally within a venue, cultural, charitable or heritage setting. Proven experience of planning and delivering events end-to-end, on time and within budget. Working with teams on a varied programme of activities for a diverse mix of audiences. Experience of working with volunteers running workshops and events, overseeing all aspects of delivery. Experience working with external partners, including community groups, local authorities and sponsors. Line management experience of an events team, including support with managing workload and personal development objectives. Experience of identifying new clients, generating leads, converting enquiries and developing repeat business or longer-term client relationships. Experience of using data, customer insight or market research to inform sales activity, pricing, service development or income targets. Experience in the charitable, cultural, or heritage sector preferred. Key Skills & Competencies: Highly organised, able to manage multiple priorities and deadlines. Ability to troubleshoot issues arising during events including those relating to AV, catering and general experience of attendees to ensure seamless delivery. Excellent written and verbal communication skills. Confidence in briefing and managing event speakers including volunteers and SBF Trustees to ensure smooth running of events. Confident relationship-builder, able to develop networks with corporate clients, event agencies, cultural partners, community organisations and other stakeholders. Able to set, monitor and report on business development activity and income-related KPIs, including enquiry conversion, occupancy, repeat business and revenue growth. Risk assessment and mitigation in event spaces and knowledge of licensing, insurance, accessibility and inclusion requirements. Financial management and budgeting, including forecasting and reporting of our events revenue. Strong IT skills, including CRM systems, ticketing platforms and newsletters. A passion for the arts, heritage, and education, with a strong commitment to the Foundation’s vision and values. Organisational Values & Expectations: Promote and uphold St Bride Foundation’s commitment to cultural preservation, lifelong learning, and community engagement. item.title: Chief Executive Officer
item.description: Over the past decade, Escapeline has become a recognised leader in the prevention of child criminal and sexual exploitation across the South West. Through awareness raising, education, direct intervention, family support, professional training and strong partnership working, we have empowered thousands of children, young people, families and professionals to better understand, identify and respond to the risks of exploitation. Our work has never been more important. As the nature of exploitation continues to evolve, so too must our response. We are therefore seeking an exceptional Chief Executive who can provide visionary leadership, inspire confidence among stakeholders, strengthen strategic partnerships and ensure Escapeline continues to be at the forefront of protecting vulnerable children and young people. Building on our strong foundations, we see significant opportunities to expand our reach and deepen our impact, particularly across Dorset and Wiltshire, where support for the charity remains strong and continues to grow. The successful candidate will have the opportunity to shape the next chapter of our development, broadening our influence, diversifying income streams, enhancing our services and securing long-term sustainability. While preventing the exploitation of children will always remain our core purpose, we are equally committed to supporting the wider impact that exploitation has on families. Our specialist helpline and parent support community provide a vital source of guidance, understanding and hope for families who often feel isolated and overlooked by traditional support services. We are determined to strengthen and expand this provision, ensuring that no family faces these challenges alone. We are looking for a leader who combines strategic vision with emotional intelligence, commercial awareness with compassion, and ambition with an unwavering commitment to our values. You will lead a dedicated team, work alongside an engaged and supportive Board of Trustees, and build on a reputation that has been earned through years of trusted and impactful work. Most importantly, you will have the opportunity to make a lasting difference to the lives of children, young people and families at a time when that difference is urgently needed. If you are inspired by our mission and share our ambition to create safer futures for children and young people, we would be delighted to hear from you.

item.title: Oxleas Care Navigator
item.description: Job description Are you someone who thrives on making a genuine difference to people’s lives? Do you have experience working in health, social care or the voluntary sector and want to play a vital role in improving how older people access the support they need? If so, we would love to hear from you. Age UK Bromley & Greenwich is seeking a dedicated and compassionate Care Navigator to join our expanding team in partnership with Oxleas NHS Trust . Based at Memorial Hospital in Woolwich, you will be embedded within a multi-disciplinary team working on the Proactive and Frailty pathways. Your focus will be on supporting older people with complex needs, helping them navigate health and social care systems, and connecting them to relevant services across the community. This is a key role that sits at the heart of person-centred care. You will attend multi-disciplinary team meetings, work alongside professionals including GPs, case managers and mental health staff, and spend time speaking directly with patients and their families. Your role will be to truly listen, identify what matters most to the individual, and help them take practical steps towards better health, independence and wellbeing. Key responsibilities include: Attending Multi-Disciplinary Team (MDT) meetings and contributing to holistic care planning Working with patients to understand their needs, provide emotional support and signpost to local services Liaising with a wide range of professionals across the NHS, social care and voluntary sectors Inputting information into systems including RIO and Framework I, with training provided Keeping accurate records and contributing to service evaluation and improvement We are looking for someone who is: Experienced in health, social care or voluntary sector settings Empathetic and a confident communicator Able to build strong relationships with a range of professionals and clients Organised, reliable and motivated by positive outcomes for others Comfortable working independently and as part of a team Passionate about supporting older people to live well and with dignity This role offers the opportunity to be part of a well-respected local charity with a strong values-led culture. You will be joining a supportive team that values collaboration, creativity and kindness. As a Care Navigator, your work will have a direct impact on people’s lives at a time when they are most vulnerable. For the full person spec and job description please download the job pack. item.title: Community Action Lead - Manchester
item.description: Job description Join a passionate committed team with a lead role in driving forward social justice through community-led action and partnership development! You will work in alliance with the Community Savers Leadership and key partners to support creative organising for gender, housing, climate, and economic justice across Manchester neighbourhoods. This role is funded by the National Lottery Community Fund (Reaching Communities). You will need: A deep understanding of the context for facilitating community action and community-led development projects in areas experiencing long term and intersecting inequalities. The ability to maintain a positive ‘can do’ attitude while negotiating complex and potentially obstructive political or relational dynamics. Skills & experience in the following areas: community-led action; advocacy; campaigns, fundraising, communications, leadership development, brokering partnerships, equality diversity and inclusion, conflict resolution, safeguarding. Role summary: You will work with the Community Savers Leadership and key partners on the strategic development of community action, projects, and partnerships that reduce health inequalities and promote social justice. This will include networking and building relationships with existing and potential statutory and non-statutory partners; bringing in appropriate expertise to achieve community-led development projects; direct support for community action such as community-led research projects and partnerships; community mapping, visioning and action planning; supporting reflection and evaluation; and sharing learning widely. You will also supervise the coordination support provided to affiliated groups and leaders by our Community Action Coordinator (Manchester); ensuring a community-led process underpins leadership and associational development. Please download the application pack for further information and a full job description noting that this is a 0.6% FTE 3-year fixed term contract (actual salary pro rata). Note that Community Savers is a majority women-led and transinclusive movement. Membership is open to anyone of any gender identity and community action aims to benefit all people in the areas where we work. Leadership and governance structures seek to celebrate and amplify the voices of working class women. item.title: Domestic Violence and Abuse Coordinator (part-time)
item.description: Job Role: Domestic Violence and Abuse Co-ordinator Salary: £15,720 per year (based on an FTE of £26,200 per year) Hours: 22.5 hours per week (3 days across Monday to Friday) Contract type: Permanent Location: BANES Additional information: A valid driving licence and access to own vehicle Participation in an on-call out-of-hours rota Regular travel across the BANES area (travel across the South West for training and events may also be required) Alongside is committed to equality, diversity and inclusion and welcomes applications from all sections of the community. However, this is restricted to women due to the nature of the role. The Occupational Requirement under Schedule 9 (part 1) of the Equality Act 2010 applies. About Alongside: Alongside is a charity dedicated to making a difference to the lives of the most vulnerable and disadvantaged people in society. We run several projects and every year we help thousands of people out of homelessness, into employment, away from domestic abuse, and more. If you’d like a real sense of job satisfaction, great career prospects and a competitive benefits package, you could be who we’re looking for! About the Role: As a Domestic Violence and Abuse Co-ordinator , you’ll play a vital role in supporting victims and survivors of domestic abuse to rebuild their lives. Working holistically, you’ll carry out in‑depth needs assessments and develop tailored support plans that reflect each individual’s circumstances, strengths, and goals. You’ll provide compassionate, trauma‑informed case management, advocacy, and resettlement support for people with a wide range of complex social and housing needs. From navigating services and securing safe accommodation to monitoring progress and celebrating milestones, you’ll walk alongside survivors every step of the way — empowering them to move forward with safety, dignity, and confidence. This is a deeply rewarding role where your work will make a meaningful, lasting difference every single day. What you’ll be doing: Conduct key works sessions on a regular basis whilst developing individual support and risk management plans. Establish the risks and needs of survivors and their children through assessing their practical and emotional support needs. Champion safeguarding by following policies and procedures to keep everyone safe, and that any concerns are brought to immediate attention of a manager. Collaborative multi-agency working to advocate for survivors ensuring their needs are met. Maintain accurate client records using our system, INFORM. Please note: Job descriptions are not exhaustive, and the successful candidate may occasionally be asked to take on other duties that align with the key responsibilities outlined. You can view the full job description by clicking here . What we’re looking for: Understanding of domestic abuse including the impact this has on victims and their children. Experience working in a housing, social or health care setting. There are many great reasons to join our team! Access to our Rewards Platform, which includes an Employee Assistance Programme and Health Cash Plan 27 days annual leave , including an extra day off for your birthday, plus bank holidays - increasing up to 30 days after 4 years of continuous employment (pro rata for part-time staff) 30% staff discount at Alongside charity shop A generous and competitive pension scheme A supportive culture where staff feedback is highly valued and regular supervisions with line managers are conducted Great opportunities for career development and free monthly training sessions from experienced facilitators For all the fantastic and valuable work, you’ll be doing, you’ll be eligible for the Blue Light Card which offers amazing discounts on thousands of brands Reflective Practice sessions from objective, external facilitators Our Ethos As an Equal Opportunities employer, we have an Equality and Diversity Action plan in place showing our commitment in ensuring continuous improvement in creating an inclusive culture. We also have a committed group of Inclusion & Diversity champions who meet monthly to ensure progress is being made. We invite applications from people from all backgrounds and cultures, especially minority groups that are underrepresented in the workplace. We also welcome applications from those with lived experience. We embrace flexibility and are proud to be a Disability Confident and Mindful employer, as well as an Armed Forces Covenant Supporter. If you have any special access requirements or other support needs throughout the application process (including interview), please contact us so that we can let you know how we can support you. We accept CVs and applications in all formats. DBS Checks We welcome applications from people with lived experience. All applicants working with our clients will be expected to undertake an enhanced Disclosure and Barring Service check. A criminal conviction will not necessarily prevent you from becoming an employee, the decision will depend on the type of offence and its relevance to the role. If you would like to discuss any convictions you may have, please contact the person named in the advert. All information will be dealt with according to our Data Protection Policy.

item.title: Carer Voice and Engagement Officer
item.description: Post purpose We are seeking an enthusiastic and organised Carer Voice and Engagement Officer to join our team at The Carers' Centre. This rewarding role will help ensure that unpaid carers have opportunities to share their experiences, influence local services and see the impact of their involvement. Working with adult carers, young carers and young adult carers, you will coordinate participation activities that are welcoming, meaningful and inclusive. You will build relationships with carers, colleagues and partner organisations, creating opportunities for carers to shape services, raise awareness and contribute to positive change. This is an exciting opportunity for someone who enjoys connecting people, supporting others to build confidence and ensuring lived experience helps drive improvement. By ensuring participation is inclusive, well organised and genuinely influential, you will help strengthen the voice of carers across Bath and North East Somerset while contributing to the continued development of The Carers' Centre and the wider caring community. Key responsibilities Carer Voice and Participation Coordinate and support Carers Voice, Young Carers Council and other participation forums. Assist in the delivery of age-appropriate engagement activities that build confidence and participation skills. Encourage carers from diverse backgrounds to share their experiences and influence services. Ensure carers receive feedback about how their involvement has made a difference. Support carers to participate in service improvement, consultations and decision-making opportunities. Promote meaningful and inclusive involvement across all services. Engagement and Community Connection Build positive relationships with carers, partners and community organisations. Coordinate requests for carer involvement from local services and partner organisations. Support carers to represent lived experience within local groups, networks and projects. Work with colleagues to create accessible and welcoming opportunities for involvement. Promote the value and impact of unpaid carers across Bath and North East Somerset. Communications and Development Coordinate participation communications, updates and engagement opportunities. Develop positive working relationships with local organisations, community groups, statutory services and partner agencies. Support carers to build confidence and develop skills through training and lived experience opportunities. Work with colleagues to promote participation and celebrate the difference carers make. Encourage involvement from carers who may not traditionally engage with services. Monitoring, Evaluation and Impact Maintain accurate and timely records of all interactions and support provided. Collect monitoring data, feedback and outcome information in line with organisational requirements. Support the delivery of programme evaluation activities. Utilise organisational systems, including Salesforce, to record activity and outcomes. General Adhere to the Carers’ Charter and provide a professional carer-focused information, advice and support service. Encourage carers to provide feedback on The Carers’ Centre services and actively participate in shaping future delivery. Undertake safeguarding training, adhere to organisational safeguarding policies and follow all safeguarding procedures. Take responsibility for ensuring communications and record keeping comply with GDPR and data protection requirements. Ensure that you adopt good practice within the Carers Trust network. Ensure that you work within The Carers’ Centre policy framework. Recognise the importance of fundraising and positively contribute to organisational sustainability where appropriate. Undertake any other duties, in consultation with your line manager, as are consistent with the responsibilities of this post.

item.title: Senior Information & Education Manager
item.description: About Action for Pulmonary Fibrosis Action for Pulmonary Fibrosis (APF) is the UK’s leading patient charity dedicated to improving the lives of individuals and families affected by pulmonary fibrosis. Our mission is underpinned by values of compassionate, bold, expert and collaborative. We believe in creating a supportive environment in which both our employees and beneficiaries can thrive. Founded in 2013 by people affected by PF and clinicians, APF has grown into a respected national charity rooted in community and evidence. We provide trusted information and support, help a growing network of support groups, campaign to improve access to care and invest in research to bring hope of new treatments. APF strives to be an organisation of equity and inclusion, welcoming people from all backgrounds – our team and volunteers aim to reflect the diverse communities we serve. We have just launched an ambitious five-year strategy (2025–2030), co-created with the PF community, which focuses on expanding support, transforming care, and accelerating research. This strategy marks a step change with a clearer focus, stronger delivery model and greater ambition to ensure no one faces pulmonary fibrosis alone. Role Purpose We are looking for a Senior Information and Education Manager to lead our patient information and education work, ensuring people affected by pulmonary fibrosis can access clear, accurate, trusted and accessible information when they need it most. This is a strategic and hands-on role. You will shape APF’s information and education offer across digital, print and live formats, develop and improve patient information, lead a review of our website content, and ensure our resources remain evidence-based, accessible and shaped by lived experience. You will also oversee our education programme and line manage our Education and Events Co-ordinator, helping us deliver high-quality events and education that respond to the needs of people affected by pulmonary fibrosis. We are looking for someone with strong experience in health information, patient education or health content. You will be an excellent writer and editor, able to make complex information clear and accessible, with the strategic thinking and project management skills to turn insight and evidence into practical improvements. This is an opportunity to play a leading role in ensuring people affected by pulmonary fibrosis have the information, education and support they need throughout their journey. To apply, please submit a CV and a covering letter of no more than two pages outlining your suitability for the role and how your skills and experience meet the requirements of the job description. Interviews will be held on a rolling basis, so we encourage interested candidates to apply as soon as possible.
item.dc:creator: Action for Pulmonary Fibrosis

item.description: About Action for Pulmonary Fibrosis Action for Pulmonary Fibrosis (APF) is the UK’s leading patient charity dedicated to improving the lives of individuals and families affected by pulmonary fibrosis. Our mission is underpinned by values of compassionate, bold, expert and collaborative. We believe in creating a supportive environment in which both our employees and beneficiaries can thrive. item.title: IRIS Advocate Educator - Haringey
item.description: About the organisation For nearly 50 years, nia has provided high quality, women-led services across North and East London. nia has three main aims: to provide services for women, children and young people who have experienced male violence, working to end men’s violence against women and girls, and to inform and influence policy and public awareness. nia’s values, and our commitment to upholding them, set us apart. We put women first – always and without hesitation: we believe women, we are run by women, for women. We leave no woman behind: we challenge inequality and discrimination and believe that uniting women of all backgrounds is essential to ending the sex-based oppression of women. About the service IRIS improves the quality of care given by GP surgeries to women experiencing domestic violence. IRIS is a collaboration between LB Haringey and nia . The IRIS Advocate Educator (AE) will support the Women’s Health Services Manager to roll out the service across London borough of Haringey and support women referred to the service. About You We’re looking for a highly organised and self-motivated woman who is passionate about ending violence against women, girls and children. You’ll have a ‘can-do’ approach and demonstrable commitment to nia’s approach to Prioritising women, upholding and promoting feminist, trauma-informed and anti-racist practice. item.title: Weekenders Programme Manager
item.description: We are looking for experienced social workers to help take the Weekenders programme into its next chapter. You will join a small, ambitious charity and play a central role in growing a relational, child-focused programme across England. THE OPPORTUNITY Salary: starting from £40,000, subject to experience Hours: full time, 37.5 hours per week Location: home-based within England, with regular team co-working and travel Contracts: one permanent post and two 18-month fixed-term posts Flexibility: occasional evening or weekend delivery, usually around once per month Travel: across England, including occasional overnight stays; reasonable expenses are covered ABOUT NOW FOSTER Now Foster brings together social work, service design, lived experience and innovation to transform fostering in England. Our vision is to bring many more wonderful people into fostering so that more children and young people can experience stable, meaningful relationships with caring adults. We are a small team with big ambitions. We value creativity, collaboration, learning and continuous improvement, and we work with partners who share our determination to do better for children and families. ABOUT WEEKENDERS Weekenders is our flagship programme. We recruit and support weekend foster carers – known as Weekenders – who build regular, long-term relationships with children and young people supported by local authorities. It is about showing up, making a difference and becoming an adult a young person can count on. The programme is entering an exciting period of growth. We are expanding our partnerships with Regional Care Cooperatives, Fostering Hubs and local authorities across England, currently including London, the South West, North West and North East. THE ROLE – Lead delivery, develop people and stay close to practice As a Weekenders Programme Manager, you will turn our ambition into consistently excellent delivery. You will lead the day-to-day support of applicants across an agreed portfolio of areas, making sure prospective Weekenders receive a warm, responsive and motivational experience and that our partners can rely on us to deliver what we have agreed. This is a people-management and delivery role with a strong connection to practice. You will line-manage Journey Guides, manage a network of independent social workers (ISWs), lead our prep group training and undertake some intro chats yourself. The role does not carry a statutory caseload. It does carry real responsibility for safeguarding, practice quality, operational oversight and relationships across a growing, geographically distributed programme. Delivery Leadership: Lead programme delivery Take day-to-day responsibility for Weekenders delivery across an agreed portfolio of Fostering Hubs and local authority partners. Turn partnership agreements and local processes into clear applicant journeys, with roles, handovers and timescales understood by everyone involved. Plan capacity across Journey Guides, ISWs, prep group training and your own direct work so that delivery keeps pace with demand. Monitor applicant progress, identify delays or risks early and work with colleagues and partners to find practical solutions. Maintain a consistent Now Foster experience across regions while adapting thoughtfully to local contexts. People Management: Manage and develop Journey Guides Provide reflective one-to-one and group supervision, clear objectives and timely feedback. Allocate work fairly, monitor workloads and create the structure needed for responsive applicant support. Coach Journey Guides in relationship-based, strengths-based and motivational conversations, using observation, role play and practice review where helpful. Support sound judgement, safe practice and professional boundaries, addressing performance or wellbeing concerns early and constructively. Build a connected team culture in which people share learning, ask for help and take ownership. Practice Oversight: Manage ISWs and assure practice quality Build and maintain a reliable pool of qualified, registered ISWs to undertake initial home visits and teach on prep group training days. Coordinate ISW recruitment, onboarding, availability, allocation and briefing in line with our safer recruitment and practice arrangements. Set clear expectations for the quality, timeliness and tone of home visits, written outputs, training and feedback. Review quality, provide constructive feedback and address concerns promptly, while forecasting capacity and arranging cover. Training: Plan, staff and lead prep group training Own the planning and delivery of prep group training across programme areas, including schedules, venues or online delivery, materials, communications and staffing. Facilitate and teach on prep groups, modelling inclusive, relational and reflective practice. Brief and support ISW co-facilitators so sessions are coherent, well-paced and grounded in the realities of fostering. Make sure applicants can reflect meaningfully on children's needs, safer caring, trauma-informed care, cultural matching and working with fostering services. Ensure observations and training feedback are recorded sensitively and on time, and use feedback to strengthen future delivery. Relationships: Stay close to applicants and partners Undertake some intro chats, particularly where additional experience, judgement or continuity is needed. Step into complex applicant situations or difficult conversations without taking over work appropriately held by Journey Guides. Develop trusted operational relationships with Fostering Hubs, Regional Care Cooperatives, local authority fostering teams and other partners. Work through differences or blockages constructively, combining persistence with curiosity about other people's pressures and perspectives. Programme Addurance: Safeguarding, quality and improvement Promote a strong safeguarding culture and ensure concerns are recognised, recorded and escalated appropriately. Maintain accurate, timely records and use pipeline data, feedback and practice observations to understand performance and improve delivery. Contribute to the development of tools, guidance, communications and digital workflows as Weekenders grows. WHO WE'RE LOOKING FOR – Experience, judgement and a strongly relational approach Essential You will need a recognised social work qualification and current registration with Social Work England . Beyond that, we are looking for someone who can combine strong practice judgement with people leadership and operational oversight. You will thrive in this role if you have People-management experience – line-managing, supervising or developing staff, including giving feedback and supporting performance and wellbeing. Operational leadership – experience leading a service, programme or complex workflow with multiple people, deadlines and handovers. Children's services experience – in fostering, children's social care or a closely related setting, with a sound understanding of safeguarding and professional accountability. Training confidence – experience planning and delivering engaging adult learning, workshops or group training. Partnership skills – experience building productive relationships across organisational boundaries and working through operational challenges. A relational approach – able to hold warm, purposeful and appropriately challenging conversations with people from a wide range of backgrounds. Strong organisation and judgement – able to prioritise, delegate, manage dependencies and recognise what needs closer oversight or escalation. Digital and data confidence – comfortable using CRM and workflow systems, interpreting delivery information and turning insight into action. The way you work matters Children first – you keep children's needs, relationships and long-term outcomes at the centre of decisions. Warm and reflective – you build genuine relationships, remain curious about your own impact and welcome feedback. Courageous and accountable – you name concerns, make decisions, follow through and own mistakes. Collaborative – you share learning generously while maintaining clear accountability. Adaptable – you are comfortable in a small, ambitious organisation where roles and systems continue to evolve. Bonus points for Lived experience of the care system. Training or experience in motivational interviewing, systemic practice, coaching or another relational approach. Experience of foster carer recruitment, initial visits, assessment, prep groups, panel or post-approval support. Experience commissioning, coordinating or quality-assuring ISWs, associates or other independent practitioners. A practice educator, adult-teaching or training qualification, or substantial equivalent experience. Experience scaling a service across regions or working with a dispersed team and multiple delivery partners. Project, budget, contract, risk or resource-management experience. Experience of co-production, service design or continuous improvement. WHAT IS IN IT FOR YOU Joining Now Foster means being part of something different. We are small, ambitious and innovative, and you will have genuine influence over how Weekenders grows. You will stay close to practice and impact without carrying a statutory caseload. You will join a supportive, collaborative team that cares about doing excellent work in a sustainable and humane way. We work a 37.5-hour week and trust people to manage their time with balance. The programme sometimes requires evening work, weekend training days or travel, and we flex working time around those commitments. Salary from £40,000. 28 days of annual leave plus bank holidays. Home-based working with regular co-working and team days. Travel and reasonable work expenses covered in line with Now Foster policy. The tools and technology you need to work effectively. item.title: Oxford & Thames Valley Peer Support Lead
item.description: Are you passionate about reducing health inequalities and supporting some of the most marginalised people in our communities? We are recruiting for a compassionate, organised, and proactive Peer Support Lead to support our hepatitis C peer project in the Oxford & Thames Valley area. Peers use their lived experience to raise awareness of hepatitis C, reduce stigma, and help people access testing and treatment. Working alongside healthcare professionals, drug and alcohol services, homelessness services, and community organisations, you will recruit, train and support volunteer peers to deliver hepatitis C awareness raising, practical and emotional support. This is a varied and rewarding community-based position involving travel across the Oxford and Thames Valley region. About you We are looking for someone who can build trust and engage people with complex needs in a respectful, non-judgemental way. You’ll be a good communicator, confident working with partner services and supporting volunteers, with good organisational skills and an understanding of confidentiality, professional boundaries and managing risk. We welcome applications from people with either lived experience or professional experience relevant to the role. This may include hepatitis C, drug or alcohol use, homelessness, the criminal justice system, or supporting people facing similar challenges. Why join us? The Hepatitis C Trust is a national, patient-led charity committed to eliminating hepatitis C and improving access to harm reduction services across the UK. We are proud to be a Living Wage Employer and are committed to equality, diversity and inclusion. How to apply The closing date for applications is midnight, Sunday 27th September 2026 .

item.title: Data Curator
item.description: Within commutable distance of Beckenham, Birmingham, Blackburn, Doncaster, Redcar, Bristol or Bradford 12-month fixed term contract At the National Institute of Teaching (NIoT), we believe teaching is a fundamental societal good, a privilege and a responsibility. We are on a mission to improve the quality of teacher and leader development at a system level, using evidence, research and partnership to help shape a stronger education system for the future. This is an exciting opportunity to join an organisation with a clear and ambitious mission. Our work brings together high-quality programme delivery, rigorous research and deep sector knowledge to generate and apply insights that can improve teaching and learning across the country. The data we collect through our programmes and partnerships is central to that mission: it helps us understand what works, strengthen professional development, and ensure evidence informs practice, policy and public debate. About the role As Data Curator, you will play a key role in making sure our data can be used safely, effectively and insightfully to support research and generate impact. You will work across teams to understand how data is generated, how it is currently used, and how systems, processes and tools can be strengthened so that our data is reliable, accessible and fit for research purposes. You will work closely with colleagues behind the NIoT’s Teacher Education Dataset (TED), helping to maintain and enhance curated datasets and explore how new sources of data can strengthen our understanding of teacher and leader development. You will also collaborate with researchers and practitioners working through the NIoT’s Professional Development Laboratory, our test-and-learn centre focused on identifying and sharing effective approaches to professional development. This role would suit someone who enjoys working at the intersection of data, research and education, and who is motivated by the opportunity to contribute to work that has real sector-wide significance. This role is fixed term due to funding, and it is too early to comment on the possibility of a permanent position. This is a hybrid role, with the requirement for in person working for a minimum of once a fortnight, occasionally this will be more due to business need. The role includes participation in our annual all-staff away day (including an overnight stay) and occasional national travel. We think a wide range of different work and educational experiences could support you to be successful in this role. We encourage applications from all backgrounds, communities and industries, and are committed to employing a team that has diverse skills, experiences and abilities. Essential Criteria : Commitment to the NIoT’s mission and to improving outcomes through rigorous evidence, strong partnerships and thoughtful external engagement. Experience working with data in an education context, such as school, MAT, university, or teacher education settings. Experience applying data quality concepts — completeness, consistency, accuracy – in professional and/or research contexts. Experience of applying data governance principles in school and/or research settings. Experience interrogating and working with structured datasets, with or without technical coding skills. Familiarity with the use of qualitative and quantitative data for research purposes, as well as key issues in data interpretation such as biases and comparability. Ability to learn and adapt quickly and take initiative in the face of new challenges. Strong communication skills with the ability to communicate clearly about data to expert and non-expert audiences, adhering to high professional standards. Strong ability to work both collaboratively and independently. Motivated to work at the interface of academic and professional priorities and working cultures, with a diverse team and multiple external stakeholders. Desirable Criteria : Degree level education, or equivalent experience. Experience working as a teacher or in another professional role in schools, such as data manager. Familiarity with school data systems (MIS systems like Bromcom, SIMS, Arbor) Strong documentation skills such as writing data dictionaries, process documentation, and data flow mapping Understanding of data linking concepts and the challenges involved Knowledge of GDPR and data sharing in an education context Experience with tools like Excel, SQL, R, Python or GitHub at a basic level Degree in a relevant field such as data science, information management, education, social science, or a related discipline Evidence of continuing professional development in data management (e.g. CDMP, or relevant training) Key Benefits: Highly competitive pay and pay progression opportunities Flexible start and end working times Flexible working opportunities, including hybrid working At least 27 days’ holiday a year (plus 8 bank holidays) rising to 33 days after five years’ service Entry to the Local Government Pension Scheme A stimulating, supportive and rewarding working environment with a dedicated team of likeminded professionals Excellent opportunities to develop your skills and experience and to progress your career For more information and to apply, please visit our vacancies page. Closing date: 4.00pm on 18 September 2026. Interview date: w/c 28 September 2026. We reserve the right to close this vacancy early if we receive a high volume of applications. Candidates must already have the right to work in the UK, as we are unable to offer visa sponsorship for this role. This post requires a satisfactory enhanced disclosure from the Disclosure and Barring Service (DBS) with a Children’s Barred List Check and Occupational Health Check is required as a condition of employment .

item.title: Digital Innovation and Development Manager
item.description: Are you excited by the potential of digital technology and data to make a real difference in people's lives? Community Action Redbridge is looking for a creative, forward-thinking Digital Innovation and Development Manager to lead the next stage of our digital journey and help shape how technology supports communities across one of London's most diverse boroughs. Redbridge is home to vibrant communities and a dynamic voluntary, community and social enterprise (VCSE) sector. We want to harness the power of digital technology and data to strengthen communities, support local VCSE organisations and help create a fairer Redbridge. Working across the organisation, you'll lead the implementation of our ambitious Digital Innovation and Development Strategy. You'll help create more consistent and effective systems that reduce duplication, improve collaboration and enable our team to focus on what matters most: supporting our communities and member organisations. You'll champion a data-driven culture, helping us turn information into insight, better understand our impact, and make informed decisions that respond to emerging needs. You'll play a key role in building digital confidence across the organisation, empowering staff to embrace new technologies, develop their skills and use digital tools effectively in their everyday work. Beyond Community Action Redbridge, you'll work directly with local charities and community groups to strengthen their digital capacity, improve access to data and insight, and foster stronger connections across Redbridge's VCSE sector. If you're excited by the power of digital technology to connect people, improve services and create lasting social impact, we'd love to hear from you. About Community Action Redbridge Community Action Redbridge is a local infrastructure organisation dedicated to building a fairer Redbridge where everyone and every community has an equal opportunity to thrive. Our work supports the development of strong and resilient communities where people lead happy, healthy, and fulfilling lives. At the heart of our work is a commitment to social justice and to tackling the root causes of inequality. We’re passionate about shifting power, amplifying community voices and working collaboratively to create social change. We do this by: What it’s like to work at Community Action Redbridge We’re committed to creating a truly inclusive workplace culture that embraces and celebrates difference. Building a team that reflects the diversity of our communities and brings together a range of experiences, backgrounds and perspectives is essential to the work we do. We want Community Action Redbridge to be a safe space for everyone to bring their whole selves to work, where all our employees have the opportunity to thrive and feel recognised and valued for the work they do. We offer some great benefits including 28 days’ annual leave (including the festive closure period) plus public holidays, a free and confidential employee helpline, face-to-face and telephone counselling, and a travel loan and cycle to work scheme. How to apply Please submit your CV and a covering letter answering the following 4 questions (no more than 500 words each): Describe a digital transformation, systems improvement or innovation project that you have led. What was the challenge, what approach did you take, and what impact did it have on the organisation, team or service users? Why do you want to join Community Action Redbridge, and how do your values, skills and experience equip you to help us use digital technology to strengthen communities and create positive social change? Please apply directly through the CharityJob website by midnight on Monday 28th September 2026. First-stage interviews will take place online on Tuesday 6th October 2026. Candidates successfully shortlisted from the first stage will be invited to attend a second-stage interview in person, which is expected to take place on Tuesday 13th October 2026. If you would like an informal conversation about the role before applying, please email us directly to arrange a suitable time.
