item.title: Side-by-Side Community Engagement Worker
item.description: About the role The Side-by-Side project supports children in care and care leavers to have the same opportunities as those who have not experienced care. For many young people, navigating the care system and especially the transition to leaving care can be complex, isolating, and overwhelming. Too often, care-experienced young people are expected to face adulthood before they are ready, without the safety nets of family, friends, and community networks that many of us take for granted. The project provides a mentoring and befriending service, offering consistent, trusted relationships that help young people feel less alone, build confidence and life skills, and navigate key life changes as they move towards independence. Side-by-Side supports young people with a range of needs, including those who may be at risk of exploitation, unaccompanied asylum-seeking children, and young people living with identified mental health challenges. The project is guided by strong safeguarding practice, built on trust, and delivered through trauma-informed, person-centred approaches. Working 18 hours per week, you will work directly with young people through engagement sessions, group activities and co-designed initiatives. You will also work alongside volunteers, supporting them to safely and effectively engage with young people. This role does not involve acting as a young person’s key worker or holding a caseload. Instead your focus is on enabling connections, strengthening community networks and creating opportunities for young people to thrive across Solihull. Please note this is a fixed term contract position for 12 months. About you We are looking for a compassionate and motivated individual with strong local knowledge and a commitment to community-based support. You will be confident working directly with care-experienced young people, including those who may be at risk of exploitation, unaccompanied asylum-seeking children, and young people living with identified mental health challenges. Your key responsibilities will include: Build community links: develop relationships with local venues, services, and partners to support young people and Side-by-Side activities. Support volunteers: recruit, train, and guide volunteers, helping them signpost young people to relevant services. Engage young people: deliver activities, gather feedback, and support co-designed initiatives to ensure young people shape the services they receive. Live our values: all work is guided by trust, reducing loneliness, providing practical and emotional support, and delivering person-centred approaches. Employee benefits We offer the following employee benefits: 26 days, increasing to 30 days annual leave plus bank holidays (pro rata for part time) Occupational sick pay (subject to completion of qualifying period) Enhanced pay for family friendly leave Free parking at some of our offices Employee assistance programme Group stakeholder pension scheme Access to BHSF health cash plan Cycle to work scheme Support and supervision from your line manager Learning and Development opportunities How to apply Please visit our website for the job description and to apply. In your application, you will need to evidence, using specific examples, how your skills and experience meet the criteria laid out in the person specification, within the job description attached. The interview date will be confirmed and are expected to take place in person in Solihull Safeguarding and Compliance NYAS operates robust safe procedures to ensure the protection of the children, young people and adults at risk we work with. To comply with NYAS’s Safeguarding and Child Protection Policy, candidates will be subject to an enhanced DBS check, references and a Digital Risk Assessment. In accordance with UK immigration law, NYAS is required to ensure that all prospective candidates have the legal right to work in the United Kingdom. Therefore, proof of eligibility to work in the UK will be required as part of the recruitment process. We reserve the right to close the advert early should the right candidate be found before the closing date. About NYAS As an established leading rights-based charity, NYAS (National Youth Advocacy Service) is well positioned to ensure that children, young people, and adults across England and Wales are fully respected, represented, and supported in expressing their views and having their rights upheld. We work with care-experienced children, young people, and adults who are often reliant on statutory services suffering the negative impact of the cuts in public expenditure. Our combination of social care and legal services places us in a unique position to ensure that they receive the services they need and that their voices are heard. We are an equal opportunities employer and we are committed to creating an inclusive environment which means NYAS welcomes applications from all individuals regardless of age, disability, gender identity, sexual orientation, ethnic origin, nationality, religion or belief, or any other protected characteristic. NYAS is proud to share that we are a Disability Confident Employer and we guarantee to interview all disabled applicants who meet the minimum criteria for our vacancies. Work with us to help change young lives.

item.title: Executive Director
item.description: Help lead the next chapter of an award-winning, volunteer-powered environmental charity As we celebrate our 10-year anniversary, Shrewsbury Food Hub is looking for an inclusive, practical and strategically minded Executive Director to lead us through the next phase of our development. We have a simple vision: a community where food is valued and not wasted. Founded in 2016, we rescue surplus food seven days a week from local suppliers and redistribute it through charities, community groups, schools and Foodshares. In the year to March 2026 alone, we rescued more than 270 tonnes of food, with our work reaching an estimated 4,000 people every week across Shrewsbury and the surrounding area. We have also developed a growing programme of community cooking, bringing people together to build skills and confidence, share food and strengthen community – while ensuring that good food does not go to waste. The opportunity Shrewsbury Food Hub has grown significantly over the past decade. Our next Executive Director will help us build on that success while strengthening the foundations beneath it. This is an exciting opportunity to lead an established and much-loved local charity through a period of organisational development: bringing greater clarity, focus, structure and resilience while protecting the energy, relationships and community spirit that make the Hub special. The Board is committed to focusing increasingly on governance and delegating day-to-day leadership and management to the Executive Director. You will have the authority and responsibility to lead the organisation, work closely with our Senior Leadership Team and create the conditions in which staff and volunteers can perform at their best. This is not a figurehead role. We need an Executive Director who can see the bigger picture, make difficult choices and turn strategy into practical action – someone equally comfortable around the Board table and spending time with the staff, volunteers and partners who make our work possible. This role is largely based in Shrewsbury, with some home working possible. This is a strongly place-based role requiring a regular and visible on-site presence. What you will lead Working with the Board, staff, volunteers and partners, you will: Lead the development and delivery of a clear, focused and financially sustainable strategy. Strengthen our structures, systems, processes and ways of working, leading organisational change with clarity and sensitivity. Provide overall leadership for safe, reliable and effective operations and organisational risk. Build an inclusive, enabling and accountable culture, supporting and developing our Senior Leadership Team and wider community of staff and volunteers. Oversee financial sustainability and the development of a strong, balanced income base. Build trusted relationships with funders, suppliers, businesses, local authorities and community partners, acting as a visible and credible ambassador for the Hub. Please see the full Job Description and Person Specification for further details. Who are we looking for? You will bring successful senior leadership experience from a charity, social enterprise, public service or other purpose-led organisation, together with experience of shaping strategy, leading change and turning plans into results. You will be financially astute, pragmatic and comfortable creating clarity in a busy organisation. Above all, you will be a genuine people leader : emotionally intelligent, approachable and able to build trust across a diverse community of staff, volunteers, trustees, founders and partners. We don't expect our new Executive Director to be a specialist in everything. You may bring particular depth in operational and organisational leadership or in income generation, fundraising and external development . What matters is that you have credible experience of the other and the leadership ability to bring different expertise together. Previous Executive Director experience is welcome, but is not essential. Our values We want our new Executive Director to share our commitment to reducing food waste and strengthening our community, and to lead in a way that reflects our values: Passion – Accountability – Inclusiveness – Integrity – Caring – Resilience These values shape not only what we do, but how we work together. We are looking for a leader who enables others to succeed, listens to different perspectives, acts with integrity and empathy, and remains purposeful and constructive through change. Our ambitions remain firmly rooted in place. We believe there is significant potential to deepen our environmental and social impact across Shrewsbury and Shropshire , rather than becoming a national organisation. How to apply: Please submit your CV and a covering letter of no more than three pages , outlining your suitability for the role, by 5pm on Friday 25 September 2026 . Shortlisted candidates will be invited to visit Shrewsbury Food Hub on Monday 5 October 2026 , providing an opportunity to meet the team, see the Hub in action and gain a deeper understanding of the organisation ahead of formal interviews. Shrewsbury Food Hub values the strength that comes from different experiences and perspectives. We welcome applications from candidates with diverse backgrounds and are committed to a fair and accessible recruitment process. #Executive Director #Executive Director Jobs #Executive Director Charity #Executive Director Non Profit #Executive Director Third Sector #Executive Director Voluntary Sector #Charity Executive Director #Executive Leadership #Senior Leadership #Strategic Leadership #Charity Leadership #Charity Leader #Charity Director #Director Charity #Director Jobs #Chief Executive #Chief Executive Officer #Charity CEO #Non Profit Leadership #Third Sector Leadership #EnvironmentalCharity #ShrewsburyFoodHub #Shropshire

item.title: Senior Data Insight Analyst
item.description: About the role We’re looking for a Senior Data Insight Analyst to be the lead analyst and data product owner dedicated to our Support and Influencing directorate. You’ll develop high-quality reporting, analysis and data products that help colleagues understand service performance, improve access and equity, and demonstrate the impact of our services, policy and influencing work. You’ll turn complex data into clear, actionable insight that supports service design, strategic planning, evaluation, partnerships and decision-making across the charity. You’ll be confident working with multiple datasets and data sources, developing reporting and analytics roadmaps with stakeholders, and presenting findings clearly to non-technical audiences. You’ll have strong skills in SQL and Excel, alongside experience using BI and data visualisation tools such as Power BI, Tableau or similar. You’ll be a collaborative problem-solver who can navigate ambiguity, build trusted relationships, champion data quality and help others feel confident using data and insight to improve services and outcomes. item.title: Head of People, Culture and Learning - Women's Environmental Network - 6 month FTC
item.description: Head of People, Culture & Learning Women's EnvironmentalCharity £50,798 pro rata | Initial 6-Month FTC | 35 hours per week | Hybrid, with remote working considered Immediate start required. Please note that CVs will be reviewed and submitted on a rolling basis, therefore early applications are strongly encouraged. Are you an experienced HR professional looking for an opportunity to combine your people expertise with meaningful, purpose-driven work? Our client is a pioneering environmental charity working at the intersection of women, health, equity and environmental justice. Through an intersectional feminist approach, they support communities to take climate action, amplify underrepresented voices and drive systemic change. This is a rare opportunity to join a respected, values-led organisation and play a key role in shaping its people, culture and learning agenda during an important period of organisational development. Reporting to the Executive Director, you will become the senior people specialist and trusted adviser, providing expert guidance on employee relations, employment law, policy development, organisational culture and learning. Working closely with senior leaders and Trustees, you'll help strengthen people practice, build management capability and embed sustainable ways of working across the organisation. Key Responsibilities Lead complex and sensitive employee relations matters. Provide expert employment law advice and guidance. Review, develop and implement people policies and processes. Coach and develop managers to confidently lead their teams. Drive organisational development, culture and leadership initiatives. Design and coordinate learning and development activity. Support senior leaders and Trustees with people-related governance and decision making. About You We are keen to hear from experienced: Heads of People Senior HR Business Partners HR Consultants You will bring: CIPD Level 7 qualification (or equivalent senior-level expertise). Significant experience in employment law and complex employee relations. Experience developing people policies, management capability and organisational culture. Strong stakeholder management, coaching and influencing skills. Excellent judgement, discretion and credibility. A commitment to equity, inclusion and values-led working. Availability to start at short notice and commit to an initial six-month contract, with potential for extension. Why Join? Join an organisation at the forefront of environmental and social justice. Shape a newly created senior people role with genuine influence. Partner directly with senior leaders and Trustees. Help build lasting capability, culture and organisational impact. Flexible hybrid working, with remote working considered. Potential for the contract to be extended beyond the initial six-month term. Please reply to this advert for further details. We want you to have every opportunity to demonstrate your skills, ability and potential; please contact us if you require any assistance or adjustment so that we can help with making the application process work for you.

item.title: Programme and Partnerships Officers
item.description: About Us Since 1854, Embrace has been serving some of the most marginalised and excluded communities (of all faiths and none) in the Middle East. We support, enable and partner with Christians in the Middle East as they work to transform lives and restore dignity through education, healthcare and community development programmes. Without our staff, this important work simply would not be possible. About You We are looking for an organised, proactive and detail-oriented professional who enjoys working collaboratively and building strong relationships with a wide range of people and organisations both nationally and internationally. You will be an excellent administrator with strong coordination and communication skills, able to manage multiple priorities, maintain accurate records and deliver high-quality work to deadlines. Confident using Microsoft 365 and digital systems, you will be comfortable handling sensitive information, supporting compliance processes and learning new systems quickly. Experience in the charity, international development, humanitarian or faith-based sectors would be advantageous, particularly where this includes programme, partnership or grant management support. Above all, you will share our values, demonstrate cultural sensitivity and be enthusiastic about contributing to Embrace's mission and Christian ethos. Role Overview This is an exciting opportunity to play a meaningful role in helping Embrace the Middle East bring hope, dignity and lasting change to some of the region's most vulnerable communities. Working alongside local Christian partners and churches in the Middle East, you will help to ensure that life-changing programmes are delivered effectively, relationships are nurtured and vital support reaches those who need it most. As a key member of the Programmes, Partnerships and Advocacy team, you will coordinate programme activities, support grant and partnership management processes, maintain high-quality information and contribute to projects that strengthen our impact across the Middle East. You will work closely with colleagues across the organisation, helping to translate programme insight into compelling stories, fundraising initiatives, advocacy work and supporter engagement. This is a varied and rewarding role that offers the opportunity to make a tangible contribution to Embrace's mission while developing your experience within international development and partnership management. Hours: Full or part-time (36.5 / 30 hours per week) applications will be considered. Contract: Two-year fixed-term contract. Location: High Wycombe / Hybrid (minimum one day a month in the office, plus extra as required). Staff benefits at Embrace the Middle East: To support every member of staff to work as effectively as possible, Embrace offers remote and flexible working arrangements. This includes flexitime and home-working arrangements. Flexitime - start work between 7:30am - 10:00am and finish between 3:00pm - 6:00pm. Our core collaborative working hours are between 10:00am to 3:00pm. Pension - option to join from day 1. Maximum employer contribution of 10%. Holiday - 32 days, including 8 bank holidays and a day off work for your birthday, rising to 33 days after 5 years' service and 34 days after 10 years' service, plus 3 days leave between Christmas and the New Year. Life Assurance - 3x salary. Access to retail discount portal. Employee Assistance Programme (confidential counselling, legal and financial advice) - available 24/7, 365 days a year. Training and development programme for all employees. Commitment to staff health & wellbeing. For more information and to apply, please visit our careers page. Closing date: midday on Thursday, 24th September 2026. We reserve the right to close this vacancy and conduct interviews in advance of the closing date should suitable applications be received. Embrace the Middle East provides equal opportunity for all job applicants and employees and is committed to providing a work environment free of discrimination. We are dedicated to an inclusive culture, and we strive to create a workplace where teams of people with diverse backgrounds, characteristics, perspectives, ideas and experiences work together. We welcome applications from all individuals irrespective of age, disability, gender reassignment, marriage or civil partnership, pregnancy or maternity, race, religion or belief, sex, sexual orientation, or socio-economic background. At Embrace the Middle East, we are committed to ensuring our recruitment process is inclusive and accessible to all. If you require any reasonable adjustments during the application or selection process, please contact our HR Team. We will be happy to discuss how we can support you and ensure you have a fair opportunity to demonstrate your suitability for the role. Any information you provide will be handled with sensitivity and in confidence. To monitor diversity in our recruitment practices you will be invited to complete an anonymous Equality, Diversity and Inclusion questionnaire as part of the application process. Sympathy with and support for Embrace the Middle East's Christian ethos, mission and values. Comfortable working within a Christian organisation and engaging respectfully with Christian practices, partners, churches and supporters. We welcome the responsible use of AI tools to support your application, for example to help with research, structure or clarity. However, your application should remain an authentic reflection of your own skills, experience, achievements and motivations. We are keen to understand your unique perspective and suitability for the role, and you may be asked to discuss and expand upon the information provided during the recruitment process. Please note that, in order to be considered for this position, you must have the right to work in the UK through nationality, settled or pre-settled status, or a relevant visa that permits you to undertake the role. Embrace the Middle East is not currently able to offer visa sponsorship for this position. The successful candidate will be required to complete a medical questionnaire and undertake a disclosure check as part of the Charity's safer recruitment policy.

item.title: Youth Volunteer Officer
item.description: Youth Volunteering Officer 35 hours per week, temporary contract until December 2028. We are Chester Zoo We're not just an award-winning visitor attraction that's home to 30,000 incredible animals within 128 acres of stunning gardens. We're a major conservation charity committed to preventing extinction and restoring nature, both locally and globally. As the world faces an extinction crisis, we're making a significant contribution to conservation when it's needed most. We are Chester Zoo and we prevent extinction. The Role We have an exciting opportunity for a Youth Volunteering Officer to join our Volunteering Team within the Conservation Education and Engagement Directorate. As a Youth Volunteering Officer, you will work closely with the Volunteer Manager and the Networks for Nature project staff to deliver an inclusive volunteering programme for young people aged 14-25. The role focuses on creating meaningful opportunities that connect young people with conservation and social action, whilst supporting their personal development and wellbeing. The Youth Volunteering Officer will recruit, train and mentor young volunteers, ensuring high-quality experiences that are inclusive, safe and impactful. The Youth Volunteering Officer will also recruit, train and support adult Youth Champion Volunteers who will be empower and support the youth volunteers to participate and engage in the volunteer programme. As Youth Volunteer Officer, you will co-ordinate a supported programme for young people that will include practical conservation, visitor engagement and the Conservation Changemakers programme, designing and delivering their own projects while recognising and evidencing the skills they gain. The role will also support the delivery of our wider youth programmes including our Environmental Leadership courses, and Youth Network events supporting pathways for young people to access training, events, and volunteer experiences. We're looking for someone who can: Programme Delivery With guidance from the Volunteer Manager, coordinate and deliver youth volunteering opportunities for young people aged 14-25, including practical conservation activities, visitor engagement opportunities and social action projects. Support young people to develop skills, confidence and experience through meaningful volunteering. Volunteer Recruitment and Support Recruit, induct, train and support youth volunteers, ensuring they receive a positive and rewarding volunteering experience. Support young people to access pathways into conservation, community action and the wider youth programme. Recruit, train and support Youth Champion Volunteers who play a key role in encouraging and facilitating youth participation within the programme. Inclusive Participation Work proactively to reduce barriers to participation and provide tailored support for young people from diverse backgrounds, including those with disabilities, neurodiversity, mental health challenges or socio-economic disadvantage. Youth-led Projects and Co-production Coordinate and facilitate youth-led conservation and community action projects through the Conservation Changemakers programme. Enable young people to generate ideas, plan activities, take ownership of projects and evidence their learning and achievements. Events, Training and Activities Planning and Delivery With support from the Volunteer Manager, deliver volunteer events, training sessions, workshops and networking opportunities for youth volunteers, working with colleagues and partners to provide engaging and high-quality experiences. Support the delivery of youth programme events, including Environmental Leadership courses. Participant Engagement Monitoring Monitor participation through surveys, feedback mechanisms and regular check-ins. Collate engagement and outcome data, contributing to project evaluation and reporting for internal stakeholders and funders. Daily Volunteer Engagement Manage day-to-day communication with youth volunteers and Youth Champion Volunteers, including responding to enquiries, processing applications, maintaining records, organising rotas and training bookings, and providing ongoing support. Safeguarding, Safety and Risk Assessments Work with the Volunteer Manager to ensure all youth volunteering activities operate within safeguarding policies and procedures. Assist with risk assessments and ensure that appropriate welfare, wellbeing and safety measures are embedded throughout all activities. Partnership Working Work with the Volunteer Manager to develop effective working relationships with schools, colleges, youth organisations, community groups and relevant internal departments to increase participation, reduce barriers to engagement and strengthen programme delivery. What makes Chester Zoo a great place to work? Well, where do we start? Here goes… We’re a huge team of conservationists, scientists, educators, animal welfare experts, marketeers, visitor experience professionals, environmental policy influencers; the list goes on. Each and every one of us is on a mission to make Chester Zoo the best in the world, and our planet a better place. As the UK’s biggest and best zoo, we have ambitious goals, exciting plans, and there’s always lots going on here. We’re an inclusive and diverse organisation, made up of over 600 permanent and 500 temporary team members, and we know how important it is to invest in our colleagues to help boost their career development. We have ambitious goals, and we want you to be with us for the long term on our exciting journey. Our working environment could not be more different from a typical office – where else can you see critically endangered orangutans from your office window, or stroll among rare giraffes and tigers on your lunch break? The Package • Fixed term contract until December 2028 • 35 hours per week • Salary £24,062.50 per annum (pro rata based on 35 hours per week) • The postholder will work 5 days out of 7 including a regular weekend day • 33 days annual leave plus the option to buy or sell up to 5 days (pro rota) • Staff pass so you can visit the zoo during your time off, plus multiple complimentary tickets for your friends and family • Cycle to work scheme • Healthcare plan • Discounted gym membership • Discounts on cinema tickets, restaurants, high street shops and more via Perks • Pension scheme with generous employer contributions Our Requirements • An understanding of and commitment to Chester Zoo's mission, vision and values. • Experience of working with young people. • Experience of coordinating, supporting or working with volunteers. • Experience of delivering training, workshops or activities with a range of audiences. • Knowledge of inclusive practice and supporting young people with diverse needs. • Strong organisational, administrative and planning skills. • Excellent communication and interpersonal skills. • Excellent communication and literacy skills including by phone, face to face and via email/online discussion boards • Ability to build positive relationships with young people, colleagues and partner organisations. • Sound working knowledge of Microsoft Office applications and digital communication tools. • Experience of working in a busy office environment as part of a team & on own initiative • Full UK driving licence. Although not essential, the following would be desirable: • Knowledge of youth work/ youth engagement which could be demonstrated by a relevant qualification in youth work, education, community development, related field or relevant experience • Experience of delivering conservation, environmental or outdoor learning activities. • Experience of supporting young people facing barriers to participation. • Working knowledge of volunteer management systems. • Knowledge of safeguarding legislation and best practice. • Experience of monitoring and evaluating volunteering activities Additional Information • Due to the nature of the role, this post is subject to an enhanced DBS check. • The closing date for applications is 27/09/2026. Networks for Nature is made possible with The National Lottery Heritage Fund, thanks to National Lottery players.

item.title: People Operations Manager
item.description: The role The People Operations Manager will be responsible for developing and embedding effective people, operational and organisational practices across The Carers’ Centre. The role will combine strong HR practice with a practical understanding of how the organisation operates, ensuring that managers have the tools, processes, guidance and confidence they need to lead effectively. A key focus of the role will be developing clear and consistent ways of working, including policies, procedures, standard operating procedures and management guidance, and supporting managers to embed these in day-to-day practice. About you You are an experienced people and operations professional who enjoys making organisations work better. You have or are working towards completing your CIPD level 5 qualification. You combine strong HR knowledge with practical operational judgement and are confident turning policies, requirements and ideas into clear processes that people can use. You are organised, proactive and confident building positive relationships with managers, staff and external partners. About us The Carers’ Centre is a local independent charity with a big vision! We want to live in a community where unpaid carers are fully recognised, valued, and supported. By joining The Carers’ Centre, you are joining a team dedicated to helping families across Bath and North East Somerset when they need us most. We provide trusted information, advice, and support to unpaid carers, from as young as 5 years old. We enable our community to maintain and improve their health and wellbeing, stay in control of their caring role and connect with others in a similar position. In addition, we work with the wider community to improve recognition and support for unpaid carers. We are committed to safeguarding and promoting the welfare of children, young people and vulnerable adults, and expect all staff and volunteers to share this commitment. All applicants are subject to a satisfactory Disclosure and Barring Service check and at least two independent references. We are committed to providing services that embrace diversity and promote equality of opportunity. Why join us? · We want our employees to have more control over their work/life balance, that’s why we offer flexible start and finish times, as well as the ability to enjoy our beautiful riverside office which come with free parking, and to work from the comfort of your home. · With work/life balance in mind and the many caring roles we know people can experience, we make sure our policies work for families. · By joining The Carers’ Centre, you’ll be part of strong and dedicated team, where collaboration and support is at the heart. We’re all in this to make the world a little better. · As a small but powerful local charity, we rely on digital innovation. You’ll have access to a large suite of digital tools to support you to make the biggest impact in your role. · As well as all this, you will receive a 5% pension contribution, generous sickness pay and 25 days annual leave plus bank holidays and an additional wellbeing day as well as discounts through an employee discount scheme. In addition, you will also get an additional day of annual leave each year, for 5 years. Key responsibilities Human Resources · Work with the Senior Management Team and People Sub Group in the development and implementation of a People Strategy. · Ensure staff and volunteers receive relevant and timely training in line with organisational plans and commissioned contracts. · Lead on supporting day-to-day performance management throughout the whole employment lifecycle. · Be the first point of contact for HR queries from staff and managers. · Monitor, report and respond to changing wellbeing needs of staff and volunteers. · Serve as a point of contact between the charity and Stone King (or similar HR legal advice), Occupational Health, Access to Work and SafeHR. Line Management · Manages the administration and volunteer officers to help them maximise their potential and effectiveness. · Provide guidance and clarity around priorities and goals, ensuring work plans are achieved. Compliance · Work with the Deputy CEO to ensure the charity is legally compliant in relation to all aspects of employment, equality and health and safety legislation. · Ensure that policies and procedures are developed, maintained, and applied across the organisation. · Provide guidance and support to staff to maintain compliance. · Help the Health and safety lead to ensure risk assessments are up to date and ensure relevant actions are taken to mitigate risks for our premises and services. · Work with the Data Protection Lead to ensure the charity’s day-to-day compliance with Data Protection policies and procedures. Operational Practice · Develop, document and embed effective organisational processes and ways of working, working with managers to ensure they are practical and consistently applied. · Develop and maintain Standard Operating Procedures (SOPs), guidance and templates for key organisational processes. · Identify opportunities to improve efficiency, consistency and quality, making practical recommendations to the Deputy CEO. · Support the implementation of organisational changes and new ways of working, ensuring that managers and staff understand their responsibilities. · Build managers’ confidence and capability through practical advice, coaching and training on people management and organisational processes. · Develop and deliver guidance or training for managers where common issues, new processes or changes in practice are identified. Administration · Oversight of the charity admin function. · Maintain HR records using Safe HR. · Process DBS checks. · Provide HR KPI’s to the Deputy CEO on a monthly basis. · Working with the CEO and Deputy CEO to undertake quality assurance assessments as agreed in the organisational plan. · Provide admin support to the People Sub-Group. Finance · Work within agreed budgets. · Contribute towards funding applications as appropriate for the role and provide relevant feedback for funders. General · Stay informed and regularly raise staff awareness of changes in employment legislation and Health and Safety · Adhere to the Carers’ Charter. · Encourage carers to provide feedback on The Carers’ Centre services and to become actively involved in shaping future delivery. · Ensure that you adopt good practice within the Carers Trust network. · Ensure that you work within The Carers’ Centre policy framework.

item.title: Advise and Navigation Manager
item.description: Advice & Navigation Manager 6-Month Fixed-Term Contract (potential to extend) 28 hours per week (4 days) Hybrid Working | North London £30,310 per annum (pro rata salary based on £37,887 FTE) ASAP Start Subject to an Enhanced DBS check A community-focused charity is seeking an experienced Advice & Navigation Manager to lead and develop a busy frontline service supporting individuals experiencing poverty, health inequalities, social isolation, housing challenges and other forms of disadvantage. This is an excellent opportunity for an experienced service manager with a strong background in casework oversight, safeguarding, service quality and team leadership . Managing a team delivering advice, navigation and social prescribing support, you will ensure residents receive high-quality, person-centred services that make a genuine difference to their lives. The Role A key focus of this position is the oversight and management of complex casework. You will ensure effective triage, caseload allocation, case progression and closure, supporting staff to deliver safe, timely and impactful interventions. Alongside day-to-day service management, you will provide leadership to a team of advice workers, social prescribing practitioners and volunteers, ensuring high standards of practice, compliance and safeguarding. You will also work closely with health partners, statutory agencies and community organisations to strengthen referral pathways and improve outcomes for residents. Key Responsibilities Lead the delivery of advice, navigation and social prescribing services. Oversee casework management, including referrals, triage, caseload allocation, quality assurance and case progression. Support staff with complex cases, safeguarding concerns and complaints. Line manage and develop a team of frontline staff and volunteers through supervision, coaching and performance management. Ensure compliance with safeguarding, data protection, health and safety and organisational policies. Monitor service performance, outcomes and impact, using data and insight to support continuous improvement. Build and maintain effective partnerships across health, local authority and voluntary sector organisations. Contribute to reporting, service planning and the delivery of contractual and funding requirements. About You We are looking for someone who can demonstrate: Significant experience managing advice, navigation, support, advocacy or community-based services. Strong experience overseeing complex casework involving vulnerable or disadvantaged individuals. Experience managing or supporting social prescribing, community health or welfare advice services. A thorough understanding of safeguarding, risk management and professional boundaries. Experience leading, supporting and developing teams through effective supervision and performance management. A track record of working in partnership with health, statutory and voluntary sector organisations. Experience using data and service insight to improve performance and demonstrate impact. Excellent communication, organisational and stakeholder management skills. Desirable Experience Social prescribing within primary care or community settings. Service development, improvement or change management. Leading hybrid or community-based teams. A relevant qualification in advice, health, social care or management. We want you to have every opportunity to demonstrate your skills, ability and potential; please contact us if you require any assistance or adjustment so that we can help with making the application process work for you.

item.title: Service Manager - LBN Support Service
item.description: REPORTING TO: Head of Services RESPONSIBLE FOR: Team Leaders and other service-based roles as required PURPOSE OF POSITION The Service Manager will have overall responsibility for the operational leadership, quality, performance and contract delivery of both the LB Newham Core and the Intensive Support Accommodation contracts. The role will ensure a joined-up support pathway for residents with low, medium, high and complex support needs, promoting safety, stabilisation, independence, move-on and long-term tenancy sustainment. The post-holder will lead staff teams to deliver high-quality, trauma-informed, strengths-based and person-centred support for vulnerable single homeless adults, including residents with multiple disadvantage, high levels of risk and complex support needs. The role will set, monitor and embed clear resettlement and support standards, ensuring residents receive consistent assessment, support planning, risk management, move-on preparation and tenancy sustainment support. The role will be accountable for safeguarding, housing management, performance reporting, quality assurance, partnership working, commissioner confidence and continuous service improvement. What makes this role different • Lead the full move-on journey, from pre-tenancy preparation to sustaining community accommodation, ensuring residents receive timely, effective support. • Combine trauma informed support, tenancy sustainment, homelessness prevention, partnership working and values-led leadership to help residents build independence. • Work with Resident Services, Intensive Housing Management team. landlords, commissioners and agencies to prevent repeat homelessness and improve outcomes. • Lead with purpose, strengthen practice and model a learning culture rooted in Growth, Inclusion, Collaboration and Compassion. The role will require participation in the on-call rota and occasional evening and weekend work in line with service needs. RESPONSIBILITIES & ACCOUNTABILITIES Key Responsibilities • Lead the delivery supported accommodation contracts in line with commissioner expectations, contract requirements, organisational policies and agreed performance standards. • Provide clear management oversight of service quality, safety, safeguarding, risk, incidents, complex cases and escalation. • Ensure residents receive effective assessments, risk management, support planning, move-on planning and outcome-focused reviews. • Set and maintain clear resettlement standards across the service, ensuring residents are supported to develop independent living skills, secure appropriate move-on options and sustain accommodation after leaving the service. • Ensure support standards are consistently applied, including timely assessments, person-centred support plans, regular key work, outcome-focused reviews, accurate case recording and clear escalation of risk or non-engagement. • Promote trauma-informed, strengths-based and psychologically informed practice across the service. • Work closely with the Intensive Housing Management team to oversee housing-related support, including referrals, placements, rent accounts, Housing Benefit claims, arrears prevention, voids, licence or tenancy obligations, move-on and tenancy sustainment. • Ensure the intensive supported accommodation service provides safe, responsive and proportionate support for residents with complex needs and high levels of risk. • Monitor performance against contract indicators, including outcomes, safeguarding, engagement, rent accounts, move-on, tenancy sustainment, voids and resident feedback. • Prepare accurate reports, evidence and performance commentary for commissioner monitoring, audits, inspections and service reviews. • Lead, develop and support staff to work as one team while maintaining service-specific boundaries, contractual standards, professional accountability and Your Place values. • Maintain effective staffing arrangements, including cover for key working, weekend, out-of-hours and intensive provision requirements. • Build strong partnerships with commissioners, Adult Social Care, health services, substance misuse services, criminal justice partners, housing providers and community agencies. • Use service data, resident feedback and quality assurance activity to drive improvement, demonstrate impact and evidence value for money. • Work closely with the Quality Assurance Manager and Impact Manager to use performance data, quality assurance findings, resident feedback and outcome measures to identify trends, strengthen practice and drive continuous service improvement. • Work flexibly to respond to urgent operational issues, safeguarding concerns, incidents, commissioner requests and service pressures. • Embed person-centred practice and meaningful co-production with residents, ensuring services are shaped by lived experience and aligned with Your Place values of Growth, Inclusion, Collaboration and Compassion PERSON SPECIFICATION The successful candidate will bring the experience, knowledge, leadership skills and values needed to manage high-quality supported accommodation services and contribute effectively to the wider Your Place team. Essential Criteria • Experience managing or supervising staff in supported housing, homelessness, social care, community support or a similar setting. • Ability to lead change, improve practice and support staff through service development. • Experience supporting vulnerable homeless adults, rough sleepers or people facing multiple disadvantage. • Strong understanding of risk, safeguarding, trauma, mental health, substance misuse, tenancy sustainment and move-on barriers. • Experience leading services that manage challenging behaviour, anti-social behaviour, safeguarding concerns, tenancy breaches, arrears or complex risk. • Experience of contract management, performance monitoring, quality assurance, reporting and service improvement. • Good understanding of housing management, including arrears, voids, tenancy or licence breaches, maintenance, health and safety, and property-related risk. • Ability to analyse performance information, identify risks and trends, produce clear reports and use data to drive improvement. • Experience building constructive relationships with commissioners, statutory services, voluntary sector partners and internal stakeholders. • Knowledge of person-centred, strengths-based, trauma-informed and psychologically informed support. • Knowledge of safeguarding adults, mental capacity, confidentiality, professional boundaries, data protection, equality and diversity, and complaints handling. • Excellent written and verbal communication skills, including clear reports, briefings and monitoring returns. • Commitment to resident involvement, co-production, equality, diversity, inclusion and anti-discriminatory practice. Desirable Criteria • Experience managing commissioned homelessness or supported accommodation contract. • Experience working within or alongside London local authority homelessness pathways. • Experience of managing voids, referrals, move-ins, move-outs and partnership-based accommodation arrangements. • Experience of using Home Star, In-Form, Pyramid or equivalent systems to monitor support, tenancy sustainment, risk, outcomes and case recording. • Experience preparing for audits, inspections, commissioner reviews or contract monitoring meetings. • Experience leading services through mobilisation, remodelling, restructure or improvement planning. Aptitude and Behaviours confidently use performance data, resident feedback and quality assurance learning to improve outcomes and value for money. Provides values-led leadership and communicates clearly with staff, residents, commissioners and partners. Use written, numerical and performance information to make sound, accountable and compliant decisions. Involving and Including Embeds resident involvement and promotes dignity, choice, equality, inclusion and cultural competence. Build and develop a high-performing team through clear direction, supervision, support and accountability. Appointment is subject to an enhanced DBS check, satisfactory references and the right to work in the UK

item.title: Quality Assurance Manager - Maternity Cover
item.description: REPORTING TO: Director of Front-line Services PURPOSE OF POSITION The Quality Assurance Manager is a blended leadership role combining strategic quality assurance, performance oversight, service management and practice development. The role is split broadly between focused on quality assurance, data-led improvement and performance oversight, and two days focused on service management, practice leadership and frontline improvement activity. The postholder will lead the development and delivery of a strong quality assurance framework across support services, ensuring that practice, performance and service delivery are safe, effective, person-centred and aligned with contractual, regulatory and organisational standards. Alongside this, the postholder will remain closely connected to frontline delivery through service management responsibilities and practice development leadership, particularly within Housing First and complex-needs services. This makes the role ideal for someone who enjoys combining strategic oversight, data insight, operational leadership and the development of high-quality, trauma-informed support practice. What makes this role different A distinctive role for someone who wants strategic influence while staying close to frontline practice. You will help shape quality, use evidence, support staff, strengthen resident outcomes and join an organisation committed to compassion, collaboration, inclusion, growth, learning and resident voice. Enjoy variety and influence work across performance oversight, service management and practice development, with scope to shape systems, standards and ways of working. RESPONSIBILITIES & ACCOUNTABILITIES Key Responsibilities Quality assurance and improvement: Lead the quality assurance function across support services, coordinating audits, quality checks, case file reviews, service reviews and improvement plans. Turn findings into practical actions that strengthen safety, consistency, resident experience, safeguarding, support planning and trauma-informed practice. Work with managers to embed learning, monitor progress and evidence improvement against internal and external standards. Performance oversight and reporting: Monitor performance against contractual, regulatory and organisational standards, including service outcomes, compliance requirements, safeguarding expectations and commissioner reporting. Identify risks, gaps, trends and good practice, escalating concerns and supporting corrective action where needed. Produce clear, evidence-based reports and briefings for senior leaders, governance meetings, commissioners and external stakeholders. Data, insight and systems: Use performance, safeguarding, complaints, incidents, resident feedback, outcomes and quality data to identify service strengths, pressures and improvement priorities. Maintain and improve reporting systems, including InForm, so information is accurate, consistent and useful. Analyse patterns, support decision-making and make practical recommendations that improve quality, accountability and resident outcomes. Information retrieval and STAIRs requests: Act as QA Manager lead for information retrieval relating to STAIRs requests, including triaging scope, gathering internal and contractor records, coordinating redaction and drafting responses within regulatory timeframes. Service and support management: Provide hands-on support management across frontline services, including Housing First improvement activity, Hope Street and St Mungo’s contracts, team rota management and the Support Manager on-call rota. Support managers and teams to manage risk, strengthen case accountability and recording, and deliver consistent, high-quality support to residents with complex needs. Practice development: Embed person-centred, trauma-informed and psychologically informed practice across support services. Develop practical tools, guidance, quality forums, workshops and reflective learning that help staff apply policy, improve support planning, strengthen safeguarding and promote consistent resident-centred practice. Resident voice and accountability: Strengthen resident engagement, feedback and involvement so resident experience informs service design, quality assurance, learning and improvement. People management and collaboration: Line manage agreed roles, including the Impact Specialist and Resident Engagement Specialist, supporting clear objectives, accountability, development and collaborative working across services. General duties: Attend key directorate, management, planning, quality and performance meetings; work flexibly across organisational priorities; and undertake other reasonable duties within the scope of the role. PERSON SPECIFICATION Assessment will be through application, interview and, where relevant, a practical assessment Quality assurance: Experience delivering quality frameworks, audits, case file reviews, standards and improvement plans that strengthen safe, consistent, person-centred and trauma-informed practice. Able to lead improvement activity, influence managers and turn findings into sustained service change. Performance and reporting: Able to monitor contractual, regulatory and organisational standards; identify risks, gaps, trends and good practice; and produce clear reports for leaders, governance forums and commissioners. Data, insight and systems: Strong analytical skills and confidence using performance, safeguarding, complaints, incidents, outcomes and resident feedback data to identify patterns, support decisions and improve services. Experience using resident feedback, consultation or involvement activity to inform quality assurance, service design and improvement, including through InForm or similar systems. Information governance: Understands confidentiality, record handling and information governance. Able to triage STAIRs requests, gather internal/contractor records, support redaction and draft timely responses. Support management and practice: Experience supporting people experiencing homelessness or rough sleeping with complex needs. Able to support managers, manage risk, strengthen recording and embed person-centred, trauma-informed, psychologically informed and anti-discriminatory practice. Safeguarding and risk: Sound knowledge of adult safeguarding, risk assessment, MARAC processes and safe information sharing with vulnerable adults. Communication and values: Strong written, verbal and facilitation skills; collaborative, organised, accurate and resilient, with commitment to compassion, collaboration, inclusion and growth. Appointment is subject to DBS check and right to work in the UK

item.title: Brand and Content Producer
item.description: Grade: 4 Salary: £37,321 per annum Hours: Full-time 37.5 hours per week (flexible working considered) Position type: Permanent Responsible to: Senior Brand Manager Direct reports: None Location: ShelterBox HQ, Truro, Cornwall or Remote (UK only) Travel: Ability to work away from home required. This may be UK (we expect up to 6 visits to Truro HQ per year) or an in-country deployment in a content gathering or representing ShelterBox role. ROLE PURPOSE: As part of in an in-house brand and creative team this role will help plan, shoot, create and oversee the production of quality audience-led graphic design and multi-media content under the ShelterBox brand. Working with the Senior Brand Manager and wider Brand and Content team, the successful candidate will deliver end-to-end projects to bring the brand alive and support our fundraising, communications and international teams to drive income, awareness and support successful user journeys. The role will advise all ShelterBox teams to work within brand guidelines and enable teams to access and use assets and templates by maintaining accurate systems. They will also support wider development of a purpose-led brand, using insight and by building strong relationships with audience and channel owners. WHO ARE WE LOOKING FOR? Are you looking to join an in-house Brand and Content team? This role would suit someone who's keen to work across all areas of the organisation, championing brand guidelines and managing and delivering a wide range of creative projects under the ShelterBox brand. You must be able to edit video and have a good knowledge graphic design and brand. It is a requirement of this role to have a working knowledge of Premier Pro, After Effects, Indesign and Illustrator, with experience across Adobe Creative Suite. You'll also be able to demonstrate great copywriting skills and have excellent attention to detail. The successful candidate will have experience in practical photography and film. You will need to be able to plan and lead a shoot and confidently pick up a camera and capture ShelterBox footage and interviews in the UK and in the countries where we work. This role will, at times, be required to deploy in both major disasters and pro-active content trips - gathering content themselves and supporting external freelancers. MAIN ROLE AND RESPONSIBILITIES: Within this role you will be a great relationship builder working across a wide range of ShelterBox teams, external agencies, partners and freelancers. A strategic thinker - able to work on multiple long and short project deadlines and prioritise to objectives. Driven by audience needs - whether that's optimising creative in response to Digital Marketing data and insight or getting under the skin of key strategic funders to make the right content at the right time to drive objectives. Experienced in working across fundraising and communications channels for both warm and cold audiences to drive income and awareness. We arelooking for a creative talent who can get to the core of ShelterBox's mission whilst remaining up to date with the detail, picking up new ideas and concepts easily. You'll understand the power of story in fundraising and communications, be self-motivated, with a can-do approach and be flexible in supporting the wider team. DUTIES WILL INCLUDE BUT NOT BE LIMITED TO: Brand: Support and train the wider organisation to effectively create content within ShelterBox brand guidelines Support the continued development of an online brand hub Support the development of a purpose led brand. Help to develop and implement a brand strategy. Help drive brand and values led storytelling across the organisation driven priority audiences Position ethical storytelling as a central thread of the ShelterBox brand Creative and content development: Manage creative projects for key ShelterBox teams working across multi-media disciplines including video, scriptwriting and graphic design. Lead projects from creative brief stage through to asset delivery including all production. Responsible for core projects split across the team including warm and cold supporter journeys, evergreen and explainer content for digital optimisation, celebrity videos, philanthropy and partnerships, Rotary. Support the digital marketing strategy. Responsible for creating asset sets for Always On and time-framed campaigns. Work to tight deadlines and respond to agency and internal feedback to continually optimise creative. Support ShelterBox to develop our in-house creative approach. Facilitate workshops and creative exercises to ensure we create objective and audience led products. Support a review of design across the organisation and enable teams to design via templates. Support the development and re-fresh of templates for both design and video. Work with external agencies, freelancers and partners. Use audience insights to inform all plans and work with the insight team and others to measure success. Ensure all projects follow sign-off processes Content gathering: Plan and lead shoots in the UK and in countries where ShelterBox works. Film a wide range of ShelterBox spokespeople including CEO, board members, programme staff, partners and high-level celebrity supporters both at an in-house studio or on location. Photograph and film events in the UK and overseas. Shoot and manage a bank of studio photography of ShelterBox aid items - responding to audience insight and channel requirements. Develop and deliver quality content training for ShelterBox staff Help to manage ShelterBox photography, sound and video equipment and studio Work closely with the ShelterBox operations team and partners to ensure we are gathering high-quality content across all our live deployments. Process and edit raw content from deployments - case studies, photos, video. Deploy to gather content or train partners - dependent on funding and strategic need. At times this may involve taking freelancers on agreed trips. Note: Deploying in major disasters or to partner organisations may involve operating within ERA areas so role will need to be HEAT trained. Interview and film communities affected by disaster Gather content to ShelterBox ethical guidelines. Planning and team working Be an integral part of team planning Offer knowledge of best practice and innovations from other organisations and sectors. Support a measurement-based approach by contributing to monthly reporting as well as spotting trends and opportunities. Any other specific projects given by the Senior Brand manager. Please note: We reserve the right to close this vacancy early if we receive a high volume of applications. We therefore encourage you to submit your application as soon as possible. Please ensure your application is completed in full and you read the applicant guidance on our website before applying.

item.title: Fundraising and Supporter Care Coordinator
item.description: Could you be the person who helps make brilliant fundraising happen behind the scenes? Natasha’s Foundation, the food allergy charity, is looking for an experienced, highly organised and personable Fundraising & Supporter Care Coordinator to join our small and ambitious fundraising team. We’re a passionate, energetic and friendly team, united by a determination to make a real difference. We work hard, move quickly and have big ambitions for a small charity – but we also really value the way we work together. Everyone brings something different, ideas are welcomed, people support one another and there’s a genuine sense of excitement about what we can achieve. This is a varied role for someone who loves working with people, takes real pride in getting the detail right and is equally comfortable supporting a donor, working with data or helping a busy fundraising team stay one step ahead. You’ll be at the heart of our fundraising operation: providing warm and thoughtful supporter care, supporting individual giving, helping us make the best use of our Beacon CRM, producing accurate fundraising and income information, and supporting proposals, reports, communications and fundraising resources. We’re looking for someone who is warm, organised, numerate and confident with data, with excellent attention to detail and practical experience of using Beacon CRM. Just as importantly, we’re looking for someone who will enjoy being part of our team – someone positive, proactive and willing to get stuck in. You’ll be joining Natasha’s Foundation at an exciting point in our journey. We are working to improve the lives of people with food allergy through education, campaigning and pioneering medical research, with one hugely ambitious goal: a future without food allergy. If you enjoy making things work brilliantly, care about giving supporters a great experience and want to bring your skills and energy to a charity where your contribution will genuinely be noticed and valued, we’d love to hear from you. 20 hours per week | Home-based | £32,000–£34,000 FTE

item.title: Energy Adviser
item.description: Energy Adviser Location : Doncaster (Office based) Salary : £27,000 per annum Hours : 37 hours per week worked over 4 days (08:00-18:00) Contract : Fixed Term until 31 October 2028 (2 years) Closing Date : 18/09/26 Help people tackle fuel poverty and improve financial resilience This role will deliver specialist energy advice and casework to residents experiencing fuel poverty, energy debt and complex energy-related problems. Working as part of a dedicated team, you will support some of Doncaster's most vulnerable households and help them achieve sustainable outcomes. About the role You'll provide in-depth energy advice and casework to clients whose circumstances require investigation, advocacy, negotiation and ongoing support. You will work directly with energy suppliers, represent clients where appropriate and help resolve complex issues including billing disputes, affordability concerns and energy debt. The role will include telephone appointments, video appointments, face-to-face appointments and occasional outreach/home visit activity. Key responsibilities Deliver specialist energy advice and in-depth casework. Conduct full assessments of client circumstances and energy needs. Investigate complex billing issues and supplier disputes. Support clients experiencing energy debt or self-disconnection risks. Negotiate with suppliers and other agencies on behalf of clients. Develop practical solutions to improve affordability and energy resilience. Maintain accurate client records and outcome reporting. Work collaboratively with colleagues and partner organisations. Contribute to achieving project targets and outcomes. About you We are looking for someone who: Has experience delivering advice, casework or advocacy services. Can manage complex cases and competing priorities. Has excellent communication and negotiation skills. Is able to work independently and take ownership of client outcomes. Has strong organisational and record-keeping skills. Is committed to empowering people and tackling inequality. Shares the values and principles of Citizens Advice. Desirable Experience of energy advice, debt advice, welfare benefits or housing advice. Understanding of fuel poverty and vulnerability within energy markets. Experience negotiating with utility providers or creditors. City & Guilds Level 3 Energy Awareness qualification, or willingness to achieve this during induction. What we offer Comprehensive training and supervision. Opportunity to develop specialist energy advice skills. Access to nationally recognised qualifications. Supportive team environment. The opportunity to make a lasting difference to vulnerable households across Doncaster. About Citizens Advice Doncaster Borough Citizens Advice Doncaster Borough provides free, confidential, impartial and independent advice to help people overcome the problems they face. Through the Energy Advice Anytime project, we are expanding access to energy advice through innovative and flexible delivery models to reach more residents, reduce fuel poverty and improve financial resilience across our communities. Citizens Advice Doncaster Borough values diversity, promotes equality and challenges discrimination. We welcome applications from all sections of the community.

item.title: Social Prescribing Link Worker
item.description: Citizens Advice Milton Keynes is a local charity that helps people to resolve their legal, money and personal problems. We have been providing free, confidential, and impartial advice since 1972 and helped over 8000 local people last year. We are looking for an enthusiastic, reliable and confident person to join us in delivering a new project based in local GP Surgeries. The ideal candidate will provide a Social Prescribing Link Worker service, to patients of Ascent Primary Care Network (Ascent PCN) in Milton Keynes, working to support patients and staff at each of their 3 medical centres across the area. The Link Worker will take referrals from the PCN’s practices, and from a wide range of external agencies, and through self-referrals. They’ll work with people to identify issues that affect their health and wellbeing and co-produce a simple personalised care and support plan that connects them to non-medical community-based activities, groups and services that meet practical, social, and emotional needs. This is a challenging role, managing a demanding caseload, working to strict quality standards and playing a full part in multi-disciplinary team of health and social care professionals. Successful candidates will be able to ensure that all work is compliant with our contract funder – Ascent PCN, and Citizens Advice standards. Applicants need to be: Computer-literate, although training on our case recording systems will be given. Able to travel between each of the 3 surgeries in Milton Keynes. Confident in working to performance targets. Able to show good communications skills, both written and verbal. These are essential in the role, as are excellent customer service skills with a non-judgemental approach. Prepared to work independently and from a variety of community-based locations. A minimum of 12 months’ experience in a social prescribing role or an agency providing advice, support and signposting (or similar setting) is desirable. The successful Applicant/s will be asked to undergo an Enhanced Disclosure and Barring Service (DBS) check. Closing date: Sunday 20th September 2026

item.title: Macmillan Project Caseworker
item.description: Citizens Advice Milton Keynes is a local charity that helps people to resolve their legal, money and personal problems. We have been providing free, confidential, and impartial advice since 1972 and helped over 8000 local people last year. As a Specialist Adviser within the Macmillan Money & More SWS Service, you will provide high-quality, confidential information, advice and support to people affected by cancer and their families across a region spanning from Milton Keynes to Cornwall. Working as part of a coordinated team of advisers across multiple Citizens Advice locations, you will take a person-centred approach to understand each client’s individual circumstances and provide tailored guidance on welfare benefits, financial support, debt, energy costs, employment issues and other practical challenges arising from a cancer diagnosis. You will help clients navigate complex systems, access available support, and improve their financial wellbeing during a difficult and often overwhelming time. Through compassionate and holistic advice, you will empower people affected by cancer to make informed decisions, build confidence, and feel supported throughout their cancer journey. The ideal candidate will provide advice and support in person, via telephone, email and video call to patients undergoing treatment for cancer. Macmillan Project Caseworkers will assist clients with complex welfare benefits and housing enquiries. This requires a good foundation knowledge of each advice area, so competence in these subjects is desirable, but full and ongoing training will be provided to support successful candidates in their professional development. This is a challenging role, managing a demanding caseload and working with people at every stage of their cancer journey. All our advice work is carried out to the strictest quality standards, and we are committed to ensuring that all our advice work complements the wider services provided by both Citizens Advice and Macmillan Cancer Care. Applicants need to be: Computer-literate, although training on our case recording systems will be given. Confident in working to performance targets. Able to show good communications skills, both written and verbal. These are essential in the role, as are excellent customer service skills with a non-judgemental approach. Prepared to work independently, sometimes remotely and also from a variety of community-based locations. A minimum of 12 months’ experience in an advice agency or similar setting is desirable. The successful Applicant/s will be asked to undergo an Enhanced Disclosure and Barring Service (DBS) check. Closing date: Sunday 20th September 2026

item.title: Services Manager (Maternity cover)
item.description: Job title: Services Manager (Maternity Cover) Salary: £44,558 – £45,895 Hours: Full-time 37.5 hours per week (part time or flexible working options considered) Location: Home-based ideally Wales or Midlands area, but any location will be considered, with travel around England and Wales Contract: Fixed term – 9 months from December 2026 Are you an experienced employability service manager who would be able to confidently step into a 9-month maternity cover position and oversee a team of up to eight passionate and person-centred Employment Consultants, helping them deliver personalised, high-quality support to veterans and their families? You will also have the opportunity to contribute to our services development and continual improvement programme. At The Poppy Factory, we believe that everyone who has served our country deserves the opportunity to build a fulfilling life beyond the armed forces. For over a century, we have stood alongside veterans and their families, evolving our services to support veterans and adult family members to overcome barriers to employment and transform their lives. What we're looking for A collaborative mindset: You will thrive working as part of a team with colleagues based across the UK who support each other in what can sometimes be a challenging role. You enjoy building strong partnerships, and work effectively with colleagues and external organisations to enhance the services we offer. Motivation and commitment: You understand that supporting people facing complex challenges can be demanding, and you're ready to bring the energy, empathy and resilience needed to support your team to succeed. Adaptability: You will often need to balance competing priorities or quickly shift focus depending on the needs of the team you will be supporting and the clients they are working with. An empowering approach: You believe in people and their potential. Whether supervising your team or developing services, your goal is to support others to grow, achieve and thrive. Why should you apply? A chance to make a lasting impact: Your work will help veterans and their families move forward in life with confidence and dignity. Competitive salary and benefits including generous holiday and pension contributions. A welcoming and empowering culture , with regular opportunities for team connecting and shared learning throughout the year. Flexibility and variety: a mix of travelling in your area, home working and to the Poppy Factory in Richmond, London Autonomy and influence: The opportunity to shape your region, build meaningful partnerships, and develop services that meet real needs. Be part of an iconic charity with over a century of history supporting the Armed Forces community. For further information, including the full job description for the role, please refer to the candidate pack. Due to the travel requirements of the role and the region covered, it is essential that the post holder is able to meet these requirements through their own transport arrangements. How to apply To apply for this position please click "Apply for this job" to submit your CV and a covering letter outlining how you meet the essential criteria in the person specification. Please address your covering letter to Debbie Boughtflower, Director of Operations. Top tip: we don't recommend using AI to generate your covering letter (we've seen a lot of covering letters and we promise, we can tell!) - we want to know what makes YOU a good fit for the role, and AI covering letters can't capture your personality, values and qualities, or what makes your specific combination of skills and experience an ideal candidate. The closing date for applications will be 23 September 2026. Please note, we cannot accept late or incomplete applications. Only applications submitted through the online process will be considered. Online interviews will be held on 1 or 2 October 2026, with potential second interviews on 12 October 2026 in person @ The Poppy Factory in Richmond, London. To arrange an informal conversation about the role, please contact Kirsty Gronow No agencies please. The successful candidates will be subject to an enhanced DBS check.
