item.title: Head of Services (Female Applicants Only)
item.description: About the role This is an exciting opportunity to join Women and Girls Network's Senior Leadership Team and lead two of our most impactful service areas: the Intersectional and Anti-Oppressive (IOS) Team and the Criminal Justice and Violence Against Women & Girls (CJS, VAWG) Team. As Head of Services, you will play a vital role in shaping and driving services that support women and girls affected by gender-based violence, ensuring they receive empowering, trauma-informed and culturally responsive support. You will lead with a strong commitment to feminist, anti-racist and anti-oppressive values, ensuring that the voices and experiences of survivors remain at the heart of everything we do. Working closely with the Director of Services and senior colleagues, you will provide strategic leadership across a diverse portfolio of services, strengthening partnerships, influencing systems and championing innovative approaches that remove barriers and improve outcomes for women facing multiple disadvantages. This is a unique opportunity for an experienced leader to make a lasting impact, both within our organisation and across the wider VAWG sector. Job description As the Head of Services, you will: Lead and inspire the IOS and CJS, VAWG teams, providing strategic direction and oversight to ensure services are accessible, high-quality, survivor-centred and aligned with WGN's feminist values and vision. Champion intersectional and anti-oppressive practice, ensuring services are responsive to the diverse experiences of women and girls, particularly those from Black and Global Majority communities and others facing systemic barriers. Drive excellence in service delivery, safeguarding and quality assurance, ensuring robust risk management and compliance while creating environments where survivors can heal, recover and thrive. Lead, support and develop Service Managers, fostering a culture of collaboration, wellbeing, accountability and continuous learning that enables staff to deliver their best work. Build influential partnerships across statutory, voluntary and community sectors, strengthening pathways for survivors and ensuring WGN's expertise informs local, regional and national responses to violence against women and girls. Use insight, evidence and survivor feedback to evaluate impact, drive innovation and shape the future development of services, ensuring they continue to meet emerging need and deliver meaningful change. Represent WGN as a sector leader, advocating for systemic change and helping to create a society where all women and girls can live free from violence, inequality and discrimination. Supporting Statement Guidance Your supporting statement should clearly demonstrate how your experience, knowledge, skills, and qualifications meet the requirements of the role. Please address the key criteria outlined in the Job Description and Person Specification, providing specific examples of achievements and responsibilities that evidence your suitability for the position. Focus on relevant professional experience, transferable skills, and the impact of your work. Where possible, use concise examples to illustrate how you have successfully applied these skills in practice. The supporting statement should be no more than 500 words and should complement, rather than repeat, the information contained in your CV or application form. Closing date and interviews This vacancy will close at 9am on Monday 28 September 2026 . Interviews will take place shortly thereafter, and shortlisted candidates will be notified of the arrangements. We encourage early applications, as we reserve the right to close the vacancy before the advertised closing date should we receive a high volume of applications or identify a suitable candidate. The selection process will consist of two interview stages and a role-related assessment task. Interviews may be conducted either in person or remotely, depending on panel availability and logistical requirements, and may involve a combination of both formats throughout the process. Candidates invited to participate will receive full details of each stage, including the assessment task and interview arrangements, in advance. About us Women and Girls Network (WGN) is a pan-London organisation that supports women and girls affected by all forms of gendered-based violence. Our overall aim is to promote, preserve and restore the mental health and well-being of women and girls who have experienced, or are at risk of, gendered-based violence, whilst working towards a society free of gendered-based violence. We do this by: Providing women-only holistic and seamless therapeutic services, which meet women and girls’ needs and contribute to total and sustainable recovery from the experiences of violence. Evidencing the impact of gendered-based violence and presenting this information in appropriate forums to affect social change in attitudes towards, and responses to, gendered-based violence. Developing good practice in the sector by providing training and guidance on specialist service provision and the development of culturally appropriate service delivery. WGN is proud to be an accredited Living Wage Employer and a member of The London VAWG Consortium, Halo Code, and Helplines Partnership. Commitment to Equity and Inclusion We are deeply committed to building a workforce that reflects the diversity, resilience and strength of the women and girls we serve. We strongly encourage applications from Black and Global Majority women and applicants with Lived Experience, including those who may not meet every criterion. WGN is an equal opportunities employer. Exemption This post is exempt under the Equality Act 2010, Schedule 9, Part 1 , and is open to female applicants only , due to the nature of the role.
item.dc:creator: Women and Girls Network

item.title: Senior Individual Giving & Campaigns Manager (Mat cover)
item.description: Senior Individual Giving & Campaigns Manager (Maternity Cover) YoungMinds Hybrid, London Bridge (1-2 days per week) £50,898 - £56,554 per annum Fixed-term, full-time contract: October 2026 to October 2027 (35 hours pw) Every day, thousands of young people across the UK struggle with their mental health. Too many are left waiting for support until they reach crisis point. At YoungMinds, we're leading the movement to change that. We amplify young people's voices, provide practical support and campaign for a future where no young person feels alone with their mental health. This work is only possible because of the incredible community of supporters who stand alongside us. We're now looking for an experienced and ambitious fundraising leader to join us as Senior Individual Giving & Campaigns Manager on a maternity cover contract and help drive the next stage of growth in our flagship mass market and individual giving activity. The opportunity This is an exciting leadership role at the heart of our Public Fundraising team. You'll lead and inspire a talented team responsible for growing income through mass market fundraising, individual giving and high-profile campaigns, including our flagship campaign, #HelloYellow which engages thousands of individuals, schools, communities and organisations across the UK to raise funds and wear yellow in solidarity for young people's mental health. You'll develop and deliver strategies that attract new supporters, deepen engagement, increase donor loyalty and grow sustainable income. Combining creativity with a data-led approach, you'll identify new opportunities, test innovative fundraising products, and ensure every supporter enjoys an exceptional experience as part of the YoungMinds movement. This is a role for someone who thrives on growth, innovation and impact. What you'll be doing Leading the Individual Giving & Campaigns team to deliver ambitious fundraising and income targets. Developing and delivering a strategy to drive the growth of regular giving and individual giving programmes. Managing major campaigns, including #HelloYellow to ensure that we maximise the opportunity to generate income Identifying and testing new fundraising products and audience engagement opportunities. Using insight, data and supporter feedback to improve performance, ROI and supporter retention. About you You'll bring significant experience of leading successful individual giving, direct marketing or public fundraising programmes and a track record of delivering growth. We're particularly interested in hearing from candidates who can demonstrate: Experience leading large-scale fundraising and supporter acquisition campaigns. Strong strategic thinking combined with excellent delivery skills. Success in developing and testing new fundraising products or initiatives. Experience managing budgets, setting KPIs and driving fundraising performance. The ability to analyse supporter data and translate insight into action. A collaborative leadership style that motivates, develops and empowers teams. Working effectively and collaboratively as part of cross-functional project teams Why join YoungMinds? This is a chance to join one of the UK's most influential charities and play a key role in helping young people get the mental health support they need. With 1-5 young people experiencing a probably mental health condition in the UK today, there has never been a more important time to lend your experience and skills to a cause that matters to so many. You'll be part of an experienced, multi disciplined, fundraising team that is friendly, supportive and collaborative, with a strong commitment to working together to achieve impact. We work hard but like to have fun while we do it. You'll also be joining a values-led organisation that puts young people's voices at the centre of everything it does, encourages innovation, supports flexible working and is committed to creating an inclusive workplace where everyone can thrive. And at YoungMinds, we believe every young person deserves mental health support when they need it - no matter what. But not all young people have equal access to help. That's why (AJEDI) Anti-Racism, Justice, Equity, Diversity and Inclusion is central to everything we do. It guides how we operate, support our people, and serve young people. We are committed to anti discriminatory policies and practices. We are also committed to safeguarding and promoting the welfare of children and young people. Apply now If you're an experienced individual giving expert with the vision, creativity and ambition to grow income and supporter engagement at scale, we'd love to hear from you. To apply, please send your CV and cover letter to Philippa at Charity People. You will also be asked to complete an anti-racism, justice, equity, diversity and inclusion task as part of your application. Key Dates Closing date: 9am Monday 21 September Interviews: in person Tues 29 September Charity People is a forward-thinking, inclusive organisation that actively and deliberately promotes equity, diversity and inclusion. We know organisations thrive when inclusion is at the forefront. We evidence our commitment by matching charity needs with the skills and experience of candidates irrespective of background including age, disability (including hidden disabilities), gender, gender identity or gender reassignment, marriage and civil partnership, pregnancy and maternity, race, religion or belief, or sexual orientation. We do this because we believe that greater diversity leads to greater results for the charities we work with.

item.title: Director of Finance
item.description: Noah's Ark Children's Hospice is partnering with Robertson Bell on a retained basis to recruit a Director of Finance on a permanent basis. This is an exciting opportunity to join a highly regarded children's hospice at a pivotal stage of its development, taking a leading role in strengthening financial performance, improving organisational effectiveness and helping shape the charity's next phase of growth. This is more than a traditional Finance Director role. Noah's Ark has undergone significant transformation in recent years, moving from a predominantly community-based service to operating a 24/7 hospice facility at The Ark. The successful candidate will join at a critical point in this journey, with the opportunity to strengthen the finance function whilst working closely with the wider Senior Leadership Team to ensure the charity is making the best possible use of its resources and delivering maximum value for children and families. For an ambitious, commercially minded finance leader, this is an opportunity to combine strong financial leadership with genuine organisational impact, helping to shape a more effective operating model and contributing directly to the future direction of the charity. The role Partner with the CEO, Senior Leadership Team and Board of Trustees to shape the charity's financial and strategic direction during a period of organisational change. Stabilise and strengthen the finance function, ensuring high-quality financial management, robust controls and accurate, insightful reporting. Lead the budgeting, forecasting and financial planning process, including modelling different care delivery approaches, investment decisions and longer-term strategic scenarios. Support the charity to improve its financial position, identifying opportunities to increase efficiency and ensure resources are being deployed to maximum effect. Oversee statutory accounts, external reporting, audit and regulatory requirements, ensuring the charity maintains strong financial governance and compliance. Ensure effective management of reserves, investments, cash flow, liquidity, insurance and restricted funds. Contribute to the development of the charity's next multi-year strategic plan, bringing commercial discipline, financial insight and a practical focus on delivery. Identify opportunities for cost efficiency and productivity improvements across the organisation, working collaboratively with colleagues to turn insight into action. Support the design and implementation of new IT and financial systems, ensuring they provide the information and controls required to support an effective organisation. Lead and develop a small finance team, setting clear expectations, building capability and creating a culture of accountability and high performance. Play an active role in wider organisational leadership, bringing constructive challenge and financial insight to decisions beyond the traditional finance remit. The organisation Noah's Ark Children's Hospice provides specialist care and support to babies, children and young people with life-limiting or life-threatening conditions, alongside their families. Its purpose-built hospice, The Ark, opened in 2019 and provides a unique environment where children can receive specialist care, therapy, bereavement support and family services in a safe and welcoming setting. Rated 'Outstanding' by the Care Quality Commission, Noah's Ark supports families across North and Central London and Hertsmere, delivering care wherever it is needed - in the family home, within the community or at The Ark. This is an organisation with a warm, supportive culture and a strong commitment to its values of Kindness, Excellence and Courage. It is now looking for a finance leader who can combine that collaborative approach with the confidence to challenge constructively, make difficult decisions and drive meaningful improvement. Essential criteria Fully qualified accountant (ACA, ACCA, CIMA or equivalent). Strong experience leading a finance function. Strong understanding of financial controls, governance, audit and statutory reporting. Demonstrable experience producing and interpreting high-quality financial information that supports effective decision-making. Experience leading and developing teams, with the confidence to set expectations, address underperformance and hold colleagues accountable. Excellent communication and relationship-building skills, with the ability to engage and influence senior stakeholders and non-finance colleagues. A proactive, hands-on and self-starting appr

item.title: Head of Fundraising (Midlands)
item.description: Location: Midlands. Regular business travel throughout our region and wider. Salary: Circa £55,000 per annum Contract: Permanent, full-time. Hybrid working with a minimum of 2 days in the office to attend weekly Senior Leadership Team meetings. FareShare Midlands is looking for an experienced and ambitious Head of Fundraising to lead its fundraising strategy and build the sustainable income needed to support its work tackling hunger, food waste and poverty across the Midlands. This is a senior role with responsibility for growing income across trusts and grants, corporate partnerships, individual giving and events, while developing new opportunities through major donor fundraising. You will lead the fundraising team, set direction and priorities, and build the partnerships and relationships needed to deliver long-term growth. Working closely with the CEO, Deputy CEO, Finance and Communications teams, you will identify new funding opportunities, develop compelling proposals and pitches, strengthen existing relationships and ensure supporters are well stewarded. You will also play an important role in developing FareShare Midlands’ fundraising infrastructure, including making better use of its database to strengthen relationships and identify opportunities. The ideal candidate will bring significant experience of securing income and building relationships with senior decision-makers, alongside a strong track record of delivering against fundraising targets. You will be confident developing strategy and turning insight into action, with the communication skills to represent the charity with donors, businesses and other external stakeholders. You will be a collaborative and hands-on leader, comfortable working in a small, dynamic team and willing to contribute across the wider organisation when needed. With strong commercial awareness, creativity and tenacity, you will bring the energy and ambition needed to grow fundraising while staying closely connected to the charity’s purpose. This is an opportunity to lead fundraising at an important stage in FareShare Midlands’ development, helping to generate the income and partnerships needed to maximise the social value of surplus food and create greater impact across the region. Please download the Candidate Pack [PDF] for further information. Closing Date: Monday, 21st September

item.title: Training Officer
item.description: Job description We’re looking for a Training Officer to help us develop and deliver high quality learning and professional development for people working with and for young people across the North West. This is a great opportunity for someone who enjoys creating and delivering engaging training and supporting others to learn and grow . Working with our Learning, Workforce Development & Equality Manager, you’ll help shape our learning offer and support a skilled, confident and connected youth sector workforce . What you’ll be doing Design and deliver engaging training and workshops (online and in person) Build relationships with learners, partners and organisations Support learning events, networks and Communities of Practice Use feedback and evaluation to improve what we do We’re looking for someone who has: experience of training, facilitation or learning and development confidence delivering engaging sessions to different audiences good communication and organisational skills an understanding of youth work or the issues affecting young people a commitment to equality, inclusion and safeguarding More information in attached recruitment pack - closing date Monday 21 Sep 2026 @ 12 pm Interviews will be held in person on Tuesday 29 September 2026. item.title: Fundraising Manager (Philanthropy and Partnerships)
item.description: This is an exciting opportunity for a senior fundraising professional who combines strategic thinking with excellent relationship-building skills and a passion for making a tangible difference. The Fundraising Manager will lead on the development and growth of several key income streams, including: Major Donors Corporate Partnerships and Giving Regular Giving Gifts in Wills (Legacies) Working in close partnership with SUDEP Action's other Fundraising Manager (who oversees Community fundraising, Trusts and Grants and other aspects of our in-memory giving), the postholder will also share responsibility for the development, delivery and performance of wider fundraising activity across the charity. A significant aspect of this role will involve re-engaging existing high-value supporters while identifying and cultivating new prospects. The ideal candidate will be confident networking, opening doors, building meaningful relationships and inspiring people to support a cause that may be unfamiliar to them. The postholder will work collaboratively with colleagues across the organisation, including fundraising colleagues, the CEO, and wider management team, drawing upon their expertise to develop effective fundraising plans, test assumptions and ensure the charity is represented professionally, authentically and consistently. Given the nature of SUDEP Action's work, the role also requires sensitivity, empathy and the ability to engage thoughtfully with people affected by epilepsy and bereavement. Full details of the role and experience required can be found in the Job Pack attachment.

item.title: Assistant Director of Services - Criminal Justice & Housing/Homelessness
item.description: 12-month fixed-term contract | Full-time Salary: £58,560 – £71,480 per annum Hours: 35 per week Location: Home-based with regular national travel Job reference number: 1766 Help shape the future of Cranstoun’s services Cranstoun is a social justice and harm reduction charity supporting and empowering people to live healthier and safer lives. Each year, we support more than 45,000 people through services including substance use, criminal justice, domestic abuse, housing and services for children and young people. Following a successful five-year strategy and significant growth, we remain ambitious about the difference we can make. As we enter our next phase, we are investing in the leadership and operational capability needed to support our continued development. We are now recruiting an Assistant Directors of Services to join our senior management team. This is a significant senior leadership role offering the opportunity to lead substantial service portfolios while helping shape how Cranstoun’s services are led and delivered across the organisation. The role Reporting to the Director of Operations, you will lead a substantial portfolio of complex commissioned services and senior operational managers. You will lead nine services with nine direct reports, spanning criminal justice and housing/homelessness provision. You will have clear accountability for ensuring services are safe, effective and well-led, with strong contractual performance, financial sustainability and positive outcomes for the people and communities we support. You will provide operational grip and evidence-based assurance, strengthen safeguarding and management accountability, build effective relationships with commissioners and partners, and ensure risks and underperformance are identified, escalated and addressed early. You will also work collectively with fellow senior operational leaders to embed a One Cranstoun approach, strengthening common standards, sharing learning, developing leadership capability and improving quality and resilience across our services. What you will be accountable for As an Assistant Director, you will take senior operational accountability for: Safe, effective and well-led services – ensuring strong safeguarding, quality, operational risk management and service user outcomes. Contractual performance – ensuring services deliver against contractual requirements and KPIs, with strong commissioner relationships and timely action to address underperformance. Financial sustainability – maintaining strong financial oversight, effective workforce management and oversight of the sustainability of individual contracts. Evidence-based assurance – using reliable performance, quality, workforce and financial information to identify risks and drive improvement. Collective organisational leadership – working beyond individual portfolio boundaries to build consistent standards, stronger leadership and shared ways of working across Cranstoun. You will lead and develop senior operational managers, set clear expectations and create a culture in which support and accountability operate together. You will also lead and contribute to service mobilisation, transformation, workforce planning and continuous improvement. Who we are looking for We are looking for established senior operational leaders with substantial experience leading complex commissioned services and geographically dispersed teams. You will bring a strong track record of: leading safe, high-quality services for people with complex needs; safeguarding, quality and operational risk management; contract and performance management; managing significant service budgets and improving financial performance; building effective relationships with commissioners, regulators and strategic partners; leading service improvement, mobilisation and organisational change; developing senior operational managers and addressing underperformance; and using performance, quality, workforce and financial information to provide assurance and drive improvement. You will need to combine strategic leadership with operational pragmatism, understanding the detail when necessary while maintaining oversight of performance, risk, quality and sustainability across a complex portfolio. Above all, we are looking for collaborative, credible and values-led leaders who can support and challenge in equal measure, build leadership capability and bring people together around common standards and organisational priorities. Specialist experience For this role, you will need significant leadership experience across both Criminal Justice and Housing/Homelessness services, including housing or accommodation-based provision. You will understand the complexity of working across criminal justice, housing, local government and other statutory systems and be experienced in building effective relationships with commissioners and partners while maintaining strong operational and contractual oversight. This is a 12-month fixed-term appointment at an important stage in Cranstoun’s transformation, offering the opportunity to lead a significant portfolio, strengthen operational performance and help shape the future development of our operating model. Be part of Cranstoun’s next chapter Our successful five-year strategy has seen Cranstoun grow considerably, extending our reach and the range of services we provide. We remain ambitious and innovative, committed to developing services that respond to the changing needs of people and communities. As we look to the future, we are investing in the leadership, operational capability and organisational infrastructure needed to support our continued development, strengthening operational governance, consistency and assurance across our services. This role offers the opportunity to do more than manage established portfolios. You will help shape the future of our services and build an Operations Directorate characterised by high standards, clear accountability, collaboration and continuous improvement. Find out more Please refer to the accompanying recruitment pack for the full Job Description, Person Specification and details of the application process. Please note: All posts are subject to an Enhanced DBS check. How to Apply: For more details and to apply, please visit our website via the apply button. Please quote the appropriate Job Ref in all correspondence. Applicants must be able to provide satisfactory evidence of their right to work in the UK at the application stage. Sponsorship is not available for this post. Applicants must have the right to work in the UK that does not require employer sponsorship for the duration of the appointment. Closing date: Sunday 20 September 2026. We are an inclusive employer, committed to promoting equality and diversity in all areas of our work. Registered Charity No: 1061582
item.dc:creator: Cranstoun

item.title: Finance Manager
item.description: We are seeking a proactive, forward-thinking, part-qualified or qualified accountant to lead the development of an efficient, AI-assisted finance function for the charity. Reporting directly to the CEO, you will be part of Home-Start Southwark and Lewisham's senior leadership team, in the only finance-focussed role within the team, taking ownership of the organisation's financial systems, reporting, and compliance — and critically, you will have the opportunity to strategically shape how finance operates over the next 6–12 months. This is a growth opportunity for someone who has an interest and belief in our work supporting local families and combines strong technical finance skills with curiosity about technology, a willingness to challenge existing ways of working, and the confidence to work at Board level. You will implement cloud-based accounting with AI-enabled features, design meaningful management reporting, and ensure the charity is fully compliant with SORP 2026 and Charity Commission requirements — all while keeping the CEO's time focused on leading the organisation, not managing the books. Why this role matters now This is not a maintenance role. We are looking for someone who wants to build something — to design and embed a finance function that is fit for a growing charity. You will have the rare opportunity to shape the tools, processes, and reporting frameworks from the ground up, working directly with the CEO to make finance a strategic enabler rather than an administrative burden.

item.description: Application Deadline : 21 September 2026 Department : Business Services Location : London/Brussels Compensation : London £76,431 / year and Brussels €7,066 / month Description If you are a strategic HR leader who thrives in complex international environments, we would love to hear from you. We are looking for an exceptional Head of People & Culture to partner with senior leaders, lead a global People & Culture function, and help build an organisation capable of delivering lasting environmental impact. This is a unique opportunity to influence strategy, culture and organisational effectiveness at a critical leadership level. If this opportunity excites you, we would encourage you to submit your application early and don't wait until the deadline. While the vacancy will remain open, we will begin reviewing candidates throughout the advertising period. Important dates to note: Deadline to submit an initial application: 21st of September If your profile passes initial screening, you will be asked to submit additional information in the form of three additional questions. The deadline to submit your answers is the 24th of September If we do not receive a response to these questions by the deadline we will assume you are no longer interested in the role. Interviews will take place from the week beginning 28 September 2026 Please also review the "Our Hiring Process" section at the bottom of this advert to learn more about the stages involved for this specific role. Key Responsibilities Act as a trusted adviser to the Global Leadership Team and, with the People Business Partners, other senior leaders, providing expert guidance on People-related organisational design implications, workforce planning, leadership effectiveness, and change. Provide functional leadership and coordination across the People team, ensuring high standards, alignment and delivery while retaining clear accountability for the overall effectiveness and performance of the global People function Lead any People-related organisational development initiatives to support growth, international expansion, and evolving organisational models Contribute to the development and leadership of ClientEarth’s EDI and Decolonisation strategy, ensuring alignment with global best practice and organisational values and measurable progress in systems, decision-making, and leadership practice See the job description for a full list of duties for this role. Skills, Knowledge & Expertise MCIPD-qualified HR professional, or equivalent senior-level experience in HR, organisational development, employee relations, or employment law (essential) Extensive experience leading or shaping a global People / HR function in a complex organisation and operating as a trusted adviser to senior leaders Experience working and negotiating with trade unions and other employee representative bodies Experience leading People-related organisational change projects in multi-country and matrixed organisations See the job description for a full list of requirements for this role. item.title: Mental Health & Wellbeing Practitioner (Hub Based)
item.description: Change Mental Health is looking for a Mental Health and Wellbeing Practitioner to join our community-based Hub in Invergordon. Our Hub provides a welcoming, non-clinical space where people can connect with others, build confidence and resilience, and improve their mental health and wellbeing through group activities, peer support and recovery-focused opportunities. About the role You’ll play an important part in the day-to-day running of the Hub, working directly with people experiencing poor mental health or mental illness. Your work will include facilitating groups and wellbeing activities, providing person-centred 1:1 support, helping people develop achievable goals and personal plans, and connecting people with wider community support. You’ll also build relationships with local organisations and help make sure everyone accessing the Hub feels respected, included and heard. We’re looking for someone who can build positive relationships, work confidently both independently and as part of a team, and bring an empathetic, strengths-based and recovery-focused approach to their work. Essential Experience of facilitating groups or community-based mental health activities. Experience providing structured 1:1 support. Ability to build positive, professional relationships with people accessing support. Willingness to work towards an SVQ Level 2 in Social Services and Healthcare (Adults) and SSSC registration, if required. Desirable Knowledge of local community resources, services and support networks. Experience supporting people affected by trauma, social isolation or complex life circumstances. The role is typically worked Tuesday and Wednesday, 10am–4pm, and Thursday, 10am–3.30pm , with some flexibility occasionally required to meet service needs. If you’re passionate about helping people strengthen their wellbeing, connections and confidence within their own community, we’d love to hear from you
item.dc:creator: Change Mental Health

item.title: Senior Practitioner
item.description: Change Mental Health is looking for a Senior Practitioner to join our team in Invergordon, supporting people through both our community Hub and Outreach services. You’ll combine direct mental health support with day-to-day guidance and supervision for Mental Health and Wellbeing Practitioners. You won’t hold overall management responsibility for the service, but you’ll be an experienced point of contact for colleagues and help maintain consistently high-quality, person-centred practice. About the role You’ll work directly with people experiencing mental illness, helping them build confidence, resilience and greater independence. The role includes structured 1:1 support, group activities, personal and outcome-focused planning, community engagement and outreach support. You’ll also provide guidance and supervision to colleagues, support reflective practice and contribute to the continued development of our services. Essential Experience providing community-based, recovery-focused or non-clinical mental health support. Experience delivering structured 1:1 support and developing or reviewing personal plans. Strong communication skills and the ability to build positive professional relationships. Understanding of risk assessment and safe decision-making. SVQ Level 3 Social Services and Healthcare (Adults) or willingness to work towards this if required. SSSC registration, or willingness to register within the required timescale. Desirable Experience providing guidance, support or supervision to staff. Experience working within a registered service and meeting SSSC requirements. Experience facilitating groups or community-based mental health activities. Knowledge of local services, referral pathways and community supports. The post is typically worked Tuesday to Thursday, 9am–5pm , with some flexibility occasionally required to meet service needs. What we offer 37 days’ annual leave (pro rata) Two paid Mental Wellbeing Days Enhanced sick pay and leave entitlements Professional development , including funded opportunities 24/7 Employee Assistance Programme , including legal, financial and medical support Cycle to Work Scheme Blue Light Card eligibility A supportive approach to flexible working and work-life balance If you’re an experienced practitioner who enjoys supporting both people accessing services and the colleagues around you, we’d love to hear from you.
item.dc:creator: Change Mental Health

item.title: Concierge
item.description: Concierge When registering to this job board you will be redirected to the online application form. Please ensure that this is completed in full in order that your application can be reviewed. Job Title: Concierge Location: Based in Croydon. Step free access is available at this service. Salary: £28,000 Shift Pattern: 37.5 hours per week Monday to Sunday on a night rota between 20:00 - 08:30. You may be required to work outside these hours including day shifts, and bank holidays as per service and resident requirements About the Role An internal opportunity for a Night Concierge to join our team based in Croydon. In this role, you will provide concierge services within our service which provides 24/7 support to residents with forensic mental health needs. As a Concierge, you will help create a safe, welcoming and well run environment, offering reassurance and practical support to residents when they need it the most. This role is key to keeping our building, residents, and service secure and responsive. You will conduct regular safety checks, monitor access, respond to emergencies, support residents with queries, and keeping records. You will be key to creating and maintaining a clean and safe environment. You will be expected to remain awake, alert, accessible, and actively engaged throughout the shift. There is a focus on welfare checks, providing resident support, and completing administration tasks, ensuring clear handovers are prepared for the day staff and managers. Some Key Responsibilities Include: Ensuring our buildings are safe by monitoring, completing welfare checks and responding affectively and appropriately to emergencies Maintaining professionalism and kindness with residents and visitors, attending to calls, managing deliveries and ensuring great communication with the team in line with policies and procedures Provide a daily report on resident activity, AINMs, safeguarding and concerns for handovers. Working with the wider team to make sure any urgent issues are picked up and followed through Remain alert and monitor CCTV throughout the shift Adapting to service needs to support risk assessments, safeguarding checks, and service standards Supporting residents to build confidence and independence, contributing to a psychologically informed space where everyone is treated with respect and dignity Noticing when someone might be struggling with their physical or mental health, and taking prompt action to prevent escalation Helping to keep the environment clean and welcoming from tidying communal spaces to reporting repairs and completing admin tasks accurately and sensitively Be a valued and reliable member of the team, completing handovers for colleagues for a seamless service Other duties include maintaining cleanliness, removing rubbish, reporting repairs, ordering supplies, and general tasks About You We’re looking for someone who understands the importance of compassion, routine and safety who’s ready to make a difference in a calm, consistent way. Whether you’ve worked in supported housing before or bring transferable skills from another role, what matters most is if you’re dependable, care about people, and want to make a difference during quieter hours. Furthermore we look for: Experience in providing high quality customer service Ability to work independently and taking responsibility for the service You will require excellent communication skills with residents, colleagues and external partners to build positive and respectful relationships Understanding the importance of diversity, equity and inclusion in everything you do You have the ability to stay calm and supportive in a fast paced and constantly changing environment Ability to take a compassionate, non judgmental approach when helping others You share our values of Ambition, Empowerment, Inclusivity, and Transparency in your everyday work Please refer to the JDPS attached for more details on the vacancy and our requirements/key criteria. What we Offer 25 days (Full time equivalent) annual leave, increasing with the length of service Employer Pension Contribution Eligibility to register with Blue Light Discount Card Access to discounted tickets for music events, shows, sports and more Reflective Practice regular sessions with a therapist provided by an external provider to support Mental Health and Wellbeing at work Training and Development, including access to courses, upskilling, and progression plans Employee Assistance Programme, including counselling Life Assurance Scheme Cycle-to-work scheme Annual Staff Awards EDI Ambassador programme About Social Interest Group (SIG) SIG is a not-for-profit organisation providing thousands of people with good-quality support and care in residential, drop-in centres, community floating support settings, probation settings, and hospitals. We do so across London, Brighton, Bedfordshire, Luton, Kent and Liverpool. Our goal is to transform lives through empowering change. We believe good care and support improves lives with the vision to create healthier, safer, and more inclusive communities. item.title: Global Head of Finance
item.description: Environmental Justice Foundation Global Head of Finance £56,000 to £62,000 per year, dependent upon experience Full-time Permanent Bath based with a minimum of 3 days per week in the office About EJF The Environmental Justice Foundation (EJF) is a global non-profit organisation working to protect the natural world and our fundamental human right to a secure environment. We work at the frontlines of environmental injustice, alongside communities most affected by climate breakdown, biodiversity loss, and exploitation - transforming evidence into action, and injustice into lasting change. Through field investigations, rigorous research, and strategic international advocacy, we expose environmental crime, challenge impunity, and catalyse systemic reform. Our work delivers real-world impact, shaping policy, strengthening governance, protecting vital ecosystems, and defending those who risk their lives to safeguard them. Our campaigns span four interconnected areas: oceans, climate, forests and wetlands, and the training, protection, and empowerment of environmental defenders and investigative journalists. From illegal fishing and plastic pollution to deforestation, land grabs, and climate breakdown, we confront some of the most complex and urgent crises of our time - always with a focus on accountability, equity, and durable solutions. EJF has a diverse team of campaigners, filmmakers and community mobilisers working across four continents, united by a shared ambition: to protect people by protecting the planet. We are bold, evidence-led, and impact-driven. We speak truth to power - and we build pathways to a fairer, more resilient future. About the role: This is a rare opportunity for an experienced and conscientious qualified accountant to join a dynamic, high-impact team working to protect the global environment and defend human rights. Reporting to the Chief Operating Officer, you'll lead the international finance team and provide financial insight and analysis to the CEO and Senior Management Team to support a fast-growing, ambitious charity. This role is right for you if you're an energetic, meticulously organised finance professional with a strong commitment to protecting the environment and the people who depend on it. You'll work globally to ensure EJF's financial administration runs efficiently in every country where we operate, securing value for money so that resources are focused on delivering impact. Key responsibilities: Maintaining and improving EJF's global financial policies, systems, controls and processes, ensuring they are applied consistently in every country where EJF operates. Managing six finance staff working in the UK and overseas. Ensuring the production of accurate, accessible and insightful monthly and annual global financial reporting for internal and external audiences. Providing strategic financial forecasts, insights and advice to the CEO, Senior Management Team and Trustees to inform planning and decision-making. Preparing budgets for funding proposals and ensuring accurate and timely financial projections of spend against grants and reporting to funders. Leading the annual organisational budget process, including multi-year financial plans. Mentoring team leads on financial budgeting, tracking and expenditure oversight. Monitoring and ensuring value for money in expenditure, identifying and removing inefficiencies and waste. Developing and executing EJF's treasury strategy, including managing currency risk and reserves. Overseeing payroll and pensions, working with external providers where relevant. Completing regulatory returns as required by the Charity Commission and statutory bodies in the countries of operation. Leading the annual external audit and overseeing the preparation of statutory accounts. Managing financial risk, including safeguarding EJF against fraud, and maintaining relationships with auditors, banks and other professional advisers. Essential skills and experience Demonstrable commitment to EJF’s vision, mission and values and a determination to change the world for the better. Qualified accountant with a superb eye for detail. Minimum of six years' work experience, preferably in the international charity sector, including responsibility for managing a finance team. Demonstrable experience designing and implementing financial controls and securing good value for money through procurement and commissioning. Strong IT skills, and experience managing IT systems and/or databases. Excellent communication skills, in writing and in person. Proactive and solution-oriented, highly organised and self-motivated. Enthusiastic, outgoing and friendly, able to work in a growing, diverse, international team with minimal supervision. Experience of working with the UK Charity SORP and the production of the annual report and accounts. Experience with multi-currency income & expenditure and management of the processes around sub-grants to overseas partners. Ability to travel to EJF's countries of operation to assess the development and implementation of financial systems and to manage finance staff. What we offer 22 days’ annual leave (exclusive of bank holidays), increasing with each year of service, plus additional paid leave between Christmas and New Year. Private healthcare package. Generous pension scheme, with employer contributions increasing over time. Flexible working hours and hybrid working (typically 3 days in the office / 2 from home). Cycle-to-work scheme. A dynamic, supportive, and inclusive working environment, with genuine opportunities for professional development and career progression. The chance to contribute to an organisation delivering real-world impact for people and planet. We are an equal opportunities employer and welcome applications from all backgrounds. Closing date 20th September Interview date 1st / 2nd October

item.title: Senior digital marketing officer
item.description: Location: Contracted to our Peterborough office with the flexibility for hybrid working Salary: £29,000 – £34,000 depending on experience Hours: Full time, 37.5 hours per week Contract: Permanent Benefits: We want all our employees to feel valued and engaged and are committed to offering a positive working culture along with a good work-life balance. As well as ensuring we pay our employees fairly, we offer the following benefits: Flexible working, Generous annual leave, Private Medical Insurance, including dental and optical, Pension Scheme, Sick Pay, Death in Service, Employee Assistance Programme, Bike Loan Scheme, Cycle2Work Scheme, Eyecare, Discount Portal. Be a part of an energetic and vibrant team who are driven by the desire to improve the lives of people living with kidney disease. Our vision is the day when everyone lives free from kidney disease. We're looking for a driven and passionate email specialist who wants to use their skills to make a genuine difference to the lives of people living with kidney disease. The digital marketing team at Kidney Research UK is ambitious, and we're in the middle of transforming the way we engage with supporters via email. The Role Write and build brilliant, on-brand emails that tell a great story and reach the right people with the right message at the right time Build on our email transformation programme, helping to develop our approach to personalisation and supporter insight Create and optimise automated email journeys, building on the ones we've just launched Use data and testing to continually improve email performance and engagement Help build a rich picture of our supporters to inform more relevant, better-targeted communications Work collaboratively across the digital marketing team to grow supporter engagement, loyalty and lifetime value What We're Looking For Proven experience in email marketing, combining technical skill with creative flair Ability to write compelling copy and build effective, well-designed emails Experience with email automation, journeys and personalisation A data-driven approach, with experience testing and optimising campaign performance Passion for using digital marketing to make a genuine difference to people living with kidney disease About Kidney Research UK: Kidney Research UK is the leading charity in the UK focused on funding research into the prevention, treatment and management of kidney disease. Our vision is the day when everyone lives free from kidney disease and for more than 60 years the research, we fund has been making an impact. But kidney disease is increasing as are the factors contributing to it, such as diabetes, cardiovascular disease and obesity, making our work more essential than ever. At Kidney Research UK we work with clinicians and scientists across the UK, funding and facilitating research into all areas of kidney disease. We collaborate with partners across the public, private and third sectors to prevent kidney disease and drive innovation to transform treatments. Over the last ten years we have invested more than £71 million into research. We lobby governments and decision makers to change policy and practice to ensure that the estimated 7.2 million people living with all stages of kidney disease in the UK have access to the most effective care and treatment, and to make kidney disease a priority. Most importantly, we also work closely with patients, ensuring their voice is heard and is at the centre of everything we do, from deciding which research to invest in to how we plan our priorities and our work across the charity. Those patient contributions are vital, always helping us and our partners to understand what life is like with kidney disease, always ensuring we see the patient behind the treatment and always reminding us that behind every statistic and every number is a person – the patients and the carers who inspire our mission and push us forward to make a difference and change the future of kidney disease. How to Apply Please complete the online application form and submit together with your CV. Closing date: Sunday 20 September 2026. Telephone interviews will be held on Tuesday 22 and Wednesday 23 September 2026. Interviews will be held week commencing 28 September 2026. We are committed to providing equal opportunities for everyone and encourage applications from all sections of the community. No agencies please. You may have experience in the following: Email Marketing Executive, Digital Marketing Officer, CRM Executive, Email Marketing Specialist, Marketing Automation Executive, Supporter Engagement Officer, Digital Communications Officer, Email Campaign Manager, CRM Marketing Executive, Charity Digital Marketing, Not for Profit, NFP, Third Sector, Charities, etc.

item.title: Executive Support Team Lead - Thomson Reuters Foundation
item.description: The Thomson Reuters Foundation is the corporate foundation of Thomson Reuters and an independent charitable organisation dedicated to advancing free, fair and informed societies worldwide. Through the combined power of journalism, legal expertise and data intelligence, the Foundation works to strengthen independent media, improve access to justice, and promote responsible business practices to address some of the world's most pressing challenges. We are seeking an experienced and proactive Executive Support Team Lead to lead the evolution of our newly centralised Business Support function. This is a unique opportunity to play a key role in shaping a centre of excellence that provides high-quality administrative, financial and operational support across the Foundation. Leading a small but impactful team, you will drive service excellence, strengthen governance and controls, and deliver efficient, customer-focused support to colleagues across the organisation. You will oversee complex invoicing and billing processes, manage key systems and vendor relationships, and identify opportunities to streamline and improve the way we work. As we transition from a decentralised administrative model to a more strategic and centralised approach, you will have the opportunity to design and embed best practices, build organisational capability, and help create a scalable support function that enables our teams to maximise their impact around the world. This role is ideal for someone who enjoys combining operational leadership with hands-on problem solving and is excited by the opportunity to build and shape a function for the future. About the Role As a Executive Support Team Lead at the Thomson Reuters Foundation, you will: Lead, coach and develop the Business Support Coordinator and Invoicing & Billing Analyst, overseeing workload planning, performance management, recruitment, onboarding and ensuring effective service coverage across the organisation. Act as a senior subject matter expert for the Foundation's core business systems (including SAP, Ariba and Convera), overseeing training, licensing, user support and escalation management while maintaining appropriate team resilience and back-up coverage. Oversee invoicing, billing, payment processing, sales order administration, vendor onboarding and procurement compliance, ensuring accuracy, strong financial controls and adherence to organisational policies. Manage organisational subscriptions, approved travel provider relationships, purchasing support and the resolution of financial administration queries, including expense investigations and budget coding issues. Lead the continuous improvement of business support processes, systems and documentation, driving greater efficiency, consistency, automation and service excellence across the Foundation. Develop and deliver guidance, training and performance reporting for business support services, identifying opportunities for further centralisation and supporting wider Operations objectives. Oversee delivery of core administrative services, including executive diary management, travel and event coordination, onboarding and offboarding administration, facilities support, shared inbox management, organisational records and contingent worker administration. Provide hands-on support for complex travel arrangements, staff induction activities, organisational website updates and logistics for Foundation-wide events, ensuring a seamless experience for colleagues and stakeholders. About You To be a Executive Support Team Lead at the Thomson Reuters Foundation, you will likely have: Proven experience in business operations, office management, business support or financial administration, including responsibility for leading and developing teams. Strong understanding of invoicing, procurement and financial administration processes, with a track record of ensuring accuracy, compliance and effective controls. Experience using ERP and financial management systems, such as SAP, alongside invoicing and payment platforms (e.g. Convera); familiarity with system administration and user support is advantageous. Previous experience within a charity, NGO or purpose-led organisation would be beneficial. Demonstrated people leadership skills, with the ability to coach, motivate and develop high-performing teams while fostering a collaborative and customer-focused culture. Excellent organisational and prioritisation skills, with the ability to manage multiple activities, balance competing demands and deliver results in a fast-paced environment. Strong analytical and problem-solving skills, coupled with sound judgement and a continuous improvement mindset focused on enhancing processes, efficiency and service delivery. Confident communicator and relationship builder, capable of working effectively with senior stakeholders, programme teams and external suppliers, while handling sensitive and confidential information with discretion and professionalism. What’s in it For You? Global Perspective and Impact: Interested in working for a dynamic global organization with a focus on social impact? With hubs all over the world from Bangkok to Madrid to Rio de Janeiro, join a truly international team with a shared goal of helping to build societies around the world that are free, fair, and informed. Unique Approach: Our expertise in media and the law is world class. We combine the power of both to address the critical issues faced by humanity. Our Relevance: With a focus on advancing media freedom, fostering more inclusive economies and promoting human rights, our work has never been more needed than right now. Industry Competitive Benefits: We offer competitive salary packages and market-leading benefits. Learning & Development: We are dedicated to the continual professional development of our employees and offer access to both in-house and external training opportunities. About Thomson Reuters Foundation TheThomson Reuters Foundationisthe corporatefoundation of Thomson Reuters, the global news and information services company. As an independent charity, registered in the UK and USA, we leverage our media, legal and data driven expertise to strengthen independent journalism, enable access to the law and promote responsible business. Through news, media development, free legal assistance and data intelligence, we aim to build free, fair and informed societies.

item.title: Data, Insight and Development Lead
item.description: Hours: 37 per week (part timemin 25 hours considered) Bradford and Airedale Citizens Advice & Law Centre is a leading provider of legal advice and information, supporting thousands of clients every year. We are a busy, client focused and dynamic service with a track record of delivering high-quality advice face to face and over the phone. Our communities are facing unprecedented challenges with rising costs. The rising cost-of-living continues to directly impact individuals and families, with more people than ever in negative budgets and experiencing personal debt. Our teams provide support and empower vulnerable clients to manage their income, maximise income and assess their best strategies and options to address debt issues long-term. Join our Team! We're looking for a curious and analytical Business Analyst to join our team and help us understand how our services work, where they can work better, and how technology and data can support the tens of thousands of people who come to us for help each year. About the Role To lead the development and continuous improvement of the organisation’s data, insight and reporting systems, ensuring that information is used effectively to improve services, demonstrate impact and support strategic decision-making. As our Data, Insight and Development Lead, you will work alongside operational colleagues, management and development teams, the postholder will combine data analysis with business analysis and service improvement. They will work with colleagues, partners and other stakeholders to understand needs, map processes, identify problems and opportunities, and define practical requirements before new systems, tools or ways of working are developed. The role will turn information from case management, telephony, digital and other systems into clear, accessible reports, dashboards and insights. These will help staff, managers, trustees, funders, commissioners, Citizens Advice and external partners understand service performance, client outcomes, emerging needs, risks, gaps and opportunities. The postholder will act as a bridge between operational teams and developers, ensuring that technology and data solutions address genuine user and organisational needs. They will support improvement projects from discovery through to delivery, including consultation, requirements gathering, testing, documentation, implementation and evaluation, helping new ways of working become embedded and effective. Other organisations may call this role Business Analyst, Business Improvement Officer, Insight & Improvement Analyst, Service Design Analyst, or Systems Analyst. The role will also strengthen the organisation’s Research and Campaigns work by identifying emerging issues affecting clients and producing robust evidence to influence local and national policy. Through this work, the postholder will help establish data as a strategic organisational asset and promote a culture of curiosity, collaboration, continuous improvement, evidence-based decision-making and organisational learning. Closing date:- 9.00 am 5th October 2026 Interview date:- Monday 19th October 2026 (in person)

item.title: Director of Finance and Resources
item.description: The British Academy is the UK’s national academy for the humanities and social sciences. We support outstanding research and researchers, bring new ideas into public debate and help ensure that evidence and expertise inform some of the biggest questions facing society. We are looking for a new Director of Finance & Resources to help us build on that work and plan confidently for the future. This is an important appointment at an exciting point in the Academy’s development. We will celebrate our 125th anniversary in 2027, following a period in which we have grown our policy work, transformed our building to create more opportunities for public engagement and developed a national network for early career researchers. As Director of Finance & Resources, you will make sure we have the resources, systems and organisational capacity to deliver our ambitions. You will lead our finance function and have overall responsibility for HR, IT & AV, Estates & Facilities, and Venue Sales & Marketing, working with experienced Heads of Department across each area. Finance will be central to the role. You will lead our financial strategy and planning, oversee our financial controls and reporting, and provide clear advice to the Chief Executive, Senior Management Team, Council and its committees. You will also help us think longer term about our financial sustainability, including our plans to diversify income through philanthropy and commercial activity. But we are looking for more than a strong Finance Director. You will be part of a close-knit Senior Management Team which works collectively to lead the Academy. We want someone who is interested in the organisation as a whole, who enjoys working across boundaries and who can help colleagues make good decisions about where we put our people, money and attention. You will also have responsibility for some important assets. These include our historic home at 10–11 Carlton House Terrace, our technology and infrastructure, and our trading subsidiary. Ultimately, your job will be to make sure these resources are working as hard as possible in support of the Academy’s purpose. About you You will be a CCAB-qualified accountant with substantial and senior finance experience, gained in a complex organisation. You will have led finance teams and significant budgets and be comfortable advising senior leaders, Boards or Trustees. You will also bring broader leadership experience. You may already have responsibility beyond finance, or have worked closely with areas such as people, operations, estates or technology. We are looking for someone who can combine sound financial judgement with a practical, collaborative approach. You will be able to deal with complexity without making things unnecessarily complicated, communicate clearly with people who are not finance specialists, and provide constructive challenge when it is needed. You should also be someone who enjoys leading through others. There are strong Heads of Department across the Resources portfolio, so this isn't about being the expert in every area. It is about setting direction, asking good questions, supporting people to succeed and bringing the different parts of the portfolio together. Why join us? The British Academy has a distinctive role in national life. In 2025/26 we awarded around £63 million in research funding. Alongside funding research, we convene academics, policymakers, businesses and civil society, engage the public with new ideas and use research to inform policy. The Director of Finance & Resources helps make all of that possible. For someone who wants to use their financial and leadership experience in an organisation with a clear public purpose, this is an opportunity to make a real contribution to the Academy’s next chapter. Recruitment Timetable Application deadline: Sunday 27th September, midnight Shortlisting: Thursday 8th October Fireside chats with CEO: week of 12th October Panel Interviews: 20th / 23rd October To apply, please send your CV, along with a supporting statement (no more than 2 pages) via the link by Sunday 27th September. For an informal conversation about the role please contact our exclusive partner, Bryony Thomas via the Allen Lane agency website.

item.title: Head of Operations
item.description: Rural Refugee Network (RRN) is a small local charity in East Hampshire, Havant and Portsmouth, working alongside refugees and people seeking asylum through the work of six board members, thirty operational volunteers, one part-time permanent employee and a small bank of project staff and contractors. The charity is widely recognised by stakeholders and the local community for sensitively and effectively addressing the many challenges people arriving in the UK face as they strive to resettle and thrive in our community. RRN is seeking an experienced Head of Operations to lead its support for refugees and people seeking asylum. This is an exciting opportunity to lead a small charity through a period of significant change, with overall operational responsibility for the charity, including partnerships, funding, coordination of delivery, safeguarding and compliance. Working directly with a range of stakeholders and beneficiaries, the ideal candidate for this complex and high trust role will be self-reliant, adaptable, and able to engage and influence through excellent face-to-face and online communication skills. This is a genuinely flexible role, with significant autonomy over when and where work is undertaken. There will be regular opportunities for in-person team management and relationship-building, alongside substantial flexibility in how the wider working week is structured and where work is carried out. We are looking for someone who is confident working independently, manages their own time effectively and values the trust and responsibility that come with this level of autonomy. A candidate who is energised by working flexibly and sensitively with a small team will thrive in this role, which offers the opportunity to make a direct and meaningful impact on people’s lives. Experience in the refugee sector is desirable. Deadline: 5pm Monday 21 September To apply, please send your CV and a supporting statement of not more than 2 sides, explaining your motivation, reflecting on how you would approach being RRN’s only core employed leader, and demonstrating your fit against the specification below. Please use the email subject heading “Head of Operations Application”. Unfortunately, we are unable to respond to all applications. Job Description Title: Rural Refugee Network Head of Operations Reports to : Board of Trustees Hours: Part-time (0.5 FTE, negotiable). Permanent contract. Salary range: £40,000 - £45,000 FTE depending on experience. Benefits: 25 days plus bank holidays (pro rata to hours agreed). 3% employer pension contribution. Location and expectations: Flexible hybrid working with frequent travel to projects, events and stakeholder meetings in Portsmouth, Havant, Petersfield and the wider Hampshire area. Occasional evening and weekend in-person working required. Purpose: To lead the day-to-day operation, development and sustainability of Rural Refugee Network, working with trustees, volunteers, funders and partner organisations to ensure refugees and asylum seekers receive practical support and RRN maintains compliance and operational sustainability. About the role: . In this small charity, the Head of Operations combines operational coordination, programme oversight, partnership development and income generation, with delivery shared across volunteers, trustees and contracted staff.The role offers a high degree of autonomy and flexibility, alongside the opportunity to shape how the organisation works and develops. It requires strong judgement in balancing opportunities, risks and priorities within limited capacity, and the confidence to work independently while bringing others with you. RRN is volunteer-led, and the Head of Operations is the organisation’s only permanent employee, holding overall coordination and accountability for day-to-day operations. This is therefore a broad, high-trust role: rather than delivering everything directly, you will enable and coordinate others, working closely with trustees, volunteers and contractors who deliver significant elements of the activity you lead. The role will suit someone who enjoys variety, autonomy and a flexible working pattern, and who is comfortable taking ownership while knowing when to collaborate, delegate or seek support. Key responsibilities: Leadership, coordination and partnerships Deliver agreed strategic objectives and support trustees in developing future priorities. Prepare quarterly Board reports. Coordinate relationships with statutory, voluntary and community partners. With the support of trustees, represent the charity in local forums, develop opportunities for collaboration and promote RRN in the local community. Programme and volunteer coordination Provide oversight of funded and core programmes. Recruit, train and manage project staff (currently two youth workers) and contracted/sessional staff. Recruit, train, support and retain volunteers. Oversee referral pathways and access. Support volunteer-led communications activity including website, newsletters, social media, impact reports and case studies. Income development and funding Write grant applications and manage reporting requirements (with volunteer/trustee input). Maintain and develop funding pipeline and actively develop new funding streams. Support relationship-building with donors and community supporters. Finance and compliance Monitor programme budgets, working with the Treasurer. Support trustees in governance, reporting and compliance responsibilities. Maintain organisational policies and procedures. Lead safeguarding practice and reporting, acting as Designated Safeguarding Lead and ensuring policies are implemented by staff, volunteers, and contractors. Maintain oversight of organisational risk, compliance with Charity Commission, data protection, employment requirements and insurance arrangements. Ensure appropriate administrative systems are in place and followed, including maintaining up-to-date records in the CRM, Lamplight. PERSON SPECIFICATION Essential Substantial experience managing programmes or services in the charity/social impact sector, including line management, budgeting and financial oversight, and grant compliance/reporting. Strong partnership-building and stakeholder engagement skills. Experience leading and recruiting volunteer teams. Deep understanding of safeguarding and compliance and recent experience leading safeguarding practice and decision-making. Up to date on requirements and best practice. Ability to work independently, exercising sound judgement about what trustees need to know and when, and to prioritise effectively within limited capacity and competing demands. Excellent written and verbal communication skills, IT proficiency. Desirable Experience working with refugees, asylum seekers or other vulnerable groups. Understanding of immigration, integration or resettlement issues. Successful fundraising and bid-writing experience. Experience of local authority commissioning or grant funding. Comfort and experience in IT, data and/or CRMs. RRN is committed to safeguarding and promoting the welfare of children, young people and adults at risk. Appointment is subject to an enhanced DBS check, including a check of the relevant barred list, two satisfactory references, including your most recent employer, and safer recruitment practice including verification of employment history and a right to work check. RRN is unable to sponsor work visas, so applicants must already have the right to work in the UK.
