item.title: Head of Communications
item.description: Join our team as Head of Communications! Location: Remote within the countries where WeMove Europe is registered to work (UK, France, Spain, Belgium, Germany, Netherlands, Italy, Poland) Preferred Start Date: January 2027 Application Deadline : September 24 2026 Employment type: Permanent contract WeMove Europe is a community of people united by a vision of a better Europe. We run campaigns that empower citizens to take action and influence decision-makers at the European level. We’re looking for a Head of Communications who will combine communications expertise and an innovative approach to storytelling to engage hundreds of thousands of Europeans in meaningful action. This role reports to the Campaigns Director and has line management responsibilities. You’ll work closely with our campaigns team and a social media manager to adapt and enhance campaigns through media, partnerships and content. This role works across multiple channels. You don’t need to be a tactical expert in all of them, but you need to be a strong strategic thinker who can carefully consider the role of each channel and asset. You will be as comfortable setting the strategic direction as you are delivering: pitching a story, briefing a journalist, running influencer outreach. What you’ll do: Advise on and support the development of our campaigns by creating and inputting into campaign narratives and communications plans Work alongside campaigners and social media manager to oversee and/or produce complementary content that builds pressure on the target: reactive posts, video, and assets timed to campaign moments Liaise with media contacts and external agencies to find appropriate opportunities to amplify our campaigns across European and national media Build partnerships with influencers, creators, and independent activists to enhance the power and impact of our campaigns Support the campaigns team to strengthen their storytelling skills and identify compelling storytelling opportunities in their partnerships, such as media hooks Build and sustain contact with journalists, produce press releases and briefings, keep our media database accurate and current across our priority countries Oversee and refresh our social media presence, line managing and coaching a social media manager. Stay close to the news cycle and to what is working on social in order to identify moments that put our campaign in front of the people we need to move Contribute to defining the success measures for communications, including social media KPIs, and oversee activity to meet them Advise senior leadership on communications and reputational considerations, including crisis communications approach Ensure consistency of messaging and tone across all public communications. The WeMove Europe team works in a culture of togetherness and passion for our issues and determination to win, so from time to time, you will be expected to perform activities outside of your normal role. Who we’re looking for: Essential skills: Storytelling : You can translate complex policy or campaign issues into compelling stories for different audiences, and generate creative news angles from unlikely material or challenging subject matter. You can write inspiring, clear, and impactful copy in English. Delivery : You have experience in at least one of the following areas: Media relations: Securing proactive and impactful media coverage which influenced policy or moved the needle - in other words, which has had an impact beyond raising profile or raising awareness. Influencer partnerships: Building relationships and impactful collaborations with influencers, content creators or other content partners. Content creation: Producing social media content which mobilised people to take action. Audiences : You have experience of engaging new audiences through communications channels, and you are able to use audience insights to influence your approach. Analysis: You are data-driven and results-oriented, eager to test, learn, and continuously improve your content and communications. Collaboration : You thrive in collaborative, international teams, eager to learn from colleagues and share your own expertise. Coaching and training : You can design and deliver practical training that changes how colleagues work, not just how much they know, and you enjoy building capability in others rather than holding it yourself. Important criteria: Values : You are deeply committed to systemic change in Europe, aligned with values of solidarity, sustainability, justice, and democracy. You are passionate about empowering people to realize their own power and become agents of change. Languages : You are fluent in English Travel : You are willing to travel within Europe when needed (at least 3 times a year) Experience level: You should have five years of relevant experience for this post. Nice to have You are familiar with a digital-first campaigns model, though you don’t necessarily need to have worked in this context before. Have recent experience of using video to tell complex stories and reach new audiences. You don’t have to have line management experience, but it could be beneficial. Knowledge of the Brussels press landscape alongside national media Other European languages are an added benefit. Why us? WeMove Europe is an independent and values-based organisation that seeks to build people power to transform Europe in the name of our community, future generations and the planet. We are people from all walks of life, who call Europe our home – whether we were born in Europe or elsewhere. Our job is to move a community of almost a million people across Europe on issues that matter - including the climate emergency, migrant rights, workers rights, better governance, and more. We know this number of people also needs to grow and diversify further so we can represent a strong critical mass that can bring about change in Europe. We are... A remote-first team working across borders and time zones Driven by an urgent, ambitious mission with people at its heart Innovating the next generation of tools for people-powered campaigning Committed to a culture of trust, collaboration, and impact over ego A place where your voice counts and your work drives real change What we offer: Working hours : Full time (5 days a week) or part time optional, (4 days a week, with a pro-rata salary adjustment.) Contract type : Permanent Location : Remote within countries where WeMove Europe is registered to work Salary ranges : Gross year salary per country, depending on experience level and location. Final calculations are based on city cost of living indexes and can differ slightly depending on your location Netherlands, UK: 62,000 - 65,000 EUR (Amsterdam, London range 12% higher) Belgium, Germany, France: 53,000 - 56,000 EUR (Brussels, Berlin range 7% higher; Paris ranges 12% higher ) Italy: 47,000 - 50,000 EUR (Rome ranges 87% higher) Spain: 44,000 - 47,000 EUR (Madrid ranges 10% higher) Poland: 39,000 - 42,000 EUR (Warsaw ranges 10% higher) Benefits: home office set up and co-working space of your choice, 30 vacation days, training, professional development, regular team calls, full week retreat in person with the whole team, and much more…! We are committed to being a diverse and inclusive workplace which is why people from communities that experience discrimination on the basis of race, ethnicity; women; people with disabilities; and LGBTQ+ people are especially encouraged to apply. item.title: International Project Manager - Agroecology
item.description: The International Project Manager - Agroecology will manage key international initiatives in Low and Middle Income Countries (LMICs), focusing on partner collaboration in Benin and Ethiopia. You will oversee project delivery, build impact-monitoring data systems, and provide technical guidance on sustainable crop and Integrated Pest Management (IPM) practices. PAN UK is the only charity in Britain dedicated solely to raising awareness of the problems caused by pesticides and working for better solutions. It is an independent, non-profit organisation, which works nationally and internationally to eliminate the use of hazardous pesticides and to support the adoption of sustainable alternatives. PAN UK operates as part of a global network of partner organisations. Its work reaches directly to partners and smallholder farmers in Ethiopia, Benin and elsewhere as well as national policy makers and global actors, such as UNEP and UNFAO. Our work includes generating evidence by working with farmers and researchers on both the impacts of pesticides and on the viability of safer and more sustainable alternatives. We use this evidence to advocate for wider change in policy and practice. The successful candidate will join PAN UK's International Team at an important time. With our partners, we have recently secured a five-year grant from the Global Environment Facility (GEF) for a UNEP-led project to support the mainstreaming of organic cotton in Benin. PAN UK’s role will be to develop data reporting systems that measure impact and support the needs of donors, supply chain actors and national authorities. The International Project Manager (Agroecology) will also support our projects with our partner, PAN Ethiopia, to support smallholder cotton and vegetable growers. This work enables us to co-create innovative tools and approaches that can be disseminated more widely. Global actors, governments, consumers and rural communities are increasingly recognising the negative impacts of pesticide-dependent, industrial agriculture on human health, climate and biodiversity. PAN UK aims to secure increasing support for agroecological approaches that help rural communities to secure sustainable and resilient livelihoods and protect the environmental resources on which they depend. PAN UK actively encourages applications from diverse backgrounds. We view diversity in its broadest form, which includes, but is not limited to, the consideration of race, nationality, gender, age, class, disability, sexuality, language and educational background. We particularly encourage applications from eligible candidates from minority ethnic groups which remain under-represented in the charity sector. The closing date for applications is 20th September 2026. Interviews will be held on Wednesday the 30th September or Thursday 1st October 2026 at our offices in Brighton. If a second interview is needed, this will take place on Friday the 2nd of October.

item.title: Fundraising and Communications Officer
item.description: Fundraising and Communications Officer We are seeking an experienced and proactive fundraiser who can build relationships, grow community support and create engaging communications that make a difference. Salary: £30,000 – £34,000 Location: Hybrid – home and Loughborough, with occasional travel across Leicester, Leicestershire and Rutland Hours: 37 hours per week Closing Date: 25th September 2026. Interviews will take place during week commencing 28th September About the role This is an exciting opportunity to join a small, committed fundraising team within a charity working to prevent homelessness and support people at risk. Working closely with the Fundraising and Partnerships Manager, you will help deliver an ambitious fundraising and communications strategy, increasing voluntary income, raising the charity’s profile and developing lasting relationships with supporters, businesses and local communities. It is a varied role combining community fundraising, supporter engagement, events, digital fundraising and communications. Key responsibilities will include: Developing community fundraising opportunities that increase income and awareness. Building relationships with schools, universities, businesses, community groups and individual supporters. Representing the charity at community events, talks and networking opportunities. Helping to create and deliver fundraising events, campaigns and challenge events. Creating engaging social media and website content, including case studies and video. Supporting digital fundraising campaigns, online giving and e-newsletters. Stewarding supporters and fundraisers, helping them feel valued and connected to the charity. Monitoring fundraising activity, budgets and campaign performance. About you You will be a confident relationship-builder who enjoys getting out into the community, meeting people and turning conversations into meaningful support. You will ideally have at least two years’ experience within charity fundraising, with experience across one or more areas such as community fundraising, corporate partnerships, major donors, digital fundraising or social media. item.title: Director of Fundraising and Communications
item.description: LCH Charity is one of the East Midlands' fastest-growing children's charities. In just five years, we have grown from an annual income of £70,000 to a forecast £1.2 million by August 2027. We have expanded our reach across the East Midlands, built strong partnerships with schools, businesses and communities, and supported tens of thousands of children and families experiencing poverty. Our growth has been driven by innovation, ambition and a relentless focus on meeting the needs of children and young people. Through close collaboration with our school partners, we deliver practical support where it is needed most, helping children to thrive regardless of their circumstances. While our impact within schools continues to grow, we know there is still enormous potential ahead. Awareness of our work beyond the education sector remains relatively low, and the opportunity to engage businesses, philanthropists, individual supporters, trusts and foundations across the region is significant. We are now seeking an exceptional Director of Fundraising and Communications to help unlock that potential and lead the next phase of our journey. The Opportunity This is not a role focused on maintaining the status quo. This is an opportunity to build on a proven success story and help shape the future of a charity with ambitious plans for growth. This is a genuinely exciting opportunity that offers the freedom to be creative and ambitious, with the autonomy to shape, lead and deliver your own strategy. Reporting directly to the CEO and serving as a member of the growing Executive Leadership Team, you will lead the creation, development and delivery of an ambitious fundraising and communications strategy that diversifies income, elevates our profile and strengthens our reputation across the East Midlands. You will inherit an organisation with strong foundations, a compelling story and a highly successful fundraising model. Our flagship School Colour Dash programme currently generates approximately 70% of our income and has become a powerful platform for both fundraising and engagement. The challenge, and opportunity, is clear. We are looking for a dynamic and entrepreneurial leader who can develop sustainable income streams capable of matching, and ultimately exceeding, the success of our flagship event. This is a rare opportunity to help create the next £1 million of income growth. About the Role As Director of Fundraising and Communications, you will: Lead the creation, development and delivery of a bold and ambitious fundraising and communications strategy. Diversify income across corporate partnerships, major donors, trusts and foundations, community fundraising, individual giving and philanthropy. Develop compelling propositions that inspire investment in our mission. Increase awareness, visibility and understanding of LCH Charity across the East Midlands. Strengthen and protect the charity's brand and reputation. Build strategic relationships with senior business leaders, philanthropists, partners and stakeholders. Identify and develop innovative new income opportunities. Lead and inspire a talented, committed and growing fundraising and communications team. Use insight, data and market intelligence to drive decision-making and growth. Act as a passionate ambassador and advocate for children, young people and families. Use systems to increase engagement across all supporters. Contribute to organisational leadership and strategic development as a member of the Executive Leadership Team. Who We Are Looking For We are seeking an ambitious, strategic and inspirational leader with a proven ability to deliver significant growth. You will be someone who combines vision with action, enjoys building relationships, and thrives in environments where there is genuine opportunity to innovate and make a lasting impact. You will bring: A successful track record of securing substantial fundraising growth. Experience working across a range of income streams, including corporate partnerships, trusts and foundations, philanthropy and individual giving. Strong commercial awareness and an entrepreneurial mindset. Exceptional communication, influencing and relationship-building skills. Experience of developing successful communications, marketing or brand strategies. Strong leadership experience and the ability to motivate and develop teams. The confidence to identify new opportunities and convert them into sustainable income. A genuine passion for improving outcomes for children, young people and families. Most importantly, you will be excited by the opportunity to take an already successful charity to the next level. Why Join LCH Charity? This is a unique opportunity to join a charity that has already demonstrated what can be achieved through ambition, innovation and determination. Over the last four years, we have transformed our income from £70,000 to a forecast £1.2 million, expanded our reach across the East Midlands and built a model that is changing lives every day. Yet we believe we are only at the beginning of our journey. We are looking for a leader who shares our ambition, who sees opportunity rather than limitation, and who wants to play a defining role in shaping the future of a growing and impactful organisation. What Success Will Look Like In this role, you will: Build income streams capable of matching the success of our flagship School Colour Dash programme. Secure transformational corporate, philanthropic and strategic partnerships. Significantly increase awareness and recognition of LCH Charity. Strengthen our influence across the East Midlands. Position LCH Charity as a charity of choice for businesses, donors and supporters. Help drive the organisation through its next phase of transformational growth. Enable thousands more children and families to access the support they need. Join Us We have grown from £70,000 to a forecast £1.2 million in just five years. Now we are looking for an exceptional fundraising and communications leader who can help us do it again. If you are ambitious, entrepreneurial and motivated by the opportunity to create lasting change for children and families, we would love to hear from you. Join us and help build the future of LCH Charity. We are looking for ideas as well as experience. Please submit your CV together with a supporting statement (maximum two pages) outlining: Why this opportunity interests you. Why this role is the right next step in your career. What excites you most about the growth opportunity at LCH Charity. Informal and confidential conversations with our Chief Executive Officer are welcomed and encouraged.

item.title: Mental Health and Homelessness Outreach Worker
item.description: Do you want to support people with mental health issues in a moment of crisis? Are you calm, non-judgemental and able to work effectively with people experiencing distress? If you can embody our values of Hope, Courage, Togetherness , and Responsiveness , and want to help others build resilience and manage their wellbeing, we’d love to hear from you. Mental Health and Homelessness Outreach Worker (Single Homeless Support Pathway) x2 Reference: 368 Salary: £26,000 – £27,000 per annum, depending on skills and experience inclusive of Outer London Weighting (OLW) Hours: 37.5 hours per week (Monday – Friday, 9am – 5pm) Contract: Fixed term 1 Year Working base(s): 1 person to be based in St Albans Wellbeing Centre 1 person to be based in Watford Wellbeing Centre About the Service The Complex Needs Housing Service works as a multi-disciplinary team with housing teams and Drug and Alcohol Services across District and Borough councils. These teams will be working with individuals who are presenting as homeless and have a number of Complex Needs. The service has been running since 2022 with a dual-district model, however, is now expanding to offer a single district outreach service. We have roles available in the service in the following areas: St. Albans – supporting individuals who are homeless, in temporary accommodation or hostels in the district with their mental health South & West Hertfordshire – supporting women who have fled domestic abuse and currently residing in refuge/safe accommodation in the area with their mental health N.B. Only female applicants will be considered for this role. The objectives of the Single Homeless Support Pathway are: To improve the mental wellbeing of people experiencing mental ill health. To increase early access to help for people experiencing mental ill health in, by providing a clear and effective pathway to services provided by Herts Mind Network and other third sector and statutory providers. To contribute to an improvement in individual mental wellbeing. To remain a source of independent support for all clients. To reduce the use of police, ASB, tenancy enforcement, housing needs and environmental health services by clients whose primary need is related to mental ill health. To reduce the use of crisis services by people experiencing mental ill health without positive outcomes for the individual. To provide an assertive outreach approach for clients who are in crisis and/ or those that may have complex or multiple needs. To work collaboratively within a multi-disciplinary team consisting of District and Borough council’s housing teams, drug and alcohol services and other professionals. About the Role The purpose of the Hertfordshire Mind Network Community Outreach Worker role is to: To provide advice, information, onward referral and holistic support to clients who are experiencing mental ill health or need support with their mental wellbeing. These will be clients who are presenting to District and Borough councils as homeless and need intervention and support with their mental health and housing. To ensure that the safety and wellbeing of the client is monitored and reviewed regularly. To remain a source of independent support for all clients. Embed a person-centred recovery orientated and trauma informed approach in all aspects of the roles. We offer: Annual leave entitlement of 25 days per year pro rata, rising in increments to a max. of 29 days after 5 years employment (plus 8 days Bank Holidays) An additional day of leave each year for your birthday following completion of probation period. Ongoing training relevant to your role. An Employee Assistance Programme. Eligibility for blue light card. Health cover (after 6 months employment) – compensation payment for Optical, Dental, Chiropody and Therapy Treatments. Being able to drive and having access to your own vehicle (or equivalent) is essential for this role. Closing date for receipt of applications is Monday 28th September at 5pm. Interviews will be held on a rolling basis. Please note we may close this vacancy early if we receive a high volume of suitable applications. We encourage interested candidates to apply as soon as possible. N.B. Please quote reference number 368 when completing your application for this role. Interested? If you would like to find out more, please click the apply button. You will be directed to our website to complete your application for this position. We welcome applications from all suitably-qualified candidates, irrespective of gender, disability, marital or parental status, racial, ethnic or social origin, colour, religion, belief, or sexual orientation. In addition, during the various stages of recruitment, specific measures can be taken to ensure equal opportunities for candidates with disabilities or special needs. Hertfordshire Mind Network is committed to the Disability Confident and Mindful Employer charters. We actively recruit staff who have a lived experience of mental ill health. Our inclusive approach recognises the unique skills, knowledge, and perspectives that lived experience brings to our team. No agencies please.

item.title: Sessional Community Keyworker - Hampshire
item.description: Are you looking for flexible and rewarding work for an organisation with the feminist agenda at the core of its ethos? Then Advance Charity could be the choice for you! Please note these posts are subject to Police Vetting, a key requirement of this is that we work together to keep your vetting up to date for the duration of your engagements with us. Post Title: Sessional Community Keyworker Location: Hampshire Pay rate: £14.31 - £16.35 per hour Contract Type: Casual We are looking for Sessional Workers to support Advance’s Criminal Justice Services. Advance’s Criminal Justice Services work with women involved in the Criminal Justice System offering safe, targeted support and advocacy to women to help them address their complex needs in relation to the 9 pathways to offending, such as substance misuse and financial difficulties, aiming to reduce re-offending, encourage desistance amongst repeat offenders, and empower women to live safe, crime free lives. You will be working in a team of Community Keyworkers in your region. Each Keyworker will provide one to one community support to women with a variety of needs simultaneously and will be co-located with partner organisations in their region. You will be expected to travel to Advance’s Head office in London for any organisational meetings and training, as and when required. This post is not fixed hours or full time, work will be offered on an ad-hoc basis as and when required to meet the needs of the business. This post is open to female applicants only as being female is deemed to be a genuine occupational requirement under Schedule 9, Paragraph 1 of the Equality Act 2010. Please note : Any offer of employment will be made subject to references, confirmation of the right to work in the UK, and satisfactory enhanced DBS check. This role is also subject to Police Vetting. About us Advance is an award-winning and innovative women-only organisation, established in 1998, providing emotional and practical support to women and girls survivors of domestic abuse and supporting women with short-term sentences to reduce offending. We believe in empowering women and girls to lead safe, non-violent, equal lives so that they can flourish and contribute to the community. We are a community-based organisation who lead in best practice approaches to supporting women in their local community. We achieve this by being available to meet and support women in local settings and at our women’s centres, and by working in close partnership with other agencies. Our values are to listen and support, to empower and respect, collaboration, innovation, and accountability. How to apply: Please apply using your CV and a cover letter through our website. Closing Date for Applications: September 20th @ 23:30PM Interviews are taking place on a rolling basis *Advance reserves the right to close the advert early, or on the appointment of a candidate ************************************************************** Under the Equality Act 2010, we are required to make any reasonable adjustments. If you have a disability as defined under this act and/or have special needs, please email the Talent Acquisition Team via the Advance website and we will aim to make the necessary arrangements to accommodate your needs. Diversity, Inclusion and Equal Opportunities We are committed to providing equality of opportunity and actively seek to recruit people from groups underrepresented in our current team. We have policies and processes in place to ensure that all employees are offered an equal opportunity in recruitment and selection, promotion, training, pay and benefits. Safeguarding Advance is committed to safeguarding and creating a culture of zero-tolerance of harm and expects all staff, including volunteers to share this commitment. We believe all individuals have the right to live their life free from violence and abuse and the right to feel and be safe. We have a suite of safeguarding policies, procedures and practice guidance, accessible to all staff, which promotes safeguarding and safer working practices across all our services and activities. When we recruit staff, we follow rigorous safer recruitment practices, this involves carrying out pre-employment checks including references, Disclosure and Barring Service (DBS) checks, and identity checks. We ensure all staff undertake mandatory safeguarding training relevant to their role and responsibilities, to empower them to be competent and feel confident in recognising and responding appropriately to safeguarding issues and promote wellbeing.

item.title: Senior Partnerships Officer
item.description: We are looking for a senior partnerships officer who will ensure our vital work to address the environmental crisis is well funded, working to secure new partnerships and stewarding existing funder relationships. This multifaceted role works across teams to coordinate and deliver Green Alliance’s fundraising activities and grant management. Collaborating with the organisation’s policy and political experts, you support the creation of creative and impactful new project proposals that address environmental problems and support the organisation’s strategy. You will identify funders for this through prospecting and relationship building and will guide proposals through processes to secure funds. You will monitor the organisation’s progress against fundraising targets and lead on management of our funding pipeline. Stewardship of existing funding relationships is a significant part of this role which means ensuring we have excellent communication with our funders, making sure they receive high quality reports on Green Alliance’s impact and supporting the team to see our funders as partners. You will manage our Business Circle and maintain relationships with its members and support efforts to recruit new business members into Green Alliance Task Forces. Excellent communication skills are at the heart of this role, both written and verbal. You will be confident, efficient, and resourceful; calm under pressure and enjoy building strong relationships with a variety of senior stakeholders, as well as working independently. Strong skills in relation to organisation, administration and prioritisation are essential. You will need to understand, or be willing to learn about, the political and environmental policy contexts we work in. Please note that we reserve the right to close this vacancy early and interview suitable candidates as applications are received. You are encouraged to apply as soon as possible.

item.title: Communications and Programmes Officer
item.description: The Calouste Gulbenkian Foundation UK Branch is looking for a Communications and Programmes Officer to join our small, collaborative London team. The Calouste Gulbenkian Foundation is an independent charitable foundation established in Portugal in 1956. It is one of the largest European foundations, with headquarters in Lisbon and offices in London (the UK Branch) and Paris. The Foundation's mission is to promote the development of individuals and organisations, through art, science, education, and charity, for a more equitable and sustainable society. The Communications and Programmes Officer will work with colleagues to support the delivery of the Calouste Gulbenkian Foundation UK Branch's strategy. This post will help deliver the UK Branch's communications activity and support the UK programme's grant-making and projects. The UK Branch aims to strengthen arts and civil society ecosystems and emphasises transnational collaboration between Portugal (where the Foundation is headquartered) and the UK. Our grantmaking programme has three focus areas: arts opportunities, NGO capacity-building and climate-health. We fund and support partner organisations working in these areas and directly deliver projects in-line with our programme goals. The UK Branch also collaborates on flagship international initiatives of the Foundation, including the Gulbenkian Prize for Humanity and the Alliance for Socially Engaged Arts. The appointed person is likely to spend around 50% of time working on communications projects, and 50% on general programmatic work (including research, events, project management, and administration). This is a brilliant opportunity for someone with around two years of relevant experience looking to extend their skills and responsibilities and develop professionally. About you We do not expect candidates to evidence that they meet every point listed below. Instead, we encourage applications from candidates who meet the majority of the specification and are excited by the role. Excellent writing skills for a variety of audiences Experience developing content for social media and digital platforms Experience using communications software, ideally Mailchimp and WordPress (or equivalent) Strong research skills Experience managing projects and/or delivering events Awareness of, and an interest in, arts, environmental sustainability and the charity sector Prior employment in communications and/or a related field (ideally around two years of experience), or experience producing written and other communications in a formal context What we offer Salary of £29,850 to £33,000, depending on the experience of the candidate Stakeholder pension scheme, which new employees are eligible to join after a successful probation period, to which the Foundation makes a matched contribution Leave entitlement at the rate of 28 days per annum in addition to UK statutory holidays Health and dental insurance coverage for all employees Access to an Employee Assistance Programme (EAP), which includes mental health support services A generous budget for employee training Hybrid working, with equipment provided by the Foundation to support effective home working How to apply Download the full job pack and submit your CV and a cover letter, following the instructions provided, by 23:59 on Sunday 20 September 2026. The postholder must be eligible to work in the UK. Equal Opportunities The Foundation has an equal opportunity policy and implements to make this policy fully effective by ensuring that no job applicant or employee receives less favourable treatment on the grounds of age, sex, sexual orientation, religion or belief, disability or race. The principle applies to recruitment, pay, terms and conditions of employment and promotion.

item.title: Head of Income Generation
item.description: Build Up aims to build the power of young people to shape where they live and to change who can make decisions about London. We are recruiting a Head of Income Generation to shape and lead an ambitious fundraising vision to grow our impact across London. The Role This is an exciting new position in our team, created to help build our case for investment, tell our story and harness the support of new audiences. You will develop and deliver a 3-year fundraising strategy that unlocks new opportunities, diversifies income and builds lasting funder relationships. With consultancy support on communications and evaluation, you’ll have the tools to make a powerful case for our work. We encourage candidates to discuss the role with our Director before applying - contact details are in the job description. Who You Are You’ll have a proven track record in leading fundraising strategy, securing charitable investment and writing successful grants. Alongside trusts and foundations, you’ll bring experience across other income streams (like corporates or major donors). You’ll balance strategy with delivery, thrive under pressure, and be excited by funding young people’s ideas. Our approach is innovative and we are looking for someone that can create clear, inspiring narratives that unlock new opportunities. About Build Up Build Up works to build the power of young people to shape where they live, and to change who can make decisions about London. Regeneration leaves young people behind. We support young people to take action by advocating for, designing and building local spaces to meet their needs. Our approach is unique – and it works. Young people gain skills, leadership and power over decisions that affect them, while local communities benefit from genuinely inclusive spaces designed by and for local residents. Why Join Us At Build Up your work has a visible, lasting and personal impact - your ideas will genuinely shape our development. We’re a small, collaborative and passionate team with a flexible approach to work - we welcome proposals for non standard work patterns. Key Details This role is available on a 4 OR 5 day a week contract, subject to candidate preference. Salary: £50,000 - 54,000 (pro rata) + 8% employer pension contribution Full / part-time: 4 days (30 hrs) or 5 days (37.5 hrs) per week Holiday: 32 days plus public holidays (pro rata) Work pattern: Flexible Location: Hybrid – at least 1 day per week in our Elephant & Castle office Contract: Permanent To Apply For more information and to apply, please see the job description. Applications close Sunday 20th September 2026. We will be reviewing applications on a rolling basis from Monday 14th September, so we encourage applicants to apply as early as possible. #fundraising #fundraising manager #head of fundraising #fundraising lead #fundraising director #director of fundraising #fundraiser #youth-led fundraising #project fundraising #unrestricted fundraising #fundraising strategy

item.title: Chief Executive Officer
item.description: We’re looking for someone inspirational, approachable, open-minded, with great communication skills and a genuine passion for supporting people experiencing mental health difficulties, their families, friends and their carers to live their best lives. If this sounds like you, we’d love to hear from you. As our current CEO prepares for retirement, we are looking for someone new to lead our organisation with the kindness and professionalism we’re known for. For more than 30 years, Pembrokeshire and Carmarthen Mind has supported people across the Pembrokeshire and Carmarthen Local Authority areas and the Hywel Dda University Health Board region. Mental health challenges affect people from all walks of life, and the need for accessible, person-centred support continues to grow. Conditions such as anxiety, depression, and other long-term mental health difficulties remain some of the most common health issues faced by individuals, families, and communities. Compassionate, local mental health support can make a meaningful difference, we help people build resilience, maintain independence, and find hope during difficult times. Across the UK, many people experience significant impacts on their daily lives, relationships, and wellbeing because of mental health problems. The wider effects on families, carers, and support networks can also be profound, highlighting the importance of early help, ongoing support, and community-based services. Who we’re looking for: We’re looking for an experienced, confident and compassionate leader who can balance people, purpose and performance. You will be responsible for implementing the organisation’s strategy, as set by the Board of Trustees, leading staff and volunteers, overseeing services and finances, and ensuring strong governance and compliance. You’ll need strong knowledge and understanding of NHS and Local Authority structures, as well as health and social care legislation in Wales. You will maintain our welcoming, inclusive culture while planning for the future by identifying opportunities, building new partnerships and income streams, managing risk, and ensuring the charity’s financial sustainability. You will be a great listener, ensuring that our community feels heard. You will amplify their voices locally, regionally and nationally. These views will also inform the design, development and delivery of all our high-quality services Application Resources For Job Role specifics and more about us please see our CEO Recruitment Pack Application Instructions Ready to lead? If you are interested in becoming Pembrokeshire and Carmarthen Mind’s next permanent Chief Executive Officer, please complete our application form and attach your CV. The application form can be found on our website. For Full Application Instructions and more about us please see our CEO Recruitment Pack Closing date for this role will be at 12:00 midday on 30/09/26 Interviews for this role will be held on week commencing 19/10/26

item.title: Training Manager
item.description: Job title: Training Manager Organisation: Immigration Law Practitioners’ Association (ILPA) Location: Hybrid. Primarily remote with one weekly hub day in London. Working arrangements may change. Deadline: 9am, Monday 21st September. Salary: £33,000-£35,000 with scope to offer a higher salary depending on experience. Hours: Full time; 9am-5pm Monday-Friday. About the role: ILPA is a charity and professional membership body working to improve immigration, asylum and nationality law. Our training programme is a core part of our work and one of our largest income streams. We deliver over 60 courses and conferences a year to an average of 2,000 practitioners across the UK, supporting lawyers, caseworkers, advisers and organisations working with migrants. The Training Manager will not directly teach any training content but will run this programme end to end, ensuring all trainings and events are delivered professionally, to a high standard. This is a hands-on role that requires strong organisational skills, confidence with digital platforms and the ability to work with experienced external tutors. The post holder will shape the training calendar with support from the Training Advisory Board and maintain ILPA’s reputation for high-quality, practitioner-led training. Key Responsibilities Programme planning and development • Build and manage the annual and quarterly training schedule with a balance of advanced, intermediate and introductory courses across immigration, asylum and nationality law • Facilitate and support the Training Advisory Board to identify priorities and emerging issues • Respond to changes in immigration law with short notice trainings where appropriate Tutor and content management • Contact, contract and manage ILPA’s panel of external tutors • Work closely with tutors on the overall planning and delivery, providing admin support in the production of accurate, up-to-date course materials • Maintain and update appropriate guidance for tutors and conference chairs Event delivery • Set up all events on Eventbrite, including pricing, discounts, communications and refunds • Host online events and support hybrid delivery of trainings and conferences when required, troubleshooting technical issues on the day Income, reporting and evaluation • Monitor and report on key data including bookings, attendance, costs and income • Optimise participant feedback rates, monitor satisfaction and take action where needed • Monitor trends and use data analysis to inform future programme planning • Review pricing strategy and initiatives to inform recommendations Marketing and engagement • Market events, including through ILPA’s weekly all-member update, targeted email updates to relevant working groups, selected social media and other communication channels to reach beyond our membership • Respond to participant queries and ensure excellent customer experience Systems and administration • Maintain accurate records, contracts, schedules and evaluation data • Ensure compliance with GDPR and internal policies • Make appropriate use of systems including Eventbrite and Salesforce to manage and analyse programme efficacy Person Specification Essential • Experience managing training or professional development programmes • Ability to think strategically and develop the training programme in response to feedback and changes in immigration policy. • Excellent communication skills and the ability to hold relationships with a range of stakeholders including senior practitioners, tutors, venues and ILPA members. •Experience in event planning and in commissioning a variety of supporting services and vendors. • Experience in event delivery and the ability to manage a small team to support delivery of an in-person event or conference. • Strong digital and numerical skills including ticket management, online event, CRM platforms as well as Excel. • Ability and confidence to host or facilitate online trainings and events • Ability to work independently in a small charity team • Strong organisational skills and confidence managing a busy scheduleand ability to resolve issues efficiently despite competing deadlines. Desirable • Knowledge of immigration, asylum or nationality law • Experience in a charity, membership body or legal-sector environment • Experience commissioning or managing external tutors or contributors • Experience of using Salesforce, Eventbrite, Quickbooks, MS Teams, Zoom How to Apply To apply, please complete the following forms and submit them as per the instructions on our website (linked). ILPA Application Form ILPA Equalities Monitoring Form Applications from individuals only – no agencies. Please do not use artificial intelligence in completing your application form. Please submit a completed ILPA application form and equalities monitoring form as a Word document or in another editable format. If an application is not submitted in this format, it will not be considered. If you need the forms in an alternative format or require adjustments, contact recruitment. The email address can be found on our wesbite (linked). Deadline : 9am, Monday 21st September.

item.title: Connect To Work Triage Co-ordinator
item.description: An exciting full time opportunity has opened up at CPSL Mind. CPSL Mind is a vibrant, values-led charity that supports local people in their recovery from mental health issues, promotes wellbeing and campaigns against stigma and discrimination. item.title: Corporate Partnerships Manager
item.description: Purpose of the role The Literacy Pirates is an educational charity working across the UK to develop the literacy, confidence and perseverance of children who are falling behind in school and have fewer opportunities in their personal lives. We offer in-person and online literacy programmes that support children to meet age-related expectations in reading and writing, succeed in school, and thrive beyond the classroom. Literacy Pirates is at an incredibly exciting point in its 15-year journey, as we embark on year two of our five-year national expansion plan, with a target to quadruple the number of young people we support over the next four years and double our fundraised income. About the Fundraising & Communications Department The Corporate Partnerships Manager reports to the Head of Development and is part of the broader fundraising and communications team along with the Trusts & Foundation Manager and Communications Manager. Corporate partnerships revenue accounts for 40% of our fundraised income and is a key strategic target for growth. The Corporate Partnerships Manager role is therefore critical to achieving our national expansion ambitions. This role is office-based in London, with the option to work from remotely two days a week. Key Purpose Duties and Responsibilities General A commitment to high standards of service delivery and customer care Regularly monitor and update all financial and KPI data on departmental reporting documents Participate actively in regular departmental meetings and support colleagues on broader fundraising and communications work. Person Specification Interest in, and enthusiasm to, identify and develop new corporate fundraising strategies and initiatives. Proven track record of securing income and managing partnerships and sponsorships within a target driven environment Experience of delivering events, both standalone and as a part of a wider partnership. Salary: £40,000 - 42,000 (incl. London Weighting) Contract: Full time, permanent Location: London based, three days in the office, with the option to work remotely two days.

item.title: Content Coordinator
item.description: We're looking for an organised and creative Content Coordinator to join our Communications team and help bring IHP's work, impact and stories to life. This is an exciting opportunity for someone who enjoys creating engaging content, managing digital communications and ensuring everything runs smoothly behind the scenes. IHP’s vision is to see a world in which all suffering due to lack of healthcare is eradicated. Our Christian faith underpins all that we do. It motivates us to care for those in need, and give our best in all circumstances, as an expression of God's love. We serve the poor in health without regard for ethnic or religious background, focusing on where the need is greatest. About the role This is a varied and hands-on role where you'll help ensure our communications are engaging, consistent and effectively showcase the impact of our work. Working closely with the Communications Manager and Senior Communications Officer, you'll play a key role in delivering day-to-day communications activity across IHP's channels. You'll be responsible for: Creating and scheduling engaging social media content Helping to tell the stories of the people and communities we support Managing and maintaining digital content and image libraries Supporting communications campaigns and partnership activities Maintaining content calendars, records and communications systems Identifying opportunities to improve audience engagement and content effectiveness About you We're looking for someone who has experience creating content for social media and digital channels, understands how to create content that engages different audiences across social media platforms, and is comfortable using analytics or communications data to understand what is working. Experience managing digital content, images or other communications assets would also be valuable. You will be: ✅ Highly organised, with excellent attention to detail ✅ Confident and engaging in both written and verbal communication ✅ Comfortable planning and scheduling regular content ✅ Able to work independently and use initiative ✅ Collaborative and approachable, with strong interpersonal skills ✅ Confident maintaining accurate records and systems ✅ Passionate about finding practical ways to improve processes and ways of working Experience in a small charity, not-for-profit or other purpose-driven organisation would be desirable, as would an interest in using communications to demonstrate organisational impact. For further details regarding responsibilities and person specification, please see the job description. Why join IHP? This is more than a communications role. Every piece of content you create will help raise awareness of our work, strengthen partnerships and support our mission to improve access to essential medicines worldwide. You'll join a supportive, values-driven organisation where your contribution will have a direct impact on the lives of vulnerable communities across the globe. Staff regularly spend time together praying for IHP’s work and there is an occupational requirement for the post holder to have a personal commitment to the Christian faith. Employee Benefits include: 25 days annual leave plus bank holidays (pro-rate for part-time hours) Health and wellbeing support through Unum help@hand Life Insurance and Critical Illness Cover Hybrid and flexible working options in a modern office near Chancery Lane Tube Station IHP is an Equal Opportunities Employer and is committed to working and embedding diversity and inclusion in all aspects of our work, including recruitment and selection. item.title: Innovation Strategy Manager
item.description: As Innovation Strategy Manager you will lead in helping Battersea learn, experiment and develop new solutions to drive forward our strategic priorities, keeping us relevant, future-focused and generating ever greater impact. All work is delivered through creativity, collaboration within and outside of Battersea and a deep understanding of our target audiences, balancing ambition and pragmatism. Why the role exists: This is a rare opportunity to lead in helping Battersea learn, experiment and develop new solutions to positively impact the lives of cats, dogs, and their owners for years to come. You’ll bring strong strategic thinking, innovation expertise, service design, and leadership skills to an environment focused on meaningful social impact, working alongside a team of smart, compassionate, and experienced colleagues. This role focuses on broad, organisation-wide innovation - spanning our services, operations, supporter offering, and income generation - with a clear focus on delivering outcomes for animals and the people who care for them. It is not a specialist digital or fundraising role; instead, it centres on identifying the right problems and shaping effective responses. While some initiatives will involve digital elements (and an understanding of this is useful), delivery is carried out by specialist teams both in-house and externally. Success in this role means identifying high-impact opportunities, aligning stakeholders around them, and ensuring they are taken forward effectively - supporting pilots and implementation where appropriate. What we can offer you: In return for your commitment to our cause and to recognise the value of our employees, Battersea offers a range of benefits to support the wellbeing of our employees. These include: 28 days of annual leave (plus 8 days paid public holidays) per year. Discounted gym memberships and cycle to work schemes. Employee Assistance Programme and access to Wellbeing Resources. Generous pension contributions - up to 10% employer contribution. Free healthcare cash plan, where you can claim for a range of treatment including dental, optical, physiotherapy, chiropody and acupuncture every year. Annual interest-free season ticket loans. We are also committed to providing learning and development to our employees. During your time with us, we provide support for your professional and career development, including access to digital and in-person training programmes, leadership and management training, mentoring and much more. Our hybrid working model: We operate a 50% onsite hybrid working model, with our office-based staff splitting their time between site based and home working. This enables our office-based staff to balance the benefits of home working with onsite collaboration and maintaining a connection to our cause. Diversity and inclusion: We are committed to providing a welcoming and inclusive experience for all staff, volunteers and trustees and those hoping to join us. We operate an anonymised shortlisting process and actively seek to ensure our process is fair and equitable for all. We understand the value of diverse voices, perspectives, and experiences to help us deliver even more for our dogs and cats, and we welcome applicants from all sections of the community. As a Disability Confident Committed Employer we will ask about any adjustments you may need at application and/or interview stage, and if you are offered a role with us, we’ll talk to you about any workplace adjustments you may need to help you perform at your best. Greyscale copies of the recruitment pack are also available on request. More about us: At Battersea, we aim to never turn away a dog or cat in need of help. We give each one lots of love, expert care and get to know their characters and quirks so we can find them a new home that’s just right for them. Join us and help us be here for every dog and cat, wherever they are, for as long as they need us. Acceptable use of AI: At Battersea, we value expertise. We recognise each candidate that applies to us will have a range of expertise they can offer us, so we want to hear about this in your own words. We understand the support that generative artificial intelligence (AI) software can offer but it can also lead to numerous applications presenting as generic and impersonal. This makes it difficult to gain understanding of your unique experience. To best showcase yourself, we encourage you to write your responses without the assistance of AI. If you require the use of AI software to aid in completing your application, we ask you use the generative responses as a prompt for writing your answers and avoid copying and pasting. You must also ensure the information presented in your application accurately reflects your experience. Closing date: 22nd August 2026 All applications must be submitted before the closing date advertised. We reserve the right to close the vacancy early if a high volume of applications is received. Interview date(s): First Round (online): 30th September & 1st October 2026 Second Round (in-person): To be confirmed For more information about the role, please download our Recruitment pack.

item.title: Digital and Social Media Officer
item.description: Do you understand digital marketing and enjoy creating compelling social media content? Can you make a video that stops the scroll? Would you like to put these skills to use to help others play their part in God’s mission? • Permanent, full-time 35 hours per week ( We would consider reduced hours) • Hybrid working available with 60 per cent home working. • Starting salary: £31,700 per annum (depending on experience) with a generous pension contribution: up to 10 per cent employer contribution on annual salary. • CMS offers 36 days of annual leave pro rata (including bank holidays) as well as enhanced paid sickness, maternity, paternity and adoption leave. • CMS supports the mental wellbeing of its employees and offers a generous rewards and wellbeing package, including: access to 24/7 employee assistance programme with qualified counsellors up to three volunteer days a year up to three family emergency leave days a year retreats and resources for prayer life We welcome applications from everyone. We particularly welcome applications from individuals from minority groups as they are currently underrepresented within our organisation. All appointments are made on merit of skill, experience and potential as set out in the job description and person specification. The organisation you’ll be joining Church Mission Society is comprised of people who are passionate about mission and fired up about helping people follow Jesus. For over 200 years CMS has been at the forefront of global mission, living out the gospel of Jesus, seeing lives changed and communities transformed. If you join CMS, you will find an organisation that has been reinvigorated with a fresh vision to make disciples of Jesus among people at the edges, both in the UK and around the world. Your role The fundraising and communications group at CMS has ambitious goals and targets and you’ll play a key role in helping successfully deliver on these. You’ll harness the huge potential of social media and other digital platforms to help CMS get the attention of our target audiences, build brand awareness, raise money and recruit people to our mission programmes. As well as having a strong working knowledge of social media platforms, you will need to be able to create and edit video as well as other forms of compelling content. What you’ll need to succeed It is essential that the post holder has proven social media, organic and paid content production experience, including video creation, and knowledge of social media posting and interaction via Facebook, Instagram, YouTube and LinkedIn in an organisational context. In addition, we are looking for proven website editing experience using a content management system such as WordPress and email marketing via a client such as DotDigital. It is also a requirement that this post holder is committed to the aims and values of CMS. Further details can be found in the job description and person specification available to download on the CMS website. Our commitment to you Our core values of being pioneering, relational, faithful and evangelistic are integral to everything we do, and we work hard to ensure that every member of staff is valued, supported and encouraged to continually learn and develop their skills. We are committed to the safeguarding and protection of the people we serve, our partners, our volunteers, and our staff. We believe that every child or adult we come into contact with has the right to be protected from all forms of harm and abuse. Our recruitment and selection processes are in line with our Safeguarding Policy and the SCHR Misconduct Disclosure Scheme, which CMS is a member of as part of our commitment to safeguarding. Closing date We must get your application by midnight on Sunday 20 September 2026 Interviews are planned to be held on Wednesday 29 September 2026 in CMS House, Oxford. To apply Please send your application form, CV and evidence of your digital and social media work, including video content that you have edited (for example, links to online work or a portfolio of work) via our website or by post to HR Team, Church Mission Society, Watlington Road, Oxford OX4 6BZ. CVs will only be considered when sent with a completed Application Form, which is available to download from our website. Candidates for all UK roles must already be eligible to work in the UK, with a valid visa and work permit if required. As a member of the Inter-agency Misconduct Disclosure Scheme, CMS has committed to systematically check with previous employers from the last five years for any ‘SEAH’ (Sexual Exploitation, Abuse or Harassment) issues relating to all potential new hires.

item.title: Education Programme Lead
item.description: For over 60 years the National Children’s Bureau (NCB) has been building a better childhood for all. We are currently recruiting an Education Programme Lead to join us on a fixed-term contract until March 2027. Education Programme Lead Contract: Fixed term until March 2027 Work Pattern: 35 hours per week. (1 FTE). We are open to flexible hours and working patterns, including accommodating part-time and compressed hours where possible Salary: £51,349 (£55,512 if based in London) Location: London E8 / Belfast, Northern Ireland / Newton Abbot, Devon / Sheffield / Remote within the UK. NCB promotes a hybrid, flexible way of working with 1 day working in the office if based in London. The Vacancy This role will lead key programmes of work related to education and equalities and will work to influence legislation, policy and practice to secure system improvement, more inclusive opportunities and better outcomes for children and young people, with a particular focus on disabled children and young people and those with special educational needs. This role will also be involved in developing opportunities for work on education and equalities to improve access and inclusion in schools, and early years and post-16 settings. They will also develop and hold relationships with partner organisations, local and national agencies, to influence and respond to national education policy affecting wellbeing and disabled children and young people and those with SEN. About NCB For more than 60 years, the National Children’s Bureau has championed the rights and amplified the voice of children and young people in the UK. We interrogate policy and uncover evidence, blending in lived and learnt experience to shape future legislation and develop more effective ways of supporting children and families. Bringing people and organisations together is fundamental to how we improve the systems that babies, children, young people and their families rely on to thrive. We push boundaries, even looking beyond childhood itself to consider transitions into adulthood and the impact of childhood issues on an entire lifespan. We are united for better childhoods and brighter futures. The Benefits 30 Days Annual Leave Generous Pension Scheme Cycle to work scheme Flexible Working Winter Holiday Closure & Break Employee Assistance Programme Applications close at 08:00am on Friday 25th September 2026 . Assessment and interviews to be conducted on Thursday 15th October 2026 . Please note that we reserve the right to close this vacancy early should we receive a high volume of applications. We encourage interested candidates to submit their applications as soon as possible. Interested? If you would like to find out more, please click the apply button. You will be directed to our website to complete your application for this position. We are actively seeking to broaden the diversity of our staff group and warmly welcome applications from candidates underrepresented in the charity sector, including those from Black and Global Majority communities, disabled people, LGBTQ+ individuals, and people with lived experience of the issues NCB works on. No agencies please.

item.title: NZC Programme Officer (fixed term)
item.description: The Diocese of Leicester is committed to reducing the overall diocesan Carbon emissions by 2030; aiming to reduce the emissions from energy consumption year on year and to incorporate sustainable working practices across all of our operations. Are you passionate about sustainability and supporting churches to be open for future generations? We are looking for somebody relational, committed to carbon reduction and adaptable to be our Net Zero Carbon Programme Officer to work with our parishes and their communities, helping to reduce their carbon footprint and ensure church buildings remain sustainable as a place of worship and a resource for the local community. This is a new fixed-term post made possible by a grant from of The Church of England through their Net Zero Carbon Capacity Building Programme. In this rewarding role, you will: develop positive relationships with key stakeholders within the Diocese, in particular with Parochial Church Councils supporting them in making informed and planned decisions to reduce carbon emissions in their churches and church halls play a key part in enabling the delivery of the NZC targets within Diocesan Environmental Programme (2026-29), by data collection, analysis, reporting, and contributing to setting the annual targets for the programme. contribute to delivering communications, training, advice and education needed to progress towards reaching Net Zero Carbon. What we are looking for A relevant degree, equivalent qualifications or relevant experience Practical experience and/or knowledge in managing buildings, with a focus on sustainability. An understanding of and commitment to working with churches and halls with a range of building construction types to improve their energy efficiency and work towards Net Zero Carbon. Knowledgeable and passionate about environmental issues and climate change. Understanding of and confidence working with numerical & technical data. Experience in successful problem solving and project management Excellent skills in interpersonal relationships, negotiation and written and visual communication and presentation The capacity to build relationships with colleagues, parish clergy and volunteers, and other stakeholders in the diocese to engage them in working towards Net Zero Carbon for church-owned buildings The capacity to work and make decisions independently. Good IT skills, including use of Microsoft Office and databases. Ability to travel regularly across the Diocese and work flexibly, including occasional evenings and weekends. Sympathy with and commitment to the values and mission of the Church of England and the Diocese of Leicester. Desirable Experience of working with heritage or listed buildings Building services professional, relevant degree or professional qualification/s in heritage management, sustainability or project management Knowledge of Church of England legislation applicable to Church Buildings Why Join Us? Be part of a new area of work within a collaborative and experienced team. Hybrid working with a Leicester office base An opportunity to work with a variety of different communities across Leicestershire, each with its own needs. Make a tangible difference to local communities and to caring for and sustaining the environment through supporting the reduction of carbon emissions. Generous pension (10% employer contribution) and annual leave (25 days plus bank holidays). Opportunities for training, development and professional growth. For an informal conversation about the role see contact details in general info document. Closing Date: Sunday 20th September Shortlisting date: Wednesday 23rd September Interview Date: Thursday 8th October We particularly welcome applications from UK Minority Ethnic / Global Majority Heritage candidates, who are currently underrepresented in our organisation. The Diocese of Leicester, part of the Church of England, is committed to the safeguarding, care and nurture of everyone within our church community. We follow the Church of England’s Safeguarding Policies and relevant statutory guidance. We believe that safeguarding is everybody’s business. This post is subject to a Basic DBS check and proof of right to work in the UK. The Diocese is unable to offer a Certificate of Sponsorship.

item.title: Funding Officer/ Swyddog Ariannu, UK Portfolio
item.description: At The National Lottery Community Fund (The Fund), we are driven by our strategy ‘It starts with community’ and its four community-led missions, as well as our commitment to tackling poverty, discrimination and disadvantage through an equity-based approach. This is an exciting opportunity to join the UK Portfolio at an ambitious moment of shaping the next phase of our strategy. We are looking for four Funding Officers (2x 12 month FTC, 1 x FTC until March 2027 and 1x FTC until July 2027) to join us and form part of a team of around 40 in total. The UK Portfolio supports the ambitions and potential of communities across the UK. We focus on scaling projects with a UK-wide benefit, through significant investments and partnerships, which enable systems-level change for communities. Our funding is intended to complement the work of other country portfolios: England, Northern Ireland, Scotland and Wales. Our Funding Officers are at the core of what we do in the UK Portfolio as we continue to develop in response to our strategy. Our team is spread across the UK, and we're looking for people from a variety of locations within the UK. Our current work includes: The UK Fund : offers long term funding to support organisations to scale proven work and approaches against two main themes: connected communities and youth voice. Funded projects consistently focus on systems change, community power and voice. Climate Action Fund : supports UK-wide ambitious, partnership-led approaches to climate and environmental challenges, bringing together organisations to deliver long-term change at scale. Working in partnership with others: Examples include Communities for Children, focused on tackling child poverty, Together for Families, supporting early intervention for children and families. We are also developing new areas of work that explore the opportunities and implications of emerging technologies including artificial intelligence. Role Expectations Funding officers help amazing things to happen in communities. They play a vital role in ensuring we provide excellent service to communities all over the UK. You will support organisations through the grant making process and use your knowledge and experience to make evidence informed judgements. You’ll manage key relationships with grant holders, responding to their needs, providing advice and considered feedback and be willing to have challenging but constructive conversations. You’ll be a great team player and play an active role in ensuring the effective running of team meetings. As a Funding Officer you will : Support enquirers, applicants and grant holders through our funding processes, assessing and managing a caseload of applications and grants of varying value and complexity. Build and maintain relationships with stakeholders at different levels, including project visits and external events. Produce and present clear reports which reflect sound judgement, sector knowledge and understanding of the Fund’s strategy, missions and policies Identify, and manage risk, supporting organisations to deliver their projects and measure their impact. Ensure our data is maintained, accurate and of high quality Ensure grant management and assessment contribute meaningfully to the Fund’s learning and impact. Demonstrate a commitment to, and ability to build understanding of the Fund’s ambition as an environmentally regenerative funder. Contribute to projects including programme development, our equity based approach to funding, impact, continuous improvement and Fund wide initiatives. Skills & Requirements You will use your critical thinking skills, curiosity, interest and understanding of our community-led missions to support and inform your approach to assessment and grant management. You’ll be joining a dynamic and welcoming geographically dispersed team, working with impactful and fascinating projects that are responding to and addressing a wide range of topics across the Fund’s four community-led missions. We are looking for talented and proactive team players from a wide range of backgrounds, cultures and experiences who share our values and are passionate about making a difference through our funding. Whatever your background, the role would suit people who: are passionate about achieving social change and have a strong commitment to equity, diversity and inclusion. have skills and experience in presentation and report writing and basic accounting and budget management. can apply their research, data gathering, insight and critical analysis skills to learn quickly about a range of themes and issues. can absorb a wide range of information and evidence and present it to others in a clear and concise manner. can work flexibly at pace and to tight deadlines, using their initiative to manage their time working comfortably with competing priorities and deadlines. are adept at building and maintaining relationships with people from a range of backgrounds and experiences. are strong team players committed to sharing learning with their colleagues and the wider Fund to improve our processes and practices. are comfortable working with an online and geographically dispersed team. are comfortable learning and working with different systems and data. You’ll report to one of our Portfolio Managers and work with other Funding Officers across different areas of the team. The role requires occasional (once a month) travel across the UK to observe and critically analyse the work of applicants and grant holders. Interview details: Format: Online – MS Teams We have a hybrid approach to working. Work pattern and location will be agreed with the successful candidate. The role can be based at any of our UK offices: Belfast, Birmingham, Cardiff, Exeter, Glasgow, Leeds, London, Manchester and Newcastle. For an informal discussion about the role, please contact us. To ask any questions, please email us. How to apply: Upload your CV in word format and write a supporting statement (1000 words) with the following criteria, we will use this to score your application. Essential Criteria: Sector insight: Knowledge and understanding of the voluntary sector and communities across the UK and a well-developed appreciation of how they can respond to our strategy and missions. Communication skills: Strong listening, written and verbal communication skills including report writing and with the ability to communicate complex ideas in an engaging and clear manner, tailored to different audiences. Analytical skills : Ability to absorb a wide range of information and evidence to reach judgement-based recommendations with confidence, offering appropriate challenge and managing risk throughout the grant making lifecycle. Organisational skills: Ability to plan and manage a caseload of assessments and grant management, balancing competing priorities and deadlines and demonstrating strong organisation and prioritisation skills. Relational skills: Ability to build and maintain effective, collaborative relationships with colleagues, customers and stakeholders. Equity, Diversity and Inclusion: A strong understanding of our vision, our commitment and our funding products - and the ability to apply this throughout the grant making lifecycle. Desirable Criteria: Continuous improvement: A learning mindset and curiosity about our work with the ability to identify opportunities for learning and improvement across the team and wider directorate through proactive problem-solving and continuous improvement. Data and finance: Ability to understand and assess data and financial information including business plans and accounts, and present this in an accessible way. Equity, Diversity and Inclusion Communities in the UK come in all shapes and sizes. National Lottery funding is for everyone – therefore, we are committed to equity, diversity and inclusion and we work hard to ensure our funding reaches where it is needed. We also believe our people should represent the communities, organisations and individuals we work with. That’s why The National Lottery Community Fund is committed to being an inclusive employer and a great place to work. We recognise and celebrate the fact that our people come from diverse backgrounds. We positively welcome applications from people from ethnic minority backgrounds, people with disabilities or longstanding health conditions, people who are LGBTQ+, and people from different socio-economic and educational backgrounds, as well as people of all ages. As a Disability Confident Employer, we take a proactive approach in making reasonable adjustments, if needed, throughout the recruitment process and during employment. (This can be related to a physical and mental health condition.)
