item.title: Money Advisor
item.description: About the role RAID has 4 main advice areas: Information Navigation, Benefits Advice, Energy Advice and Money Advice. The Cost of Living Crisis has disproportionally impacted Disabled people, who are more likely to face higher living costs, barriers to employment and reduced financial resilience, making it harder to cope with rising household expenses. Many of the people we see are in challenging situations; struggling with debt, experiencing food and fuel poverty, facing homeless and dealing with loneliness and isolation. The work can be emotionally challenging. The Money Advisor will provide high-quality, accessible and person-centred money advice to Disabled people and people with long-term health conditions, supporting them to understand their financial situation, maximise their income, manage financial pressures and exercise their rights. The Money Advisor will be required to undertake training to again gain accreditation from the Money and Pensions Service (MaPS), as part of their Quality Framework for Individuals, and will be expected to retain this qualification through continual professional development. Free training will be provided through the Wiser Adviser platform. The Money Advisor will provide practical advice and support on a range of financial issues, budgeting, debt, household costs and financial inclusion. You will work closely with our Welfare Benefits team and undertake casework yourself as required to resolve issues. The role will recognise the barriers created by social, economic and environmental factors and work alongside people to identify solutions that increase financial security, choice and independence. The postholder will work within RAID's rights-based and Social Model of Disability approach, ensuring that Disabled people are listened to, treated with dignity and supported to make informed decisions about their lives. About You You are a knowledgeable, approachable and compassionate adviser who is passionate about helping Disabled people improve their financial security and exercise their rights. You will have experience of providing money, welfare benefits or related advice and be confident supporting people to navigate what can sometimes be complex financial and benefits systems. You will be able to explain information clearly and in an accessible way, helping people understand their options and make informed decisions. You will take a person-centred and rights-based approach, recognising that Disabled people can experience significant financial barriers, including additional costs associated with disability, inaccessible services, discrimination and barriers to employment and income. You will understand the importance of listening to people and working alongside them rather than making assumptions about what they need. You will be comfortable supporting people with a range of circumstances and levels of support needs. You will be patient, non-judgemental and able to build trust with people who may have had difficult experiences when accessing services. You will be organised and able to manage your own caseload, prioritise effectively and maintain accurate records. You will also enjoy working collaboratively with colleagues and external organisations to find practical solutions and achieve positive outcomes for the people we support. You do not need to be an accredited money advisor to apply but you must successfully complete the required training and be able to demonstrate an interest and aptitude for money advice.
item.dc:creator: Richmond Advice and Information on Disability (RAID), TW11

item.title: Corporate Partnerships Fundraiser
item.description: Are you an experienced fundraiser who enjoys building relationships and wants the opportunity to shape a role around your skills and experience? We’re looking for a Corporate Partnerships Fundraiser to join Enham Trust and help grow our corporate fundraising. You will manage and develop our existing partnerships while also building new relationships and identifying opportunities to bring new supporters on board. This is a role where you will have the opportunity to take ownership, bring your own ideas and help shape how our corporate fundraising develops. What you will be doing You’ll build and maintain relationships with our corporate partners, while also identifying new organisations and opportunities to grow our income. You’ll work closely with businesses to develop fundraising, sponsorship, volunteering and other ways they can support Enham Trust. You’ll also: Manage and develop existing corporate partnerships, while building relationships with new supporters. Identify and secure new fundraising and partnership opportunities. Develop corporate fundraising programmes and activities that encourage businesses to support Enham Trust. Develop effective processes and workflows to support corporate fundraising and supporter engagement. Meet with corporate partners, volunteers and other stakeholders Coordinate corporate volunteering opportunities and support positive experiences for our partners. Work closely with the wider fundraising team and contribute to wider fundraising activity where needed. There is plenty of scope for the role to develop, so we’re looking for someone who is confident working independently, takes ownership and happy to bring new ideas to the table. About you You’ll already have fundraising experience and understand how to build strong relationships with supporters and develop those relationships into fundraising opportunities. Corporate or partnership fundraising experience is important, as you’ll be managing existing relationships while also looking for new opportunities. You will be responsible for growing income to support Enham Trust’s fundraising targets. We’re looking for someone who is: Confident, organised and able to manage their own workload. Comfortable building relationships with businesses and other stakeholders. A strong communicator, both face to face and in writing. Confident presenting, networking and representing a charity externally. Able to spot opportunities and take them forward independently. Passionate about fundraising and motivated by making a difference. Experience of working within the disability sector would be useful but isn’t essential. Fundraising training and support will be available, so we’re looking for someone who has the right fundraising experience and wants to develop their career with us. You will need to be based within or near Hampshire, as we’re looking for someone who can work from our Enham Trust office around 2 to 3 days a week. You’ll also need to be comfortable travelling to meet corporate partners and attend external meetings, so you’ll need a full UK driving licence and access to a vehicle for work purposes. About Enham Trust We are Enham! Together we have been making a difference to the lives of disabled people for over 100 years and we are looking forward to continuing this for the next 100 years! Together we explore opportunities with people so they can live the lives they choose by overcoming limitations and expanding possibilities. Through first class care, personal development, housing options, and employment, we support people to exercise individual choice and control in their lives. We live by our values, TOGETHER we do amazing, we WOW people every day and we dare to be DIFFERENT !
item.dc:creator: Enham Trust.org, Andover

item.title: Public Affairs and Campaigns Manager
item.description: Help us achieve our vision that fewer people die by suicide. Suicide can be prevented but urgent action is needed. We are looking for an experienced Public Affairs and Campaigns Manager to lead our work to mobilise our campaigners and maximise our political relationships to push for action to prevent suicide. Samaritans is the UK and Ireland’s leading suicide prevention charity. While we are best known for listening to those who need us, we also work to influence change through our policy, advocacy campaigning and relationships with political stakeholders. The Policy, Public Affairs and Campaigns team of five works alongside people with lived experience, our campaigners, supporters and volunteers to push for the public policy and legal changes that will help us achieve our vision. We work to achieve system change through our work with the Westminster parliament, UK Government departments, policy makers and service leads, alongside our offices in the nations. We're looking for a Public Affairs and Campaigns Manager to lead this area of work. We know that to make a real difference to those who are affected by suicide, we need to drive meaningful change in UK legislation and policy, funding and research. If you're a strategic thinker with a track record of successfully influencing for change, we'd love to hear from you. Contract terms: £42,000 - £44,000 per annum, plus benefits Permanent 35 hours per week (full-time) We are passionate about flexible working, talk to us about your preferences Hybrid, linked to our Ewell (Surrey) office We value meeting in person and working collaboratively. We work in person around 2 days or more per month. This role will also involve regular travel to Westminster. 28 days annual leave, plus bank holidays What you'll be doing: You'll lead our public affairs and advocacy campaigns work focused on influencing decision-makers and driving advocacy campaigns. Your key responsibilities include: Overseeing our advocacy campaigning activity across England and line managing the Public Affairs and Campaigns Officer, ensuring that our advocacy campaigns are rooted in lived experience, and that our supporters have a positive ongoing experience. Leading the implementation of our public affairs and campaign strategies to achieve change on Samaritan’s key influencing priorities Identifying, creating, and evaluating opportunities and mechanisms to increase political engagement and persuade decision makers to take positive action on suicide prevention Identifying, cultivating and maintaining excellent relationships across the UK parliament and key political decision makers. Working across the charity to connect all of our relevant work to Parliamentary audiences, including support for Samaritans branches and volunteers on public affairs activities You’ll play a pivotal role in leading our efforts to drive meaningful change to help prevent suicide. What you’ll bring: Great people skills with the ability to turn contacts into action Proven experience in successfully influencing within the UK Parliament Experience of leading effective advocacy campaigns and trialling new and exciting campaign tactics Excellent communication skills, with the ability to engage diverse audiences effectively A passion for involving people with lived experience in your campaigns and public affairs work For full details, please see the Job Description and Person Specification Why Samaritans? At Samaritans, you’ll join a values-led organisation with a powerful mission. You’ll be part of a collaborative and supportive team where your voice matters, your expertise makes a difference, and your work helps save lives. We offer flexible hybrid working, great benefits, and the chance to make a tangible difference in suicide prevention across the UK and Ireland. To find out more about Samaritans, please read our recruitment brochure. We are committed to building a diverse and inclusive organisation that reflects the people we support and who support us. We welcome applications from people of all backgrounds and walks of life. We are committed to creating an inclusive culture where everyone feels seen, heard and supported, at all levels of the organisation. Apply now If this sounds like the opportunity for you, we’d love for you to apply. You will be asked to answer some short application questions and to upload your CV. If you require adjustments at any stage of the recruitment process, please let us know. Applications close: 20th September 2026 Interviews: w/c 28th September At Samaritans, human connection is at the heart of everything we do. We do not use AI at any stage during the selection process. Your application will always be carefully reviewed by the recruiting manager or a member of the Talent Attraction Team. We kindly ask that you avoid using AI tools to generate your application or interview answers. We want to hear your own ideas, insights, and writing style so your unique strengths can shine through. We recognise that some candidates may use assistive technology or tools to help with accessibility, structure or grammar.

item.title: Research Manager
item.description: Ataxia UK Research Manager This is a part-time 12 month fixed term maternity cover post Salary: £44,000 pa pro-rata Conditions: 25 days annual leave pa pro-rata (not including Bank Holidays) 5% employer contribution to a personal pension plan. Hours: 21 hours pw with provision for flexible working in line with Ataxia UK’s policy. Some out of hours work may be required for which time off in lieu will be granted. Location: Hybrid working between home and office: Ataxia UK Office, 12 Broadbent Close, London N6 5JW. Reporting to: Director of Research About Ataxia UK Ataxia is the umbrella term for a group of neurological conditions and Ataxia UK is the UK’s leading ataxia support and research charity. Ataxia UK collaborates with the global ataxia community through our Research team, and we are on the board of the international non-profit association, Euro-ataxia. Our Services team focuses on helping people affected by ataxia across the UK live well with their condition. Our Helpline and Advocacy services provide information, and one-to-one support on a range of issues, while our Community Engagement services deliver activities, events and volunteering opportunities that bring the ataxia community together and help reduce isolation. Job Description Research: The post-holder is expected to gain an understanding of the ataxias, keep updated with developments in the ataxia research area, and liaise effectively with researchers and other stakeholders. Research Grants Programme: Global collaborations: Research communication: Support for people with ataxia: Improving healthcare: To coordinate annual reviews of current Ataxia Centres, and accreditation reviews of new Ataxia Centres To coordinate the Ataxia Grand Rounds programme To manage the updating of Ataxia UK’s Medical Guidelines and similar publications To support the Director of Research in the development of new projects and policy work aimed at improving the healthcare of people with ataxia as required Other: Participate in supervision, and staff meetings as required Undertake professional development and training To manage the Research Communications Officer Comply with the data protection regulations, ensuring that information on clients, supporters, employees and volunteers remains confidential Implement Ataxia UK’s health and safety policy and procedures, ensuring that all practices and procedures are undertaken in accordance with a healthy and safe working environment and that all staff and volunteers for whom you may be responsible are aware of their responsibilities in respect of their role, monitoring data and recommending action as required Administer and organise own work to ensure that it is accurate and meets quality targets, agreed deadlines and reporting requirements Take responsibility for personal learning, training and development, and support the learning and development of others and the whole organisation Work to embed a culture of inclusion and collaboration, within and beyond Ataxia UK Note: This job description sets out the duties of the post at the time it was drawn up. item.title: Trusts & Foundations Fundraiser
item.description: Trusts & Foundations Fundraiser Bethlehem Care & Hospice Trust Salary: £34,000-£40,000 FTE, pro rata depending on experience | Hours: 14.8-18.5 hours per week (0.4-0.5 FTE) | Location: Home-based anywhere in the UK | Contract: 12 months initially, with a view to extension subject to funding and performance Help sustain Palestine's first and only licensed palliative care service Bethlehem Care & Hospice Trust (BCHT) is a small UK charity supporting the development of specialist palliative and hospice care in Palestine. In August 2023, the service we support became the first licensed palliative care service in Palestine. Since then, its specialist nurses have cared for more than 350 patients and their families and delivered more than 5,000 home visits. The service has demonstrated what can be achieved. Our challenge now is to secure its future. We are investing in professional fundraising for the first time and are looking for an experienced Trusts & Foundations Fundraiser to help us build the sustainable income needed to protect and strengthen this pioneering service. The opportunity This is an unusually autonomous role in which you will work directly with BCHT's Trustees and colleagues in Palestine. You will take responsibility for developing income from charitable trusts, foundations and grant-making organisations: identifying prospects, developing compelling propositions, preparing high-quality applications and building long-term funder relationships. We currently raise approximately £60,000-£80,000 each year against a core service requirement of around £150,000. Your initial focus will therefore be sustainability of the existing service, with opportunities subsequently to support its development and growth. Our Year 1 income target for this role is £70,000. This role could be for you if you have proven experience of successful trusts and foundations fundraising; can demonstrate success in preparing grant applications; write persuasively; can research and develop a strong prospect pipeline; are highly organised; can work independently; and would value the opportunity to use your professional expertise to make a direct and measurable difference. Experience of healthcare, hospice or palliative care, international development, small charities or faith-based organisations would be useful but is not essential. BCHT is inspired by Christian values of compassion, dignity and service. Applicants should be sympathetic to the values and mission of the charity. The palliative care service we support is provided to people regardless of faith, ethnicity, background or ability to pay. What we offer: flexible home-based working; 25 days' annual leave plus UK public/bank holidays, pro rata; and a workplace pension scheme with a 5% employer contribution, subject to scheme rules. You will have considerable scope to shape BCHT's approach to trusts and foundations fundraising and direct access to Trustees and decision-makers. To apply, please submit your CV and a covering letter of no more than two pages explaining why you are interested in the role and how your experience meets its requirements. Please download the Recruitment Pack for further information. Closing date: Friday 25 September 2026 | Interviews: Week commencing 5 October 2026 | Start: As soon as possible by agreement

item.title: IAA Adviser Level 2
item.description: About RSG: The Refugee Support Group was established in 1994 to address the pressing needs of refugees and asylum seekers in Reading. Over the years, RSG has evolved into a key player in the community, dedicated to upholding the rights and well-being of those seeking sanctuary. With a vision of creating a welcoming and inclusive Berkshire, RSG aims to ensure that every sanctuary seeker is embraced and valued within the community. Our mission focuses on providing comprehensive support and advocacy for refugees and asylum seekers, promoting their well-being, integration, and active participation in society. About the Role: The Level 2 IAA Adviser will provide high-quality, regulated immigration advice within a charity setting, supporting refugees, asylum seekers, migrants and other people facing immigration-related barriers. The postholder will manage a varied caseload within their authorised Immigration Advice Authority level and category, deliver accessible and compassionate advice, prepare applications and representations, and help clients understand their rights, options and next steps. The role will contribute to the charity’s mission to promote dignity, inclusion and access to justice for people who may be vulnerable, marginalised or unable to afford private legal advice. Essential Criteria: Provide IAA-immigration advice within the permitted scope of Level 2. Conduct sensitive and thorough client interviews, identify immigration issues, assess eligibility, and agree practical case strategies with clients. Prepare and submit immigration applications, write representations and submit supporting evidence. Draft clear advice letters that are accessible to clients. Support clients to understand Home Office processes, evidence requirements, deadlines, rights and responsibilities. Identify when matters fall outside Level 2 competence or the charity’s remit and make timely referrals. Maintain accurate, confidential and up-to-date case records in line with charity policies, data protection requirements, funder requirements and regulatory standards. Work sensitively with clients who may have experienced trauma, destitution and exploitation. Contribute to outreach, drop-in advice sessions, workshops or community-based advice activity where required. Build positive working relationships with partner organisations, community groups and local authorities. Keep up to date with immigration law, Home Office policy, IAA professional standards and relevant charity sector practice through continuing professional development. Desirable Criteria: Experience supporting refugees, asylum seekers, migrants or people with complex support needs. Knowledge of welfare, housing, safeguarding or community support pathways relevant to immigration clients. Experience delivering advice through outreach, drop-ins, community venues or partnership settings. Experience using case management systems and contributing to audit, quality assurance, monitoring or funder reporting. Language skills or experience working effectively with interpreters. Understanding of the voluntary and community sector, including grant-funded service delivery and impact reporting. Benefits: Annual leave (pro-rata where applicable): 25 days plus bank holidays. Additional day of leave added per year of employment (max 5 days) Pension: 6% employer contribution Employee Assistance Program (EAP): 24-hour confidential support line and access to counselling. Cycle to work scheme Annual Welfare Days Probation period: 6-months Interview Type: In-person / via Teams Opening date: 24th Aug 2026 Closing date: 28th Sep 2026 Our commitment to equity and safeguarding: Refugee Support Group is committed to equality, diversity, and inclusion and welcomes applications from people of all backgrounds. We particularly encourage applications from individuals with lived experience relevant to our work. item.title: Bishop's Chaplain in the Diocese of Southwell and Nottingham
item.description: The Diocese of Southwell & Nottingham has a vision of bringing God's Living Hope to the city, towns and villages of Nottinghamshire and is committed to its mission of Growing Disciples of Christ with Compassion, Confidence and Courage. A key aspect of that vision is the articulation of seven Areas of Focus that healthy churches attend to: Inspiring Worship, Reaching Younger, Enhancing Diversity, Growing Leaders, Enabling Commitment, Encouraging Generosity and Nurturing Prayer. Working closely with the Bishop of Southwell & Nottingham, this is an opportunity to join the Bishop's Office team, working with and for the bishop across the diocese in service of the Church's mission. Day to day, the Chaplain works closely with others to support the Bishop's public ministry, with key accountabilities for liturgical, pastoral and ministry support, as well as liaising with the Safeguarding Team and Registrar, and overseeing episcopal administration. The role also focuses on supporting the bishop's ministry in the areas of inspiring worship and nurturing prayer. We are looking for someone who brings theological wisdom, pastoral sensitivity, discretion, and sound judgement, alongside the ability to manage a varied and demanding workload, helping to sustain the Bishop's ministry in both strategic and personal ways. This role would suit someone who is prayerful, collaborative, and adaptable, and who is equally at ease supporting worship and ministry, working with senior colleagues in sensitive and sometimes complex matters. It offers an opportunity to combine spiritual maturity with practical leadership, with the growth of their own ministry under the Bishop's guidance. Responsibilities Liturgical, Pastoral and Ministry Support (30%) Oversee planning for key services across the diocese, including confirmations and institutions, maintain digital resources for churches and support the Bishop at these services as needed. On the Bishop's behalf, consult and advise Cathedral, incumbents and churchwardens on the planning and delivery of any service in which the Bishop plays a part, ensuring Orders of Service are signed off and accessible to the Bishop as appropriate. Discern the next season of support for 'Nurturing Prayer' at both diocesan and parish level, work in collaboration with the Discipleship & Ministry team to develop a strategic approach. As required, lead on the planning and delivery of activity. Support the worship and prayer life of key gatherings; such as Bishop's Council and Diocesan Synod, as well as other diocesan events. Assist the bishop in his teaching ministry as needed, research matters, attend key leadership training days, and support and contribute to the programme as appropriate. Take opportunities to lead and preach at services or teaching events at the invitation of parishes across the diocese. Advise on and provide bespoke prayers and liturgies, faithful to the Anglican tradition, for a variety of civic and ecclesiastical occasions. In collaboration with Bishop's Ecumenical Advisor and Churches Together Nottinghamshire (CTN) fulfil the role of Diocesan Ecumenical Officer (DEO) Safeguarding & Episcopal administration (35%) In conjunction with the Registry, advise on and ensure that clergy licences and Permissions to Officiate are administered in a timely and appropriate manner, in line with all requirements for Safer Recruitment and House of Bishops' policies. Ensure the Bishop's Office support parishes in their compliance with all legal requirements including in relation to the suspension of benefices and pastoral reorganisation, service provision and building usage. Oversee administration for C4 applications, the Overseas Clergy Measure and Eucharistic Assistants. Support the administration of the Clergy Discipline Measure and complaint and grievance procedures relating to clergy. Be the first point of contact in the Bishop's Office for safeguarding matters; liaise with the Diocesan Safeguarding Officer; and attend diocesan and national safeguarding planning group meetings on behalf of the bishop, where appropriate. Represent the diocesan bishop at the Diocesan Safeguarding Advisory Board (DSAP). Work with the Bishop's Office team to ensure the effective management of clergy files and processes, in line with the 2021 Clergy Files Policy Guidance, GDPR, and clergy appointments, including the accurate maintenance of the National Clergy Register. Work with the Bishop and Head of Staff & Strategic Projects in circulating key communications, including Pastoral Letters and Ad Clerum. Also ensure that existing Ad Clera are updated to reflect latest House of Bishops' practice guidance and policies. Respond to 'Bishop to Bishop' enquiries and Current Clergy Status Letters (CCSL) to provide reference requests as required. Oversees the work of the Senior Administrator in in managing effective administration of processes and use of data in relation to Ministers and Church Officers. Collective working (20%) Work closely with the Head of Staff & Strategic Projects in making recommendations and proposals to the Bishop on the effective management of key issues, which may arise. Work with the Head of Staff & Strategic Projects and the wider diocesan team to support communication of the bishop's ministry and missional priorities through diocesan communication channels and other public or parliamentary channels. Play an active role in the life of the Bishop Office team, working in collaboration with Advisory roles and as part of strategic projects as required. Help foster good communication and support between the diocese, the Bishop's staff and the Cathedral staff. Assist the Bishop and his wife in their personal ministry and mission, including significant hospitality events, leadership training or evangelistic outreach. Healthy cultures (15%) Attend to the spirituality and prayer that underpin the work of the Bishop's Core Team in sustaining momentum during a season of considerable growth and change. Be someone to whom the Bishop can turn and speak in confidence. Assist with the theological and pastoral dimensions of the Bishop's ministry, ensuring that pastoral concerns are redirected and followed up appropriately. Help protect the Bishop from the pressures of the present moment, guard his humanity, and ensure faithfulness to the wider vision of his ministry. The Chaplain will be expected to be a regular worshipper in a local congregation. Person Specification Ordained priest in the Church of England, with several years' experience in a post-ordination role. Some experience of working with Archdeacons, Area Deans and Parish oversight and governance. Some knowledge of Church of England's processes and procedures in relation to Clergy management and episcopal administration. Excellent knowledge of safeguarding, safeguarding leadership and Clergy Discipline Measure in order to support the Bishop. Theologically alert to situations that might arise, and able to prepare responses that reflect this. Aligned with the Bishop's priorities in order to support his ministry effectively, demonstrating this through all aspects of the role. A prayerful person, calm and effective in stressful and pressured situations. Enjoys collective working, providing leadership and support as required. Emotionally intelligent, able to respond to diverse situations with understanding and appreciation of those involved. Committed to the growth of their own ministry under the Bishop's guidance, with theological, teaching and pastoral interests. Willing and able to work flexibly, recognising that Church life does not fit normal office hours. You can expect to work some evenings and weekends, and to attend and participate in meetings and events. Creative skills in liturgy to lead diverse forms of worship. A commitment to growing disciples, evangelism and supporting church growth. Ability to nurture rhythms of prayer and worship for themselves and others. Digitally literate; a confident user of the Microsoft suite, databases and other applications. Excellent communication skills, verbal and written. Ability to represent the Bishop and provide pastoral support on his behalf. Ability to work to deadlines and manage a varied workload. Closing date: Monday 28 September 2026 Interviews: Thursday 8 October 2026

item.title: Head of Frontline Welfare and Wellbeing Services
item.description: Lead services that support those who serve on the frontline DMWS is seeking an experienced operational leader to develop and deliver high-quality services for blue light organisations and their workforces. This senior role combines strategic thinking, practical delivery, partnership building and strong project management. A key part of the role is bringing services together. You will work closely with DMWS welfare teams, psychological services and clinical governance colleagues to strengthen referrals, coordinate support pathways and ensure operational delivery is safe, responsive and well governed. What you will do · Lead operational plans, service performance, contracts, budgets and improvement activity. · Manage service mobilisations, pilots and improvement projects from scope through delivery, evaluation and handover. · Build effective working relationships across welfare, psychological, occupational health and partner services. · Coordinate cross-functional teams, project governance, milestones, risks, dependencies and reporting. · Strengthen relationships with military, blue light organisations, commissioners, public-sector partners, funders and suppliers. · Use evidence, outcomes and feedback to improve services, demonstrate impact and create opportunities for sustainable growth. · Lead and develop staff while maintaining high standards of governance, safeguarding and compliance. What you will bring · Senior operational leadership experience in a complex service environment. · Strong project or programme management skills and a track record of delivering change. · Credibility with varied stakeholders and the ability to work effectively across professional boundaries. · An understanding of welfare, wellbeing and psychological support pathways and the importance of clear clinical and safeguarding escalation. · Commercial awareness, sound financial judgement and a commitment to quality and value for money. · A collaborative, evidence-led and values-driven approach. Why join DMWS? This is an opportunity to shape a growing area of work, strengthen integrated support for military Services, blue light communities and help DMWS turn trusted expertise into sustainable, high-impact services across the UK. This role is progressive and offers the right candidate an opportunity How to apply Please submit your CV and a supporting statement explaining how your experience meets the requirements of the role by 28th September 2026. Applicants must hold a full UK Driving Licence and have access to a vehicle which is required for this role. DMWS is committed to equality, diversity and inclusion and welcomes applications from people of all backgrounds.

item.title: Advice Programme Manager (IAA Level 3)
item.description: Job description About RSG: The Refugee Support Group was established in 1994 to address the pressing needs of refugees and asylum seekers in Reading. Over the years, RSG has evolved into a key player in the community, dedicated to upholding the rights and well-being of those seeking sanctuary. With a vision of creating a welcoming and inclusive Berkshire, RSG aims to ensure that every sanctuary seeker is embraced and valued within the community. Our mission focuses on providing comprehensive support and advocacy for refugees and asylum seekers, promoting their well-being, integration, and active participation in society. About the Role: The successful candidate will lead and oversee the organisation’s advice service, ensuring compliance with Immigration Advice Authority (IAA) standards and deliver high-quality casework support across asylum, protection, and immigration matters. The postholder will supervise advisers and volunteers, manage complex immigration and asylum cases, maintain regulatory compliance, and contribute to the strategic development of the organisation’s services. We are only considering applicants with relevant legal experience. Qualifications needed are either o IAA Level 3 o IAAS Level 2 Supervising Senior Caseworker Key Responsibilities: Advice: Provide Immigration Advice Authority (IAA) Level 1 & 2 advice in asylum, protection, and immigration. Manage a personal caseload of asylum and immigration cases. Ensure clients receive accurate, timely, and trauma-informed advice. Adhere to and further develop casework procedures as outlined in the casework manual and the IAA code of standards. Advocate on behalf of clients and refer to other agencies as appropriate. Maintain comprehensive records on the case management system. Work with colleagues across the organisation to ensure a high-quality service. Consider and develop sustainable funding options such as a fee-charging service or a legal aid contract. Service Management: Lead the day-to-day delivery of the advice service. Ensure compliance with IAA standards, policies, and audit requirements. Develop and maintain effective case management systems and file reviews. Monitor service quality, outcomes, and performance targets. Support organisational reporting and funder requirements. Supervision & Leadership: Supervise and support advisers, caseworkers, interns, and volunteers. Provide mentoring, training, and quality assurance for casework staff and volunteers. Identify and implement staff development and training needs. Promote a collaborative and inclusive team culture. Partnerships & Advocacy: Build positive relationships with external partners, legal aid firms, local authorities, and community organisations. Advocate for clients’ rights and access to services with statutory agencies and other organisations. Attend and be part of relevant networks, meetings, and forums. General: Promote the aims and abide by RSG policies and procedures. Always have due regard in the planning and execution of duties to RSG. Carry out any other related tasks as required by the RSG management team and Trustees. Abide by health and safety guidelines and share responsibility for your own safety and that of colleagues. Undertake such duties as may be identified as generally compatible with the functions of the post. Essential Criteria: Current Immigration Advice Authority (IAA) Level 3 accreditation or IAAS Level 2 Supervising Senior Caseworker accreditation with significant years of experience in asylum and immigration legal casework. 4-years’ experience managing an advice team. Expert knowledge of UK immigration and asylum law. Experience supervising staff, volunteers, and advisers. Ability to manage sensitive cases independently without supervision. Excellent written and verbal communication skills. Excellent organisational and case management skills. Commitment to the rights and wellbeing of refugees and asylum seekers. Ability to work effectively in a small charity. Ability to work from the office. Desirable Criteria: Experience working within the voluntary sector. Experience working within the refugee sector. Experience of legal aid or funded immigration services. Knowledge of safeguarding and trauma-informed practice. Ability to speak more than one relevant language. Values & Behaviours: The successful candidate will demonstrate: Compassion and empathy Professional integrity Cultural sensitivity Accountability Collaborative working Commitment to social justice and equality Additional Information: Enhanced DBS check will be required. The role may involve occasional evening or community outreach work. Ongoing training and CPD will be supported. Benefits: Annual leave: 25 days plus bank holidays. Additional day of leave added per year of employment (max 5days) Pension: 6% employer contribution Employee Assistance Program (EAP): 24-hour confidential support line and access to counselling. Cycle to work scheme Annual Welfare Days Probation period: 6-months Interview Type: In-person Starting Date: Immediate start possible Opening date : 24th Aug 2026 Closing date: 28th Sep 2026 Our commitment to equity and safeguarding: Refugee Support Group is committed to equality, diversity, and inclusion and welcomes applications from people of all backgrounds. We particularly encourage applications from individuals with lived experience relevant to our work. Posted on: 02 September 2026 Closing date: 28 September 2026 at 23:30 Tags: Advice / Information, Training / Learning, Advocacy, Volunteering Management, Compliance / Quality, Data Protection, Database Management, Health and Safety, Partnerships, Refugee / Immigration, Safeguarding, Governance / Management

item.title: HR & Office Coordinator
item.description: We're looking for an organised and proactive HR & Office Coordinator to support the smooth running of our people processes and office environment. This is a varied role that would suit someone who enjoys working across HR administration, recruitment, compliance and office coordination in a small organisation. As a close-knit team of around 30 staff (18 FTE), this role offers a broad range of responsibilities and the opportunity to be involved in many aspects of organisational life. Much of the role centres on coordination, administration and maintaining effective systems and processes, helping to ensure colleagues have the support they need to work effectively. About the role Working closely with managers and colleagues across the organisation, you will play a key role in supporting our people, maintaining compliance and helping our office environment run smoothly. Key responsibilities include: Coordinating HR administration throughout the employee lifecycle, including onboarding, probation monitoring, employee records and contractual changes. Supporting recruitment activity, including advertising vacancies, arranging interviews, coordinating pre-employment checks and communicating with candidates. Maintaining accurate HR, safeguarding and compliance records and supporting organisational reporting requirements. Providing first-line support on HR processes and policies, escalating more complex matters where appropriate. Supporting health and safety, data protection and compliance activities through effective administration and record keeping. Coordinating office administration, supplies, room bookings and relationships with external providers. Helping to improve processes and systems while ensuring colleagues have the information and support they need. About you We're looking for someone who: Has experience in HR administration, recruitment, office management or a similar business support role. Is highly organised and able to manage a varied workload effectively. Has excellent attention to detail and is comfortable working with confidential information. Has strong written and verbal communication skills and enjoys building positive working relationships Is confident using Microsoft 365 and organisational systems. Is proactive, approachable and enjoys working as part of a small, collaborative team. Experience of HR systems, office coordination, compliance administration or working in the charity, education, social care or public sectors would be beneficial but is not essential. Why join CCS Adoption? This is an opportunity to join a supportive organisation where your contribution will have a genuine impact. As a small team, we value collaboration, flexibility and a shared commitment to improving outcomes for children and families through adoption. In return, we offer: Flexible working arrangements. Hybrid working. A supportive and friendly team culture. Opportunities to develop your skills across HR, recruitment, compliance and organisational support. Meaningful work that helps support children, families and communities. If you're an organised and motivated administrator who enjoys variety and wants to make a difference, we'd love to hear from you. Anyone joining the CCS team is subject to our safe recruitment and pre-appointment checks. This includes providing documentation to evidence the right to work in the UK, a Disclosure and Barring Service (DBS) check and written and telephone references.

item.title: Charity Shop Manager
item.description: Job description We are seeking an experienced and dynamic Shop Manager to oversee the daily operations of our RSPCA Surrey East charity shop in Redhill. You will take full day-to-day ownership of the store, driving retail sales, recruiting and inspiring volunteers, and leading community engagement to generate vital funds for local animal welfare. Key Tasks/Job Description Shop Operations Manage all aspects of the charity shop, including staff and volunteer management, stock management, merchandising, and financial procedures. To meet the agreed sales targets and ensure that direct costs are kept to a minimum Ensure that the shop and window presentation standards meet our Branch vision, including the rotation of goods, window displays and promotional activities Ensure the appropriate standards of cleanliness are maintained throughout the shop Be proactive in the generation of donated stock, managing stock collection efficiently and effectively in accordance with Branch & Society guidelines Ensure trading hours are strictly adhered to Process donated stock to the agreed standards and timescale Ensure all financial management, cash handling, daily banking and security procedures are followed Ensure all relevant administration is completed within the agreed timescales Manage the sales and administration of any bought-in (i.e. new) goods Manage the sale of goods online. Property Assume overall responsibility for the shop premises, including key holding Ensure compliance with the branch’s health and safety policy (including fire safety, risk assessments and security procedures) and relevant legislation People/Line Management Recruit, train, manage and support staff & volunteers while adhering to the agreed Branch standards, policies and relevant legal legislation Complete annual appraisals, including the setting of targets for shop staff within the agreed timescales, and conduct regular one-to-one review meetings with staff Ensure that the level of volunteers is sufficient to operate an effective charity shop operation Complete relevant training for volunteers and ensure volunteers feel included and motivated Ensure that appropriate HR policies and procedures are adhered to in compliance with the relevant employment legislation and branch employment policies and procedures, seeking guidance from the Branch Manager as required General Actively promote all Branch & Society initiatives and campaigns to promote awareness of the charity Ensure high levels of customer service are maintained Build and develop positive internal and external relationships to ensure maximum income for the charity Promote the shop in the local area using all available promotional opportunities (subject to any Branch rules for communication with the media) To carry out such other tasks as directed by the Branch Manager Branch Policies Adhere to the Branch’s charitable objectives. Fully comply with RSPCA Surrey East Branch’s procedures, ensuring these are carried out in relation to the post. To be an ambassador for the Branch and professionally represent the Charity at all times. Health And Safety While at work, all staff are required to: Take care of their own health and safety and that of others who may be affected by their acts and omissions. Co-operate with Branch health and safety policies and procedures. Ensure, so far as is reasonably practicable, the health, safety and well-being of their staff, volunteers and others who may be affected by branch activities Knowledge, skill and experience ______________________________________________________________ EDUCATION & TRAINING Essential Good general level of education, at least to GCSE standard or equivalent Desirable Retail management qualification EXPERIENCE Essential Comprehensive retail management experience Proven line management experience Experience of managing budgets and accounts Experience of handling difficult people management issues Experience of cash handling and financial management procedures (including completion of sales records) Desirable Charity retail management experience Fashion retail experience Experience of recruiting and working with groups of volunteers Training, coaching and mentoring skills SKILLS AND COMPETENCIES Essential Excellent communication skills both written and oral Excellent organisational skills, with an ability to follow procedures and pay attention to detail. Computer literate Ability to motivate and influence others Ability to prioritise workload, balancing competing demands Ability to meet tight deadlines Knowledge of health and safety legislation Desirable Understanding of charity law PERSONAL QUALITIES Essential Sympathy with the RSPCA’s aims and policies A proven leader with drive and enthusiasm Calm under pressure Resilient in the face of setbacks Ability to relate well to people from all backgrounds Honest, trustworthy and reliable Desirable Ability to be flexible when working with volunteers, willing to seek compromise rather than the “perfect solution” Willingness to learn and acquire new skills through training and development SPECIAL CIRCUMSTANCES Essential Willing and able to work longer than the contracted hours on occasion, when the job demands Desirable Full valid UK Driving licence _____________________________________________________________ Additional Duties To foster the highest standards of performance, discipline, honesty, and integrity from Branch staff and volunteers. To maintain and cultivate a culture where everyone is valued, respected and equipped to do their job. To carry out such additional or other duties of a reasonable nature as directed by the Branch Manager from time to time, in consultation with the post holder, to meet the needs of the Branch. Review The main responsibilities of this job will be reviewed on a regular basis in conjunction with the post holder to comply with agreed Branch Strategies and operational needs. Job Context The Branch Shop Manager plays an important role in driving the performance of the charity shop and guiding staff and volunteers to meet the shop’s targets. Posted on: 02 September 2026 Closing date: 23 September 2026 at 18:01 Tags: Retail / Sales, Volunteering Management, Customer Service, Environment / Animal, Fashion The client requests no contact from agencies or media sales.

item.title: Senior Programme Officer
item.description: We’re delighted to be recruiting a full-time Senior Programme Officer to join GoodWork in November 2026. You’ll be a senior member of our growing programmes team, working to manage the delivery of high-quality employability programmes. GoodWork is a youth employment and social mobility charity, creating fairer opportunities for young people from lower socioeconomic backgrounds. Founded in 2022, we’re a fast-growing organisation with real impact and big ambitions to drive systemic change for the community we serve. Key Info Full time, 37.5 hours per week. Starting in November 2026, with some flexibility depending on candidate notice periods. Salary: £35,880 with 4% employer pension contribution. Hybrid (London), 3 days a week in-person with the team at GoodWork HQ, Warren Street. 25 days holiday per year, plus Bank Holidays and additional leave during our annual Winter Break between Christmas and New Year. Appointment is subject to Enhanced DBS Check. GoodWork operates in line with safe recruitment practices and adherence to our Safeguarding Policy is essential. We are unable to sponsor visas; applicants must have the right to work in the UK. About the role We’re looking for a Senior Programme Officer to join our team, taking ownership of programme delivery while also building the systems and structures that help our programmes grow. You’ll join as a senior member of our programmes team, taking a leadership role across our programme design and delivery, as well as contributing to the strategic direction of our work with young people. You’ll report to our Programme Manager. This role will involve: Programme Management You’ll take ownership of end-to-end delivery across multiple programmes, managing recruitment, onboarding and logistics. You’ll independently scope, plan and deliver programmes, setting clear milestones and flagging early where timelines or expectations need to shift. You’ll recruit, onboard and manage volunteers, ensuring we deliver a great volunteer experience and maximising impact for our young people. You’ll work with our Programme Manager to scope and deliver strategic projects across the programmes team, using data, feedback and learning to improve our programmes over time and looking for opportunities to strengthen our systems, processes and quality. Programme Delivery You’ll provide 1:1 support to young people, checking in on their progress and goals, and offering advice, support and accountability throughout their journey. You’ll design and deliver training for young people, alongside information sessions and training for our corporate partners and volunteers. This will include taking ownership of specific content areas, and supporting more junior team members to build confidence and consistency in facilitation. You’ll uphold a rigorous approach to safeguarding, making sure the welfare of the young people we support is prioritised throughout our work. Stakeholder Engagement You’ll lead stakeholder engagement at all levels, from scheduling volunteering days with corporate partners, to checking in with employer partners on how young people are progressing in their roles. You’ll support youth engagement and outreach activity where needed. Team Contribution and Leadership You’ll line manage up to two members of the programmes team, holding regular check-ins, providing feedback, and supporting their goal-setting, development and retention. You’ll develop others through mentorship, guidance and feedback, particularly in areas where you have stronger knowledge or experience. You’ll support hiring, onboarding and training as the team grows. You’ll help shape the organisation for the future, sharing feedback and ideas, and researching, proposing and testing new approaches that support team and organisational learning. What we're looking for We’re especially interested in candidates with demonstrable experience owning programme delivery and managing others, alongside strengths in areas like curriculum development, volunteer management, or monitoring and evaluation. You don’t need to have worked in youth employment or the charity sector before, but a commitment to our mission and good understanding of the barriers to work faced by young people from low-income backgrounds is essential. This is an experienced hire role, and we’re looking for someone with solid professional experience, including some prior experience managing or mentoring others, who can apply sound judgement and hold real ownership in a fast-moving environment. You don’t need to have a degree. Programme ownership and delivery. You have a track record of independently planning and delivering a programme or project end-to-end, setting your own milestones and adapting when timelines or expectations shift. You’re comfortable managing multiple priorities at once, and delivering to a high standard in a fast-paced environment. Line management and development of others. You’ve supported someone else’s development directly - through formal line management or informal mentoring - holding check-ins, giving constructive feedback, and helping them grow. You’re someone others can turn to when they need guidance, particularly in areas where you have stronger knowledge or experience. Strategic thinking and problem solving. You can think creatively, spot where a system, process or piece of delivery isn’t working, and take the initiative to improve it. You respond positively when things don’t go to plan, and can manage both the day-to-day detail and the bigger picture. Communication and facilitation. You have excellent written and verbal communication skills, with good attention to detail. You’re confident facilitating workshops and delivering training yourself, and able to help less experienced colleagues build their own confidence in the room. Relationship building. You’re comfortable building relationships with a wide range of people, including partners and volunteers, and representing the organisation in a warm and professional way. You’re able to build trusting relationships with young people. You approach others with empathy, warmth and good judgement. Resilience and a growth mindset. You can operate well in uncertainty, learn as you go, and stay motivated through challenges. Adaptability and perseverance are crucial to the success of the young people on our programme, and it’s important that our team models these behaviours too. We work with a diverse group of young people from underserved communities. We encourage applications from candidates from minoritised ethnic backgrounds, and those who have lived experience relevant to our programme - particularly non-graduates and those from lower socioeconomic backgrounds. How we work We’re a small but fast-growing team. You’ll join our staff team (and office dog, Annie) working day-to-day in the business, but will also engage with young people, our funders and partners, our Board, and many of the amazing volunteers who help us deliver our programme. We use Slack, Notion and Claude day-to-day to keep in touch and support our work across the team. Our team works together in-person at least three days a week at GoodWork HQ, our beautiful space on Warren Street in central London where we host events, deliver training and work with our community. You’ll need to be able to attend occasional in-person events, including possible evening sessions for which time off in lieu will be given. You should also expect to attend regular in-person meetings with our London-based partners. Life at GoodWork Making GoodWork a great place to work is hugely important to us, and as a small charity we’re continuously working to improve our offer. For now, our team benefits from: Personal training budget to invest as you’d like, as well as access to more in-person and online training through our membership of London Youth and the Charity Learning Consortium Access to individual coaching to support professional development with qualified coaches, through our corporate partners Quarterly official team socials and ad hoc team social activities, recent highlights have included a team Iftar, pottery painting, a Monopoly Deal and Pizza Night and team crafting lunchtime Access to our Employee Assistance Programme with Health Assured Enhanced Maternity and Shared Parental Leave, after a year’s service A dog-friendly office 🐶 The option to work up to two weeks a year ‘super remote’ (from anywhere) A values and mission driven team (find out more about our values on our website) and the opportunity to be part of shaping a rapidly growing organisation Application process Apply by 9am on Monday 21 September 2026 . You’ll need to submit a CV of no more than two pages and answer the following questions* in no more than 1,700 characters (about 250 words) each. Why are you a good fit for this role? Please tell us about your relevant personal and/or professional experience. Why do you want to work for GoodWork? Shortlisted candidates will be invited to a 40 minute online interview with Zoë, Programme Manager, and Sajni, Partnerships and Development Manager, between 28-29 September. The final stage will involve a task and in-person interview with Felicity, CEO, and Zoë at our offices on 12 October . If you get to this stage, you’ll be reimbursed for your time. An offer will be made subject to referencing and satisfactory completion of an Enhanced DBS check. The successful candidate will start as soon as possible - ideally in mid-November - dependent on any notice periods in their existing role. If you require adjustments to this process, please let us know by emailing us as soon as possible. * Please note: answers that have obviously been AI generated, with little personalisation to relevant skills, experience and motivations, will be immediately screened out. You’re welcome to use AI to support your application, but we want to hear your answers in your voice.

item.title: Centre Manager
item.description: Centre Manager Norbrook Youth Centre, Bordley Walk, Wythenshawe, Manchester M23 0AR Grade 6 Point 20 – 25, £30,750 - £34,303. (Full Time 35 hours, Permanent) Introduction Greater Manchester Youth Federation (GMYF) is a long-established charity running vibrant youth centres across Greater Manchester. We are dedicated to raising aspirations and creating opportunities for children and young people, particularly those facing disadvantage. Our work is rooted in youth voice, inclusion, strong relationships, and high-quality youth work practice that supports young people to develop confidence, resilience, and skills for life. GMYF also delivers outdoor education and residential experiences, including provision at Ormside Mill in Cumbria and other residential settings nationwide, as part of its wider youth work offer, working across teams to ensure young people benefit from safe, inclusive, and developmental opportunities beyond their local communities. Purpose of Role: The Centre Manager provides strategic and operational leadership for the youth centre and its wider community reach, with responsibility for high-quality youth work delivery and day to day centre operations, working within GMYF’s wider operational ad estates frameworks. high-quality, inclusive local provision. The postholder is the professional lead for youth work practice and delivery within the centre, with responsibility for shaping, developing, and continuously improving provision in line with GMYF’s values, safeguarding standards, and strategic priorities. Reporting to the Director of Programmes, the Centre manager leads people, partnerships, and placebased development, ensuring the centre delivers strong outcomes for children and young people while contributing to the wider aims of GMYF. Outdoor Education and residential opportunities are an integral and embedded part of the centre’s youth work offer, and the Centre Manager plays a key role in shaping, embedding, and developing these opportunities in partnership with the Outdoor Education Team to ensure they meet the local need and are accessible to young people. This is a hands-on leadership role, balancing operational oversight with visible presence, relationship based practice, and continuous improvement. Key Responsibilities: Leadership and Management of Youth Work Delivery Provide strategic leadership for youth work delivery at centre level, including centre-based provision, outreach, and integrated Outdoor Education and residential opportunities, ensuring provision is planned, resourced and developed in response to local need, youth voice, and GMYF priorities. Provide clear professional leadership for high quality, inclusive youth work across centre based provision, outreach, offsite venues, and outdoor education youth work. Embed and champion GMYF’s youth work values, including youth voice, equality, diversity, and inclusion. Line manage staff including Youth Work Coordinator(s), Youth Workers, cleaners, and volunteers. Provide supervision, appraisal, and performance management, promoting reflective practice and professional development. Ensure staffing structures, rotas, and skills mix support safe, effective delivery. Foster a positive, professional, and supportive team culture. Safety, Safeguarding and Compliance Act as a Deputy Designated Safeguarding Lead. Hold overall safeguarding responsibility for the centre and linked activities. Ensure safeguarding procedures are embedded, understood, and consistently applied. Promote inclusive, restorative and trauma informed practice. Ensure all safeguarding and behaviour related incidents are recorded, reviewed, and followed up. Maintain compliance with legislation, statutory guidance, and GMYF policies. Centre Operations, Site Management and Health & Safety The Centre Manager holds responsibility for day-to-day site oversight and compliance, with additional estates support provided through GMYF’s central operations arrangements. Ensure the centre meets all Health & Safety and statutory requirements, working with GMYF’s Central Team and systems to maintain compliance. Oversee day-to-day site issues, Planned Preventative Maintenance (PPM), compliance checks, and inspections, escalating and co-ordinating works as required through organisational processes. Maintain oversight of building safety, security, and use of space. Ensure accurate records are maintained for staff, visitors, and young people. Ensure all off site activities, outreach, visits, and residentials are risk assessed and appropriately staffed. Hold overall responsibility for the safe opening and closing of the centre and the planning and oversight of fire, evacuation, and lockdown procedures, delegating operational leadership as appropriate when not on site Maintain good relations with neighbours and the local community. Quality, Development and Partnership Working Lead centre-level self evaluation and contribute to GMYF organisational development and quality frameworks. Monitor outcomes for children and young people and use learning to improve provision. Contribute to funding bids, monitoring, and reporting. Develop and maintain partnerships with stakeholders including schools, community organisations, statutory services, and internal teams to support joined-up opportunities for young people. Represent the centre in organisational initiatives and networks. Outdoor Education and Residential Provision Hold responsibility for pastoral leadership of young people accessing Outdoor Education provision linked to the centre, while the Outdoor Education Team is responsible for developing and providing outdoor education opportunities. Work collaboratively with the Outdoor Education Team to plan high-quality residentials and Outdoor Activities for the young people from the centre. Ensure good pastoral and wellbeing leadership before, during, and after residentials. Act as Group Leader and drive the minibus where required and appropriate, in line with compliance regulations. Lead reflective reviews following residentials and outdoor education activity. Professional Conduct and Organisational Responsibilities Uphold GMYF’s values, policies, and professional standards. Ensure conduct reflects the responsibilities of a leadership and management role. Maintain a strong commitment to continuous professional development and reflective leadership practice, using supervision, learning, and organisational feedback to enhance personal effectiveness and support high-quality youth work delivery. Contribute positively to the wider culture and strategic development of GMYF. Undertake other duties commensurate with the role. Person Specification Essential Criteria Qualifications & Professional Development Relevant qualification in Youth Work OR significant experience delivering youth work or related children and young people’s provision Commitment to continuous professional development (CPD) and reflective leadership practice Willingness to undertake further relevant professional or leadership qualifications and development as required Experience Experience delivering youth work or similar provision in a centre based, community, or outreach setting Experience supporting, supervising, or coordinating staff and/or volunteers. Experience working within safeguarding frameworks, including recording concerns and escalating appropriately Experience working with children and young people facing additional barriers to participation (e.g. SEND, trauma, disadvantage) Experience contributing to the planning, delivery, or improvement of provision, balancing operational delivery with quality and learning Knowledge & Skills Sound understanding of safeguarding, risk management, and inclusive practice within youth or community settings Ability to promote positive behaviour cultures using restorative and trauma informed approaches. Ability to provide clear professional direction and guidance to team and colleagues Strong communication and interpersonal skills, adaptable to young people, families, partners, and professionals Ability to oversee the safe delivery of centre based, outreach, and off site activities Ability to maintain accurate records and contribute to reports and organisational learning Competence in using IT systems to support communication, administration and service delivery Leadership & Personal Attributes Ability to provide visible, values-led leadership within a busy operational environment Sound judgement and confidence in decision-making, with appropriate use of supervision, escalation and advice Ability to work collaboratively within a wider organisational structure and across internal teams Strong commitment to equality, diversity, safeguarding, and young person-centred practice Resilience, adaptability, and the ability to manage competing priorities and pressures Additional Requirements Willingness to work flexibly, including evenings and occasional weekends Willingness to complete required training (e.g. First Aid, safeguarding, fire safety) within agreed timescales Enhanced DBS check Desirable Criteria Degree level qualification in Youth Work Leadership or management qualification, or experience of leading teams in a youth work setting Experience contributing to funding bids, monitoring, evaluation, or reporting processes Experience leading or contributing to centre self evaluation or quality assurance frameworks Experience working in partnership with schools, local services, or community organisations Other requirements GMYF is committed to safeguarding and promoting the welfare of children and young people. An Enhanced DBS is required for this post. We welcome applicants from all backgrounds. This is a UK-based post and applicants must be living in and have the right to work in the UK. If applicable, please detail your Visa status in your covering email. Please let us know if you need us to make any reasonable adjustments during the application or recruitment process and we’ll be happy to support

item.title: Senior Marketing and Relationship Officer
item.description: We are seeking a proactive and relationship-focused Senior Marketing and Relationships Officer to help grow membership of the HIV Confident Charter Mark. The postholder will work to generate interest with prospective member organisations and clearly communicate the value of the programme, resulting in tangible growth in memberships. They will use their experience in targeted marketing activity, stakeholder engagement and relationship management to nurture relationships with current and emerging networks. In this role, the postholder will demonstrate visible commitment to tackling HIV stigma, improving inclusion and supporting good practice in workplaces. If you can see yourself contributing to this mission, we’d love to hear from you. Diversity and inclusion National AIDS Trust is committed to becoming a diverse and inclusive organisation. We strive to create a workplace that represents our mission and the people we serve, and where all voices are valued and heard. To reflect this, we actively encourage applications from people of all backgrounds, regardless of age, race, gender, sexual orientation, physical ability, disability or religion. As the UK’s HIV rights charity, we particularly encourage applications from those with an understanding of the issues faced by people living with HIV. At National AIDS Trust, we would like our application process to be as accessible as possible. Please speak to us about any reasonable adjustments that you might require throughout the interview process or the role.

item.title: Head of Children and Family Services
item.description: Mind In Enfield and Barnet combines over 50 years of experience to improve peoples mental health in Enfield, Barnet and beyond. We are led by lived experience and driven by a passion to support and protect people’s mental health in ways that they want. The Head of Families and Children’s Services will provide senior leadership and strategic direction across services that support families, parents, children, and young people. The role will ensure delivery of high-quality, evidence-based interventions that promote wellbeing, strengthen family resilience, and safeguard vulnerable children. This postholder will oversee Perinatal Coaching, Crisis Outreach, Family Hubs, and Parenting Programs, embedding a culture of excellence, innovation, and partnership working to achieve meaningful outcomes for families. This is a part-time position across 21 hours per week, (Monday to Friday 9-5). Based at Head Office in Fore Street, Edmonton N9 0PD Please see full attached job description.

item.title: Finance Co-ordinator
item.description: About Us Young Life International is a fast-growing Christian charitable organisation. Our aim is to share the message of Jesus with young people all over the UK. We do this through building relationships with them and earning the right to be heard. Our Operations team strives to help our staff and volunteers to thrive by anticipating, developing and delivering excellent operational services and our Finance team focuses specifically on providing excellent financial services in a Christ-centred way. About the Role As the Finance Co-ordinator you will build good relationships with the wider staff team and be a friendly and knowledgeable source of advice for all queries relating to finance. As a key member of the team, you will be the primary user of many existing processes, and will be the key person in implementing new systems we are planning to enable us to be more efficient. You thrive on knowing you are using both your numerical and organisational skills and your relational skills to support others. More Details and How to Apply Download the Application Pack for the following information: Welcome from the Operations Director How this role fits into the wider YLI and Operations Team Full Job Description and Person Specification Details of how to apply online (application form) Deadline and interview dates YLI Faith and Conduct Policies - check we're in alignment with one another's beliefs Accessibility & Support We want to ensure our recruitment process is accessible to everyone. If you require any reasonable adjustments or accommodations at any stage of the application or interview process, please let us know. You can reach out to us in confidence at the email in our application pack, and we will be happy to support you. We care about your data privacy - to find out more please visit our website to view our Privacy Policy.
