item.title: IPS Employment Advisor
item.description: About Working Well Trust Working Well Trust is a mental health and employment charity in London. All of our projects share the aim of improving the lives of people with mental health support needs, learning disabilities and/or complex issues through training and employment. We are expanding our team of IPS Employment Advisors in our IPS service in the London Borough of Enfield . You will be based in one of NHS mental health treatment teams in Enfield Town and Edmonton areas. This IPS service at Working Well Trust has been awarded the IPS Grow quality mark and adheres to the principles of the IPS model in supporting people in to employment. This role will be working with clients who have mental health support needs, wanting to gain and sustain paid employment. Experience of employment support is not essential, it is more important that you share our passion and commitment to employment as an integral aspect of wellbeing and supporting people to find the right job for them. You will receive training on the IPS model and in supporting people with mental health issues. We welcome applications from people with lived experience of mental health, either personally or through a close contact. You need to have a desire to support people to achieve their employment goals, and the ability to multitask and manage your workload effectively. Good organisation skills are essential for this role, in addition to an interest in mental health, and the role it plays in the workplace. The successful candidate will need to become comfortable in approaching employers, and showcase the advantages of our service in order to work with them to recruit our clients to fill vacancies and sustain employment. This is a part time post working 17.5 hours, please note salary listed is FTE. What you’ll be doing You will work with clients (managing a caseload) who have mental health support needs, to assist them in securing sustainable paid employment in line with their preferences. You will deliver the IPSapproach (for which training will be given); providing person centred support and guidance to clients, whilst building positive relationships with local employers to enable clients to move into suitable employment. You will work as part of a mental health team (NHS Trust) maintaining positive and integrated relationships, fostering a holistic approach to recovery through employment. You will work closely with clinical teams, providing a coordinated approach thatalways remainsclient led. You will be based at one of the following NHS mental health treatment teams: Enfield's Early Intervention in Psychosis (EIP) service, Lucas House Edmonton Community Rehabilitation Team Enfield, Park Avenue, Enfield Town You will spend up to 65% of your week working in the community of Enfield to provide localised support to residents of the Borough. You will also be working to contract targets whilst maintaining a high-quality service. What you’ll need Experience in employment support is not essential. We are looking for someone who brings: A genuine desire to support people into meaningful employment. Commitment to person-centred work and either experience of or enthusiasm to learn the IPS approach. Confidence engaging with employers and promoting the benefits of our service. Good organisation skills and the ability to manage a caseload effectively. Beneficial (but not essential): experience working with people with mental health difficulties. Beneficial (but not essential): local knowledge/ experience of the Borough What we offer £33,000 per year (FTE) 30 days annual leave plus public holidays, (FTE) Employer pension contribution of 6% Supportive environment within a growing, dedicated team Meaningful, rewarding work supporting people into employment Expenses paid for mandatory travel during work hours. Flexible, paid Wellbeing Hour every fortnight (FTE) What’s next Before you apply, please note the following: We actively recruit and carefully review all applications. Due to rapid service expansion, we have onboarded 20 external hires in the last six months. To ensure we can best support the people and communities we serve, we progress applications only where candidates provide meaningful answers to the screening questions. Career development is real here : in the past year, 10 colleagues have progressed internally into Senior roles, Project Lead, Team Lead, and Operations Manager positions. We value ambition and celebrate progression. If you require any reasonable adjustments at the interview stage, for example due to a disability, learning difficulty or health condition, please let us know in advance so that we can make appropriate arrangements. Working Well Trust is an equal opportunities employer and Confident about Disabilities. If you are ready to help us build a service that supports people into meaningful work, click Apply to submit your CV and answer the screening questions. Start your application today and take the next step in a rewarding career. Closing date: Wednesday 30th September 2026 (09:00) . Please note, we may be actively interviewing during this time and may close the vacancy early. First stage interviews: 5th - 9th October 2026 (subject to change if advert closes early) Final Stage interviews (in person in Edmonton): w/c 12th October 2026 (subject to change if advert closes early) Considerations: Please note: This post involves access to NHS clinical records through RiO. For confidentiality, information-governance and wellbeing reasons, successful candidates cannot be appointed within the same secondary mental health service area in which they are currently receiving care. We will not ask applicants to disclose health information during the application or interview process. A confidential service-location conflict check will only take place following a conditional offer. Where a conflict is identified, we may explore an equivalent vacancy in another area, but alternative employment cannot be guaranteed.

item.title: The FA Independent Mental Health Expert Panel
item.description: Our Organisation The Football Association (The FA) is the governing body of football in England. We are responsible for promoting and developing the game at all levels; from grassroots through to the professional game, The FA Cup and the England Teams, and we have two world class assets: Wembley Stadium and St. George's Park. Our vision is to inspire positive change through football; our national game that breaks down barriers and unites people from very different backgrounds. Today, we are the governing body of a national community that includes more than 15.7 million football participants, almost 30 million fans and more than 90,000 grassroots teams. At The FA mental health and wellbeing is a core enabler of everything we do, personally and professionally, on the field and off the field, in how we perform, deliver, and navigate the world around us. The Role As an organisation we are increasingly responding to a range of complex mental health related cases that often involve ethical, psychosocial, and occupational challenges that impact individuals as well as presenting, in some cases, increased organisational risk. As we continue to evolve our internal support structures, we recognise the value that an independent expert panel will bring. The purpose of the Independent Mental Health Expert Panel (IMHEP) is to bring together specialists to provide independent multidisciplinary oversight, consultation, reflective supervision and expert guidance regarding complex mental health cases. The focus of the panel is to support our internal workforce of c.1000 colleagues, for whom we have a duty of care to support and protect mental health and wellbeing. We are looking for individuals with a strong passion for delivering human centred, multidisciplinary mental health care, and a broad knowledge of the mental health challenges faced by individuals working in high performance sport cultures. We are seeking individuals with a sound understanding of the modern game of football in its various forms, and who have a comprehensive working knowledge of the most up to date policy and research progressions in their respective field. Key Accountabilities As a member of the IMHEP you will be required to: Provide twice yearly independent expert case consultation for the Mental Health and Wellbeing (MH&WB) and HR teams Improve quality and consistency of internal case management Strengthen safeguarding and risk management Ensure the safety of, and ethical practice by, internal practitioners and the organisation Identify common themes and learning opportunities Support the MH&WB and HR teams (and in some cases line managers) in managing particularly complex cases (where such support is requested by the MH&WB and HR teams) Offer advisory recommendation, observation and learning Where appropriate support psychologically informed governance and policy The panel will offer recommendation only and The FA retains operational, legal, clinical, safeguarding and managerial accountability for all decisions. The MH&WB team will be responsible for coordinating the panel, chairing meetings, recording and securely storing/sharing relevant information, and remain accountable for all case related decision making. There will be two formal meetings per year where a selection of complex cases will be taken to the panel for review and discussion. Examples of selected cases might include: High-risk mental health concerns Suicidality or self-harm concerns Repeated safeguarding concerns Complex interpersonal challenges or behavioural risk Significant psychological or emotional trauma Ethical uncertainty Multidisciplinary or cross function conflict of interest Organisational risk Longstanding mental health and/ or performance support needs What we are looking for Members of the Panel will include: Consultant Psychiatrist Clinical Psychologist Occupational Psychologist or Organisational Consultant Neurodiversity Specialist Health and Safety Representative Human Resource Specialist Members of the Panel will be expected to participate independently and objectively, and within the boundaries of their professional competence. Any conflicts of interest (case specific or in relation to the organisation whole) must be declared to the Chair of the Panel prior to participation. Contributions must be constructive and offered for the good of The FA and its employees. Members are expected to promote safe and ethical practice at all times and maintain confidentiality throughout ( The panel may decide that confidentiality be broken where there is a legal obligation to disclose information, where there is a risk of serious harm to an individual or others, or where the sharing of information is needed to safeguard an individuals welfare) Time Commitment As a minimum, IMHEP members should attend two scheduled meetings per year to review and discuss a selection of identified complex cases. Meetings will usually be face to face on weekdays at The National Football Centre St George's Park, or Wembley Stadium. Additional Panel meetings may be called at the discretion of the Panel Chair. Panel members will also be available for ad hoc consultation on specific matters within the Panel's remit as required. Ad hoc meetings will be kept to a minimum and usually be held online. Members will receive a set fee for attending meetings, and reasonable expenses incurred in order to travel to meetings will be reimbursed. Members will be appointed for an initial term of two years, after which they will be eligible to reapply for another two years, up to four times (maximum of 8 years). Members can resign from the Panel at any point with written notice, and The FA can also terminate appointments where necessary. Role Descriptors The FA are looking to appoint the following specialist roles: Consultant Psychiatrist Providing specialist medical and psychiatric expertise regarding complex mental health presentations, risk assessment considerations, diagnostic complexity, treatment pathways, and psychiatric considerations. Key Responsibilities Provide expert psychiatric consultation Advise on risk formulations Consider diagnostic complexities Provide expert understanding of severe mental illness Advise on treatment considerations and appropriateness of support plans Contribute to reflective discussions Essential Qualifications Registered medical practitioner Specialist registration in psychiatry Professional registration with General Medical Council (GMC) and indemnity insurance Significant experience in the management and review of complex mental health Clinical Psychologist Providing psychological formulation, behavioural understanding, trauma-informed diagnosis, and psychologically informed perspective on complex cases. Key Responsibilities Provide psychological formulation Advise on trauma-informed approaches Identify behavioural and systemic factors Advise on safe and ethical practice Support reflective learning process Essential Qualifications HCPC-registered Clinical Psychologist Current professional registration Significant experience working with complex cases Experience working within a multidisciplinary team Occupational Psychologist or Organisational Consultant Providing expertise on workplace mental health and wellbeing, psychosocial risk factors, systemic stressors, and psychologically well organisations. Key Responsibilities Advise on workplace psychosocial risk factors Consider organisational impact Provide perspective on psychologically informed workplace approaches Support broader workplace wellbeing considerations Essential Qualifications Registered Occupational Psychologist or relevant equivalent Relevant professional memberships, including HCPC registration Significant experience in organisational mental health Neurodiversity Specialist Providing expertise on neurodiversity, psychosocial risk factors, equality and inclusion support, and systemic risk factors concerning neurodiverse cases management. Key Responsibilities Provide expert advise on appropriate support infrastructure for cases involving neurodiverse diagnoses Advise on behavioural and systemic factors Support reflective learning process where neurodiverse factors are involved Support escalation process where required Essential Qualifications HCPC-registered Clinical Psychologist Current professional registration Significant experience working with neurodiverse populations in the workplace Health and Safety Representative Providing expertise regarding workplace health and safety requirements, psychosocial risk management, and organisational safety obligations. Key Responsibilities Support organisational safety considerations Identify systemic risk implications Advise on safe systems of work Support governance and risk compliance Advise on psychosocial risk management Essential Qualifications CertIOSH or CMIOSH membership, or equivalent MIIRSM membership Significant experience working with organisational risk management Understanding of organisational risk management legislations including ISO45003 Working understanding of psychosocial risk factors Working understanding of supporting organisational wellbeing obligations Human Resource Specialist Providing expertise on employment practice, people management, workplace policies, employee relations, and organisational processes to inform consideration of complex workplace mental health cases. Key Responsibilities Provide advice on HR policies and employment practices Consider employee relations and workplace processes Advise on reasonable workplace adjustments and organisational procedures Support fair, consistent, and legally compliant decision-making Contribute a people management perspective within multidisciplinary discussions Essential Qualifications Chartered Member or Fellow of the CIPD (or equivalent professional body) Significant senior HR experience, including employee relations and complex workplace cases Experience advising on workplace wellbeing, absence mana

item.title: Operations Manager

Working closely with senior leaders across the Diocese, you will play a key role in driving continuous improvement, promoting excellent customer service and ensuring robust governance and compliance. Reporting to the Deputy Diocesan Secretary, you will provide leadership to a small team responsible for governance and central support services. You will oversee the smooth running of Church House, manage facilities and operational contracts, lead on health and safety, and act as the Diocese's Data Protection Officer. Key responsibilities: Lead and develop operational and support services across Church House Manage facilities, suppliers, contracts and operational budgets Act as Data Protection Officer and lead on GDPR compliance, including Subject Access Requests Oversee information governance, records management and organisational systems Maintain and develop business continuity and risk management processes Manage organisational policies and complaints administration Support the Diocese's digital development through Microsoft 365, automation and AI-enabled solutions Coordinate operational arrangements for major diocesan events and conferences About You We are looking for someone who combines strong operational expertise with excellent leadership and relationship-building skills. item.title: Senior Manager, Trusts & Foundations
item.description: The National Youth Orchestra is the UK’s leading organisation championing orchestral music as a powerful agent for teenage development. We activate teenagers’ confidence, optimism and skills to play their part in the world today, through performing and sharing extraordinary music. We are looking for an entrepreneurial and collaborative trusts fundraiser to play a leading role in growing the investment that supports NYO’s work with teenagers across the UK. Trusts and foundations contribute more than £600,000 annually, and this new role will help deepen existing partnerships, develop new opportunities and secure significant support for NYO’s future. As an ambitious and growing organisation, we need to communicate new and evolving programmes with agility, articulating their potential clearly and building the support needed to make them possible. This is an opportunity to build from a position of strength, sustaining successful programmes while securing investment to create opportunities for many more teenagers. You will manage a substantial portfolio of trust, foundation and statutory funders, leading relationships from cultivation and application through to stewardship, reporting and renewal. You will develop compelling, evidence-led proposals and reports, including significant and strategically important bids, and work closely with colleagues to bring together programme, financial and impact information. This is an excellent opportunity for an experienced fundraiser who combines excellent writing and relationship-building skills with strategic judgement and careful delivery. You will take ownership of agreed income targets and play an active part in a collaborative Fundraising & Communications team working across Individual Giving, major donors and Trusts & Foundations to achieve shared goals. At the National Youth Orchestra, you'll work as part of a supportive, friendly, and adventurous staff team. Learning and personal growth are intrinsic to every role. Our offices near Holborn in central London are a hive of activity, a space for collaboration and ideas. Hybrid working is standard for most roles, with a flexible and supportive culture. NYO offers a season ticket loan scheme, cycle-to-work scheme, health cash plan, retail and entertainment discounts, and a 24/7 counselling and support helpline. Deadline for applications: 10am, Monday 21 September 2026

Our passionate employees and dedicated volunteers are helping people with mental health issues find somewhere to turn for advice, information, and support. We won’t give up until everyone experiencing a mental health issue gets both support and respect. About the Role and the Service The Safe Haven is a core part of Oxfordshire Mind’s Housing and Safe Haven (Crisis Support) portfolio. We work collaboratively with local health, Mental Health and VCSE services to offers effective, inclusive and responsive support to people experiencing mental health issues or poor mental wellbeing, Oxfordshire Mind offers a variety of services including: Wellbeing Centres throughout the county The Information Service, including the information line, website and Oxfordshire Mind Guide publication Physical Activity and Wellbeing Oxford and Banbury Safe Havens alternatives to NHS support for Mental Health crises Embedded workers offering evidence-based 121 support in Primary and Secondary Care in Oxfordshire and Berkshire Services for Children and Young People Open 365 days a year, Oxfordshire Safe Haven is a safe and welcoming space for when it feels like there’s no way out. The Senior Service Manager for Safe Haven will support the leadership, development and continuous improvement of our Safe Haven, Crisis Alternative Service, readying us for successful retendering while ensuring services are safe, effective, high quality, contractually compliant and aligned with Oxfordshire Mind’s values and strategic objectives. About You We are currently looking to recruit a Senior Service Manager and would really welcome applications for it. We would really like to know how your skills and experience match our requirements. If you feel they do, please tell us how you meet the below requirements: Experience managing a similar service Strong understanding of mental health issues, in particular suicidality, and their impact on individuals, carers and communities. Good understanding of clinical and non-clinical mental health services. Good working knowledge of safeguarding practice and how to apply it in a relevant setting. Good facilitation skills Knowledge of voluntary sector leadership or community-based service delivery. Commitment to ongoing learning and personal development. Substantial experience of leading and managing services and teams. Experience of contract monitoring and funder reporting. Experience of managing budgets and resources. Experience of working to quality assurance and service standards. Experience of using feedback to make positive service improvements. Experience of effective internal and external partnership working. Ability to build rapport and develop trust with a range of people. Ability to work well as part of a team and contribute to a collaborative management culture. Excellent organisational, IT and administrative skills. Ability to manage issues with a solution-focused attitude. Ability to support, motivate, develop and appropriately challenge managers and staff. Ability to take responsibility, use initiative and work creatively. Strong communication and interpersonal skills with staff, partners, funders and the public. If you would like to find out more, please click the apply button. You will be directed to our website to complete your application for this position. We welcome applications from people from all sections of the community, irrespective of race, ethnicity, gender, age, disability, sexual orientation, religion or belief. This is an exciting opportunity to play a key role in the delivery of a nationally funded programme, working alongside clergy, lay leaders and senior church stakeholders to: facilitate training, communications, events, and resource development to support parishes and priests affiliated to the society. If you are an experienced administrator with excellent communication skills, strong attention to detail and a passion for supporting effective programmes, we would love to hear from you. item.title: Chief Executive Officer
item.description: This is a rare and rewarding opportunity to lead a well-established and highly respected charity, dedicated to improving the lives of adult survivors of childhood sexual abuse, sexual violence and rape. S.H.E. UK is seeking an exceptional, community-focused leader with a strong track record in fundraising, relationship building and organisational development. At an exciting point in our journey, we are looking for a CEO who can strengthen and sustain our foundations, inspire support across our communities, diversify income streams, and translate our ambitious new strategy into meaningful action. You will bring proven experience of securing sustainable funding from a range of sources, including grants, donors, community supporters and strategic partnerships. Equally important is your ability to lead with compassion, champion survivor-centred services, and build trust with a wide range of stakeholders. As Chief Executive Officer, you will provide strategic, operational and financial leadership, ensuring the charity remains resilient, impactful and well governed. Working closely with the Board of Trustees, you will maintain the highest standards of safeguarding, governance and service delivery, while creating the conditions for long-term sustainability. This is an exciting opportunity for an inspiring and compassionate leader to build on our achievements, bring our strategy to life, and help shape the next chapter of S.H.E. UK's development. This is a hybrid role, with a minimum of three days per week working in person from our Mansfield base. If you are passionate about creating lasting change, have a proven track record of leadership, and are committed to improving the lives of survivors, we would love to hear from you.

item.title: Policy Manager
item.description: Policy Manager We’re thrilled to announce an exciting opportunity for a Policy Manager to join our vibrant and highly respected Policy, Public Affairs and Campaigns Team! In this influential role, you’ll be at the heart of shaping our policy agenda, helping drive real and positive change for those affected by dementia. You’ll have the chance to champion innovation and research breakthroughs, bringing fresh energy and insight to areas that truly matter. By combining your expertise in policy analysis, advocacy, and stakeholder engagement, you’ll help steer strategic initiatives that impact government decisions, public health priorities, and vital research funding. You’ll collaborate with a diverse and inspiring group of people, including policymakers, researchers, clinicians, and those with lived experience of dementia. Together, you’ll work to strengthen the case for greater investment in dementia care, championing improvements in healthcare pathways and clinical practice. You’ll be advocating for fairer, more accessible diagnosis and treatment, and supporting health systems to adopt best practices as we prepare for the future of dementia therapies. Key Responsibilities: Policy development · Develop and manage programmes of work on key strategic policy areas that position ARUK as a key influencer both nationally and internationally. This may include the commissioning of external evidence generation. · Provide expertise on the relevant evidence, insight, and policy context to enable the development of new innovative policy ideas and solutions that deliver on our strategic priorities. · Manage the development of substantial and credible policy outputs, including briefings, reports, submissions to government departments and their agencies, parliamentary committees, and other UK and international organisations as appropriate. · Work with the Policy Communications team to ensure our policy work is disseminated to our key audiences via a range of appropriate channels to maximise our reach and impact. · Develop and maintain mechanisms to keep abreast of the policy environment. · Analyse, interpret and make judgements on complex project activities, delegating and managing the policy advisors to achieve set deliverables through their management of day-to-day activities. As Policy, Public Affairs and Campaigns works in a matrix structure this may include managing deliverables with policy advisors across the team. · Support the join-up between projects and across the wider team to ensure shared knowledge and the opportunity to maximise influence and impact. Stakeholder engagement and management · Develop and manage stakeholder engagement of key policy contacts. · Actively promote patient and public involvement in the development and delivery of projects. · Work with Public Affairs colleagues to strengthen existing and emerging relationships with political and other parliamentary stakeholders to maximise the impact of our policy work. · Attend external working groups and help develop partnerships beneficial to ARUK. · Work with other charities to ensure ARUK is playing a leadership role in shaping government medical research policy. Research and data analysis · Oversee the analysis of necessary data and evidence, working with other ARUK colleagues, to produce accurate, timely and insightful policy materials, briefings and media stories. Line Management Responsibilities · Line manage and develop two Policy Advisors, providing coaching, mentoring and performance management as appropriate. · Work with Senior Policy Manager and other Managers to support our team mission, wider team development and our commitment to excellence. Knowledge, skills and experience needed: · Experience in policy development and implementation within a healthcare setting. · Experience involving clinicians and the public/patients in policy work. · Proven success in developing, implementing, and influencing policy at a national level. · Experience managing staff and supporting their development. · Strong track record of building effective relationships with stakeholders, particularly in biomedical research or health settings. · Skilled in producing and reviewing complex policy reports and consultation responses, and in working with government teams to embed ideas. · Understanding of diverse channels for communicating policy work. · Collaborative, hard-working team player with a strategic outlook and a clear focus on impact. · Skilled at managing and developing people. · Shows initiative and adaptability in a complex, changing policy environment. · Strong negotiation and communication skills, effective with people at all levels both in person and remotely. · Excellent organisational, prioritisation, and programme management abilities. · Professional writing skills, with the ability to adapt style for different audiences. · Confident user of Microsoft Office. Additional Information: Ways of working: As part of our Agile ways of working you will be required to work approximately 2 days a week from the office, which is subject to the requirements of the role and the business needs. Flexibility on where you work can be split between working from home and our office. Roles that are classed as part of the Agile ways of working are not able to claim any costs for Mileage/Travel on Public Transport, Accommodation and/or Meals. This includes when attending the office for various meetings/events. Our Office : Our office is at 3 Riverside, Granta Park, Great Abington, Cambridge, CB21 6AD. Salary : Circa £45,000 per annum, plus benefits Please download the Vacancy Pack on our website for more information. The closing date for applications is the 20th September 2026 , with interviews being arrange once shortlisting has been completed. Please indicate in your covering letter if you are unable to attend an interview on a certain date. We would encourage you to submit your application at the earliest opportunity, as on occasion we may have to bring forward the interview date and/or the closing date based on the needs of the business. Although a possibility, this will only happen in exceptional circumstances. Please indicate in your covering letter if you are unable to attend an interview on a certain date. We value diversity and are committed to creating an inclusive culture where everyone can be themselves and reach their full potential. We actively encourage applications from people of all backgrounds and cultures, particularly from those in the global majority, those with disabilities, men and those from the LGBTQIA+ community. Any offer of employment is however subject to you having the right to work in the UK. As part of our commitment to being an inclusive employer and ensuring fairness and consistency in our selection process, we will handle your CV and application with the utmost confidentiality. Should you require any adjustments at either the application or interview stage, please contact us via our website. How to apply: Please create an online account using our Online Recruitment Platform which can be accessed through our Job Vacancies page. You will be able to attach your CV to your application and track the status of your application. About Alzheimer’s Research UK: Alzheimer's Research UK is the UK's leading dementia research charity. Our mission is to accelerate progress towards a cure. Today 1 in 2 people will be impacted by dementia, either through caring for a loved one, developing it themselves or tragically both. But there is hope.

item.title: Press and Communications Officer
item.description: Salary: £34,000 FTE (£20,400 actual salary) Contract: Permanent, part-time, 0.6 FTE Hours: 21 hours per week with flexibility as to how these are worked subject to business need and prior agreement Location: Hybrid, with regular attendance at our central London office (40%) Reporting to: Head of Policy and Advocacy Help shape public understanding of data and evidence We are looking for an experienced and proactive Press and Communications Officer to help raise the profile of the RSS, secure media coverage for our work, and ensure our expertise reaches policymakers, journalists and the wider public. This is an exciting opportunity for a communications professional who enjoys translating complex topics into compelling stories and wants to contribute to evidence-informed public debate. About the role As Press and Communications Officer, you will lead and coordinate media and communications activity across the Society's policy, advocacy and public engagement work. You will build relationships with journalists, identify opportunities to showcase RSS expertise, support media-facing spokespeople, and deliver communications campaigns that enhance our influence and reputation. You'll work across a wide range of issues, helping to explain the role of data, statistics and evidence in public life while ensuring the RSS is recognised as a trusted and authoritative voice. Key responsibilities include: Developing and delivering communications campaigns and media plans. Generating positive media coverage and building strong relationships with journalists. Drafting press releases, statements, briefings and opinion pieces. Managing media enquiries and supporting RSS spokespeople. Creating and scheduling social media content. Identifying opportunities to contribute RSS expertise to current public debates. Monitoring and evaluating media coverage and communications impact. Supporting the development of a diverse network of expert ambassadors and spokespeople. About you We're looking for someone who combines excellent communications skills with a strong news sense and a passion for making complex information accessible. You will have: At least two years' experience in communications, press, public affairs or media relations. A strong track record of securing media coverage and building media relationships. Experience creating high-quality communications content, including press releases and social media content. Experience planning and delivering communications campaigns. Excellent writing and editing skills. Strong organisational and project management abilities. Confidence working with senior stakeholders and subject matter experts. The ability to explain complex issues clearly to non-specialist audiences. Experience in a membership organisation, charity, professional body, learned society, or policy-focused organisation would be advantageous, as would an interest in research, evidence, data or public policy. Why join us? At the RSS, you'll be part of a friendly and collaborative team committed to improving the use of data and evidence across society. We offer: Generous pension scheme with employer contributions of up to 10%. 25 days annual leave plus bank holidays and Christmas closure (pro rata). Hybrid and flexible working arrangements. Training and development opportunities. Cycle-to-work scheme. Season ticket loan. Employee Assistance Programme. Apply now If you're an enthusiastic communications professional looking to make a meaningful impact through evidence, data and public engagement, we'd love to hear from you. Join us in helping ensure that statistics and evidence are at the heart of understanding and decision-making.
item.dc:creator: The Royal Statistical Society

item.title: Executive Assistant
item.description: Location: Hybrid: home-based with weekly attendance at the London office, plus additional days as required for meetings, board meetings or events Salary: £35,200 per annum rising to £38,100 after 1 year of service Responsible to: CEO Contract type: Full Time (37 hours per week), Permanent Closing date: 18th September, Midday Who we are Futures for All (formerly Speakers for Schools) is a UK charity founded in 2010 to tackle educational and social mobility inequality, connecting state-educated young people with inspirational speakers and high-quality work experience. Since its founding, the charity has supported almost two million young people, working with a national network of schools, colleges and employer partners to level the playing field for young people who are educated in the state sector, with those that attend the best fee-paying schools. Having grown from its original speaker programme into a broader work experience offer, the charity is now the largest provider of work experience in the UK, with ambitious plans to ensure all young people have access to the workplace, whilst at school. Role Summary This is a genuine opportunity to contribute first-hand to the strategic running of a national charity, with close visibility of how the organisation is led and governed. You will be trusted with sensitive information, exposed to strategic decision-making, and given the chance to shape how the CEO's office and the wider senior leadership team (SLT) operate day to day. Beyond the traditional diary, travel and correspondence duties, you will play an active part in the mechanics of governance and decision-making- supporting board meetings, tracking actions to completion, and ensuring that what lands on the CEO's desk is accurate, well-presented and ready to act on. You will also work closely with the newly appointed Project Management Office (PMO) Lead, helping ensure that updates on risks, issues and KPI tracking reach the CEO promptly and in a digestible form, so that the CEO's time and attention are focused where they are needed most. It is an ideal role for an experienced EA or Personal Assistant who wants more ownership, more variety, and closer involvement in the strategic life of an organisation than a traditional support role typically offers. This role offers direct exposure to the strategic and governance rhythm of the organisation- from board papers to senior stakeholder meetings- for someone who wants their EA experience to build towards broader organisational and governance expertise. Key Duties / Responsibilities Supporting the CEO: Proactively manage the CEO's diary, resolving clashes and prioritising competing demands on their time in line with organisational priorities. Act as a first point of contact for the CEO, screening and triaging correspondence, calls and requests, and responding or redirecting where appropriate. Build strong working relationships with the CEO's key internal and external contacts, acting as a trusted and professional representative of their office. Diary, Travel & Logistics: Coordinate complex diaries across multiple stakeholders, both internal and external, including scheduling and rearranging meetings at short notice. Book and manage travel, accommodation and venues, including researching options, managing costs, and having contingency plans in place. Prepare itineraries and briefing packs ahead of trips, meetings and events, ensuring the CEO is fully prepared. Process expenses and invoices relating to the CEO's activity in line with company policy. Meetings, Minutes & Action Tracking: Attend meetings chaired by or involving the CEO to take accurate, concise minutes and notes, distinguishing decisions from discussion. Maintain a live action log across meetings, proactively chasing owners and reporting progress back to the CEO so nothing is missed. Organise logistics for meetings and away days, including rooms, catering, materials and technology. Work closely with the Project Management Office (PMO) Lead to ensure that risk, issue and KPI updates are routed to the CEO promptly and in a clear, digestible format, helping the CEO focus attention where it is most needed. Liaise with the PMO Lead on scheduling and papers for any meetings that bring project or programme updates to the CEO, ensuring consistency with the wider action and decision tracking maintained for the CEO's office. Board & Governance Support: Support the coordination of board and committee meetings, including scheduling, collating and distributing papers to agreed deadlines. Take and produce minutes for board and committee meetings, working closely with the CEO (and Chair/Company Secretary, where applicable) on accuracy and follow-up. Maintain a board actions and decisions tracker, and support the CEO in preparing for board cycles. Maintain confidentiality and good document control over board papers, minutes and related governance records. Document & Presentation Production: Produce first drafts of documents, reports, briefings and PowerPoint presentations for the CEO to review, amend and finalise. Format and polish documents and slide decks to a professional, consistent, on-brand standard. Review documents and correspondence prepared by others before they reach the CEO, checking for accuracy, clarity, tone and fitness for purpose, and flagging any concerns. Support to the Senior Leadership Team: Provide reasonable and proportionate admin support to other members of the SLT, prioritised in agreement with the CEO. Minute meetings with senior internal and external stakeholders on behalf of SLT members, as required. Assist with occasional diary, travel or document support for the SLT where this does not conflict with the needs of the CEO. Office & General: Maintain efficient filing, contact and information systems for the CEO's office. Handle sensitive and confidential information with discretion and sound judgement at all times. Undertake other duties reasonably commensurate with the role, as required by the CEO. Skills / Experience / Knowledge: Essential: Significant experience as an EA, PA or senior administrator supporting a CEO, director or other senior executive. Experience taking minutes and tracking actions for senior-level or board/committee meetings. Excellent written English, with the ability to draft clear, well-structured documents, correspondence and presentations. Expert in using common business software/ applications such as Microsoft Office Word, PowerPoint, Excel and Outlook. Strong organisational skills and the ability to manage multiple, competing priorities under time pressure. Sound judgement and discretion when handling confidential or sensitive information. A proactive, solutions-focused approach, comfortable using initiative rather than waiting to be asked. Excellent interpersonal skills, with the confidence and professionalism to liaise with senior stakeholders, board members and external contacts. Flexibility to travel to, and work from, the London office on a regular (weekly) basis, with occasional flexibility around hours for travel, events or board meetings. Desirable: Experience supporting board or governance processes (e.g. in a charity, membership body, or regulated organisation). A relevant qualification (e.g. in business administration or executive PA practice), though experience will be weighted more heavily than formal qualification. Confident and effective use of AI tools (e.g. Microsoft Copilot, ChatGPT, Claude) to support drafting, summarising and formatting work- for example, producing first-draft documents, presentations or minutes for review, while applying good judgement on accuracy, confidentiality and when human review and rewriting is needed. Experience providing ad hoc support across a wider senior team, not just a single executive. Behaviours and Style: Calm and unflappable under pressure, with good humour and resilience. Trustworthy and discreet, with a strong sense of confidentiality. A genuine interest in the wider organisation and how it operates, not just the transactional tasks of the role. Collaborative- happy to support colleagues across the SLT while keeping the CEO's priorities front and centre. Diversity at our core Futures For All is committed to an inclusive and accessible recruitment process and encouraging equality and diversity among our workforces. We acknowledge that some candidates may require additional support to overcome barriers experienced during the application process. If you require any reasonable adjustments to support your application or interview, please reach out to us. The Application Process: Please apply as soon as possible by clicking the 'apply for this job' button in the top right-hand corner of the job advert. Once clicked, you will be asked to complete your application by submitting your CV and a cover letter. The cover letter is an opportunity for you to share the skills and knowledge you have to be successful in this role. Appointees are subject to a DBS check. You must have the right to work in the UK to apply. The deadline to submit your application is the 18th September 2026, Midday . Futures For All is committed to safeguarding the young people we work with and expects all staff members to share this commitment. Appointees are subject to a DBS check. Having a criminal record will not automatically exclude applicants. You are also required to have the Right to Work in the UK for this role. Annual Leave Staff receive 25 days annual leave, increasing incrementally after 2, 3 and 5 years of service to a maximum of 28 days. This is in addition to bank holidays and gifted leave between Christmas and New Year. Futures For All Values PASSION: We are committed to levelling the playing field for young people across the UK, creating social mobility and tackling disadvantages. AGILITY: We challenge our ideas of what is possible in order to better meet the needs of those we support. We are human, make mistakes, learn, evolve

item.title: Head of Legal
item.description: Could you use your legal skills to support mission, providing in house legal support and leading a project focusing on international land issues? • Fixed Term 1 year / Part-time 17.5 – 21 hours per week • Hybrid working – approximately one day a week at CMS House, Oxford. • Starting salary £50K per annum Full-time Equivalent depending on experience with a generous pension contribution: up to 10 per cent employer contribution on annual salary • CMS offers 36 days of annual leave pro rata (including bank holidays) as well as enhanced paid sickness, maternity, paternity and adoption leave. • CMS supports the mental wellbeing of its employees and offers a generous rewards and wellbeing package We welcome applications from everyone. We particularly welcome applications from individuals from minority groups as they are currently underrepresented within our organisation at this level. All appointments are made on merit of skill, experience and potential as set out in the job description and person specification. Your role As Head of Legal, you will provide legal expertise and support across the organisation, ensuring compliance with UK charity law and regulatory requirements. You will work closely with trustees, senior leadership, and operational teams to mitigate risk and enable the charity to achieve its objectives efficiently and legally. The organisation you’ll be joining Church Mission Society is comprised of people who are passionate about mission and fired up about helping people follow Jesus. For over 200 years CMS has been at the forefront of global mission, living out the gospel of Jesus, seeing lives changed and communities transformed. If you join CMS, you will find an organisation that has been reinvigorated with a fresh vision to make disciples of Jesus among people at the edges, both in the UK and around the world. What you’ll need to succeed The successful candidate will be a qualified solicitor or barrister in England and Wales with an understanding of commercial property and employment law. It would also be helpful to have had charity sector experience (and possibly experience with overseas property issues). It is also a requirement for this post holder to be a committed and practising Christian as well as committed to CMS’s values and aims. Further details can be found in the job description and person specification available to download on the CMS website. Our commitment to you Our core values of being pioneering, relational, faithful and evangelistic are integral to everything we do, and we work hard to ensure that every member of staff is valued, supported and encouraged to continually learn and develop their skills. We are committed to the safeguarding and protection of the people we serve, our partners, our volunteers, and our staff. We believe that every child or adult we come into contact with has the right to be protected from all forms of harm and abuse. Our recruitment and selection processes are in line with our Safeguarding Policy Closing date We must get your application by midnight on Sunday 27th September 2026 Interviews are planned to be held on Wednesday 7th October 2026 at CMS House, Oxford. To apply Please send your application form and CV via our bebsite or by post to HR Team, Church Mission Society, Watlington Road, Oxford OX4 6BZ. CVs will only be considered when sent with a completed application form, which is available to download from our website. Candidates for all UK roles must already be eligible to work in the UK, with a valid visa and work permit if required. As a member of the Inter-agency Misconduct Disclosure Scheme, CMS has committed to systematically check with previous employers from the last five years for any ‘SEAH’ (Sexual Exploitation, Abuse or Harassment) issues relating to all potential new hires.

item.title: Head of Community Investment
item.description: The Queen Elizabeth Trust is a new, ambitious UK-wide independent charity established to deliver a lasting legacy to the extraordinary life of service of Her late Majesty Queen Elizabeth. Inspired by Queen Elizabeth's belief that "everyone is our neighbour", the Trust works hand in hand with communities to restore and sustain the buildings, green spaces and shared places that bring people together across generations and from all walks of life. Through funding, strategic partnerships and targeted support, the Trust will help create safe, inclusive and vibrant places that thrive long into the future. Backed by an initial £40 million UK Government endowment, the Trust will act as a catalyst for change, investing not only in physical regeneration but also in the people, skills and activities that enable communities to flourish. Working with partners who bring deep local knowledge and expertise, the Trust is committed to ensuring that opportunities reach communities across the UK, particularly those that have historically faced barriers to accessing major funding programmes. Working closely with the CEO, the Head of Community Investment will design and lead the Trust’s funding strategy, building a strong pipeline of opportunities, shaping innovative funding packages, securing co-investment, and managing a portfolio of high impact community projects across the UK. Combining strategic leadership with hands on delivery, you will play a pivotal role in creating the Trust’s approach, processes and partnerships from the ground up. We are seeking an experienced grant-maker, social investor or funding leader with a deep understanding of community organisations and the role they play in building social cohesion. You will bring a strong track record of assessing investments, developing partnerships, influencing diverse stakeholders and managing complex funding arrangements. Equally important is your approach: entrepreneurial, collaborative and impact-driven, with the ability to thrive in ambiguity, build trusted relationships and move effortlessly between strategy and execution in a dynamic start-up environment. Please visit the Attenti website to read the appointment brief for more information and details on how to apply. For an informal and confidential discussion, after having read the appointment brief, please contact our advising consultants Anita Denton or David Fielding at Attenti. Closing date for applications – 5th October 2026

item.title: Art Collection Officer
item.description: The Vacancy This is a newly-created role in the Methodist Church’s Connexional (national) staff team, managing the Church’s unique collection of c.60 post-war religious artworks, which includes pieces by Sutherland, Frink, Burra, Souza and Muafangejo: The Methodist Modern Art Collection - The Methodist Church Working with the Collection’s expert volunteer Management Committee, you will be responsible for facilitating the conservation and touring programmes, including supporting local churches with exhibition planning, logistics, venue and condition checking, and for making related funding bids. You will have the opportunity to enhance the interpretation of the Collection and to develop creative new uses of the artworks. The Methodist Church is actively seeking a partner organisation with whom to establish a permanent new home base for the Collection. It is expected that part of your role will be to support relocating the artworks and helping to establish new ways of working as a result. About You We are seeking an experienced and innovative, fine art curator. You will be as comfortable supporting volunteers to stage exhibitions around Britain, as working with art gallery professionals, conservators and technicians. You will understand the potential for visual art to communicate the spiritual, and be able to demonstrate how to engage audiences in reflection and encourage conversation about God and Christian faith inspired by art. This role has an occupational requirement to be a practicing Christian in accordance with the Equality Act 2010. If you meet most of the requirements, we encourage you to apply; transferable skills and experience will also be taken into consideration. We are also open to considering remote/homeworking arrangements (salary may vary accordingly). Disclosure and Barring Service An enhanced DBS disclosure is required for this position. The Methodist Church will cover the associated costs. Informal Enquiries For an informal conversation about the role, please contact Jo Hibbard, Director of Heritage & Art. For questions or reasonable adjustments during the recruitment process, please email HR Team. Key Dates Closing Date for Applications : 27 September 2026 Interviews (on-site in London): 9 October 2026 Please note: We reserve the right to close this advert early if sufficient applications are received.

item.title: Accommodation and Community Services Lead – Care Services (Sussex)
item.description: Role/Job Title: Accommodation and Community Services Lead – Care Services (Sussex) Location: 19 High St, Battle TN33 0AE [hybrid working with regular travel across our Sussex services. A visible leadership presence within services is an important part of this role] Mileage expenses will be paid for travel to locations away from your main workplace, in accordance with the organisation's mileage policy. Hours: 37 hours per week (Monday – Friday) Salary: £40,000 - £45,000 per annum (dependent on experience) Closing date for applications: Wednesday 23rd September 2026 Please note that we may close this vacancy before the advertised closing date should we receive sufficient suitable applications. We encourage you to submit your application at the earliest opportunity. Equal Opportunity/Accessibility and Accommodations Statement: As a Disability Confident employer, Aspens Charities is committed to fostering an inclusive and supportive environment for individuals with disabilities. We actively promote the recruitment, retention, and career development of people with disabilities, recognising the invaluable contributions they make to our organisation. We are dedicated to ensuring an accessible recruitment process for all candidates. If you require any accommodations during the application or interview process, please don’t hesitate to reach out. Aspens’ mission is to provide high-quality care and support to individuals on the autism spectrum and with learning disabilities; meeting their needs and aspirations and empowering them to learn and grow through an integrated network of services across the South-East. Lead high-quality services. Develop great managers. Make a lasting difference. Aspens is entering an exciting new chapter. Following a recent organisational restructure, we've strengthened the way we deliver care, creating an even more effective, responsive and sustainable model of support for the people we support. As part of this transformation, we've created new opportunities to join our leadership team - roles that didn't previously exist. We're looking for an experienced social care leader to join Aspens as our Accommodation & Community Services Lead - Sussex, providing operational leadership across a portfolio of residential, supported living and outreach services. Reporting to the Head of Sussex, you'll provide leadership and support to our Service Managers, driving service quality, safeguarding, performance, compliance and continuous improvement across the area. This is a senior operational role for someone who is ready to take the next step from a Registered Manager, Home Manager, Deputy Manager, Operations Manager or similar multi-service leadership position. This is an opportunity to make a real impact - shaping the future of our services, inspiring high-performing teams, and ensuring every person we support receives exceptional care, regardless of where they live or who is supporting them. If you're ready to shape the future of social care and be part of an ambitious organisation dedicated to improving lives, we'd love to hear from you. Join us and help lead the next stage of the Aspens journey. About the Role: As Accommodation & Community Services Lead, you will oversee Service Managers across Sussex and play a critical role in shaping service quality, culture and performance. You will combine operational leadership with practice excellence, ensuring services are safe, compliant, outcomes-focused and aligned with Positive Behaviour Support (PBS) principles. Key responsibilities include: Leading residential, supported living and outreach services across Sussex. Managing and developing Service Managers to achieve excellent outcomes. Providing senior oversight of safeguarding, risk management and service performance. Driving quality assurance, continuous improvement and regulatory compliance. Supporting service development, innovation and sustainable growth. Building positive relationships with commissioners, regulators and external partners. Championing co-production, inclusion and neuro-affirming practice. About You We're looking for a confident and compassionate leader who can balance strategic thinking with hands-on operational oversight. You'll bring: Significant experience within residential and community-based social care services. Strong multi-site leadership and people management experience. Extensive safeguarding knowledge and leadership capability. Experience working with CQC-regulated services. A strong understanding of autism, mental health, complex needs and Positive Behaviour Support. Budget management and service performance experience. Excellent communication, analytical and problem-solving skills. A Level 5 qualification in Leadership & Management in Health & Social Care (or equivalent experience/qualification). What We Offer: · Comprehensive paid training and excellent career progression opportunities, including recognised qualifications in health and social care · Paid DBS check · Flexible work arrangements, with the option to take on additional bank shifts · Nest Pension and Death in Service benefit · Access to a dedicated Employee Assistance Programme and Mental Health First Aiders · Blue Light Card discounts · 20% discount at Aspens High Street Stores for all staff · Discounted staff menu available at the Bluebell Café (Pembury) · Refer a Friend scheme - earn up to £250 for every successful referral · Employee recognition programmes, including ‘Employee of the Month’ Apply now and one of our team members will reach out to discuss the role further. If shortlisted, we will contact you directly to schedule an interview. We strive to respond to all applicants; however, if you have not received a response within a reasonable timeframe, please feel free to contact us for a status update or feedback (where available). After the interview, you will be notified of the outcome. If successful, you’ll receive a formal offer in writing. Upon acceptance, we’ll guide you through the onboarding process, providing you with all the details you need Please note, any offer of employment will be subject to Disclosure and Barring checks (which we will arrange on your behalf if you don’t already have one) and satisfactory employment references.

item.title: Story and Voice Specialist
item.description: Story and Voice Specialist The Children's Society Flexible Location (On-site) £30,600 FTE Contract Job description Social Impact Advert Contract: 12 month fixed-term contract Part time: 21 hours per week Location: Flexible within the UK (remote, hybrid or working from our London Old Street office or one of our regional offices). Occasional travel will be required. Salary: £18,360 (21 hour week, pro-rated from £30,600) Flexible working hours: 8-4, 9-5, 10-6 or in between (agreed with your manager) Benefits include but not limited to: -36 days' annual leave (pro rata for part time roles), inclusive of flexible bank holidays, increasing with length of service -Enhanced maternity/paternity leave -We match up to 8% pension -Free counselling service -Opportunities to develop and widen your skills -2 days of paid volunteering time per annum to support another part of the organisation About us: Across the country, young people are suffering unseen and unheard. They're facing overwhelming challenges - struggling with their mental health, caught in poverty, and in danger from exploitation and abuse. Too often, teenagers miss out on the support they need. Teenagers are children too, and a future of hope and happiness belongs to every one of them. The Children's Society has been helping children and young people in this country for over 140 years. We run local services that support children when they are at their most vulnerable and in desperate need of help. We're there for children, every step of the way. At The Children's Society, we know that this brighter future is possible. Our services support thousands of children every year, and our campaigning impacts the lives of many thousands more. Every day, we see the incredible difference the right support can make. We're hugely proud of all that we achieve year-on-year and of the incredible young people we work with. About the role We are looking for a creative writer and empathetic listener to join our passionate, dynamic team who's excited about participation. This role will embed and amplify the voice of young people across our communications. Working closely with our colleagues in youth impact, youth voice, creative, fundraising, campaigns and others across the organisation, you will gather powerful and compelling stories from those with lived experience, using a trauma informed, person-centred approach. This role sits within our Storytelling Team within our Social Impact Domain which works to engage our audiences and inspire social change across society. As an experienced Story and Voice Specialist, your role will be to empower children and young people and others to become storytellers, supporting them to be comfortable, confident and in control of sharing their experiences. The stories we tell are vital to achieving our mission, helping to change social attitudes and urging people to take action with young people, by offering their time, their money or their voice to our cause. Skills and competencies In order to be successful in this role: -You have experience conducting sensitive trauma-informed interviews with young people and adults -You are skilled at writing long-form stories that focus on the storyteller leading the narrative in their own words. -You'll be eager to amplify stories with our colleagues across the organisation, stewarding the content through campaigns, web and social content, and much more. -You're plugged in to contemporary storytelling techniques and have an ear for a great narrative. -You'll have the ability to build relationships quickly and warmly to ensure trust. Closing date: Midnight on Sunday 20th September 2026 Interviews: Interviews will be held in two stages. The first round will be held over w/c 5th October 2026 and w/c 12th October 2026. The second round will be held with young people shortly afterwards. The Children's Society is committed to safeguarding and protection of the children and young people we work with. As such, our safer recruitment process includes a Basic or Enhanced DBS check, 2 years of references, and additional vetting checks relevant to the role. We have a comprehensive range of policies and procedures in place to promote safeguarding and safer working practices across all areas of our organisation.In support of our commitment to diversity and inclusion, shortlisting is carried out on an anonymised basis. Personal details are hidden from the shortlisting panel, and candidates are referenced by a candidate number only. item.title: Assistant Head (Safeguarding)
item.description: Safeguarding sits at the heart of life at The Perse School. We are seeking an exceptional leader to join our senior team as Assistant Head (Safeguarding), taking strategic responsibility for safeguarding and child protection across our 3 Cambridge schools and serving as Designated Safeguarding Lead (DSL) for the Upper School. This is a significant leadership opportunity for an experienced safeguarding professional who can combine expertise, sound judgement and compassion to ensure every pupil feels safe, supported and able to flourish. The successful candidate will lead safeguarding strategy and practice, oversee complex child protection matters, provide guidance and training to colleagues, and work closely with pupils, families, staff, governors and external agencies. We welcome applications from experienced teachers, educational leaders and safeguarding professionals from related sectors. While experience in education is highly desirable, we are equally interested in candidates who have developed substantial safeguarding expertise through social care, local authority safeguarding services, the LADO function or other child protection settings. The Perse enjoys a prestigious reputation and values a mixed approach to teaching and learning. We aim to respect tradition and innovation, industry and fun, and academic and personal growth. All teachers and pupils are required to demonstrate all-round excellence and contribute to the academic, pastoral and extra-curricular life of the school. At The Perse School, we value the well-being of all staff and offer a supportive environment that balances professional ambitions with personal growth, opportunity and work-life balance. Further details including how to apply can be obtained from our website: Work with us - The Perse School Cambridge Closing date: Friday 18th September at 9.00am. Interviews will be a two stage process; preliminary online on Wednesday 23rd September followed by in person for successful candidates in the week commencing 28th September. The School actively supports equality, diversity and inclusion and encourages applications from all sections of society. Safer Recruitment The Perse School recognises that an important element in safeguarding our pupils is a robust recruitment process that incorporates measures to deter, reject or identify people who might abuse children, or who are otherwise unsuited to work with them. We are committed to safeguarding and promoting the welfare of children and applicants must be willing to undergo child protection screening appropriate to the post including: references from previous employers, a Disclosure and Barring Service check at the enhanced level, as well as eligibility to work in the UK (in compliance with UK immigration regulations).All work carried out at the School on a regular basis amounts to regulated activity. This role is also exempt from the Rehabilitation of Offenders Act 1974. Safeguarding and promoting the welfare of children is everyone's responsibility. The School is committed to acting in the best interests of the child so as to safeguard and promote the welfare of children and young people. The School requires everyone who comes into contact with children and their families to share this commitment. Interviews will be conducted in person, and they will explore candidates’ suitability to work with children.

item.title: Service Manager
item.description: About the role: For someone moving away from rough sleeping, having a safe place to stay can be the first step towards something much bigger. Gray’s Inn Road is a 16 bed short stay service in Camden, giving people the stability, support and breathing space they need to begin rebuilding their lives and move towards a home they can sustain. As Service Manager, you’ll lead the team that makes that possible. You’ll create a service where people are treated with dignity, listened to and supported as individuals, while giving your team the leadership, challenge and encouragement they need to do their best work. From the quality of assessments and support planning to safeguarding, risk management and move on, you’ll set the standard for practice and make sure residents receive consistent, psychologically informed support that responds to what matters to them. You’ll also build the relationships that help people move forward. Working closely with housing, health, substance use, criminal justice and other partners, you’ll help remove barriers, strengthen pathways into support and create more opportunities for residents beyond the service. Alongside this, you’ll take ownership of the wider performance of Gray’s Inn Road – keeping a close eye on quality, outcomes, housing management, health and safety, budgets and contractual expectations, and always looking for ways the service can become even better. At Single Homeless Project (SHP), we want our managers to do more than keep services running; we want them to shape what great support looks like. You’ll have the space to bring ideas, develop your team and influence how Gray’s Inn Road continues to grow, while building your own leadership experience within one of London’s largest homelessness charities. With training, support and opportunities to develop across SHP, this is a role where you can grow your career while seeing the difference your leadership makes to people’s lives. About you: You’re an experienced and compassionate leader who knows how to get the best from a team, set clear standards and create a culture where both staff and residents can thrive. You understand the realities of homelessness and multiple disadvantage, and can lead psychologically informed, person-centred practice that balances choice, independence, safeguarding and risk. You’re confident navigating complex situations and making sound decisions, while supporting your team to stay curious, consistent and focused on what will make the biggest difference for each person. You’re a natural relationship builder who can bring partners together, challenge when needed and create stronger pathways into housing, health and other support. You’re comfortable taking ownership of the whole service — from quality and performance to housing management, health and safety and budgets — and you’re always looking for ways to make things work better. About us: Single Homeless Project is a London-wide charity. Our vision is of a society where everyone has a place to call home and the chance to live a fulfilling life. We help single Londoners by preventing homelessness, providing support and accommodation, promoting wellbeing, enhancing opportunity, and being a voice for change. From supporting people in crisis to helping people take the final steps towards independence and employment, we make a difference to 12,000 lives every year across all 32 boroughs. We offer you more than a job; we offer you a chance to be part of a compassionate, driven team that's committed to making a real difference in people's lives. You'll have the opportunity to lead, co-create, and inspire change while enjoying a collaborative, growth-oriented environment. Join us in creating a brighter, more hopeful future for individuals in need. Important info: Closing Date: Sunday 20th September at midnight Interview Date: Wednesday 30th September online via Microsoft Teams Please note there will be a second stage interview in service in Camden for suitable candidates This post will require an Enhanced DBS check to be processed for the successful applicant. Please note applications are reviewed for AI use in application questions. Applications with insufficient/without current right to work or requiring sponsorship will not be accepted for this role.

Our members have a unique depth and breadth of knowledge about the discipline. The Society’s role is to help unlock and harness the potential of that knowledge. Our commitment to anyone who studies microbes is “ whoever you are, wherever you are, we will amplify your voice ”. About you The Head of Engagement and Storytelling leads communications and engagement across the organisation. This role involves working with members and colleagues to develop and curate scientific content designed for impact across our wide-ranging audiences, including members, the wider scientific community, the media, influential stakeholders and the public in order to achieve the Society’s ambitious vision of a world in which the science of microbiology provides maximum benefit to society. The postholder will have experience working within science communication, displaying strong scientific knowledge while delivering high impact engagement campaigns. It is essential to have experience in People Management as this role oversees the different branches of the Engagement and Storytelling theme covering Communication, Policy and Membership.
