item.title: Philanthropy and Partnerships Manager (Maternity cover)
item.description: About the Role Our small Fundraising team has benefitted from significant investment in recent years and this maternity cover role will provide vital continuity as EIA develops and expands its network of philanthropic supporters and strategic partners. You will be joining EIA at a pivotal time, working closely with the Head of Fundraising to sustain momentum across philanthropy, support the launch of our giving circle, Nature Network, and help strengthen selected partnership opportunities that contribute to our fundraising ambitions. The fundraising team at EIA, is responsible for raising income across trusts and statutory funders, as well as raising funds from individuals. The income raised from individuals has increased in recent years and we are investing further in this area so that we can conduct even more investigative and campaigning work to protect our planet. The role will focus on developing and strengthening relationships with High Net Worth Individuals (HNWIs), inspiring supporters to give generously, and stewarding donors so they feel closely connected to EIA’s work to combat environmental crime and abuse around the world, as well as supporting partnership activity where it aligns with philanthropic giving, cultivation and long-term relationship development. The Philanthropy and Partnerships Manager (Maternity cover) will lead the day-to-day delivery of EIA’s philanthropy programme during the maternity cover period. This will include tailored stewardship for HNWIs, prospecting and cultivation, donor funding propositions, implementing and growing the Nature Network giving circle following its launch in September, engaging our network of ambassadors, Future Stewards, and maintaining effective systems to support growth in philanthropy. The role will also contribute to a focused partnerships pipeline, ensuring partnership activity supports philanthropic income growth and deepens engagement with EIA’s mission. Key areas of responsibility Responsibilities will include, but are not limited to, the following: Development of the existing supporter base: Develop and deliver a tailored stewardship programme for higher level donors. Establish appropriate KPIs to track progress and measure success. Expand the donor base by acquiring new high value prospects: Conduct regular prospecting and cultivation to identify new potential supporters. Use network mapping to identify potential connections with existing stakeholders. Lead the development and delivery of cultivation events and exploratory meetings. Develop donor funding propositions: Work with campaign teams and the wider fundraising team to develop funding propositions for HNWI and a Case for Support for the different areas of our work. Launch and develop Nature Network and associated stewardship: Following the September launch of Nature Network, EIA’s giving circle, recruit new members and provide a compelling stewardship journey for supporters giving at this level. Support aligned partnerships activity: Maintain and develop a focused pipeline of prospective partners where there is clear alignment with EIA’s campaigns, values and philanthropic priorities. Work with the Head of Fundraising and colleagues to support partnership cultivation, proposal development and stewardship. Lead the prospecting and stewardship of our brand ambassador programme, Future Stewards, including developing a social media communications plan with the Social Media and Digital Engagement Manager Strategy development, budgeting and campaign reporting: Work with the Head of Fundraising to deliver philanthropy plans during the maternity cover period and contribute to wider fundraising strategy where relevant. Monitor income and expenditure across philanthropy, Nature Network and relevant partnership activity to ensure they meet budget and contribute to the mid-year reforecast process. Produce regular income reports that monitor performance against KPIs and feed back to the Head of Fundraising and wider organisation to share successes with the EIA team. Person Specification Essential Significant experience of identifying, cultivating and stewarding relationships with high value supporters and securing significant gifts. Considerable experience of developing and communicating high value funding propositions and writing compelling cases for support and applications. Strong verbal communication skills, confident in communicating effectively and passionately with supporters, team members across EIA and senior stakeholders. Excellent networking and presentation skills. Experience of planning and delivering stewardship events for HNWIs. Experience of managing or supporting giving circles, membership-style donor programmes or structured supporter journeys would be advantageous. Experience of partnership development, corporate relationships or cross-sector collaboration, with the ability to identify opportunities that support philanthropic income growth. Driven to provide the very best supporter experience. Energetic self-starter able to work on own initiative with attention to detail. Dynamic and positive attitude. Creative and innovative thinker. Well-organised, able to prioritise work and meet deadlines. Fully proficient in Microsoft SharePoint and Office 365. Fully proficient in Fundraising databases (CharityCRM would be an advantage but not essential) Solid knowledge of Charity Law and Fundraising regulations Strong interest in or knowledge of wildlife trade and environmental issues Flexibility to work out of hours at a few events through the year.

Want to help shape the future of customer engagement at British Heart Foundation? We're recruiting a Digital Journeys Senior Executives on 12-month fixed-term contracts to support one of our biggest digital transformation programmes. About the role British Heart Foundation is investing in Enterprise Foundations, an organisation-wide transformation programme designed to help us become a more customer-centric organisation through new technology, better use of data and more connected ways of working. As a Digital Journeys Senior Executive, you'll help deliver one of the programme's most significant workstreams: migrating our marketing automation platform from Dotdigital to Adobe and redesigning hundreds of campaigns into customer-centred journeys. You'll own assigned customer journeys from brief through to delivery, translating journey designs into live Adobe builds and configuring audience segmentation, workflow logic, personalisation and automation. Through rigorous testing and optimisation, you'll help ensure every communication delivers a relevant and connected customer experience. Working through a series of transformation sprints, you'll contribute to rebuilding and improving existing campaigns while helping establish new standards, processes and ways of working across the organisation. You'll work closely with colleagues across Digital, Data, Retention and Customer Journeys, gaining valuable experience in marketing automation, customer journey orchestration and digital transformation delivery. Your work will directly influence how we engage audiences and support more people to connect with BHF's mission. About You As our ideal candidate, you'll already have experience designing, building and delivering customer journeys, email campaigns or SMS communications within a marketing automation platform, alongside a strong understanding of audience segmentation, workflow logic and personalisation. You'll bring strong knowledge of customer journey design, marketing automation and campaign delivery, together with experience using customer data to create relevant, targeted communications. Experience with Adobe Campaign or Adobe Journey Optimizer would be beneficial, but we're equally interested in candidates with experience using platforms such as Dotdigital, Salesforce or Braze who are excited to develop their Adobe expertise. You'll be confident translating briefs and requirements into live journey builds, using performance insight to identify improvements and working collaboratively with stakeholders across digital, data, technology and marketing teams. Strong attention to detail, testing and quality assurance will be key to your success. Most importantly, you'll be customer-focused, organised and naturally curious. You'll enjoy learning new technologies, solving problems and finding better ways to create journeys that deliver measurable results. Working arrangements These 12-month fixed-term roles provide additional capacity for the Digital Content & Journeys team during the Enterprise Foundations (EF) transformation programme. These roles will specifically support the migration to Adobe and the building of hundreds of personalised customer journeys through sprint cycles until May 2027, followed by optimisation and hypercare. These roles provide the additional capacity needed to deliver the EF programme’s goals. As this role is linked to a time-limited transformation programme, it is not intended to form part of BHF's ongoing permanent structure beyond completion of the project and associated optimisation activity. Following completion of the programme, responsibility for the ongoing management and optimisation of journeys will sit within the permanent Digital Content & Journeys team. The contract is expected to end after 12 months when the additional funded programme activity and associated resourcing requirement are expected to conclude. This is a hybrid role, where your work will be split between your home and at least one day per week in our London office. This may vary from time to time so you will need to work in a flexible way to unlock your best work for our cause. Interview process The interview process will consist of two stages. We plan for first stage interviews will be held over MS Teams on w/c 28 Sep 26 . For those successful, there will be second stage interviews in-person at our London Office (NW1 7AW) on 08 Oct 2026.

item.title: Individual and Church Giving Lead
item.description: Job description A Rocha UK is a unique Christian nature conservation charity, mobilising Christians and churches to care for the natural world. We are a member of the Worldwide A Rocha Family, a federation of Christian conservation charities, and we have sister organisations in 23 other countries. A Rocha UK has a staff of 25 and many volunteers. We run nature conservation activities on our own reserves, advise a national network of conservation partners, inspire Christians to protect nature and act on climate change through our Wild Christian scheme, and run the popular Eco Church scheme for local churches. Our office is close to overground and tube stations, with its own secure cycle and parking facilities. In 2026 we launched a new three year strategy with exciting goals of deepening our support to those in each of our programmes and increasing our reach in order to see more people equipped to care for creation. We also have a heightened focus on cross-cutting issues of social justice, climate resilience, becoming more prophetic and ensuring we are both learning from and serving all of the UK. Among others, a key enabler to fulfilling this strategy is growing our income from just under £1m to £1.25m by the end of 2028, which this new role will play an important part in. A Rocha UK is engaged with a large Christian constituency (Nearly 23,000 individuals on its e-mail lists, over 9000 churches registered for Eco Church across 25 denominations, over 60 Partners in Action, ranging from Christian conference centres through to community farms, and over 8000 individuals in Wild Christian - for individuals and households looking to live more sustainably). This role is focused on growing Individual and Church giving from this constituency. There is work to do on developing engaging supporter journeys and fundraising appeals. There is also opportunity to develop fundraising propositions and take creative approaches to growing new donors. As well as the opportunity to be involved in developing our Wild Christian programme. For more information please click on the job description below. item.title: Individual Giving and Legacies Manager
item.description: This role is based at the National Greyhound Centre, Horley, Surrey, RH6 9SX, with a minimum of three days in the office and the option to work two days from home. Job role: Each year, thousands of greyhounds across the UK rely on the generosity of supporters of the Greyhound Trust to find safe, loving homes. With an annual income of around £4.5 million, individual giving and gifts in Wills is central to our income generation strategy and this role lead its growth and development. This role is perfect for an experienced fundraiser ready to own the individual giving and gift in Wills strategy end to end. You will set the direction for donor communications, appeals and the legacy pipeline, taking responsibility for income from individual donors and KPIs while working closely with the Head of Income Generation and Engagement to contribute to the overall income generation and engagement strategy. You will take the lead in developing, testing, learning and growing the direct marketing programme and developing supporter journeys both online and offline. You’ll develop our email marketing and online supporter journeys for now and the future. This is a broad, varied role, for a senior fundraiser. Whether your background is strongest in individual giving, community fundraising, legacies, digital or data, if you are a confident communicator with proven experience of owning fundraising strategy, income and supplier relationships ready to take your next step in animal welfare, this is the role for you. Key responsibilities: Lead the development of the individual giving and legacies strategy and annual planning, budgeting and KPIs, reporting performance to the Head of Income Generation. Set the direction for a sustainable individual giving programme, growing the supporter base across all channels and developing strategies to engage and motivate supporters. Own the planning and delivery of engaging, multi-channel fundraising campaigns and appeals. Provide advice and support to branches for one-off lottery or other individual giving initiatives; ensuring compliance with our gambling commission licence nationally and through branches. Lead the ongoing development of the charity’s programme of appeals, regular giving and sponsorship products, lottery and donor development programmes. Maximise digital fundraising opportunities whilst recognising the contribution of non-digital approaches for certain audiences and product types. Own email marketing and online supporter journeys. Lead the legacy giving and in-memory fundraising strategy. Own monthly analysis of income and expenditure against KPIs, reporting on progress and forecasting future results. Design and implement a stewardship programme with particular attention to supporter journeys for new and existing supporters that increase average values and long-term support. Own compliance of the individual giving programme, identifying and managing risk and escalating to the Head of Income Generation and Engagement where necessary. Ensure data collection, management, use, storage and destruction comply with data protection law and best practice. Work closely with other members of staff and senior managment to ensure individual giving products and initiatives are integrated with other areas of the charity, such as brand and marketing programmes, retail development and homing campaigns. Own direct relationships with external suppliers, agencies and freelancers, setting briefs, managing budgets and holding them to account. Act as the organisation’s senior specialist on individual giving and legacies, advising and influencing colleagues, volunteers and homing centres on how their roles can support fundraising opportunities, without formal line authority. Essential skills and experience: Experience of working in a senior individual giving, direct marketing, community, or general fundraising role. Demonstrable track record of delivering sustained income growth and establishing new programmes of activity. Experience owning a budget and KPI set, forecasting, reporting to senior management and adjusting plans in response to performance. Proven ability to get the best out of external suppliers and agencies (copywriters, designers, mailing houses, platform developers, etc.) to maximise outcomes, setting budgets and holding suppliers to account for results. Demonstrable experience of donor development, journeys and stewardship at a strategic level. Proficient written and verbal communicator with the ability to adapt tone to engage and inspire different audiences and write compelling fundraising copy. Excellenet relationship and influencing skills with the ability to gain buy in and shape the approach of colleagues without formal authority over them. Excellent stewardship skills with the ability to communicate with supporters via letter, email, telephone and face to face with care and compassion. Able to plan and prioritise independently across several income streams. Track record of writing clear, engaging supporter communications (appeals, newsletters, thank you journeys). Confident using data to select, segment, or report on supporter groups. Experience managing ongoing relationships with individuals (donors, supporters or clients). Experience of legacy marketing. Proficiency in using a CRM to manage donor relationships and supporter journeys. Strong working knowledge of charity law, GDPR and the Fundraising Code of Practice with experience of ensuring organisational compliance. A collaborative approach and willingness to develop new areas of fundraising. Desirable experience and qualifications: Relevant fundraising or marketing qualification (e.g. Institute of Fundraising / CIOF certificate, CIM), or evidence of ongoing professional development. Experience of legacy marketing, legacy administration, or legacy pipeline management. Experience of writing or approving legacy-specific communications (in-memory, will-writing campaigns, pledger updates). Experience designing and evaluating acquisition or retention campaigns and activity across a variety of offline and digital channels. Experience of building or improving email marketing programmes or automated supporter journeys. Experience of working with fundraising databases (e.g. Raiser's Edge, Donorfy, Beacon) and GDPR-compliant data handling. Experience of liaising with solicitors, executors, or handling sensitive/bereavement-related conversations. Experience of managing a pipeline or CRM-tracked process from enquiry through to completion. Have empathy and enthusiasm for the mission of the Greyhound Trust. You will be required to work or provide support outside of standard working hours for events and operational needs, so flexibility is key. This post and its role requirement will develop with the needs of the charity.

item.title: Youth Programmes Officer
item.description: Youth Programmes Officer Hours: 35 hours per week Reporting to: Youth Programmes Manager About us The Ben Kinsella Trust is one of the UK’s leading anti-knife crime charities. We were set up following the tragic murder of 16-year-old Ben Kinsella in 2008, and everything we do is guided by his legacy. Our mission is to prevent knife crime through education and campaigning. Ben was a kind, creative young person who loved art, music, Arsenal FC, and making people laugh. He had big dreams of becoming a graphic designer. His death was a senseless act of violence, and the outpouring of grief and public support that followed marked the start of a movement. Ben’s own words, written shortly before his death, called for change, and his voice continues to inspire our work. Through immersive workshops in our Choices and Consequences Exhibitions and free online resources, we have reached over 50,000 young people so far. Our work challenges myths about knife crime, strengthens peer influence, and sparks meaningful conversations. As we grow, we remain committed to honouring Ben’s life by making a real, lasting difference to young people across the UK. We’re a small but growing team of 11 (rising to 14), working across Programmes, Fundraising, Communications, Finance and Operations, and Leadership. Our Programmes team is supported by a brilliant pool of freelance facilitators and actors who help bring our workshops to life. We’re now looking for an Youth Programmes Officer to join us at this exciting time. We’re looking for someone who is passionate about evidence-based interventions, thrives in a collaborative environment, and is confident working to establish and maintain relationships with external organisations. Ben’s legacy is our guide – we exist to stop knife crime About the Role We are looking for an education or youth work professional who can deliver our programmes to a very high standard. You will be a skilled facilitator and communicator who can engage with young people from a diverse range of backgrounds. Additionally, we are seeking someone who shares our values and is passionate about using education as a tool to support and empower young people and to stop knife crime. As Youth Programmes Officer you will be responsible for the delivery and coordination of our flagship knife crime prevention workshops to young people, to a high standard. You will work alongside the Programmes team to ensure workshops at our London exhibitions (currently Islington and Barking & Dagenham) operate smoothly and consistently to serve young people through the achievement of quality outcomes and maximised engagement. You will play a key part in the delivery of our Youth Ambassador Programme and contribute to the development of new programmes and opportunities during an exciting period of growth for the charity. Key Responsibilities Programme delivery Deliver workshops to a range of groups (primary, secondary, PRU/AP and adults), adapting to different needs Ensure sessions are engaging, high quality, and responsive to feedback Programme development Gather and analyse feedback to improve programmes Support the development of new projects and resources Workshop coordination Coordinate day-to-day delivery across two sites Manage bookings, enquiries and pre-visit information Maintain strong relationships with schools and partners Keep CRM and booking systems up to date Coordinate freelance facilitators and support their onboarding and training General Carry out other duties as required Person Specification Experience Delivering workshops or training to young people Adapting structured programmes to different needs Managing behaviour and supporting young people with additional needs Coordinating multiple tasks or stakeholders General admin and use of digital systems (Desirable: programme design, training adults, relevant qualification in teaching/youth work) Skills and knowledge Strong facilitation and communication skills Ability to build positive relationships Understanding of youth violence or knife crime Knowledge of inclusive teaching approaches Personal qualities Passionate about supporting young people Reliable, organised and proactive Collaborative and professional Committed to equality, diversity and inclusion Open to learning and continuous improvement Benefits Flexible working where possible 27 days’ annual leave (+ bank holidays), rising with service Enhanced sick pay Pension scheme Cycle to work scheme Development opportunities How to apply Submit a CV and supporting statement outlining how you meet the person specification. Please also answer the two additional questions on the application form. Applications close: Friday 18th September 09:30am Interview schedule: 1st stage, Week Commencing 21st September (Virtual) 2nd stage, Week commencing 28th September 2026 (in person) We reserve the right to close this vacancy early if a suitable candidate is identified, so we encourage early applications.

item.description: Senior Principal Gifts Manager – The British Museum – Location: London – Salary: £54,000 Help shape one of the most ambitious cultural transformation projects of our generation. The British Museum is embarking on a landmark £1.3 billion Masterplan, reimagining one of the world's most iconic cultural institutions for the 21st century while preserving its unique role as a museum for everyone. To support this vision, we are launching a major philanthropic campaign with a target of raising £500 million+. item.title: Admin and Grants Officer
item.description: Could you play a crucial role within our busy and friendly team and take responsibility for managing our benevolent fund? We are looking to recruit an Administration and Grants Officer to support the output of our HQ, including benevolent fund caseload management, member support, and general Association output. Some travel is expected to support membership events inc. evenings & weekends, with occasional overnight stays. We offer generous holiday entitlement, 6% employer pension contribution, free parking, access to gym/swimming pool, canteen, café and shop. We are the UK’s largest membership organisation of female veterans and serving women - a financially sustainable £8m charity which aims to provide camaraderie, benevolence and support to women who have served in the Army. Additionally, we aim to exert influence within the military charity sector to broaden support for all female veterans of the UK Armed Forces. Our benevolent fund awards over £200k in grants per year to an average of 120 applicants, from minor requests to major grants, and annual maintenance. We organise both national and local events for our members to attend where they meet up with old friends, remember those we have lost, support each other, have fun and make new and lasting memories. We have approaching 5000 active members which we hope to grow as we reach out to many more female veterans eligible to join our Association. You will: have experience of working in a member or public-facing organisation, supporting and liaising with a diverse cohort of individuals in a wide variety of interests and needs have experience of managing caseloads and carrying out detailed casework have a sound knowledge of how individual grants are awarded have a strong understanding of the work of SSAFA, TRBL & other caseworking and almonising agencies understand the value of strong communication and be experienced in engaging people from many walks of life, tailoring your communication style to a variety of audiences be skilled at building positive working relationships, with a friendly and engaging manner be highly organised with great attention to detail, and work well within a small staff team where each team member is expected to pitch in and work collaboratively Be engaging and welcoming, able to attend events and interact with members of the public The charity is governed by a Board of Trustees with a number of sub-committees, all volunteers. We are a small staff team of 5, led by a CEO, who are motivated by the good work we do to support some amazing, brave and pioneering women. We are proud of the work we do to support female veterans, many of whom are now well into retirement. Some have fallen on hard times and need our financial support, whilst others may be lonely or have reduced mobility, and rely on our association to keep them in touch with like-minded comrades. We are an inclusive employer seeking to attract and employ the best people from the widest talent pool, committed to supporting our staff and the female veterans we serve. All applicants must be able to demonstrate current eligibility to work in the UK. If you are a motivated, self-starting and engaging individual with a passion for working with people and supporting their needs, then we look forward to receiving your application by way of a CV and a detailed supporting statement demonstrating your suitability for the role with regard to the above person specification.

item.title: North-West GCSE Resits Senior Programme Coordinator
item.description: Our charity delivers a series of interventions that help disadvantaged learners in Further Education to secure gateway English and maths qualifications that unlock opportunities. These interventions include our award-winning GCSE Resit Tuition Programme, for those resitting GCSEs, our Functional Skills Tuition Programme, supporting those on or aspiring to undertake apprenticeship programmes, and training and resources to support teachers and leaders of English and maths in Further Education. Our benefits include: About the role As a Senior Programme Coordinator, you will lead the day-to-day delivery across a portfolio of partner colleges. Acting as the main point of contact for students, tutors and college staff, you will build strong working relationships, maintain a consistent on-site presence and ensure programmes are delivered smoothly, professionally and in line with agreed standards and KPIs. You will take ownership of programme performance across your portfolio, with a particular focus on student enrolment, attendance, and session dosage targets. You will oversee programme logistics, monitor delivery quality, and work proactively to maximise student participation and tutor effectiveness. This role requires strong organisational skills, attention to detail and the ability to respond quickly and effectively to operational challenges. You will also play an important role in maintaining high-quality partnerships with colleges, ensuring stakeholders receive clear communication, accurate reporting and responsive support throughout programme delivery. Alongside this, you will contribute to wider organisational priorities, including safeguarding, tutor development, programme improvement and initiatives that strengthen student outcomes. As a Senior Programme Coordinator, you will be expected to role model best practice to the wider Programme Coordinator team, working collaboratively to problem solve, and work with your Programme Manager to ensure strategic approaches to meeting KPIs. This is a highly collaborative, delivery-focused role suited to someone who enjoys a challenge, is confident managing relationships. MAIN DUTIES & RESPONSIBILITIES See recruitment pack ABOUT YOU You will: Thrive in a busy, fast-paced environment and enjoy managing multiple priorities effectively. Be passionate about improving outcomes for young people, with a genuine commitment to tackling educational inequality. Enjoy working collaboratively with colleagues, tutors and college partners to achieve shared goals. Be comfortable working independently, taking ownership of your workload and delivering results with minimal supervision. Demonstrate initiative and a proactive approach, identifying opportunities and resolving challenges effectively. Be highly organised, detail-oriented and able to manage competing demands without compromising quality. Take accountability for your work and be confident making decisions and driving progress. Be resilient, adaptable and solutions-focused when responding to challenges. Be motivated by working in a mission-driven organisation where your contribution has a direct impact on learners' success and future opportunities. You will be able to expense your travel for this interview. item.title: Senior Legacy Marketing Manager
item.description: Compassion in World Farming International is a global movement transforming the future of food and farming. Lead our UK and international legacy marketing programme and help inspire supporters to leave a lasting gift for farm animals, people and the planet. Senior Legacy Marketing Manager (UK and International) Role type: Full time; Permanent Location: Godalming, Surrey - HQ. Hybrid working pattern 2x days per week in the office: Tuesdays & Thursdays. The office is located close to Godalming station, with direct trains from/to London Waterloo in approximately 45 minutes. Salary: £45,000 to £50,000 per annum (depending upon skills and experience) About the role As our Senior Legacy Marketing Manager (UK and International), you’ll lead the strategic development and delivery of Compassion in World Farming’s legacy marketing programme across the UK and internationally. This is a vital role within our Global Fundraising team, helping to shape a sector leading legacy strategy that inspires supporters to leave a lasting gift for farm animals and the planet. As part of this exciting role, you’ll be responsible for: Legacy strategy and coordination – Leading the development of Compassion’s UK and international legacy marketing strategy, reporting on KPIs and identifying opportunities to strengthen engagement and investment. UK legacy marketing delivery – Overseeing and delivering legacy communications across direct mail, email, social media, website content, events, supporter engagement and promotional campaigns. International legacy delivery – Supporting fundraising teams in France, Italy, the Netherlands, Spain, the USA and Poland to deliver locally relevant legacy campaigns, content, training and enquiry handling. Supporter care – Responding sensitively and efficiently to legacy enquiries and helping colleagues feel confident talking to supporters about gifts in wills. About you To succeed as our Senior Legacy Marketing Manager (UK and International), you’ll be a confident and strategic legacy marketing professional with a strong track record of delivering impactful campaigns that inspire supporters to leave a very special gift. You’ll bring a deep understanding of legacy fundraising, ideally gained within the charity or NGO sector, and feel comfortable working across both UK and international markets. You’ll be highly organised, proactive and detail-oriented, with the ability to craft compelling messages for direct response and manage multi-channel campaigns. Skills and experience you’ll need to bring as part of this role: Track record and knowledge of legacy marketing and legacy strategy, ideally as a practitioner. Strong understanding of direct marketing, digital marketing or supporter fundraising, with excellent copywriting and creative skills. Proven strategic planning skills, with the ability to manage budgets, suppliers, data and reporting. Experience of working collaboratively with international teams across multiple countries and time zones. Ability to engage supporters with sensitivity, care and confidence, including through legacy events and enquiry handling. Proficiency in relevant fundraising or database systems, ideally Salesforce CRM. A demonstrable interest in farm animal welfare issues and Compassion’s mission. If you don’t meet every requirement but believe you could thrive in this role, we encourage you to apply. Why join us This is a rare opportunity to lead a global legacy marketing programme that directly supports a mission to end factory farming. We offer a supportive, flexible workplace with a strong focus on wellbeing and development, including: 25 days annual leave + bank holidays Health Cash Back Plan and 24/7 GP access Employee Assistance Programme and MHFA support Premium Calm App subscription Electric car scheme available Defined contribution pension scheme Enhanced discretionary sick pay Hybrid working model (role and location dependent) Free onsite parking and office next to mainline station Cycle Benefit scheme and other savings options Ongoing learning and development opportunities How to apply and key dates If you’re ready to make a global impact, we’d love to hear from you. Please submit your CV and a cover letter outlining how you meet the Person Specification. To support a fair and unbiased recruitment process, we kindly ask that you do not include a photo in your CV. Please note that we may begin interviews on a rolling basis, so early applications are encouraged. Closing date: 29 September 2026 1stStage (Teams) Interview 2ndStage (Face to Face at HQ) Interview, with task “ Join us in building a more compassionate future for animals, people, and the planet.” As part of Stage 1 interviews, shortlisted candidates may, for some roles, receive pre‑shared, values‑based interview questions to support a positive candidate experience. If you require any adjustments during the recruitment process, please let us know, we’re always happy to support candidates. About Compassion Compassion in World Farming International is a leading global organisation working to end factory farming. Founded in 1967 by British farmer Peter Roberts, we’ve spent over 50 years driving change, successfully campaigning to ban cruel practices such as barren battery cages, veal crates, and sow stalls across the UK and Europe. Our work combines advocacy, campaigning, and collaboration with policymakers and businesses to promote animal welfare and sustainable food systems. We envision a future where animals are treated with compassion, and farming supports both people and the planet. To learn more about our mission, culture, and opportunities, please explore our Candidate Pack, and Careers Page on our website. To comply with legal requirements in the UK and internationally, all applicants must be able to demonstrate their right to work in the country where the role is based. Compassion in World Farming is absolutely committed to providing equal opportunities for everyone regardless of their background. We value diversity and live experience and acknowledge the underrepresentation of people from certain backgrounds, both within our organisation and across the sector. We welcome applications from underrepresented groups, whether these be of ethnicity, gender, identity, religion, physical ability, sexual orientation or other.

item.title: Trusts and Grants Fundraiser
item.description: JOB TITLE: Trusts and Grants Fundraiser SALARY: £35,447 per annum HOURS: Full-time - 36 hours per week LOCATION: Sydenham Site, 51-59 Lawrie Park Road, London SE26 6DZ with occasional work at the Orpington site, Tregony Road BR6 9XA Please note that this position includes occasional evening and weekend working. About Us This is a fantastic opportunity to work at a leading Hospice who aspires to a world in which all dying people and those close to them have access to care and support, whenever and wherever they need it. St Christopher’s Hospice was founded in 1967 by Dame Cicely Saunders, and became the first hospice of the modern hospice movement. We provide invaluable care and support to over 7,500 people across the five London Boroughs of Bromley, Croydon, Lambeth, Lewisham and Southwark. The work of the hospice extends beyond care to the local community. St Christopher’s Professional Learning offer continues to advance national and global leadership in palliative care through a range of impactful initiatives. Other programmes include supporting and shaping palliative care leaders of the future. The fundraising team generates more than £10m every year, around half of which comes through gifts left to the charity as legacies. We organise a programme of appeals, campaigns and events, administer our own lottery, make applications to charitable foundations, engage with local business and support individuals who give in-memory of a loved one. This is delivered by a strong employed fundraising team, supported by a number of wonderful volunteers. Your new role We are looking for an experienced Trusts and Grants Fundraiser to join our friendly and dedicated team. If you are detail oriented, highly organised, and able to manage multiple tasks and deadlines with confidence — and if you’re motivated by making a real difference to end of life care for patients across five London boroughs and beyond — this could be the perfect role for you. In this hands-on position, you will have the opportunity to shape and grow our income from trusts, foundations and charitable funders. You will be responsible for researching, writing and submitting high quality funding applications, nurturing relationships with existing supporters, identifying new funding opportunities, and ensuring that all communications reflect our mission and impact. About you: We’re looking for someone who: Wants a fulfilling role where their work genuinely makes a difference. Enjoys a challenge, is proactive in solving problems, and is self motivated. Values being part of a supportive team working together towards a shared purpose. If this sounds like you – we’d love to hear from you. What you will get in return is a stimulating and rewarding career with an opportunity to influence and make a real difference on a local, national and global scale. In addition, you will benefit from access to excellent training and development opportunities, a number of health and wellbeing schemes, a competitive contributory pension scheme and life assurance scheme with generous beneficiary plan. You will also have access to free on street parking nearby and an onsite staff canteen at our Sydenham site. What you need to do now if you have experience in driving significant income through trusts and grants and you have initiative, enthusiasm and passion for the work of a hospice, please do apply for this great role. How to apply: Please review the Job Description and Person Specification Criteria Please address the criteria in the person specification form. This information will be used to select candidates for interview Click the ‘Apply Online’ button To find out more about St Christopher’s Hospice please have a look at our website. item.title: Complex Needs Caseworker
item.description: Are you a creative person looking for role where you can make a lasting difference to people experiencing homelessness in Oxford? This post is offered as a 12 month fixed term contract until 11 October 2027, or secondment for internal staff (maternity cover) We are looking for a Complex Caseworker to join our Rough Sleeper team in Oxford who provide intensive support to people with complex needs experiencing homelessness. This passionate team offer person centred support service to help people who require a specialist intervention approach to support them through the transition from rough sleeping into sustainable accommodation. In this role you will work collaboratively with the Rough Sleeper Navigator Coordinator and Outreach team as well as relevant partner agencies in Oxford to deliver sustainable outcomes to clients. You will advocate for clients who have been some of the most marginalised in the local area, to make a real and long lasting difference to their recovery. You will be responsible for overseeing a caseload of clients and providing day to day support to clients with their transition from the streets into accommodation and independent living with a strong focus on tenancy sustainment and rescue. This includes working with people on health, housing, employment and training support. You will be given support to build strong relationships with a range of other services to find creative and sustainable routes to recovery for clients. You’re typical working hours will be Monday – Friday, with flexibility to work outside of these hours at times to support the team through SWEP. About you Above all we are looking for people who share our values; who are passionate about supporting our clients to sustain their recovery. Even if you don’t think you match 100 % of the criteria, we would still like to hear from you as we value transferable skills. Potential can be equally as important as experience, so if you think you have what it takes, please do apply! If you have good communication skills, with the ability to network and build effective relationships with a variety of people, You should have a good working understanding of supporting vulnerable with complex needs, such as substance use, mental and physical health issues, and the ability to understand the difficulties they experience in accessing services that full meet their needs. We will provide you with support, supervision and training so that you can develop the necessary skills to offer a high quality service to clients. St Mungo's are committed to creating a diverse and inclusive workplace. We strongly encourage applications from all under-represented groups. How to apply To view the job description and guidance on completing your application form, please click on the ‘document’ tab on the advert page on our website. To find out more and apply please go to the St Mungo’s careers page on our website. Closing date: 10am on 23 September 2026 Interview and assessments on 6-9 October 2026 What we offer Excellent Development and Growth Opportunities A Diverse and Inclusive Workplace Great Pay and Other Benefits

item.title: Process Analyst
item.description: Are you an experienced Business or Process Analyst who enjoys untangling complex systems, understanding how data really works and finding better ways to connect the dots? Great Ormond Street Hospital Charity is looking for a Process Analyst to help us build a clearer, more joined-up understanding of how data moves through our organisation. This is a hands-on, data-focused role. You'll work across systems, teams and processes to map how information is captured, transformed and used; identify where things break down; and help create clearer rules and more sustainable ways of working. You'll need to be comfortable getting into the detail of data, asking challenging questions and working closely with technical and non-technical colleagues to turn complexity into practical solutions. Salary The salary for this role is £48,192 per annum and this is a 12 month fixed term contract. We operate a hybrid working policy of a minimum of 2 days per week in the office. In line with our EDI strategy and Total Reward policy, we calculate our salaries based on benchmarking data across the charity sector. To ensure fairness for existing staff and new joiners, we do not offer salaries above the advertised rate. Key Responsibilities Build an end-to-end view of our data landscape, documenting how systems connect, how data moves between them and where key dependencies sit. Map complex data flows and business processes across platforms including Salesforce, Snowflake, Marketing Cloud and other connected systems. Identify duplication, manual workarounds, data quality issues and points of failure, digging into root causes rather than simply fixing individual problems. Help establish clear and consistent business definitions, data rules and governance across areas such as matching, deduplication, consent, retention and data ownership. Work with stakeholders to understand the business need before considering the technology solution, constructively challenging existing assumptions and ways of working. Translate complex business and data requirements into clear process maps, requirements, user stories and documentation that technical teams can use. Work closely with Data Management, Data Engineering, Salesforce and business teams to turn findings into practical improvements across systems and processes. Support new integrations, testing and implementation, ensuring changes work effectively across the whole data lifecycle rather than solving one part of the process in isolation. Create clear documentation that strengthens organisational knowledge and reduces reliance on individual or undocumented technical knowledge. Skills, Knowledge and Expertise Experience working as a Business Analyst, Process Analyst, Data Management Analyst or in a similar role involving complex systems and data. Strong experience mapping and documenting end-to-end business processes, system interactions or data flows. Experience working across integrated systems such as CRM, data warehouse, marketing automation or other enterprise platforms. Strong analytical and problem-solving skills, with the ability to investigate problems, identify root causes and recommend sustainable improvements. An understanding of data management concepts such as data quality, governance, business rules, data lineage and ownership. Strong stakeholder management and facilitation skills, with the confidence to ask challenging questions and constructively challenge established ways of working. Ability to translate between business and technical teams, making complex requirements clear and understandable. Strong documentation and process-mapping skills, with the ability to bring structure and clarity to ambiguous or complex problems. Experience with Salesforce, Snowflake or Marketing Cloud would be useful, but specific platform expertise isn't essential. DBS - note a basic DBS check is required for this role How to Apply Please click on the apply button in the top right-hand corner where you will be taken to a short application form to complete. Closing date: 23 September 2026 Applications will be reviewed on an ongoing basis and we reserve the right to close the roles prior to the closing date should suitable applicants be found. Therefore, you are encouraged to apply early to avoid disappointment.

item.description: Head of Earned, Shared and Paid Digital (2666) Location: Oxford UK/ (with the ability to work from home under Oxfam GB's hybrid working arrangements) Workplace Type: Hybrid Hours: 36 hours per week Salary: £49,601 with a discretionary range up to £56,518 depending on experience Job Family: Communications Division: CEO Office Grade: B Job Type: Open ended Closing Date: 30 September 2026 Country: United Kingdom Oxfam is a global movement of people working together to end the injustice of poverty. The Role: As Oxfam's Head of Earned, Shared and Paid Digital, you will work collaboratively across teams to shape the strategic direction for how Oxfam earns attention, engages audiences, and grows its reach across organic social, paid digital and channels beyond our own. Together, you'll ensure that this engagement translates into income, influence and long-term support for our mission. You will lead and empower our organic social and paid digital teams, holding oversight of day-to-day activity while focusing on elevating and optimising our channel, platform, targeting and digital marketing strategies. You will support your teams to deliver brilliantly by setting a clear creative direction, providing strong editorial and brand stewardship, and embedding a data-led approach to performance and learning. You'll create the space, confidence and connections that enable teams to think beyond individual channels and deliver integrated, audience-focused work. Working closely with the Head of Digital and Head of Owned Digital, you will help shape Oxfam's wider digital strategy and strengthen our impact across the organisation. By building strong relationships with colleagues and stakeholders, you will bring audience insight into campaigning, fundraising and public engagement activity, ensuring digital expertise informs decision-making and positioning the team as a trusted strategic partner. If you have any questions about the role, we'd love to hear from you.Please e-mail us at , making sure you include the job title and reference number of the role you're asking about.Please be aware we are unable to accept CVs or applications via e-mail.To apply, please use the "apply now" button on the right hand side of this advertisement. What we are looking for: We’re looking for a candidate who cares about Oxfam's mission to end poverty and is personally aligned to our feminist principles and values of empowerment, accountability and inclusion in all you do. An ideal candidate for the role will also have: Experience of managing a multi-disciplinary team and the performance of others Lived experience (s) or evidence of learning/taking action on anti-racism and inequalities. Strong knowledge of digital platforms, marketing technologies and industry trends. A proven track record of growing income, influence and audience engagement through digital channels, ideally within the charity, campaigning or wider social impact sector. Proven experience of crisis and reputation management within digital channels. Proven success in developing audience-led digital strategies and integrated campaigns across earned, shared and paid channels that deliver measurable impact. Excellent stakeholder management skills, experienced in proactive collaboration across organisations. Outstanding communication skills, with the ability to engage, inspire and influence a wide range of audiences. A strong commitment to Oxfam's values. We offer: We offer a competitive salary and a range of additional benefits to staff including flexible working options, generous pension scheme, annual leave, additional leave allowances, company sick pay, life assurance and a range of other benefits. From the day you join Oxfam we invite you to stretch and learn in your role. Our wide range of Learning & Development opportunities includes in-house courses, e-learning modules, on-the job learning opportunities, coaching and mentoring, and much more. You can read more about all Oxfam has to offer Flexfam: We believe flexible working is key to building the Oxfam of the future, so we’re open to talking through the type of flexible arrangements which might work for you. How to apply: As part of your online application, please upload your up to date CV and Cover Letter explaining your suitability against the essential criteria in the job profile. Our values and commitment to safeguarding Oxfam is committed to preventing any type of unwanted behaviour at work including sexual harassment, exploitation and abuse, lack of integrity and financial misconduct; and committed to promoting the welfare of children, young people, adults and beneficiaries with whom Oxfam GB engages. Oxfam expects all staff and volunteers to share this commitment through our code of conduct. We place a high priority on ensuring that only those who share and demonstrate our are recruited to work for us. The post holder will undertake the appropriate level of training and is responsible for ensuring that they understand and work within the safeguarding policies of the organisation. All offers of employment will be subject to satisfactory references and appropriate screening checks, which can include criminal records and terrorism finance checks. Oxfam GB also participates in the .In line with this Scheme, we will request information from job applicants’ previous employers about any findings of sexual exploitation, sexual abuse and/or sexual harassment during employment, or incidents under investigation when the applicant left employment. By submitting an application, the job applicant confirms his/her understanding of these recruitment procedures. We are committed to ensuring diversity and gender equality within our organisation and encourage applicants from diverse backgrounds to apply. About us Oxfam is a global community who believe poverty isn’t inevitable. It’s an injustice that can be overcome. We are shop volunteers, women’s right activists, marathon runners, aid workers, coffee farmers, street fundraisers, goat herders, policy experts, campaigners, water engineers and more. And we won’t stop until everyone can live life without poverty for good. is a member of of 21 organisations working together with partners and local communities in the areas of humanitarian, development and campaigning, in more than 90 countries. A thriving diverse Oxfam: It’s people power that brings about change. To play our part as a global organisation working to overcome poverty and inequality, we need equality, diversity and inclusion across our community of staff, partners and volunteers. Together, we’re committed to becoming a more diverse workforce, better able to tackle the global challenges that face our world today. To do that: We need to dismantle the unequal power structures that exist everywhere, this including Oxfam and the wider development and charity sectors. We need an inclusive Oxfam where everyone can bring who they are to our work and feels celebrated for the differences they bring. We want and need everyone, and that means we need you .

item.title: Policy Officer
item.description: Job description About the British Society for Heart Failure The British Society for Heart Failure (BSH) is the UK's leading charity and membership organisation dedicated to improving care for people living with heart failure. We bring together healthcare professionals, researchers and decision-makers to improve prevention, diagnosis, treatment and long-term outcomes through education, awareness, research and policy influence. This is an exciting time to join BSH as we deliver our ambitious new strategy and continue to drive forward our national 25in25 campaign to reduce mortality from heart failure and improve outcomes for patients across the UK. About the Role This is a high-profile opportunity to shape and deliver BSH's policy agenda and strengthen its influence across the healthcare sector. Reporting to the Chief Executive, you will work with clinical leaders, parliamentarians, NHS stakeholders and partner organisations to ensure BSH remains a credible and influential voice on heart failure policy. You will help develop evidence-based policy positions, influence decision-makers and support improvements in heart failure prevention, diagnosis and care across the UK. Key Responsibilities Lead the delivery and development of BSH's policy framework and priorities. Develop policy papers, briefings, consultation responses and stakeholder communications. Build relationships with parliamentarians, NHS leaders, policymakers and healthcare organisations. Represent BSH at meetings, consultations, forums and policy discussions. Identify opportunities to influence policy and improve outcomes for people living with heart failure. Work collaboratively with partner organisations on advocacy, campaigns and policy development. Monitor the healthcare and policy landscape, identifying emerging issues and opportunities. Support wider organisational activity including communications, events and strategic initiatives. Our Commitment to Inclusion We welcome applications from people of all backgrounds and experiences. If you're excited by this opportunity but don't meet every requirement, we'd still encourage you to apply. As this role is primarily remote we also encourage applicants from any location in the UK that enables occassional travel into London and elsewhere in the UK. We’re investing in growth, but we’re realistic about what that means and what it will take to get there, and we want to have fun along the way and provide opportunities for people to progress and grow as we do. Some of the main duties of this role include: Win new business, develop relationships, and provide first class stewardship and account management across a mixed high-value portfolio of trusts, foundations and philanthropists to support RSBC’s income generation growth Working closely with the High Value Lead to develop plans for account management and new business across your portfolio Compose tailored funding proposals to support RSBCs strategic goals and objectives Develop compelling cases for support and assist the testing of new approaches, including working with the service delivery and support teams to ensure detailed knowledge of the organisation’s activities, outcomes and impact to translate into compelling asks Proactively and creatively identify high value funding opportunities and cultivate new funding relationships, working with colleagues across the charity The ideal candidate Our idea candidate will be skilled and experienced in writing compelling proposals for funding; will have strong interpersonal skills and able to build warm, trusting relationships with funders; excellent knowledge of the high value landscape; and proven ability of achieving income targets. item.title: Head of Marketing & Communications
item.description: ABOUT THE ROLE The Head of Marketing and Communications will strategically lead Trees for Cities’ marketing and communications to grow reach, influence and engagement, delivering agreed organisational objectives, OKRs and KPIs. This role leads the strategic direction and delivery of Trees for Cities’ marketing and communications function, ensuring campaigns, communications and audience engagement activities support organisational objectives and deliver measurable growth. The postholder oversees team performance, external partners, media relations, fundraising communications and marketing for the Trees for Streets programme, while driving audience development, supporter stewardship and digital innovation. As a senior leader, they contribute to organisational strategy, provide expert communications counsel, manage budgets and resources, and foster a high-performing, inclusive team culture that strengthens the organisation’s profile, reputation and long-term impact. ABOUT TREES FOR CITIES Trees for Cities is an ambitious, far-reaching organisation. Trees for Cities is the only charity that focuses on planting, protecting and promoting urban trees across the UK. We are a rapidly growing and developing organisation that suits ambitious, dedicated and passionate staff. ABOUT YOU This is an exciting opportunity for a strategic, creative and purpose-driven marketing and communications leader who wants to use their skills to help our vital work to plant and establish urban trees where they are needed the most. As our Head of Marketing and Communications, you'll be a confident and inspiring leader with a proven track record of growing audiences, building influential brands and delivering impactful multi-channel campaigns. You'll be equally comfortable shaping long-term strategy as rolling up your sleeves to make things happen, bringing energy, creativity and commercial awareness to everything you do. We're looking for someone who can spot opportunities, tell compelling stories and build meaningful engagement with supporters, partners, policymakers and the public. You'll have strong experience across marketing, communications, PR, digital engagement and brand management, alongside excellent stakeholder management skills and the ability to lead and develop a high-performing team. Most importantly, you'll be motivated by our mission. As the climate and biodiversity crisis intensifies, urban trees have never been more important. They help cool our cities, improve health and wellbeing, support biodiversity and create greener, more resilient communities. We need an ambitious communications leader who can raise our profile, inspire action and help grow a movement that puts trees at the heart of healthier cities for everyone. Key skills and experience: Strategic marketing and communications leadership Audience growth, brand development and campaign delivery Media relations, PR, thought leadership and reputation management Digital marketing, audience insight and data-led decision making Team leadership, coaching and people development Stakeholder, partner and agency management Budget and project management A passion for creating positive environmental and social impact Trees for Cities is committed to the principles of equal opportunity. We value diversity and are committed to promoting diversity within the workplace. We aim to ensure that our employees achieve their full potential and that all employment decisions, including recruitment, are taken without reference to irrelevant or discriminatory criteria. A full copy of our Equal Opportunities Policy can be provided on request. HOW TO APPLY Please visit our website to view full job description. To apply, use the application link on our website to submit your CV and supporting statement (no more than 2 sides of A4) outlining why you are interested in the role and your fit with the Person Specification. Please note we are unable to provide visa sponsorship for this role, you must therefore have a valid right to work in the UK to apply. The deadline to apply is: 11.59pm on 30th September Interviews are scheduled for: w/c 12th October Please note that we reserve the right to close this vacancy early if we receive a high volume of applications. Therefore, early submission is encouraged. If you are shortlisted for interview, you will normally be contacted within two weeks after applying. If you do not hear from us within this period, then you should assume that on this occasion you have not been selected for interview. Trees for Cities is the first UK environmental organisation to have been awarded social value management certification. Trees for Cities is an equal opportunities employer. Registered Charity No: 1032154. No Agencies Please.

As an Independent Visitor you will be required to complete and report on settings via independent visits The purpose of this role is to ensure that judgements are consistent with evidence provided and that the feedback given is an element of continuous improvement. Experience and an understanding of child and adult safeguarding procedures. Experience of quality assuring reports for regulatory bodies. Ability to analyse a range of information to assess effective evidence-based judgements of reports. Proven experience of using QA to improve report writing. item.title: Community Outreach Worker
item.description: We are looking for an enthusiastic, compassionate and dedicated Community Outreach Worker to join our experienced team, supporting adults with acquired brain injuries across Leicester, Leicestershire and Rutland. This is a varied and rewarding role, providing information, advice, guidance and practical support to individuals who may be facing significant health, social and emotional challenges following a brain injury. You will help people to identify appropriate support and work towards greater independence, confidence and wellbeing. You will work closely with individuals, their families and carers, as well as a wide range of health, social care, public and voluntary sector organisations, helping to ensure people receive the right support at the right time. No two days will be the same. The role involves working independently in the community and travelling throughout Leicester, Leicestershire and Rutland, so flexibility and the ability to organise and manage your own workload are essential. We are looking for someone with excellent communication and interpersonal skills, a person-centred approach and the confidence to work with people in sometimes complex or sensitive circumstances. If you are motivated by helping people rebuild their lives following brain injury and would like to be part of a supportive and committed team, we would love to hear from you. item.title: Customer Engagement Business Partner
item.description: Customer and Community Engagement Business Partner Rochdale £37,326 Permanent, 36.25 hours per week Our client is looking for an enthusiastic and proactive Engagement Business Partner who is great at building relationships, to work with customers, colleagues and communities across the Borough. You will identify and create innovative and new engagement opportunities, helping to strengthen customer influence and driving real and meaningful improvements About the Role The Customer Engagement Business Partner plays a key part in their Customer Experience team and reports to the Community Engagement and Investment Manager. You'll help bring our engagement opportunities to life by developing meaningful opportunities for customers to shape, influence and scrutinise services. They are keen to increase uptake in our engagement activities so you’ll be comfortable using a variety of communication channels to encourage people to take part. From organising and facilitating engagement events and focus groups, to creating digital content and sharing outcomes, you'll help ensure customer feedback drives continuous improvement. As part of this role, you will regularly travel across the Borough of Rochdale to engage directly with customers and communities, therefore a full UK driving licence and access to a vehicle insured for business use is essential. You will be reimbursed for business mileage What You'll Be Doing Supporting the delivery of the Customer Engagement plan Creating and delivering meaningful engagement opportunities for customers and our communities. Working collaboratively with customers and colleagues to improve services. Developing innovative ways for customers to influence, monitor and scrutinise service delivery. Building inclusive engagement approaches that encourage participation from a diverse range of customers. Facilitating meetings, workshops, focus groups and consultation activities. Creating engaging communications content across digital, social media and other channels. Monitoring engagement activity and outcomes, ensuring customers understand how their feedback has influenced decisions. Supporting colleagues across the organisation to embed customer engagement and involvement into service delivery. Using insights and feedback to identify opportunities for service improvement. About You You'll be passionate about customer engagement and committed to ensuring they have the opportunity to influence the services that matter to them. You'll bring: Experience in customer engagement, community engagement, customer service or a related field. Excellent written and verbal communication skills. Strong presentation and facilitation skills, with the confidence to engage a range of audiences. Experience of developing positive relationships with customers and stakeholders from diverse backgrounds. The ability to manage competing priorities and work effectively across multiple projects. Experience delivering and monitoring projects and initiatives. A creative approach to communications and engagement, including digital and social media platforms. Confidence using Microsoft Office applications, including Word, Excel and PowerPoint. Knowledge of customer engagement and participation principles within housing or related sectors. A genuine interest in customer engagement, service improvement and social impact. Awareness and understanding of the issues affecting customers and communities. This is a fantastic opportunity to be part of an ambitious programme of engagement at a time when the voices of their customers have never been more important. You'll help shape how our client works with customers, ensuring their experiences and insights influence decision-making at every level. You'll join a supportive and passionate Customer Experience team where your ideas, enthusiasm and expertise will make a genuine difference to customers and communities across the Borough. What Do They Have to Offer You? In addition to a competitive salary, you will benefit from: 30 days annual leave plus bank holidays Option to buy up to 5 additional days annual leave An additional 5 days annual leave after 5 years' service Business mileage reimbursement Pension scheme with employer contributions matched up to 8%; death in service benefit Flexible, smart working arrangements Healthcare cashback plan, virtual GP access and subsidised gym membership Employee Assistance Programme available 24/7 Paid volunteering days Enhanced family-friendly policies Plus, so much more! We encourage you to apply as soon as possible, as we review applications as they are received and our client may close the advert earlier than indicated.
