item.title: Digital Marketing Officer
item.description: Join us in using good food to create fuller plates, stronger communities and transformed lives across the Midlands Job Title: D igital Marketing Officer Reporting to: Senior Marketing & Communications Manager Location: Flexible within the Midlands, with regular travel around the region required. Birmingham, Leicester or Nottingham base with hybrid/home working available. Hours: 37.5 hours per week Benefits: 25 days holiday, pro-rata, 5.5% Employer Pension Contribution including Life Cover, Occupational Sick Pay Benefits & Enhanced Maternity, Adoption and Paternity Leave and Pay, plus more Contract: Permanent Salary: £27,845 per annum About FareShare Midlands FareShare Midlands rescues good-quality surplus food and gets it to people experiencing hardship through hundreds of community organisations across the region. Last year, we redistributed more than 5,000 tonnes of food – the equivalent of 11 million meals – reaching around 60,000 people every week. But our impact goes beyond food. We strengthen communities, create opportunities through our SkillsShare employability programmes, and help protect our planet by reducing food waste. Over the next three years, we aim to double the food we rescue and extend our impact across the Midlands. Good food can do extraordinary things. The Role We are looking for a creative, enthusiastic and hands-on Digital Marketing Officer to join our Marketing & Communications team during an exciting period of growth and development for FareShare Midlands. Working closely with the Senior Marketing & Communications Manager and colleagues across our MarComms, Fundraising and Corporate Partnerships teams, you will help us reach new audiences, tell compelling stories about our impact and inspire people and organisations to support our work. This is a varied role with plenty of opportunity to develop your digital marketing skills. You will work across our website, social media, Google Ads, email marketing and digital campaigns, as well as helping us capture and share powerful video-led stories from across FareShare Midlands. A particular focus will be supporting activity that helps generate the partnerships and resources needed to sustain and grow our impact. This includes individual fundraising, corporate partnerships, events and other campaigns designed to engage supporters and inspire action. We don't expect you to be an expert in everything from day one. We're looking for someone with good digital marketing foundations, strong content and communication skills and the enthusiasm to develop further. You might already be particularly strong in social media, video, websites or digital campaigns and be looking for an opportunity to broaden your experience across the digital marketing mix. You'll receive support from an experienced MarComms team, while having the opportunity to take ownership of your own activity and develop specialist skills in areas such as WordPress, Google Ads, digital fundraising and performance marketing. This could be a great next step for someone who has gained practical digital marketing experience and is ready for a role where their work can make a visible difference. Key Responsibilities Digital Campaigns, Fundraising & Partnerships Work with MarComms, Fundraising and Corporate Partnerships colleagues to plan and deliver engaging digital marketing activity. Support fundraising campaigns and appeals, helping to attract new supporters and engage existing donors. Develop digital content and campaigns to support corporate partnerships, lead generation and engagement with businesses. Support the promotion of fundraising, corporate and other relevant events. Help tailor messaging, content and calls to action for different audiences, including donors, businesses, partners and supporters. Support integrated campaigns across website, social media, email, digital advertising and other communications channels. Work with external agencies and partners on campaigns where appropriate. Use campaign results and audience insight to understand what works and help improve future activity. Website & WordPress Support the day-to-day management and development of the FareShare Midlands website. Create, edit and update website content, campaign pages and landing pages. Help ensure website content is engaging, accessible, up to date and easy for different audiences to navigate. Work with our external web/digital partners on technical developments and improvements where required. Apply good practice in areas such as SEO, accessibility, user experience and conversion. Use website analytics and audience behaviour to help identify opportunities for improvement. Google Ads & Paid Digital Support the day-to-day management of FareShare Midlands' Google Ads activity. Help create, monitor and optimise campaigns supporting fundraising, corporate engagement and wider organisational priorities. Monitor performance and use data to help improve targeting, messaging and results. Support paid social advertising activity alongside organic social campaigns. Work with colleagues and external partners where appropriate on digital acquisition and lead-generation campaigns. Develop your knowledge and expertise in paid search and digital advertising, keeping up to date with new opportunities and good practice. Social Media Play a key role in planning, creating and managing FareShare Midlands' social media activity. Create engaging content tailored to different platforms and audiences. Help plan and schedule social media content around organisational priorities, campaigns and events. Identify opportunities for timely, engaging and reactive content. Support community engagement and help ensure appropriate and timely responses across our channels. Contribute to both organic and paid social media campaigns. Monitor performance and use insight to understand which content is working and how we can improve. Keep abreast of platform developments, trends and emerging formats. Video, Content & Impact Storytelling Help identify and develop compelling stories that demonstrate the impact of FareShare Midlands' work. Introduction to the role The Digital Communications Coordinator will coordinate the digital communications for Surrey Coalition of Disabled People as well as the projects/networks that we coordinate such as The Independent Mental Health Network (IMHN). Purpose of the role To lead on the coordination, design and delivery of vibrant and engaging communications for The Coalition. We want to expand our reach and increase our engagement. You will help us to achieve this: Through building our existing social media channels as well as researching/implementing new channels Keeping The Coalition website updated with fresh and engaging content Developing marketing materials for our events/social activities and services/projects Being the expert in digital accessibility Main responsibilities Craft/develop content for the Coalition’s social media channels including You Tube and the website Co-ordinate and develop an ongoing schedule of new content for each of the social media platforms, ensuring this is in line with the overall organisation’s activities Monitor networks/trending topics to ensure that the Coalition maximises any opportunities to respond to appropriate topics Provide analysis of the effectiveness of our content through regular reporting including key metrics such as reach, impressions and engagement Keep the website updated – including making changes to pages as well as building new ones To ensure that our communications are available in a wide range of formats that meets the accessibility needs of our membership Working with the wider staff and volunteer team, to identify and generate compelling case studies and examples of our work To be the brand guardian for the organisation To develop the knowledge of the staff team around effective communications, and contribute to team training and development To develop Coalition News, our quarterly Newsletter To attend member events to capture content for communications across all channels To support fundraising with developing appropriate content for funding applications and reporting Help develop and implement a 3 year communications and marketing strategy for the charity Draft press releases as required and liaise with members, staff and journalists to organise coverage. We are looking for someone with: Outstanding organisation and planning skills (E) Excellent written communication skills and experience with copywriting for social media platforms (E) Some experience of creating and editing basic graphics, video and animation using software such as Photoshop, Illustrator, Canva, Adobe Effects and/or photo editing software (E) Experience of editing web pages and building web pages (E) Able to analyse and evaluate reports from social media activity (E) A high degree of self-motivation and able to work on own initiative (E) A creative flair, ideas and understanding of current media trends, identifying opportunities etc. (E) Experience of working in a Disabled Peoples Organisation or in the wider Voluntary Community and Social Enterprise (VCSE) sector (D) Experience and knowledge of working with people who are Disabled and/or carers or lived experience of Disability or being a family Carer (D) This role requires the successful applicant to be subject to an Enhanced Disclosure and Barring Check (we will organise and pay for this for you if you are successful). item.title: Head of Campaign Success (NGOs & Political Parties)
item.description: 💚 About Movement Movement builds the campaign infrastructure behind some of the most effective progressive organisations in Europe. Our platform powers CRM, communications, and campaigning for trade unions, NGOs, charities, and political parties. The Labour Party used Movement to win the 2024 General Election. The NEU, UNISON and Greenpeace use it every day to organise, mobilise, and win. 🎯 The role Our clients split into two worlds. Trade unions run ballots, organise workplaces, and mobilise reps. NGOs and political parties run campaigns, fundraise, and fight elections. Each world deserves a dedicated lead who knows it inside out. You'll be that lead for NGOs and political parties, working alongside our Head of Campaign Success for Trade Unions. You'll take on our priority NGO and political party accounts. The shape of the role will shift as the segment grows. Our trade union book is deep. Our NGO book has flagship names but fewer of them, so at the start you'll spend a lot of time helping us win new NGO and political party clients. Sales for this segment is founder-led, and you'll be the founder's right hand: running demos, working events, building relationships across the sector, and onboarding what we win together. As the book fills out, the role tilts towards account management and campaign success. You'll be growing your own future job. This is a hands-on role. You'll set up accounts from scratch, work out how a client's structure maps onto the platform, and troubleshoot technical issues as readily as you'll run a demo or a renewal conversation. You'll also take your turn on the support rota alongside other campaign success team members. You'll manage one direct report. Their role covers our client community, training, webinars, case studies, frontline support, and some of our smaller NGO accounts. 🛠️ What you'll do 🚀 Help grow the NGO and political party segment (the biggest part at first) Work alongside the founder leading sales for this segment as their right hand on every deal Run product demos, solo or as part of a founder-led pitch Represent Movement at sector events, conferences, and meet-ups. Build the network that brings deals in Follow up inbound leads and keep longer conversations warm Help build proposals and contribute to RFP responses 🤝 Own our priority NGO and political party accounts (growing as we win) Build strong relationships with campaigners, digital leads, and data teams at our NGO and party clients Run onboarding for the accounts we land: kick-off, training, launch planning, and the first 90 days Drive adoption of the features that move the needle for each client, from branded RCS to share testing to organiser dashboards Lead renewal conversations. Spot churn risk early and act on it Find expansion opportunities and turn them into proposals Run quarterly reviews that clients actually find useful 🔧 Be the technical lead for your accounts Set up new accounts: provisioning, custom fields, tags, segments, and templates Configure integrations, single sign-on, and sender domains Triage and resolve technical issues for your accounts, escalating to engineering when needed Take your share of support days on the rota, covering the inbox for the whole client base alongside the rest of the team Translate between campaigners and engineers. You'll be fluent in both languages 🌱 Manage and develop your direct report Set priorities for our client community, training, webinar, and case study work Oversee our smaller NGO & WhatsApp only account book, which your report manages day to day Support their development as their role grows Build support workflows that scale as the client base does 🔍 Who we're looking for You've probably done one of these: Worked in sales, account management, or implementation at a campaigning platform or similar such as Action Network, Engaging Networks, or NationBuilder, and know how NGOs buy Run digital, data, or a CRM at an NGO, charity, or political party, and been the person who actually built the segments and fixed the emails Led campaigns with serious digital infrastructure behind them and managed the platform relationship from the client side Experience inside the NGO, charity, or party world counts for a lot here, especially alongside commercial experience. We're not ruling out people from outside the sector. ✅ You'll need Confidence running demos and holding your own in commercial conversations, plus a genuine appetite for events and networking Real experience with campaigning or CRM platforms as a power user or administrator The technical depth to build an organisation from scratch. Give you a client's structure, branches, regions, teams, campaigns, and you can work out how it maps onto fields, tags, lists, audiences, and permissions The ability to read HTML or SQL and follow a technical conversation. You don't need to be an engineer, but you can't be scared of the tools Strong relationship skills. Clients should feel you're on their team A track record on retention. Renewals landed, churn spotted early, accounts kept and grown Experience managing someone, and the appetite to develop a report whose role is growing Willingness to take your share of support days. Everyone here covers the inbox, us included Genuine commitment to progressive causes. Our clients will feel if you don't mean it ✨ It would help if you have Knowledge of email deliverability, GDPR in a campaigning context, or the European progressive tech landscape A second European language 🎉 Why this role You'll own the priority accounts in a whole segment, and work shoulder to shoulder with a founder to grow it You'll see the whole company, not one corner of it A four day week as standard, remote-first with a London office when you want it Your clients will be organisations fighting for things that matter, and your work will directly affect whether they win Movement is profitable and growing, and this role grows with the segment you build
item.dc:creator: Movement

item.title: Donkey Welfare Adviser
item.description: Donkey Welfare Adviser We now have an excellent secondment opportunity for a dynamic and resourceful individual with a proven track record of community-based animal welfare work, excellent decision-making and time-management skills and a strong customer service ethic to join the team as Donkey Welfare Adviser for South Wales. Position: Donkey Welfare Adviser Location: Home based (it is preferable that candidates live centrally within region to gain easy access to travel and communication networks. However, locations close to the defined area may be considered if operationally viable) Hours: Full-time, working an average of 37.5 hours per week on an annualised hours basis. Salary: £40,389 per annum Contract: Fixed term maternity cover contract starting on 14 December 2026 until 3 March 2028 Closing Date: Sunday 27 September 2026. Please note this role may close earlier than advertised so apply as soon as possible. Interview Date: Sidmouth, on Tuesday 27th Wednesday 28th October 2026 About the Role Donkey Welfare Advisers are professionals in the field of donkey and mule welfare. They play a key front-line role in the work of the Sanctuary: responding to donkeys in need, supporting donkeys in the community, growing and managing a high-quality rehoming scheme, and acting as an ambassador for the charity at all times. Your principal duties and responsibilities will include: Promoting good welfare for donkeys and mules by working proactively to support, guide and educate key audiences and by sharing best practice. Communicating effectively with groups from all social, racial, and cultural backgrounds, often in highly emotive and sometimes confrontational circumstances. Delivering high quality, impactful training to a range of stakeholders in a style suitable to the audience and the resources available. Responding to future care enquiries, working creatively to identify suitable alternatives to sanctuary care where appropriate, and gathering and co-ordinating relevant information to inform donkey placement decisions and help owners make informed choices for their donkeys, including end of life decisions. Supporting a good quality rehoming scheme by ensuring donkeys are placed in the most suitable environments for their needs. Working proactively to prevent/alleviate suffering, referring to and/or collaborating with enforcement agencies when necessary. Providing reliable evidence for welfare investigation cases, including witness statements and other relevant evidence in court compliant formats, and attending court to give evidence as required. About You You will be a positive influencer able to promote and model our values in all areas of your work, with a high level of equine knowledge with significant experience of working with equines. You will also have: A working knowledge of legal practicalities and experience of the application of relevant animal welfare legislation. An understanding of equine behaviour and demonstrable practical experience in the field. Able to influence change and respond appropriately in emotional challenging or confrontational situations. Excellent communicator able to deliver advice and training to stakeholder groups with varying experience. Strong interpersonal skills, comfortable with making new contacts and able to develop and maintain strong working relationships with internal and external stakeholders. Before applying, please ensure that if successful in being called to interview, you would be able to attend in person on the specified date, as we cannot guarantee that we will be able to accommodate requests for alternative arrangements. Benefits include: Competitive pension. Life assurance – 2 x annual salary 31 days holiday (including Bank holidays), rising to 34 will each full year of service pro rata Wellbeing team. Recorded Pilates and Yoga classes. Long service awards. Healthshield plan Free parking. Life assurance. Subsidised restaurant and shop. About the Organisation Join one of the UK’s largest international animal welfare charities, currently supporting projects in over 35 countries worldwide, working for a world where donkeys and mules live free from suffering and their contribution to humanity is fully valued. The Charity is a Disability Confident Employer, committed to safeguarding and promoting the welfare of vulnerable people (children and adults) and expects all staff and volunteers to undertake this commitment. Applicants will be subject to safer recruitment processes, including an application for a Disclosure and Barring Service (DBS) check where required for the post. You may also have experience in areas such as Welfare, Animal Welfare, Equine, Donkey, Animal Welfare Advisor, Donkey Welfare Advisor, Animal Welfare Officer, Donkey Welfare Officer. Please note this role is advertised by the recruitment agency acting for the client, Not For Profit People. #INDNFP

item.title: RNCSF Springboard – South East Regional Coordinator
item.description: Seeking an enthusiastic, proactive individual with excellent communication skills and a committment to improving outcomes for vulnerable children. We are delighted to share this role on behalf of Christ's Hospital who the Royal National Children's Springboard Foundation (RNCSF) are working alongside. We are seeking a term time only, Regional Coordinator to support the relationship between RNCSF and local schools in the South East to secure independent day and boarding school bursary placements and access to partnership activities for care experienced children (CEVC). The post holder will be involved in engaging school stakeholders by attracting suitable school partners and being a powerful advocate for the programme. The successful candidate will need to use their excellent communication skills to influence stakeholders in Local Authorities and schools, ensuring the continued success of the “Broadening Educational Pathways” programme – a Department for Education programme delivered by RNCSF. As you will be responsible for all applications in your region it is also essential that you are organised and efficient, with superb time management skills. You will be joining a dynamic, vibrant team of 8 Regional Coordinators who operate all over the country but who work closely together, via Teams, to support CEVC into bursary places in independent day and boarding schools. Our regional coordinators work out of a local host school (with some remote working possible). This position will be based at Christ’s Hospital School in Horsham. The role is for 2-3 days per week, term time only. You will need to be available for up to 10 ‘in person’ days, and some travel may be required for this (for which you will be reimbursed). You will report into the Head of Bursary Activity as part of the Programmes Team at RNCSF. Please read more about the role in the Job Speicification below. We look forward tor receiving your application!

item.title: Chief Executive Officer
item.description: Job Details Wessmaps Housing Trust is seeking an exceptional Chief Executive Officer to lead the organisation into its next chapter. This is a unique opportunity to shape the future of a values-driven housing provider that delivers high-quality homes and support for vulnerable individuals across Hampshire and neighbouring counties. Every day, our work helps people with complex needs find stability, independence and the opportunity to thrive within their communities. As Chief Executive, you will ensure that mission remains at the heart of everything we do, whilst providing the strategic leadership needed to strengthen our organisation and drive sustainable growth. Reporting to the Board, you will provide inspiring leadership across the Trust, setting a clear vision and ensuring excellent governance, financial stewardship and regulatory compliance. You will lead and develop a talented senior team, championing a culture that reflects our mission of providing good quality, bespoke housing solutions for vulnerable people in Hampshire. As the public face of Wessmaps, you will build influential relationships with local authorities, commissioners, statutory agencies and sector partners, raising the Trust’s profile and creating opportunities that enable us to deliver even greater impact for the people we serve. We are looking for a credible and experienced senior housing leader with strong knowledge of the housing regulatory framework and a track record of delivering strategic and operational success. You will combine commercial acumen with strong values, bringing the vision, resilience and authenticity needed to lead through opportunity and challenge alike. Most importantly, you will be passionate about improving lives through the provision of safe, high-quality, person-centred housing services. If you are a values-led leader who wants to make a meaningful difference, inspire people, and help shape the future of an ambitious organisation with a strong social purpose, we would love to hear from you.

item.title: Executive Director
item.description: Change for Good Community Chaplaincy is looking for an experienced and committed Executive Director to lead our charity through an exciting stage of growth. Founded in 2012, Change for Good began as a mentoring project in HMP Wandsworth and has grown into an established resettlement charity working across London. We support people before and after release through in-prison support, "through the gate" work, volunteer mentoring, and our peer support group, Next Chapter. Mentoring, advocacy, and peer support sit at the heart of everything we do. As we grow, we're looking for a hands-on Executive Director who can lead the development and implementation of our strategic plan, lead and inspire our small staff team, champion the vital work of our volunteer mentors and our peer support group Next Chapter, and strengthen our relationships across the criminal justice and voluntary sectors - including our partner multi-faith prison chaplaincies. About the role Leadership & Strategy Lead the development and implementation of Change for Good's strategic plan, working closely with the Board of Trustees Serve as ambassador and primary spokesperson for the charity, promoting our mission and programmes Programme Delivery & Impact Ensure the effective delivery of our programmes: in-prison support, through the gate, volunteer mentoring, and Next Chapter Monitor and evaluate programme outcomes, and produce quality impact reports for funders and stakeholders Income Generation & Sustainability Contribute to funding strategy, diversifying and growing income streams to secure the charity's long-term sustainability Produce high-quality reports that meet funders' requirements and maintain strong funder relationships People & Volunteers Lead, motivate, and support high-performing staff team, building a positive and inclusive team culture Oversee the recruitment, training, and development of staff and volunteer mentors Support the vital role of our volunteer mentors, ensuring they feel well trained, supervised, and valued External Relations Build and maintain relationships with key stakeholders across the criminal justice and voluntary sectors About you This role would suit an experienced manager ready to take the step up into their first leadership role, as well as someone with prior senior leadership experience. The ideal candidate will have: Management experience within the charity or voluntary sector, with the confidence and ability to lead a high-performing team A genuine passion for prisoner and ex-prisoner welfare, and a commitment to our mission Experience working with vulnerable or marginalised populations Experience within the criminal justice system or resettlement sector Ability to work closely with the Board of Trustees to develop and deliver strategic goals Strong relationship-building skills, with the ability to represent the organisation externally Resilience, and the ability to thrive in a challenging and evolving environment Experience of, or willingness to lead on, fundraising and income generation Change for Good is committed to equality, diversity, and inclusion, and we particularly encourage applications from candidates who are currently underrepresented in charity leadership. We warmly welcome applications from people with lived experience of the criminal justice system. Change for Good has a Christian foundation and works within multi-faith prison chaplaincy settings. Applicants should be comfortable working within, and respectful of, our faith-based ethos and multi-faith environment.

item.title: Stakeholder Engagement Manager
item.description: About This Job The role requires a strong communicator who can translate complex information into accessible content and build trusted relationships across key stakeholder groups, particularly within the ACF. As well as a requirement to attend events across the UK to promote the charity. Essential Skills · GCSE English or equivalent experience · At least two year’s experience of drafting award citations or funding applications · Experience of working with partners, internally and externally · Ability to extract information from people with varying powers of written expression · Information gathering and analysis skills · Excellent written and verbal communication skills. Please refer to the attached Job Description for further information. Our charity ACCT UK is a national youth charity dedicated to improving the life chances of young people. The Combined Cadet Force Association (CCFA) is a charity dedicated to the promotion of the ideals and activities of the Combined Cadet Force in schools. Together we want to ensure that every young person has the opportunity to learn new skills, build confidence and be inspired through their cadet experience. We want to develop the youth leadership and training abilities of adult volunteers whilst also helping young people to access cadet activities through fundraising, grant-making, developing new resources and direct support. We strongly believe that everyone benefits when you help young people to develop their character and values through activities that stretch and mature them. We also know that when young people engage with others at a range of levels in their communities it builds confidence and improves empathy for other’s lives. Who we are By joining the charities, you will help us to reach more young people and make a greater difference and we look forward to working with you. We actively promote and encourage you to explore ideas that improve all aspects of the charity’s work in pursuit of its charitable aims. The charities are proud of our diverse teams, with people on different working patterns, from different backgrounds and at different life-stages. Our experience has taught us that having people with different perspectives and different lived experiences leads to better outcomes for our beneficiaries. If you are wondering if our organisation is for someone like you, the answer is yes! Please apply and explain how you, your experience, your talent and your potential are the right fit for this role. What we can offer you In addition to your salary, we offer all staff: · Flexible working arrangements (you agree a working pattern with your line manager). · The ability to work both from home and from our London office. · Personal Accident Insurance, including loss of earnings cover and death benefit. · 15 days of sick pay in any 12-month period (after 12 months employment - pro-rata for part time staff). · A contributory pension scheme (you contribute at least 5% and we will contribute 10%). · Good leave allowances (which are offered pro-rata for part time staff): o 20 days annual leave plus Bank Holidays. o Additional privilege leave, on set days each year, such as between Christmas and New Year. o An additional five days of volunteering leave. · Support for qualifications and personal development. · Employee Assistance Programme. · Season ticket loan. · Railcard (if you are eligible). · A caring and supportive team environment. How to apply Please send a CV and Cover letter that details how you meet the requirements of the job description by 2359hrs by Sunday 4th October 2026. Interviews will be held virtually via Microsoft Teams shortly after the closing date. While AI tools can be beneficial, we value the personal touch and authenticity in job applications. We encourage you to highlight your unique experience, knowledge, skills, and abilities, ensuring all information is accurate. Please use AI tools responsibly and with integrity throughout the application and selection process. Please note that as a charity dedicated to improving the lives of young people, we require staff to make a declaration about any relevant convictions, undergo a Disclosure and Barring Service check. In addition, we will follow up with references. Please be advised that this position may close earlier than the stated deadline if a sufficient number of high-quality applications are received. To ensure your application is considered, we strongly recommend submitting it as soon as possible. Candidates will be notified of the next stage in the recruitment process if they are shortlisted.

item.title: Corporate and Philanthropy Executive
item.description: OVERVIEW OF THE ROLE This exciting role will support on the delivery of income from a range of high-value donors within our philanthropy and corporate income streams. This position is key for both Helen Bamber Foundation and Asylum Aid and the postholder will work closely with the fundraising team, enabling the Senior Corporate and Philanthropy Executive and the Group Director of Fundraising to build successful funding partnerships. We’re looking for a someone who is an effective communicator with a flair for writing, who is results-focused and organised. This role best suits someone who is eager to learn and work as part of a tight-knit and successful team, and who can respond creatively and consistently to our current and future donors’ requests. This is an exciting opportunity for someone looking to begin their career in charity fundraising. The candidate will preferably have some experience working or volunteering in the charity sector, and we welcome applications from candidates with transferrable experience, such as working in a client-facing role, in communications, copywriting or in event planning. item.title: Carbon Project Officer
item.description: The Woodland Trust is looking for a Carbon Project Officer. The Carbon Project Officer will support the project management of the Trust’s estate and third-party carbon Woodland and Peatland code projects, in turn supporting Operations teams to deliver carbon on the ground and meet long term carbon code requirements. The Role: Manage multiple carbon project workstreams simultaneously, ensuring deadlines are met and work is delivered to a consistently high standard. Produce high-quality Woodland Carbon Code and Peatland Code project documentation, including project design documents, cashflows, carbon calculations, mapping, management plans, monitoring plans and risk assessments. Develop specialist knowledge of carbon standards and markets, staying informed on industry developments and communicating their implications across the organisation. Analyse, interpret and present complex datasets and technical information to support project development, reporting and decision-making. Create and maintain accurate project records, trackers and databases, ensuring effective project management, reporting and compliance. Build and maintain strong relationships with internal teams, landowners, auditors, regulators and other stakeholders to support the successful delivery of carbon projects. Plan and undertake site surveys, validations and verifications, providing technical expertise and support throughout the carbon project lifecycle. Act as a trusted source of advice on the Woodland Trust's carbon offer, managing enquiries and communicating complex information clearly to a range of audiences. This is a hybrid position with a mix of home working and from our head office in Grantham, Lincolnshire. Head office attendance would be required once a month on average. Occasional travel to other offices and remote locations may also be required. The Candidate: Experience supporting the development and delivery of environmental, natural capital, forestry, land management or carbon-related projects. Experience producing high-quality technical documentation, reports and project information that meet organisational, regulatory or industry standards. Experience using GIS or mapping software, such as ArcGIS Pro, to support project planning, delivery and reporting. Strong analytical skills, with the ability to accurately interpret, manage and present data to support decision-making and project outcomes. Excellent communication and stakeholder management skills, with experience building effective relationships across a range of internal and external partners, including landowners, auditors, regulators and sector bodies. The ability to work collaboratively within multidisciplinary teams while also taking a proactive and self-motivated approach to managing your own workload. An understanding of woodland creation, peatland restoration and carbon projects, or a willingness to develop expertise in the Woodland Carbon Code, Peatland Code and emerging UK carbon standards and grant mechanisms. Strong organisational skills, with the ability to prioritise competing demands and consistently deliver high-quality work to agreed deadlines in a fast-paced environment. Full UK Driving Licence and willingness to travel throughout the UK, including overnight stays and visits to remote sites. Successful completion of pre-employment checks, including Right to Work and employment history verification. Benefits and Wellbeing: Joining our team means you’ll be part of our fight for a greener, healthier planet for people and wildlife. We take good care of our staff, offering support and training opportunities. We also offer: Enhanced Employer Pension Life Assurance Flexible and hybrid working options (7am - 7pm) Generous annual leave - 25 Days plus Bank Holidays (pro rata for part-time) Buy and sell holiday scheme Enhanced parental pay Employee assistance programme To support inclusivity and remove barriers for candidates, we publish all salaries upfront and proudly follow the We Show the Salary pledge. The salary listed is the set salary for this role, and we don’t ask applicants to state their current pay or expectations. If you choose to apply, we’ll take that as confirmation that the advertised salary meets your expectations. About Us: The Woodland Trust is the UK’s largest woodland conservation charity. We want to see a world where woods and trees thrive for people and nature. The Trust engages and inspires people to make a difference by protecting, restoring and creating woodland and getting more trees in the ground. Our commitment to Diversity and Inclusion: To achieve our mission, we need to better reflect society and the communities we work in. People of colour and disabled people are currently under-represented across the environment and conservation sector. If you identify as a person of colour and/or disabled, we particularly encourage you to apply. Application information and advice: For fairness we keep our candidates’ personal details hidden from the hiring managers, and we do not ask for your CV at application. Make sure that your personal statement clearly shows how your skills and knowledge link to the specifications in the job description and you share with us your passion for the role. Completed applications will be reviewed by a hiring manager and/or a member of the recruitment team, and you will receive an update on the outcome of your application via email. Acceptable Use - Artificial Intelligence (AI): We understand that candidates may choose to use AI tools to support their job applications. However, we ask that any information submitted reflects your own experience, skills and understanding. During interviews, candidates are expected to respond independently without the use of AI tools. Apply now: If you're ready to make a difference and grow with us, apply today. We might close advertising early if we get a lot of applications, so it's a good idea to apply soon. If we do close the advert early, and you have an application in progress, we will email you prior to closing to give you time to complete. Interviews will take place via teams on October 28th 2026.

item.title: Grants Officer - Rural Payments
item.description: The Woodland Trust is looking for a Grants Officer - Rural Payments. This role will work collaboratively as a member of the Land & Property team and members of connected teams in Nature Recovery to help deliver on our plans to reduce adverse herbivore impacts and improve Woodland Ecological Condition, contributing to our work to protect woodland biodiversity and nature recovery. The Role: Identify, secure and maximise income from government and non-government funding streams to support woodland creation, conservation and priority species work. Build and maintain strong relationships with key external stakeholders including DEFRA, the Rural Payments Agency (RPA), Forestry Commission, Forest Research and other sector partners. Provide expert advice and year-round support to Estate Managers, Site Managers and regional teams on grant opportunities, applications, scheme delivery and compliance. Lead the administration of environmental funding schemes, including annual claims, record management, remittance reconciliation and oversight of historic agreements. Maintain accurate land and scheme records through the Rural Payments online portal, ensuring compliance with eligibility requirements and timely updates to land ownership, parcel and land cover information Keep abreast of evolving rural funding programmes, including SFI, CSMT and CSHT, providing guidance on opportunities and implications for the organisation. Use GIS and LandApp to design, validate and map funding schemes, supporting high-quality submissions and successful outcomes. Apply strong analytical, IT and problem-solving skills to resolve funding, land management and scheme administration issues, while working closely with operational and nature recovery teams to achieve strategic objectives. This is a hybrid position with a mix of home working and from our head office in Grantham, Lincolnshire. Head office attendance would be required once a month on average. Occasional travel to other offices and remote locations may also be required. The Candidate: Good understanding of and ideally experience working with, environmental and land-based grant schemes that support nature recovery, conservation and woodland management objectives. Experience developing, coordinating and delivering grant-funded projects or schemes, working collaboratively with a range of stakeholders to achieve successful outcomes. Ability to establish and maintain effective monitoring, evaluation and reporting processes to demonstrate delivery, compliance and impact. Experience producing high-quality grant applications and supporting documentation, with the ability to coordinate contributions and deliver to deadlines. Knowledge of, or experience within, the conservation, environmental, forestry or charitable sectors. Strong team-working skills, with the ability to build effective relationships and work collaboratively across an organisation while also managing your own workload independently. Confident using a range of IT systems and software, with excellent attention to detail and the ability to manage information accurately. Excellent written, verbal and interpersonal communication skills, alongside an understanding of project management, budgets and resource planning. Degree-level qualification or equivalent practical experience in a conservation, fundraising or related environment. Benefits and Wellbeing: Joining our team means you’ll be part of our fight for a greener, healthier planet for people and wildlife. item.title: Suicide Bereavement Specialist Manager
item.description: The Suicide Bereavement Specialist Manager leads and manages a team of approximately 10–12 Suicide Bereavement Specialists, providing strong and supportive management alongside clear professional accountability and oversight of practice. The postholder will also maintain a small caseload of approximately 5–10 beneficiaries, enabling them to remain connected to frontline practice and the experiences of people accessing the service. The postholder has operational responsibility for the beneficiary journey from the point a referral enters the service through assessment, triage and allocation to a Suicide Bereavement Specialist, and for ensuring that subsequent support is safe, timely, appropriate, person-centred and delivered to Pete’s Dragons’ expected standards. Relationship with the Beneficiary Services Manager The Beneficiary Services Manager holds overall strategic responsibility for Beneficiary Services , including the direction, development and performance of beneficiary-facing services across Pete’s Dragons. The SBS Manager holds operational responsibility for the day-to-day delivery, management and quality of the Suicide Bereavement Specialist service . The SBS Manager is expected to exercise appropriate professional and managerial autonomy in the daily operation of the SBS service, escalating significant safeguarding, workforce, performance, capacity, service-quality or organisational concerns to the Beneficiary Services Manager. The two roles will work closely together to ensure that strategic decisions are translated into consistent, safe and effective practice. Key Responsibilities Referral, Triage and Allocation The SBS Manager will: Take overall responsibility for all incoming referrals to the SBS service from the point of entry through to allocation. Review referrals to establish need, urgency, risk, suitability and any additional considerations affecting the provision of support. Ensure referrals are processed promptly and in accordance with Pete’s Dragons’ referral pathways, eligibility criteria and service standards. Identify and appropriately escalate safeguarding, suicide risk or other significant concerns arising during the referral process. Allocate beneficiaries to the most appropriate SBS, considering individual need, practitioner skills and experience, existing caseload, capacity, location and other relevant factors. Maintain oversight of referrals awaiting allocation and ensure that beneficiaries do not become lost or unnecessarily delayed within the system. Monitor demand, waiting times, caseloads and team capacity and raise emerging pressures with the Beneficiary Services Manager. Ensure referral and allocation decisions are clearly and appropriately recorded. Management and Leadership of the SBS Team The SBS Manager will: Provide day-to-day leadership and management to approximately 10–12 Suicide Bereavement Specialists. Lead regular individual management 1:1s with each SBS. Lead group supervision and reflective practice opportunities as required. Lead daily SBS team meetings and scheduled practice meetings. Create a team culture which combines compassion and psychological safety with professional accountability and consistently high standards. Maintain regular contact with staff working across different Pete’s Dragons locations. Ensure staff have appropriate opportunities to raise concerns, discuss difficult work and seek management guidance. Monitor individual workload, caseload and capacity and intervene where concerns arise. Support staff wellbeing while maintaining clear expectations regarding professional responsibilities and service delivery. Provide appropriate telephone management support for SBS staff working outside normal office hours as required. Quality Assurance and Practice Standards The SBS Manager will hold responsibility for the quality of SBS practice and will: Undertake formal case audits for each SBS on a quarterly basis. Regularly review the quality, accuracy and completeness of beneficiary records and case documentation. Monitor SBS practice against Pete’s Dragons’ policies, procedures, practice standards and expected professional boundaries. Arrange and review recorded beneficiary sessions at appropriate intervals as part of ongoing practice quality assurance and practitioner development. Provide constructive feedback following practice reviews and agree actions or development plans where required. Identify excellent practice and ensure learning is shared across the team. Identify practice which falls below the expected standard and take timely action to support improvement. Monitor beneficiary engagement, missed appointments, case progression, case duration and closure practices. Ensure concerns regarding practice, conduct, competence or beneficiary safety are appropriately documented, addressed and escalated. Promote reflective professional practice and continuous improvement throughout the SBS team. Safeguarding and Risk The SBS Manager will: Act as a Designated Safeguarding Officer (DSO) for Pete’s Dragons. Appropriate DSO training can be provided where required. Share responsibility for the management and oversight of safeguarding cases within the organisation. Provide advice and support to SBSs where safeguarding concerns arise. Ensure safeguarding concerns are identified, recorded, escalated and acted upon in accordance with Pete’s Dragons’ Safeguarding Policy and relevant statutory guidance. Work collaboratively with other safeguarding leads and senior managers where complex or significant concerns arise. Promote confident and consistent safeguarding practice throughout the SBS team. Ensure staff understand the distinction between safeguarding, suicide risk, clinical concern and other forms of beneficiary risk and follow the appropriate organisational pathway. Beneficiary Casework To remain connected to frontline practice, the SBS Manager will: Maintain a small caseload of approximately 5–10 beneficiaries. Provide high-quality suicide bereavement support in accordance with Pete’s Dragons’ practice model, policies and standards. Maintain timely, accurate and appropriate case records. Model excellent professional boundaries, beneficiary communication and case management. Participate in appropriate clinical supervision for their own beneficiary work. Ensure management responsibilities remain the priority of the role and that their personal caseload does not compromise their availability to manage the service or support the SBS team. People Management and HR The SBS Manager will be responsible for all routine HR management relating to their direct reports, including: Recruitment and selection of Suicide Bereavement Specialists. Induction and probation. Regular management supervision. Annual appraisal and performance review. Identifying individual and team development needs. Supporting professional development and CPD. Attendance and absence management. Managing annual leave and ensuring adequate service capacity. Addressing performance, capability, conduct or behavioural concerns promptly and appropriately. Supporting staff wellbeing and identifying when additional support may be required. Working with the Beneficiary Services Manager and other appropriate colleagues on formal HR matters where necessary. Maintaining appropriate and confidential management records. Training and Development The SBS Manager will: Identify individual and collective training and development needs across the SBS team. Ensure mandatory training remains current. Support SBSs to develop their knowledge, confidence and professional practice. Use case audits, recorded-session reviews, supervision, beneficiary feedback and other quality measures to identify areas for development. Contribute to the development and delivery of internal practice training and workshops. Support newly appointed SBSs through induction and their transition into independent practice. Policy, Procedure and Service Development The SBS Manager will: Ensure organisational policies, procedures and agreed ways of working are consistently implemented within the SBS team. Communicate changes in policy or practice clearly and ensure staff understand what is expected of them. Monitor compliance and address inconsistent practice. Contribute frontline operational knowledge to the review and development of policies, procedures, pathways and practice standards. Support the Beneficiary Services Manager in implementing service developments and organisational change. Identify opportunities to improve beneficiary experience, efficiency, quality and consistency. Monitoring and Reporting The SBS Manager will maintain an accurate operational picture of the SBS service, including: Referral volumes. Referral processing and allocation. Waiting times. Individual and team caseloads. Team capacity. Beneficiary engagement. Case progression and closures. Safeguarding and risk themes. Quality assurance findings. Staff performance and development. Emerging operational risks or pressures. The postholder will provide appropriate information and reporting to the Beneficiary Services Manager and ensure significant concerns are escalated promptly rather than waiting for routine reporting arrangements. General Responsibilities The postholder will: Work across Pete’s Dragons Devon locations as required. Represent Pete’s Dragons professionally with beneficiaries, colleagues, partners and external agencies. Maintain appropriate confidentiality and comply with data protection requirements. Work within Pete’s Dragons’ policies, procedures, values and professional standards. Attend relevant internal and external meetings. Maintain appropriate professional boundaries at all times. Undertake relevant training and continuing professional development. Work flexibly where reasonably required by the needs of the service. Participate in a limited out-of-hours telephone support arrangement for SBS staff undertaking authorised out-of-hours work. Undertake ot

item.title: Business and Operations Manager
item.description: Make a difference every day by helping a growing autism charity deliver the very best support for autistic people and their families. Space4Autism is looking for an experienced, organised and people-focused Business & Operations Manager to help drive our organisation forward and ensure everything behind the scenes runs effectively. Space4Autism has been a lifeline for autistic individuals and their families across Cheshire East since 2005. What started as a parent-founded, volunteer-run charity has grown into an organisation delivering over 4,000 activities a year - social clubs for children and young people, parent and carer support, services for autistic adults, an autism-friendly community café, a charity shop offering work experience for autistic adults, training and workshops, and space for private hire. Everything we do is guided by one simple promise: we listen, we help, we care. Now, as we grow, we need someone who can help us grow well - a Business & Operations Manager who will work hand-in-hand with our CEO to keep the organisation running smoothly, sustainably, and with the same care we bring to every family we support. The opportunity… This is a hands-on senior leadership role for a pragmatic, confident operator who's just as comfortable in a budget spreadsheet as they are supporting a team, and who genuinely wants their work to change lives. You'll be a trusted partner to the CEO, taking ownership of the day-to-day so that strategy turns into action - across business planning, finance, funding, people, operations, and governance. You'll report directly to the CEO and line manage the whole Space4Autism team, giving you real influence over how the charity runs and grows. What you'll be doing… Business planning & strategy: help shape, implement, and monitor our business plan, turn strategic goals into clear action plans, and keep leadership priorities, projects, and timelines on track. You'll attend Trustee Board meetings and bring your insight, challenges, and ideas to the table. Budgets & finance: support budget planning, monitoring, and reporting, and keep a close eye on spend so we stay financially sustainable, working alongside our finance team and external accountants. Funding & income: help drive our funding strategy and income diversification, track grant requirements and deadlines, and coordinate funding applications and stakeholder communications. Operations: own the smooth running of the organisation day to day: improving systems and processes, spotting operational risks before they become problems, and supporting governance and compliance. People Management & Leadership: line manage the whole team, lead on recruitment, and support onboarding, performance, and development, building a working culture that's positive, collaborative, and accountable. Policy & governance: develop and maintain our policies and procedures, keeping us compliant with legislation and best practice, and supporting our wider governance and compliance reporting. What we're looking for… · Strong business management and operational leadership experience · Proven financial and budget management capability · Experience managing people, teams, and organisational processes · Sound knowledge of governance and compliance, including regulatory frameworks, safeguarding, and best practice · Somebody who is able to occasionally attend off-site fundraisers and other events outside of core working hours · A track record of supporting organisational growth — scaling services, managing change, building capacity · A confident, pragmatic decision maker with sharp problem-solving skills · Excellent organisational skills and the ability to juggle competing priorities · A hands-on style that works both strategically and operationally · Strong communication and stakeholder management skills It would also be great if you have… · Experience building strategic relationships and partnerships · A background in the charity, healthcare, or NHS sectors · Knowledge of charity governance, safeguarding, or regulatory frameworks · An understanding of autism services or neurodiversity-informed practice · Experience working in a growing organisation or service environment You'll fit right in if you're… Proactive and solutions-focused, calm under pressure, a collaborative leader with a strong sense of accountability and integrity and genuinely passionate about improving outcomes for autistic individuals and their families. What you’ll get in return… · Salary of £38,000 - £42,000 DOE · Enrollment into employee pension scheme · 31 days holidays including bank holidays · Wellbeing social days · Charity discount scheme Ready to apply? Here’s what you need to know… Please submit your most up to date CV via this advert. It is highly desirable that you also attach a cover letter to highlight your relevant experience and motivations for wanting to join Space4Autism. Suitable candidates will be contacted for an initial telephone discussion prior to final shortlisting. Those shortlisted will be invited to attend a competency-based interview where you will also be tasked with preparing a short presentation. If you are successful in the competency-based interview, you will be invited to attend a final meeting with the CEO to ensure you align and to answer any questions you may have about the role and the charity. We are anticipating a high volume of applications for this role and while we will endeavor to respond to all applications, if you have not been contacted prior to the closing date, please assume you have not been successful on this occasion. Disability Confident Employer Space4Autism is proud to be a Disability Confident Employer (reg no. DCS021234). We guarantee an interview to any disabled applicant who meets the essential criteria for this role, as set out in the job specification. If you'd like to apply under this scheme, please let us know by stating this clearly on your CV / covering letter and telling us that you wish to be considered under the Disability Confident scheme. You're welcome to share as much or as little detail about your disability as you're comfortable with, we only need enough information to confirm you meet the criteria. If you're invited to interview, please also let us know of any reasonable adjustments you'd need to take part. For example, accessible interview arrangements, extra time, alternative formats for materials, or a different interview format. You can tell us this at the same time as applying, or at any point once you've been invited, and it won't affect your application in any way. #BusinessandOperationsManager #BusinessandOperations #OperationsManager

item.title: Senior Service Manager - Swindon
item.description: BASED IN SWINDON NO CVS ACCEPTED and STRICTLY NO AGENCIES/RECRUITMENT CONSULTANTS. This role requires the submission of a completed Medaille Trust Application Form which you can download from the Vacancies page on Medaille Trust website. This is to be uploaded to the 'Other Document Upload' button. Your application will not be considered without an application form as we do not accept CVS. Interview date will be confirmed with the applicant We are currently looking for a Senior Service Manager to oversee safe houses based in Swindon area. This role is a chance to combine your leadership skills, compliance excellence and compassion. In the role you will: · Lead and Inspire: Manage and motivate a dedicated team, ensuring they receive high quality supervision, training, and support. · Champion Safety & Quality: Take ownership of Health & Safety compliance, safeguarding standards, and quality assurance measures including CQC and internal audits. · Drive Operational Excellence: Oversee budgets, payroll, and service delivery with a focus on efficiency and high standards. · Empower Survivors: Ensure service users receive the care and advocacy they need to rebuild their lives. What we are looking for: · Proven experience in team management and compliance within a care or support setting. · Strong knowledge of Health & Safety, safeguarding, and quality frameworks. · Excellent communication, organisational, and IT skills. · Experience in modern slavery support is desirable, but not essential as training will be provided. Closing date: Friday, 25 September 2026 at 10am Interview Date: TBC Applications will be reviewed as they are received, and we reserve the right to interview/ appoint before the closing date. Early applications are therefore strongly encouraged. This role is a subject to satisfactory Disclosure & Barring Service checks. The ability to drive with a valid licence with use of own vehicle insured for business purposes is essential. About Us Medaille Trust is one of the leading providers of support to survivors of modern slavery and human trafficking in the UK. We are working to provide refuge and freedom for survivors and fighting to see slavery in all its forms become a thing of the past. The need for this work has never been higher, there are more than 50 million estimated victims of modern slavery worldwide, and over 120,000 potential victims in the UK. We operate ten safe houses and five outreach hubs, staffed round the clock by specialist staff, working with more than 600 men, women and dependent children each year. We work to raise awareness in the UK and to provide preventive work in source countries. Our Pursue work helps survivors to engage with police and within the legal system to seek justice and to secure convictions against their perpetrators.

item.title: Independent Domestic Violence Advocate
item.description: Are you looking for a rewarding role within an intersectional feminist organisation? We have an incredible opportunity for an Independent Domestic Violence Advocate (IDVA) to join Solace Women’s Aid. Solace exists to end the harm done through gender-based violence. We work to prevent violence and abuse and provide services to meet the individual needs of survivors, particularly women and children. Our core values reflect our history and were developed in consultation with staff and service users. Feminism and intersectionality are key to our work, and we are committed to the principles of being survivor-led, trauma-informed, empowering, diverse, anti-racist and anti-discriminatory. About the Service Solace Women’s Aid provides a wide range of services to victim/survivors of domestic and sexual abuse in Islington including a large advocacy and support service and specialist projects co-located in a number of services. About the Role We are seeking an IDVA to provide high-quality case work support, advocacy and information services to survivors of domestic abuse who are experiencing significant harm from interpersonal harm and relationship abuse. You will carry out DASH Risk Assessments in a timely manner and refer high-risk cases to MARAC where appropriate. Our IDVA’s work alongside statutory partners to promote a coordinated, multi-agency response for survivors and their families, strengthen professional relationships, and enhance collaboration with IDVA colleagues and wider support services. About You You will be highly organised, self-motivated applicants and passionate about ending VAWG and hold a solid understanding of how domestic or sexual violence against a parent can affect a child in the home. You will have a “can-do‟ approach, experience of working with families and demonstrable commitment to Solace’s feminist approach to supporting survivors and their children to be safer. The postholder will have an in-depth knowledge of domestic abuse and its impact on survivors and children, experience of providing emotional and practical support to victims of VAWG and a strong understanding of statutory systems including housing and social care. A relevant qualification in VAWG is desirable. Additional Information This is a hybrid role, with a minimum requirement to work one day per week at our Head Office in Camden and one day per week at Islington Council offices. This arrangement may vary depending on the needs of the service and/or service users. The salary for this post is £29,385 - £30,671 (Unqualified) or £ 30,671 - £32,623 (Qualified). What we can offer you We provide a comprehensive benefits package to all our employees, including: Flexible working Focus on learning and development (internal career progression and training) Generous holiday entitlement Employer pension contribution Family-friendly leave and enhanced maternity pay Access to Inclusion Networks Daily clinical debriefing Two paid wellbeing days Employee Assistance Programme providing free 24/7 support and advice Employee Benefits Platform offering staff discounts, benefits, and savings Flow & Restore yoga classes Meditation sessions Cycle to Work Scheme How to apply Please submit your CV and Supporting Statement through the recruitment portal. When applying for this role, kindly highlight in your Supporting Statement how your values, knowledge, transferable skills, and experience align with each point within the following sections of the Job Profile Document: Values, Behaviours & Competencies Knowledge, Experience and Skills Solace Women's Aid values diversity, promotes equity, and challenges discrimination. We encourage and welcome applications from candidates of diverse cultures, abilities, perspectives, and lived experiences. We have policies and processes in place to ensure that all employees are offered an equal opportunity in recruitment and selection, promotion, training, pay, and benefits. Our Inclusion Networks support staff with protected characteristics and offer inclusive spaces to connect. We anticipate and provide reasonable adjustments as needed and support employees who acquire a disability or long-term health condition, enabling them to stay in work. This service is run by women for women and is therefore restricted to female applicants under the Equality Act 2010, Schedule 9, Part 1. Section 7(2)(e) of the Sex Discrimination Act 1975 applies. The post is exempt from the Rehabilitation of Offenders Act. As part of safer recruitment practices, we carry out pre-employment checks including references, Disclosure and Barring Service (DBS) and right to work in the UK checks. No agencies

item.title: Business Development and Philanthropy Assistant
item.description: We are looking for a motivated team player to join our Business Development and Philanthropy Team, which leads and co-ordinates our global fundraising from institutional and philanthropic sources. You will provide crucial support to our team’s function by providing relevant and timely business intelligence and coordination to support our work with donors, including support for internal and external events that we organise to deepen donor engagement with our work. Accountabilities You will support the organisation of inspiring donor events, in person and online, working across multi-disciplinary teams and drawing together reflections and learnings afterwards to improve our donors' experience. You will help colleagues prepare for funding meetings — contributing to cases for support, proposals, donor reports and appeals— and support day-to-day stewardship, from thank-you letters to stewardship activities such as annual thankathons. You will manage your own small portfolio of individual donors and charitable trusts giving at the £5,000 level, sending proposals and reports, and will maintain a strong knowledge of Practical Action's programmes so you can share stories of change and impact data confidently with current and prospective supporters. You will support the team's intelligence hub: gathering, interpreting and sharing insight on key donors including governments, foundations and multilaterals; analysing funder strategies and calls for proposals; and working with regional and country teams to understand and meet their business intelligence needs. You will help ensure intelligence is shared and acted on across the organisation, including through the monthly news bulletin, and work with your manager to develop "so what" analysis that BD teams globally can act on. You will also keep our SharePoint and donor portal registrations accurate and well organised. Skills, Abilities and Competencies: To be successful in the role, the ideal candidate will be able to demonstrate: · A keen interest in international development and environmental issues. · Excellent research, numeracy and analytical skills – not taking everything at face value and being able to discern the “so what” questions from trends and data. · Proficient usage of Microsoft 365, especially Excel, Word (including mail merge) and Powerpoint. · Ability to take complex data and synthesize it into consumable, actionable insight. · Excellent presentation skills, able to synthesise information in written format, info graphics and other visual formats and will be proficient with using a range of software and digital tools to do this. · Ability to work proactively and collaboratively with people from a range of cultures and across time zones. · You are a self-starter, happy to work with various research resources and have an ability to work with imperfect systems and information. · You are organized, conscientious and work well as part of a team. · Ability to manage multiple responsibilities and to set priorities. · Excellent written and spoken English. · Commitment to development principles and Practical Action’s vision, mission and ambition. Why join us? The opportunity to work for an organisation that is taking practical action against poverty and the environmental crises to start the big changes the world urgently needs. A friendly and supportive culture, working with values driven and highly engaged colleagues, work life balance and flexible working – these are just some of the reasons we think Practical Action is a great place to work. In the UK, our open plan offices are located in the centre of Rugby and near to Rugby train station but we also offer free parking. In addition, we offer the following benefits: · Full time roles are contracted at 35 hours per week. · It is our normal practice to operate a hybrid working policy, where flexible working hours are enabled as well as remote working. · 27 days holiday rising with continuous service, in addition to public holidays · Pension scheme - employer contributes 10.5% of salary and the employee contributes 5%. · Enhanced family friendly policies, including maternity, adoption, paternity, and shared parental leave. · Life assurance (3 x annual salary). · Cycle to Work scheme · Employee Assistance Programme – access to our Wellbeing platform · Learning and Development Opportunities · Sit / Stand desks available in our modern offices. How to apply: To ensure that Practical Action meets its obligations of safer recruitment, appointment to posts within Practical Action will be subject to a satisfactory criminal check. Criminal checks will be conducted for all roles. The successful applicant must already have the right to both live and work in the country that they are applying for, in this case, the United Kingdom and should be willing and able to travel. If you want to work for an organisation with significant people ambitions, then we would like to hear from you. Please submit a copy of your CV (Maximum 2 pages) and a supporting statement that describes your suitability for the role and include answers to the following questions, Questions 1. Interest and motivation: What draws you to international development and environmental issues, and why does Practical Action's mission and approach appeal to you specifically? Have you done anything (through study, volunteering, work experience, or personal interest) to explore this area so far? 2. Research and analytical skills: Tell us about a piece of research or analysis you've done — this could be from your studies, a work placement, a personal project, or volunteering — where you had to work with data or information and turn it into something clear and useful for someone else. What tools did you use, and how did you decide what mattered most? 3. Working with others and staying organised: Give an example of a time you worked as part of a team, possibly with people remotely in different geographies, and had to juggle several priorities or deadlines at once. This could be a group project, part-time job, society, or placement. Closing date for applications: September 21st 2026
