item.title: EDIS Programme Manager
item.description: Job Title: EDIS Programme Manager (Equality, Diversity and Inclusion in Science and Health) Reporting to: Head of EDIS Responsible for : Project staff, contractors, consultants and delivery partners as required. Based: Our Head Office is based in London, but we have an agile working policy enabling people to work at another UK location up to 4 days/week. Requests for permanent remote working will be considered and we welcome applications from people based in other parts of the UK. Hours: Full-time (35 hours per week). Requests for part-time or flexible working will be considered Contract: Permanent Salary: £40,517 to £44,423 FTE per annum About Us The British Science Association (BSA) was founded in 1831 and is a registered charity. We are creating a future where science is more relevant, representative, and connected to society. We have ambitious goals to put people at the heart of science. About the role The EDIS Programme Manager will provide the stewardship and coordination needed to translate EDIS's strategic ambitions into practical, high-quality delivery. The role will lead programme planning, reporting, risk management and delivery oversight across the EDIS portfolio. It will ensure that activity is well sequenced, clearly governed and focused on practical progress against EDIS priorities. A central focus will be the development and stewardship of the Embedding EDI workstream. The postholder will work closely with members, partners and stakeholders to shape priorities, agree shared approaches, co-create practical tools, guidance and resources, support implementation across member and partner settings, identify learning and improvement opportunities, and help embed inclusive practice across EDIS activity. Working with EDIS members, delivery partners, the Francis Crick Institute, Wellcome and colleagues across the British Science Association, the postholder will help to ensure that programme activity is joined up, evidence-informed and focused on meaningful, sustainable change across the science and health research sector. This role would suit someone who combines strong programme management with collaborative leadership, systems thinking, and a clear commitment to and knowledge of equity, diversity and inclusion. The successful candidate will be confident moving between strategy and delivery, helping to shape the future direction of EDIS while ensuring that programmes, partnerships and workstreams are delivered effectively. Key responsibilities Lead programme delivery across the EDIS portfolio, ensuring activities are strategically aligned, effectively planned and delivered against agreed priorities, objectives, budgets and timelines. Provide programme leadership, governance and oversight, maintaining programme plans, risk and issue management processes, action tracking, performance monitoring, financial reporting to support informed decision-making. Lead the development and stewardship of the Embedding EDI workstream, working with members and partners to develop practical tools, guidance, resources and implementation approaches that support sustainable organisational change across the sector. Coordinate delivery across EDIS workstreams and partnerships, ensuring member engagement, commissioned activity, evidence generation, communications and reporting are joined up and contribute to shared outcomes. Develop and maintain effective relationships with members, funders, delivery partners, suppliers and key stakeholders, acting as a trusted point of coordination and supporting collaborative delivery across the EDIS network. Manage the procurement, contracting and performance of consultants, commissioned partners and suppliers, ensuring high-quality delivery, effective resource management and value for money. Lead approaches to monitoring programme performance, impact, learning and continuous improvement, ensuring evidence and insight are used to strengthen delivery and demonstrate progress against EDIS objectives. Prepare and present high-quality reports, briefings and recommendations for the Head of EDIS, BSA leadership, governance groups, funders and other stakeholders, communicating progress, risks, opportunities and key decisions clearly and effectively. Support funder engagement, strategic partnership development and long-term sustainability planning, helping to identify opportunities for growth, influence and future investment in EDIS. Champion equity, diversity and inclusion throughout programme delivery, ensuring inclusive practice, accessibility and meaningful participation are embedded across planning, implementation, governance, learning and evaluation. About you The successful candidate will bring the following experience, skills and approach. Essential criteria Significant experience managing complex programmes, projects or portfolios with multiple workstreams. Experience developing and maintaining programme plans, milestones and reporting systems. This will include maintaining programme plans, governance arrangements, risk and issue management processes, delivery reporting, budget monitoring and financial reporting, ensuring accurate oversight of programme performance, expenditure, value for money and organisational accountability. Substantial experience applying equity, diversity and inclusion in practice at a programme or organisational level, including using inclusive design principles, accessibility considerations and relevant legal duties to shape planning, delivery, governance and learning. Experience of facilitating collaboration between multiple stakeholders, members or partners with different insights and perspectives. Experience of maintaining programme governance, including identifying and managing risks, dependencies and delivery challenges across multiple workstreams. Experience working with multiple partners, stakeholders or suppliers to deliver shared outcomes. Ability to produce clear, well-structured written outputs, such as reports, briefings, decision papers or similar materials, that support understanding, discussion and decision-making for different audiences. Ability to take ownership of agreed areas of programme delivery, manage priorities across workstreams and make progress with appropriate support, while keeping managers and senior colleagues informed about key risks, decisions, dependencies and delivery progress. Desirable criteria We do not expect candidates to have all of the following, but one or more would be helpful in the role. Experience working in science, research, health, public engagement, charity or membership settings. Experience commissioning or managing consultants, suppliers or delivery partners. Experience developing practical toolkits, guidance or resources for organisational change. The closing date for applications is Friday 2nd October 2026. First interviews are due to take place online w/c 26th October 2026, with second interviews (in person in London) expected on Monday 2nd November 2026. Interested? If you would like to find out more, please click the apply button. You will be directed to our website to complete your application for this position. As part of the British Science Association’s commitment to being a Disability Confident employer, all disabled applicants who meet the ‘essential criteria’ for this vacancy will be offered an interview under our guaranteed interview scheme. No agencies please.

item.title: EDIS Community and Engagement Officer
item.description: Job Title: EDIS Community and Engagement Officer (Equality, Diversity and Inclusion in Science and Health) Reporting to: Head of EDIS Responsible for : No direct reports Based: Our Head Office is based in London, but we have an agile working policy enabling people to work at another UK location up to 4 days/week. Requests for permanent remote working will be considered and we welcome applications from people based in other parts of the UK. Hours: Full-time (35 hours per week). Requests for part-time or flexible working will be considered. Contract: Permanent Salary: £34,572 to £36,506 FTE per annum About Us The British Science Association (BSA) was founded in 1831 and is a registered charity. We are creating a future where science is more relevant, representative, and connected to society. We have ambitious goals to put people at the heart of science. About the role The EDIS Community and Engagement Officer will provide the coordination, communication and relationship-building needed to support the growth, participation and value of the EDIS membership community. The role will support day-to-day member onboarding, engagement activity, communications, events and community-building processes across the EDIS portfolio. It will ensure that members are supported to connect with each other, contribute to EDIS priorities and access opportunities to learn, share and collaborate. You will work with the EDIS team and with BSA communications team colleagues to support their work. A central focus will be building effective, inclusive and accessible routes for member participation. Working with EDIS members, partners and colleagues across the British Science Association, the postholder will help to ensure that engagement activity is joined up, responsive to member needs and focused on meaningful participation across the science and health research sector. This role would suit someone who combines strong organisational approaches with proactive communication, relationship building, and a commitment to and knowledge of equity, diversity and inclusion. The successful candidate will be confident supporting communities, networks and membership groups, helping to strengthen the EDIS community while ensuring that engagement, communications and events are delivered effectively. Key responsibilities Support day-to-day member onboarding and support processes, ensuring new and existing members understand how to participate in EDIS activity. Coordinate with the Communications Team to develop member communications, newsletters and engagement content, ensuring activity is joined up, accessible and responsive to member needs. Plan and support delivery of events, workshops, peer learning sessions including ‘special interest’ groups and network activity that create practical opportunities for members to learn, share and collaborate. Maintain accurate membership records, contact lists and engagement data, supporting clear information flow across BSA, EDIS members and partners. Gather member insight and feedback, identifying themes, opportunities and barriers to participation that can inform programme design and delivery. Apply inclusive practice in all communications, events, engagement activity and member support, reflecting a clear commitment to and knowledge of equity, diversity and inclusion. Support membership growth and retention by helping demonstrate the value of involvement in EDIS and strengthening routes for member participation. Work with the Research and Policy Officer and Programme Manager to ensure member insight informs evidence, programme design, engagement activity and delivery. Support the production of accessible resources, meeting materials and event content that help members connect with each other and contribute to EDIS priorities. Contribute to the promotion of EDIS activity across sector networks and communication channels, supporting meaningful participation across the science and health research sector. About you The successful candidate will bring the following experience, skills and approach. Essential criteria Experience of coordinating activity within a membership organisation, community group, network, events or engagement programme. Strong approach to organisation, with the ability to coordinate varied tasks, manage competing priorities and work towards agreed deadlines with appropriate support. Demonstrable commitment to equity, diversity and inclusion, with practical experience applying inclusive approaches in events, communications, member support or engagement activity. Ability to communicate clearly in writing and through other appropriate channels, tailoring style and content to encourage understanding and engagement across varied audiences. Experience developing communications tailored to specific professional audiences, including meeting materials, event content and/or engagement updates. Experience maintaining accurate records, contact lists, membership information or engagement data, with attention to detail and appropriate handling of information. Ability to build positive working relationships with members, partners, community groups or stakeholders, supporting participation and responding constructively to different needs. Experience gathering feedback, insight or views from members, participants or stakeholders, and identifying practical themes that can inform activity or improvement. Proactive and reflective approach to problem solving and continuous improvement, with the ability to identify practical improvements and support an evolving programme. Desirable criteria We do not expect candidates to have all of the following, but one or more would be helpful in the role. Experience working in science, research, health, charity or membership settings. Experience using CRM, event or membership management systems. Experience supporting consultation, co-design or peer learning activity. Experience producing digital content or newsletters. The closing date for applications is Monday 5th October 2026. First interviews are due to take place online on 4th November 2026, with second interviews (in person in London) expected on 11th November 2026. Interview dates have been scheduled outside the school holiday period to support participation from the broadest possible pool of candidates and to minimise potential barriers for those with caring or family responsibilities. Interested? If you would like to find out more, please click the apply button. You will be directed to our website to complete your application for this position. As part of the British Science Association’s commitment to being a Disability Confident employer, all disabled applicants who meet the ‘essential criteria’ for this vacancy will be offered an interview under our guaranteed interview scheme. No agencies please.

item.title: Communications and Events Coordinator
item.description: About the role: Working closely with the small team at SIDA this post will promote the work of SIDA through the provision of high-quality digital communication to our members, external stakeholders and the general public, and provide logistical, digital and administrative support for a range of member events including our annual conferences. The Communications and Events Coordinator will develop engaging content for use across SIDA’s digital platforms, including the Member Hub, and be proactive in finding new ways to share messages and reach a wider audience. The postholder is responsible for putting together, disseminating and promoting regular email newsletters. The post will contribute to a variety of projects and initiatives, and a willingness to collaborate and work closely and flexibly with colleagues is essential. Responsibilities · Support the implementation of SIDA’s communications strategy · Build digital assets to raise awareness of SIDA’s activities and services; engage the public; and promote the work of members · Gather content, write copy, and produce engaging regular email newsletters about SIDA and the sector · Manage and develop initiatives to grow SIDA’s Member Hub · Maintain and deliver a social media schedule and seek opportunities to reach new audiences · Manage and maintain the front-end of SIDA website · Provide communications, technical and administrative support for events run by SIDA · Assist with responding to general enquiries and correspondence from members, key stakeholders and members of the public · Provide general digital and design support as and when required · Any other tasks as may be reasonably required Skills, knowledge, experience Essential · Excellent written communication skills and experience in producing content relevant for websites, social media, publications and leaflets across a range of audiences · Strong attention to detail, with an ability to synthesise specialist information into clear, readable copy · Good design skills and experience of creating engaging content using Canva · Experience of promoting engagement on social media · Experience maintaining and updating front-end of websites, including familiarity with WordPress or similar platforms · Ability to work with minimal supervision and to deadlines · Ability to multi-task and prioritise workload effectively · Strong administrative skills · Commitment to the values of SIDA, and supporting the role of SIDA in working towards a decolonised, actively anti-racist approach · Works well as part of a team Desirable · Relevant experience in the development and delivery of communications and campaigns strategies · Experience of gathering and organising content for monthly newsletters, researching relevant news articles and updates across the sector · Experience maintaining and growing online communities · Interest or experience in global sustainable development · Creativity - an ability to tell compelling stories using a range of formats and media, including familiarity with producing video and audio content. · Experience of supporting in-person and hybrid events · Experience of putting together and marketing podcasts · Experience of using CRM and communications platforms including Beacon and Campaign Monitor Safeguarding Commitment SIDA is committed to safeguarding and protecting the people we serve and work with. We are a proud member of the Inter-Agency Misconduct Disclosure Scheme. In line with this scheme, we systematically request information from previous employers regarding any findings or pending investigations of sexual exploitation, abuse, or harassment during employment.

item.title: High Value Development Officer
item.description: High Value Development Officer We are seeking a talented writer and relationship-builder to help create compelling propositions that inspire high-value donors to support vital work. Position: High Value Development Officer Salary: Circa £31,700 per annum, with London weighting where applicable Location: Home-based Hours: 36 hours – flexible 4 day week or 9 day fortnight Contract: Fixed term until April 2027 Closing date: CV’s reviewed on a rolling basis About the role This is an exciting opportunity to join a High Value Engagement team and play an important role in developing compelling donor communications, propositions and stewardship materials. Working across Philanthropy, Trusts & Grants and Corporate Partnerships, you will help ensure high-value donors receive timely, accurate and engaging information that demonstrates the impact of their support and encourages long-term relationships. Key responsibilities will include: Developing compelling cases for support, bespoke proposals and donor materials. Researching and gathering information, data, case studies and evidence for bids, pitches and proposals. Creating fundraising toolkits including budgets, case studies, digital assets and stewardship materials. Supporting the development of the high-value donor stewardship programme. Helping to organise donor stewardship activities, webinars and small events. Turning complex health, impact and business intelligence data into accessible and persuasive fundraising content. Building strong relationships across internal teams to source the information fundraisers need. Working alongside creative colleagues to develop visual content that helps bring the organisation’s work and impact to life. About you You will be an excellent writer and researcher who can take complex information and turn it into clear, concise and compelling content. You will have strong research and analytical skills, excellent attention to detail and the ability to manage competing priorities and deadlines. Comfortable working collaboratively across an organisation, you will be confident building relationships with colleagues at all levels and able to work independently using your own initiative. You will also be confident using Microsoft Office and databases and have strong administrative and communication skills. Fundraising experience would be valuable, but the skills required could also have been developed within communications, research, bid writing, marketing, business development or another environment where persuasive written content and relationship-building are central. About the organisation You will be joining a leading UK charity supporting people affected by stroke. Working across the organisation, you will gain exposure to a wide range of services and impact, helping high-value fundraisers tell compelling stories that inspire supporters and strengthen long-term donor relationships. You will be joining an organisation committed to its values, equal opportunities and diversity. Other roles you may have experience of could include: Fundraising Officer, High Value Fundraising Officer, Development Officer, Trusts and Grants Officer, Bid Writer, Proposal Writer, Fundraising Communications Officer, Philanthropy Officer, Corporate Partnerships Officer, Donor Engagement Officer or Fundraising Content Officer.

item.title: Business Development Executive
item.description: What are we looking for? Are you a confident relationship-builder who can spot potential in a conversation and inspire businesses to support a local cause? We are looking for a creative and results-focused Business Development Executive who understands what motivates businesses and can build mutually beneficial partnerships. You will develop new business, build relationships with prospective partners and create tailored opportunities that generate income and wider support for St. Michael’s Hospice, while helping existing corporate supporters deepen their involvement. Key Responsibilities: Be an active and visible presence within the local business community, building new relationships through purposeful networking, meetings and consistent follow-up. Research and approach prospective corporate partners, identify shared opportunities and develop a strong pipeline of new business. Secure new income and support by presenting compelling ideas, making confident asks, negotiating effectively and following opportunities through to agreement. Develop fresh and creative partnership opportunities that go beyond traditional fundraising and offer genuine value to both the business and the Hospice. Grow existing corporate relationships by understanding each business’s priorities and identifying opportunities to increase or broaden its support. Work collaboratively with colleagues across the Hospice to shape and deliver successful corporate partnerships. What We’re Looking For: Experience in business development, sales, recruitment, account management, corporate partnerships or fundraising. Charity-sector experience is welcome but not essential. A proactive and self-motivated approach, with the confidence to take ownership, initiate conversations and actively seek out new opportunities. A track record of building strong relationships and securing new business, partnerships or other tangible results. Confidence in networking, presenting, negotiating and making a clear ask, combined with the determination to follow opportunities through. A creative thinker who can spot potential, generate new ideas, make a persuasive case for them and take responsibility for turning them into action. Highly organised, with a consistent approach to follow-up and the ability to manage multiple relationships at different stages. A collaborative approach, a full driving licence, access to a car and flexibility to work occasional evenings and weekends. Why work with us? You will join a supportive and ambitious fundraising team with an established network of corporate relationships and a clear corporate strategy to build upon. This is an outward-facing role with genuine scope to take ownership, introduce new ideas, test different approaches and influence the next stage of our corporate development. We offer office or hybrid working with an expectation to be in the office a minimum of 3 days per week and a location close to the hospice for ease of access. Plus, you’ll love working in an environment where every day brings new challenges and rewards. St. Michael’s Hospice is committed to safeguarding and promoting the welfare of vulnerable adults, children and young people. All staff are expected to share this commitment. Successful candidates will be required to undergo relevant background checks, including a DBS check and provide satisfactory reference before starting the role. About St. Michael’s Hospice St. Michael’s Hospice (North Hampshire) is a registered charity and provides support to people diagnosed with a life-limiting illness. It is a Hospice for adults providing invaluable palliative and end-of-life care services in North Hampshire, offering comfort, support, and dignity to those facing life's most challenging moments. As a charity, we depend on the kindness and support of our local community to continue offering our services free of charge. It may come as a surprise, but only 22% of our funding comes from the government. End-of-life care is an essential service, not a luxury, yet it is not funded like other care services. To keep the Hospice’s services running, we need raise an additional £15,000 every day. Our benefits We offer a competitive salary with attractive benefits, including, free parking, life assurance, 28 days annual leave plus bank holidays, and an extensive health and wellbeing plan and company pension. Interested? For more information or an informal chat about the role, please contact the fundraising team. How to Apply: To be considered for this role, please submit the following: Cover letter explaining why you’re an ideal candidate for this position. Please note that applications without this will not be considered. CV outlining your relevant experience and skills. Closing date: Friday 25 September at 12 noon Interview Date: Wednesday 30th September in person at Millennium House, Priestley Road, RG24 9GZ

item.title: Junior Developer
item.description: £28,860 per year (London Living Wage) Permanent full-time (37.5 hours per week) Hybrid working with 3 days a week in our London Bridge Office What the job involves We’re looking for a Junior Developer to join our Technology and Solutions team and help colleagues across the charity make better use of data, systems and automation. You’ll work alongside our small development team, reporting to the Product and Delivery Manager and supported by experienced technical colleagues. You’ll contribute across the full development lifecycle, from understanding requirements and writing code to testing, deployment and support. You’ll develop and maintain software applications and automation, troubleshoot issues, document solutions and respond to first-line requests involving data development and analysis. You’ll also help improve SharePoint and Microsoft 365 processes and work with tools such as Microsoft SQL Server, PHP, Power Automate, TOCA.IO and Copilot Studio. As our use of AI develops, you’ll help identify, prototype and test practical solutions that reduce manual effort and improve how teams work, while making sure they are accurate, safe, well documented and used with appropriate human oversight. This is a hands-on development opportunity where you’ll build your technical skills, share learning and see the practical difference your work makes across the charity. What we want from you You’ll be at the beginning of your technology career, with demonstrable IT skills gained through formal study, a bootcamp, self-directed learning or practical experience. You’ll have good programming fundamentals, an understanding of the software development lifecycle and some familiarity with software development tools, methods, databases or automation technologies. We’re looking for someone who is naturally curious, thoughtful in their approach to problem-solving and attentive to detail. You’ll be comfortable working both independently and collaboratively, asking questions, sharing ideas and learning from others. You’ll be able to explain technical concepts clearly to non-technical colleagues and will be motivated to keep developing your knowledge and skills. Experience with tools such as SQL Server, PHP, Power Automate, SharePoint, robotic automation or AI platforms would be an advantage, but you won’t be expected to know everything from day one. Most importantly, you’ll be eager to learn, generous in sharing your knowledge and committed to using technology responsibly to make a positive difference. Why work with us? Every man needs to know about the most common cancer in men – prostate cancer. It’s a real and present danger that takes over 12,000 of our dads, grandads, brothers and friends each year. Prostate Cancer UK is the largest men’s health charity in the UK. We have a simple ambition – to stop prostate cancer damaging lives. We invest millions in research to revolutionise testing, treatment and care. We’re blazing a trail to a screening programme that could save thousands of lives with regular, accurate tests for all men at risk. And we work tirelessly to spread the word about risk and offer specialist support to people living with the disease. Work with us and you’ll see your efforts pay off as we give men and their families the power to navigate prostate cancer. Our commitment to equity, diversity and inclusion At Prostate Cancer UK we’re committed to righting health inequalities across the UK, starting with those faced by Black men. This includes ground-breaking research into Black men's risk and working with communities directly to overcome barriers to the diagnosis and treatment of prostate cancer. To make this happen, we're dedicated to being an inclusive, proactive organisation, as we strive to be Allies to Black communities. We’ll achieve this by advocating and working alongside those communities to promote change. We're also working to be Allies to each other, not only protected groups. In 2024, we launched our New Allyship Training Programme. All colleagues at Prostate Cancer UK will be trained to act and identify as an Ally. We've also signed Business in the Communities Race at Work Charter, as a dedication to our Black health equity work and wider EDI priorities. As a signatory, we're responsible and accountable for driving positive change. How and where we work Colleagues attend the office at least four days per month (pro rata for part-time colleagues) to collaborate, build relationships, and support projects and decision-making. You can choose where to work the rest of the time. Travel to the office is a commute, so we pay our own travel costs. Additional in-person attendance will be required during your first few months for induction and training, to support you to learn the role and get to know colleagues. We trust colleagues to work flexibly while balancing personal commitments with the needs of the charity, and we are committed to making reasonable adjustments for colleagues with a disability, neurodiversity, or a long-term physical or mental health condition. How to Apply Visit our Prostate Cancer UK Careers page to learn more about this role and the benefits we offer. We’re expecting the interviews for this role to be held in person at our London Bridge office. Prostate Cancer UK is a registered charity in England and Wales (1005541) and in Scotland (SC039332). item.title: Specialist Multiple Disadvantage Worker
item.description: About the role: For women facing multiple disadvantage, the right support can be the difference between remaining trapped by systems and beginning to rebuild safety, choice and control. As our Specialist Multiple Disadvantage Worker at Grace House, you’ll provide skilled, persistent and compassionate support to women whose experiences may include homelessness, domestic abuse, trauma, substance use, poor mental health and contact with the criminal justice system. Using a gender and trauma-informed approach, you’ll build trusting relationships and work alongside women at their own pace. You’ll manage complex casework, advocate firmly on their behalf and help navigate services and systems that can often feel fragmented or difficult to access. You’ll use creativity, professional judgement and tenacity to challenge barriers and help women move forward on their own terms. You’ll also bring your expertise into multi-agency discussions, ensuring women’s voices, experiences and priorities remain central to the decisions made about their support. Working closely with colleagues and external partners, you’ll help shape responsive, coordinated support and contribute to the continued development of practice across Grace House. This is an opportunity to deepen your specialist skills, take real ownership of your work and make a visible difference in women’s lives. You’ll be supported by an experienced team, reflective practice and ongoing learning and development at Single Homeless Project (SHP), giving you the tools and confidence to grow while delivering support that genuinely changes lives. *For genuine occupational requirement reasons, we are seeking applications from women only for this post (exemption under the Equality Act 2010; Schedule 9 Part 1). About you: You know how to build trust with women who may have been let down by services before, working with patience, honesty and consistency. You bring strong experience of supporting women facing multiple disadvantage and understand how trauma, abuse, homelessness, poor mental health and substance use can overlap. You stay calm when situations are complex, using sound judgement to assess risk, make decisions and keep support moving forward. You are a determined advocate who will challenge barriers, bring partners together and keep pushing when systems are not responding. You are reflective, curious and ready to deepen your specialist practice, with support, supervision and development opportunities at SHP. About us: We’re London’s leading homelessness charity – and we get things done. In a city where hundreds are forced into homelessness every day, our work has never been more needed or more challenging. And we’re not shying away. We’re rolling up our sleeves to make change and helping over 10,000 Londoners every year. We prevent homelessness, provide safe places to live and give people the opportunity to rebuild their lives and transform their futures. And we never give up. We’re here for Londoners wherever they are on their journey. We start with trust, building relationships that help people feel safe, supported, and ready to move forward. Every day, we put people first in everything we do, challenging injustice and barriers that keep people from the safety, stability and opportunity they deserve. We stand alongside people as they rebuild and shape a future that feels their own. Joining Single Homeless Project means joining a team that’s bold, compassionate and determined to do better for the people we support and for each other. You’ll work alongside colleagues with lived experience, in a space that’s trans-inclusive, disability-friendly, and actively striving to be anti-oppressive and equitable. We’re not perfect, but we’re real. We listen. We learn. And we push forward, together. Because this isn’t just a job. It’s a chance to lead with empathy, spark change, and help build a London where no one is left behind. Important info: Applications will be reviewed and suitable candidates invited to interview online as they are received. Therefore, please submit your application as soon as possible to be considered. We reserve the right to close the vacancy as soon as a suitable candidate is identified. Please note there will be a second stage interview in service in Camden for suitable candidates. This post will require an Enhanced DBS check to be processed (by SHP) for the successful applicant. Please note applications are reviewed for AI use in application questions. Applications with insufficient right to work or requiring sponsorship will not be accepted for this role.

item.title: Policy Development Lead
item.description: The Role Policy Development Lead We are looking for a Policy Development Lead to provide strategic leadership, coordination and expertise in proactive policy development across NDCS. This exciting new role will help us think beyond immediate policy activity, identify where system change is needed, and develop longer-term policy positions that are informed by evidence, specialist insight, lived experience and external practice. The role will initially focus on Education , while retaining the flexibility to support wider policy development across areas such as early years, social care, health, benefits, sign language and other emerging priorities. Working closely with Platform Leads, Policy and Nation Leads, and colleagues across the organisation, you will help ensure NDCS develops strong, evidence-based policy positions that create meaningful change for deaf children and their families. What you'll do Lead and coordinate proactive policy development activity across NDCS, identifying opportunities for deeper policy thinking and systems change. Apply systems thinking to identify complex challenges, explore interdependencies and develop practical solutions Identify emerging trends, risks and opportunities, using systems thinking and horizon-scanning approaches to inform future organisational priorities. Translate complex evidence, research and lived experience into clear recommendations that support organisational decision-making and influence. Influence senior leaders and key stakeholders by providing strategic policy advice, insight and recommendations. Lead and coordinate policy development activity across multiple teams, ensuring expertise, insight and activity are aligned. Build productive relationships with external researchers, policy networks and sector experts to bring innovative thinking into NDCS. Identify cross-cutting themes and opportunities for change by bringing together insight from local, regional and national sources. Facilitate strategic conversations that help colleagues explore complex issues, understand system interdependencies and develop long-term solutions. Champion a proactive, evidence-informed approach to policy development across the organisation. What you'll need Significant experience in policy analysis, development or strategy within a complex organisation, sector or policy environment. Proven ability to translate complex evidence, research and lived experience into recommendations that drive organisational action and influence. Experience influencing senior decision-makers and shaping organisational, sector-wide or public policy direction. A track record of leading and coordinating complex work across multiple teams, functions or stakeholders. Excellent communication skills, including the ability to produce high-quality briefings, policy positions and strategic recommendations. Experience bringing together evidence and insight from multiple sources to identify emerging issues, trends and opportunities for change. Strong systems-thinking skills and experience developing long-term solutions to complex challenges. The ability to lead through collaboration, credibility and specialist expertise, building alignment across diverse teams and stakeholders. Strong understanding of the policy, practice and systemic issues affecting deaf children and families, and the ability to apply this knowledge to strategic policy development. Strong digital skills and a sound understanding of agile values & principles. Acriminal record check / DBS disclosure (if offered the position). What you'll get Home-based working with flexible hours . 25 days holiday - plus an additional 3 days at Christmas (& bank holidays). Pension (5.5% employer contribution). Healthcare Cashplan. Annual performance-based salary increase . Employee Assistance & Wellbeing Programmes. What we do The National Deaf Children's Society are the leading charity for deaf children. We give expert support on childhood deafness, raise awareness and campaign for deaf children's rights, so they have the same opportunities as everyone else. Pre-employment checks As part of our commitment to creating a safe and trusted environment for the children, young people and families we support, all offers of employment are subject to background checks. These include Right to Work verification, Criminal Record Disclosure, and ID and address verification. To complete an online Right to Work check, you will need a valid UK or Irish passport, or a government share code if you are not a British citizen. If an online check is not possible, we’ll need to verify your documents in person at our London office. Please be aware that travel time and expenses for this appointment cannot be reimbursed. Disability Confidence We are a Disability Confident Employer and committed to offering interviews to candidates who request to be considered under the disability confident scheme and meet the minimum requirements for the role. The National Deaf Children’s Society is a registered charity in England and Wales no. 1016532 and in Scotland no. SC040779.

item.title: Community Programme Manager
item.description: WEST LONDON SYNAGOGUE Job Description Job Title Community Programme Manager Department Community: Social Action, Interfaith Line Manager Director of Operations & Community Hours Full time, 36.5 hours per week (some evening and Sunday working required, in line with the programme calendar) Salary £42,000-£45,000, dependent on experience Background West London Synagogue, founded in 1840, has a long-standing reputation as a leading and innovative institution within Progressive Judaism. It has played a significant role in shaping modern Jewish life and continues to hold a unique and influential position within the UK Jewish community. With approximately 3,000 members, WLS is a lively, engaged and diverse community, with a strong commitment to Jewish life, social responsibility and engagement with the wider community. WLS has an established and valued portfolio of Social Action and Interfaith activity, reflecting our commitment to making a positive contribution both within and beyond our congregation. We are now looking to build on this strong foundation, developing and expanding these areas to increase participation, strengthen partnerships and deepen their impact. The Role This newly combined role brings Social Action and Interfaith activity together under one postholder. The Programme Manager will be responsible for developing these areas strategically, growing participation and impact, building relationships and partnerships, and identifying new opportunities for meaningful engagement and community contribution. The purpose of the role: • To implement an integrated strategy for the delivery of WLS's Social Action and Interfaith activities, and the associated role of volunteers. • To facilitate the smooth running and ongoing development of current WLS projects, alongside the introduction and implementation of new projects in these areas. • To work with other members of staff, clergy and lay leadership to consolidate, and expand WLS's Social Action and Interfaith provision. • To recruit, train, empower and retain an increasing number of community members as volunteers. • To assist with funding applications and expense control relating to projects, working closely with the fundraising and finance teams. Summary of Tasks 1. Social Action Projects – Maintain and enhance existing social action projects, including the ongoing recruitment of participants and ensuring their financial viability, including cost control. – Support the ongoing development of the WLS flagship Drop-in Programmes - for families seeking asylum and the Rainbow Drop-in for an LGBTQ population – Develop a range of self-sustaining, hands-on social action projects for each age group at WLS, especially youth, students and young adults. – Prepare timely reports, fundraising administration and formal feedback, as needed. 2. Interfaith Projects – Execute and enhance our newly drafted Interfaith strategy, which focuses on education and awareness, grassroots initiatives, celebratory events and representation in the broader community; – Attract and retain volunteers on an ad hoc basis for the interfaith initiatives; – Work collaboratively with the community team and with the trustee responsible for Interfaith. 3. Experimental & Cross-Cutting Projects – Identify, develop and lead selected new initiatives that align with WLS's strategic priorities and community needs General Responsibilities · Develop, maintain and manage an annual programme plan for Social Action and Interfaith activity, ensuring that projects and initiatives are aligned with WLS’s strategic priorities and community needs. · Establish appropriate measures and processes to assess the reach, participation, outcomes and wider impact of programmes, regularly reviewing performance and using insight, feedback and data to improve existing activity and inform the development of new initiatives. · Identify opportunities to increase the reach , relevance and impact of Social Action and Interfaith programmes, ensuring that activity continues to respond to the needs and interests of the WLS community and the wider community. · Develop and manage a strong volunteer programme , including recruitment, induction, training, support, recognition and retention, and create meaningful opportunities for members to contribute their time, skills and experience. · Manage relevant programme budgets including planning expenditure, monitoring income and expenditure, and ensuring that activity is delivered within agreed budgets. · Build and maintain effective relationships with internal stakeholders, community organisations, faith communities, charities and other external partners, identifying opportunities for collaboration and developing new initiatives where appropriate. · Collaborate with the engagement team to develop and implement appropriate communications and engagement plans to promote programmes and encourage participation. · Attend and contribute actively to regular staff meetings, Board and committee meetings, and relevant project and working groups , providing updates on programme development, progress and impact as required. · Contribute to the wider life of WLS , including festival celebrations and other community activities, as appropriate to the role. · Support the development and implementation of WLS’s vision, policies and procedures, particularly in relation to Social Action and Interfaith activity involving adults, young people and children. · Maintain awareness of, and ensure compliance with, all relevant regulations and WLS policies relating to safeguarding, particularly when working with children and vulnerable adults. · Contribute to the development of funding and income-generation opportunities , including grants, sponsorships and partnerships, where relevant to the programme. Person Specification Essential • Proven experience of managing projects and/or volunteers, with a track record of managing a varied workload and conflicting priorities to deadline. • Experience of, or a strong interest in, social action and/or interfaith work. • Excellent organisational skills and strong IT skills, including Microsoft Office 365. • Excellent written and spoken English, with the ability to prepare clear reports and communications. • Outstanding interpersonal skills, and a demonstrated ability to relate well to a diverse audience across all ages within the community. • Demonstrated ability to balance the expression of views and values with respect for all. • A high standard of personal integrity, and the ability to handle sensitive information with discretion and confidentiality. • Self-motivated, proactive and comfortable working both independently and as part of a team. • Flexibility to work some evenings and Sundays in line with the programme calendar. • A good knowledge of, and enthusiasm for, Judaism. • A good knowledge of Child and Vulnerable Adults safeguarding law and best practice. • Willingness to obtain, or already holding, a recognised First Aid certificate. Desirable • Experience of grant fundraising or completing funding applications. • A UK driving licence. • Experience working closely with boards, volunteers and clergy. Personal Qualities • A collaborative team player who embraces change and is willing to get hands-on to deliver results. • Proactive, enthusiastic, friendly and committed to making a difference. • A good sense of humour and a warm, approachable manner. Please note that this post is subject to: • Two satisfactory references • Confirmation of eligibility to work in the UK • An enhanced DBS check

item.title: Fundraising Officers: Birmingham, London, Bradford/North
item.description: As a Fundraising Officer with Islamic Help, you’ll play a vital role in securing funding for our humanitarian programmes, and supporting and improving the quality of life for the most vulnerable around the world. POSITION: Fundraising Officers: Birmingham, London, Bradford/the North SALARY: £28k - £33k dependent on experience DURATION: Permanent, Full Time (40 hours per week) WORKING HOURS: Variable (Core Office Hours are Mon-Fri 10am to 6pm. Due to the nature of the role, the successful candidate will be required to work flexible hours, including evenings and weekends, in line with business needs. REPORTING TO: Head of Fundraising Deadline for applications: 6pm Wednesday 30th September 2026 THE COMPANY Islamic Help is a UK-based international relief and development organisation that has developed rapidly since being established in 2003. Our programmes aim to support and empower disadvantaged communities in the UK and abroad. Some of the key areas we work in are emergency response, WASH, education, livelihood and environment conservation. As part of our continued commitment to improve community relationships, deliver events nationwide and generate income for our humanitarian programmes, we are expanding our fundraising teams across the country and are looking for fundraising officers in Birmingham, London and Bradford/the North. These are performance-based roles and postholders will be expected to meet financial and other related targets. WHAT WE OFFER Islamic Help acknowledges that our employees are our most valuable resource. Therefore, we provide a variety of benefits aimed at promoting their professional growth, as well as supporting their mental and physical well-being, and maintaining a healthy work-life balance. Holiday entitlement of 30 days per financial year (includes bank holiday entitlement -due to the nature of the role, you may be required to work on bank holidays). Personal learning and development opportunities. Automatic enrolment into our workplace Pension Plan (option to opt out). Employee Assistance Programme for support with health & wellbeing, financial matters, and other personal support. Free office car park for staff (at our Birmingham HQ). ABOUT THE ROLE The Fundraising Officer/s will be responsible for planning, co-ordinating, and executing all fundraising activities and initiatives. The role requires the development and implementation of strategies to maximise donations and enhance donor relationships, in alignment with Islamic Help’s fundraising strategy. This position involves engagement with individual donors, businesses, and community partners to secure financial support for Islamic Help’s life-saving projects. This is a great opportunity for someone who enjoys connecting with people, thrives in a fast-paced environment, and is passionate about making a real difference. As a Fundraising Officer, you’ll play a vital role in securing funding for our humanitarian programmes, and supporting and improving the quality of life for the most vulnerable around the world. KEY RESPONSIBILITIES Plan, coordinate and deliver income-generating fundraising campaigns, appeals and community events in line with Islamic Help's fundraising strategy and organisational objectives. Generate income in line with agreed monthly and annual fundraising targets, taking ownership of individual fundraising performance and proactively identifying opportunities to maximise income. Build and maintain strong relationships with donors, fundraisers, businesses, mosques, community organisations and other stakeholders to secure financial support and develop long-term partnerships. Identify, develop and pursue new fundraising and partnership opportunities at local and regional levels. Recruit, support, brief, co-ordinate and motivate volunteers to assist with fundraising activities, community events and campaigns, ensuring they are appropriately supported and equipped to represent Islamic Help. Recruit, support and steward individual fundraisers, providing guidance, resources and ongoing engagement to help them maximise their fundraising potential. Manage and accurately record online and offline donations, pledges and fundraising activity, ensuring donor records are maintained appropriately and communications are timely, accurate and professional. Maintain accurate fundraising and donor records, ensuring relevant information is captured on Islamic Help's CRM and other internal systems. Monitor fundraising performance and provide regular updates and reports to the Head of Fundraising on income, activities, opportunities, challenges and outcomes. Represent Islamic Help professionally at fundraising events, community activities, meetings and other external engagements, acting as an ambassador for the organisation and its work. Support donor stewardship and engagement, ensuring supporters receive an appropriate and positive experience throughout their relationship with Islamic Help. Ensure fundraising activities are delivered in accordance with Islamic Help policies, safeguarding requirements and relevant fundraising regulations and legal standards. Attend and support fundraising events, collections and community activities, including occasional evenings and weekends where required. Work closely with the Head of Fundraising and collaborate with the wider fundraising, marketing, finance and operations teams to ensure the smooth and effective delivery of key campaigns and fundraising activities. KEY ATTRIBUTES: This job is for you if you: are results-driven and target-focused, with a strong motivation to achieve fundraising targets can show a proven and demonstrable track record of achieving fundraising goals or similar/related objectives, through either direct or transferrable experience are creative, enthusiastic and proactive, with a passion for fundraising and community engagement are an excellent communicator with strong inter-personal and relationship-building skills, and confident in engaging diverse audiences flexible and adaptable, with a willingness to work evenings, weekends and travel nationally have a full UK driving licence, as the role will require frequent travel locally and across the country. Note: The Birmingham job/s will be office-based, while others will be hybrid/remote depending on the situation. HOW TO APPLY Deadline for applications: 6pm Wednesday 30th September 2026 We regret that only shortlisted candidates will be contacted for an interview. You must have proof that you have the right to work in the UK. We are an equal opportunities employer and welcome all applications regardless of age, gender, ethnicity, faith or disability. Please note: Interviews are expected to take place on an ongoing basis until the vacancy is filled. The advert therefore may close sooner than the deadline date.

item.title: Personal Assistant - Governance and Audits
item.description: Creative Support is a national provider of social care with charitable status. We are seeking a capable and highly professional PA to support our audit and governance functions. Creative Support delivers person-centred care and support to people across England with a wide range of needs. We are also a Registered Social Landlord managing around 1,000 units of supported housing. This role inolves the provision of all necessary administrative, secretarial and organisational support to the Company Secretary, the Internal Audit Team and the Board of Trustees. Internal Audit & Executive Support - Provide dedicated PA and secretarial support to the Internal Audit Team, including inbox triage, diary management, and minute-taking. - Service the Finance & Audit and Risk Committees by gathering report submissions, distributing packs, and taking formal minutes. - Take discreet, verbatim minutes during sensitive investigations and formal reviews. - Log and track internal finance incidents and support the administration of the Supported Holidays process. - Provide flexible PA cover for Executive Team members during peak periods or absences. - Coordinate administrative tasks for working groups, co-production forums, and corporate campaign events. Governance & Board Support - Coordinate board and committee calendars, meeting logistics, catering, and virtual links. - Collate and distribute meeting packs, maintain the online Board portal, and track attendance records. - Track post-meeting action items and assist the Company Secretary with governance filings and compliance tracking (e.g., trustee registers, conflict of interest forms, DBS renewals). - Assist with AGM coordination, trustee recruitment administration, and site visit logistics. - Book travel and accommodation for trustees and senior leaders, and process expense claims promptly. General & Professional Responsibilities - Serve as a welcoming first point of contact for trustees and members, triaging queries efficiently. - Uphold strict confidentiality, data protection (GDPR), and equal opportunities policies. - Embody Creative Support’s person-centered values in all interactions and commit to ongoing professional development. Applicants for this role must be passionate about Creative Support’s work, values and ethos. You will have significant prior experience gained in a responsible secretarial or administrative role. Experience of working for a charity or a social care or public service organisation is desirable, but not essential. You will be proactive, professional and able to maintain confidentiality. You will be well-organised, able to prioritise work and to achieve deadlines. You must have good communication skills with the ability to liaise effectively and coordinate the work of others. You must be helpful and responsive to requests for assistance. You will be willing to work flexibly in accordance with the needs of the organisation and trustees, including attending evening meetings (1-2 evening meetings a month). A good standard of literacy is required and you must be competent in the use of IT and online applications including MS Word, Excel and Powerpoint. You will be conscientious and diligent in managing data and information and keeping records on behalf of the Company Secretary. You must be able to take direction and be accountable to the Company Secretary. You must be committed to the principles of co-production as you will be expected to support the voice and active involvement of people we support in governance and quality assurance. This job could be full time (37.5 hours) or part-time by agreement, subject to a minimum of 30 hours per week. This post is not suitable for home working. Our offices are readily accessible on public transport as we are based in in the centre of Stockport close to the mainline train station and with frequent buses to Manchester. Creative Support is a welcoming and inclusive Equal Opportunities employer. We embrace diversity and encourage applicants from all backgrounds and cultures. As a Disability Confident Employer we welcome applications from people with a disability, and as a proud Stonewall Diversity Champion we actively encourage applications from the LGBT+ community. We will be interviewing for this role as suitable applications are received and may close this role before the closing date upon a successful candidate being appointed. Vacancy Reference Number: 84516 Applications for this post must be submitted via the Creative Support website, quoting the above vacancy reference number.

item.title: Welfare Rights & Debt Adviser
item.description: Job Title: Welfare Rights & Debt Adviser Contract Length: One-year fixed term commencing November 2026 Hours: 37.5 hours per week Line Manager : Advice Service Manager Location(s): Salford Salary: £26,400 per annum About Us Mind in Salford is an independent, user focused charity providing vital services to make a positive difference to the wellbeing and mental health of local people. We represent the voice of Salford in campaigning to dispel stigma and influence political, social and cultural change around mental health. This role offers the opportunity to make a direct and practical difference to people in Salford who are experiencing financial difficulty, welfare rights challenges and mental health needs. The Welfare Rights & Debt Adviser will: Deliver high-quality welfare rights advice, debt advice, budgeting support, grant applications and financial capability support to people experiencing mental health difficulties. Manage a caseload of clients on a one-to-one basis, ensuring advice is accurate, holistic, person-centred and responsive to individual needs. Contribute insight from frontline advice work to service development, partnership working and Mind’s wider campaigning activity. Main Duties & Responsibilities Client advice and casework: provide welfare rights advice, debt advice, grant applications, information and support through appointments, telephone support, drop-ins and community-based settings. Quality and compliance: maintain accurate case records, work within agreed case-working standards, meet monitoring requirements and keep knowledge of welfare rights policy, systems and legislation up to date. Partnership and team working: work collaboratively with colleagues and external professionals to provide joined-up support for clients across different service settings. Service development: contribute to service planning, improvement activity and wider organisational learning based on client needs and service evidence. The successful candidate will have at least one years’ experience delivering both welfare rights advice and debt advice in a relevant setting and be able to understand the wishes and needs of people using mental health services and advocate appropriately on their behalf. They will be able to engage effectively with vulnerable adults and build positive working relationships with professionals across disciplines, have good negotiation, problem-solving and organisational skills. This role will need the ability to prioritise and manage a caseload while meeting agreed case-working standards, targets and service goals, someone who can maintain accurate and comprehensive records on a client management database and someone with a commitment to equal opportunities, diversity, service user empowerment and reliable team working. Benefits of working for Mind in Salford: We provide face-to-face training to strengthen your knowledge of mental health, alongside access to a learning platform with a wide range of courses across different subject areas. The role offers flexible working, agreed in line with service needs. Generous annual leave entitlement, including three days leave over Christmas. You will receive an additional day of annual leave for your birthday. You will also have access to three hours of wellbeing leave each month. Application deadline: 5PM on Friday 2nd October 2026 Interviews will be held on Thursday 15th October 2026. Interested? If you would like to find out more, please click the apply button. You will be directed to our website to complete your application for this position. We are committed to achieving equal opportunities in employment and the service we provide, and welcome applications from people with lived experience of mental health issues. We encourage applications from everyone, irrespective of age, disability, gender reassignment, race, religion or belief, sexual orientation, marriage and civil partnership and pregnancy and maternity. We work with children and adults who may be at risk of abuse and therefore everyone is subject to a DBS check (level of check is dependent on the nature of the role) and receipt of two satisfactory references. No agencies please.

item.title: Evidence & Impact Manager
item.description: Our Vision for Transformation through Forests This is a defining moment for the National Forest, with a renewed Vision to harness the transformative power of forests to restore nature, connect communities, and drive enterprise for a positive future. Over 30 years, this 200 square mile landscape has been reshaped, more than 10 million trees planted, and forest cover increased from 6% to 26%. Now, we are ready to build on this success enabling three new national forests and championing a forest network for England. We are now looking for an Evidence and Impact Manager to join us on a permanent, full-time basis, working 37 hours per week. The Benefits - Salary of £48,575 - Civil Service Pension scheme - 30 days’ annual leave plus 10.5 days’ public and privilege holidays - Staff bonuses - Flexible working options - Cycle to Work Scheme - Employee Assistance Programme - Discounts on gym memberships This is an outstanding opportunity for an experienced performance and evidence professional with GIS expertise to join our ambitious organisation. You’ll have the chance to work on a wide variety of projects that shape our work, ensuring insight sits at the heart of our future direction, and we can continue to deliver on our vision. What’s more, you’ll discover a passionate and dedicated team all working towards the same goal of a future where people, nature and the economy can grow together. If you’re passionate about evidence, impact and the power of forests to transform places and lives, read on and apply today. The Role As our Evidence and Impact Manager, you will lead the development and continual improvement of our Outcomes Framework, helping us evidence progress towards our vision of ‘Transformation through Forests’. Working to deliver our vision for nature, communities and enterprise, you’ll establish meaningful metrics, effective data collection, evaluation and reporting processes. Managing a small team, you will oversee the generation and delivery of robust evidence and insight, translating complex information for a range of audiences to inform decision-making, support programme development, and inform external messaging for communications and advocacy work. Additionally, you will: - Oversee reporting for the Defra England Tree Planting Programme - Line manage a Grants Officer who administers £2m of grants for forest creation and woodland management Some evening and weekend work may be required, for which time off in lieu will apply, and you may also need to travel to sites across rural locations. About You To be considered as our Evidence and Impact Manager, you will need: - At least five years’ experience in a similar role - Experience of leading corporate performance monitoring and reporting within the environmental field - Proven experience of using GIS for dataset analysis and the presentation of spatial information - Knowledge of qualitative and quantitative research and information presentation techniques - An understanding of the benefits of tree planting and habitat creation for nature, communities and enterprise - A relevant degree or postgraduate qualification The closing date for this role is the 28th September 2026. Other organisations may call this role Impact Manager, Evidence Manager, Monitoring and Evaluation Manager, Environmental Performance Manager, Research and Impact Manager, Insights and Impact Manager, or Evaluation and Impact Manager. The National Forest is an equal opportunities employer, we value diversity and are strongly committed to providing equal employment opportunities for all employees and all applicants for employment. Equal opportunities are the only acceptable way to conduct business and we believe that the more inclusive our environments are, the better our work will be. So, if you want to use evidence and insight to help demonstrate the transformational potential of forests as an Evidence and Impact Manager, please apply via the National Forest website.

item.title: Independent Living / Scheme Manager
item.description: Independent Living / Scheme Manager Manchester £26,265.12 + Excellent Benefits inc up to 31 days plus bank holidays and attractive pension scheme Full Time (35 hours per week) Our client has a proud heritage in helping to create vibrant and sustainable multi-cultural neighbourhoods in inner city areas. They believe that everyone has the right to live independently and safely, so, it’s no surprise that they recruit passionate people who want to make a difference and take responsibility to get things done. They are looking for an individual with experience within social care to deliver high-quality housing and support services for tenants within the associations over 55s housing schemes. Acting as the main point of contact for tenants, you will play a vital part in fostering a positive culture, driving continuous improvement and supporting innovation and efficiency to help achieve the organisation's strategic goals You will ensure the provision of high-quality services, effective risk management, and full compliance with health and safety requirements; while overseeing repairs and planned works to ensure they are completed to a high standard. In this role, you will be responsible for: Support Services - Deliver support services to tenants, carrying out risk assessments and support plans with tenants and complete daily check-ins Tenant Involvement & Social Activities - Promote communication by involving tenants in decisions about the running of schemes. Facilitate events which promote tenant interaction. Scheme Management - Be responsible for the day-to-day management of facilities and services, liaising with tenants about repairs and contractor access and report repairs Safeguarding responsibilities - Be alert to and recognise welfare issues and signs of abuse. We would love to hear from you if you have: Experience of working with older people Exceptionally high standard of customer care and service Strong problem solving and decision-making skills Excellent communication, interpersonal and negotiation skills Able to promote and maintain a positive “can do” attitude Whether you’re wanting to take on more responsibilities or share your experience with colleagues, this is an excellent opportunity to join a company that values staff and tenants, is passionate about building communities where people can thrive and will support your career every step pf the way What they can offer you A friendly supportive team where you're known as a person- not just an employee. The opportunity to develop your skills, take on early responsibility and grow your career Up to 31 days annual leave, plus bank holidays and an additional 3 concessionary days over Christmas. A generous pension scheme with a 3% employee contribution and an 11.4% employer contribution Flexible and family-friendly working policies. Perkbox membership, giving you discounts on shopping, travel. leisure and gym memberships. item.title: Assistant Shop Manager Brighton
item.description: We're looking for an inspirational people person to join us as an Assistant Shop Manager in our Shelter shop in Brighton. This is an exciting opportunity, and we'd like you to join us to help raise vital funds for homeless and badly housed people. You will work closely with the Shop Manager to ensure the shop looks welcoming, visually appealing and the team of volunteers are motivated and keen to engage with customers and maximise sales. About Shelter A home is a fundamental human need, as essential as education or healthcare. Yet millions of people across Britain struggle on a daily basis with homelessness, bad housing conditions, soaring rents, discrimination and the threat of eviction. So, we are striving for change, with individuals, in communities, across society, and leading the way to a safe home. We need ambitious, best-in-class individuals who are passionate about our cause to join us at this exciting time. This is your chance to play a part in the fundamental change we are striving to achieve. At Shelter we are united by our purpose to defend the right to a safe home. Our enemy is the social injustice at the core of the escalating housing emergency. We believe that to win that fight, we must be representative of the people we are here to help and those who support our movement for change. In all our people decisions, we take pride in being inclusive, fair, equitable and transparent. We have committed to combat racism both within and outside Shelter and welcome you on our journey to becoming a truly anti-racist organisation. About the role You will assist the Shop Manager in the recruitment, support and development of a strong community focused shop team and empower them to maximise Shelter's income. Representing Shelter in your local community, ensuring that you and your team share your knowledge of Shelter's cause with customers, volunteers, donors and potential Shelter clients will also be important aspects of the role. You will always ensure a safe, clean, bright and happy environment for your team to work in and for your customers to shop in, in turn attracting potential donors and volunteers. About you You are a naturally energetic person with an enthusiasm for managing and empowering people. Your extraordinary motivational skills will enable you to inspire your team to increase sales and control costs. Above all, you are ready to take on a new challenge and have a keen interest in Shelter's cause. We’re looking for someone friendly and personable, who can work well as part of a team and is proficient using Microsoft Office application and other systems used. Apply to be part of our team and be the change you want to see in society How to Apply Please click ‘Apply for Job’ below. You are required to submit your work history and a supporting statement. Please provide specific examples of how you meet the criteria in the 'About you' section of this advert, following the STAR format, and ensure you demonstrate how you address the behaviours below throughout your responses: We prioritise diversity and have an inclusive and open mindset Any applications submitted without a supporting statement will not be considered Benefits We offer a wide range of benefits, including 30 days of annual leave, enhanced family friendly policies, pension and interest free travel loans. Our employees also have access to a tenancy deposit loan, payroll giving, cycle to work scheme and an employee assistance programme. Shelter helps millions of people every year struggling with bad housing or homelessness through our advice, support and legal services. And we campaign to make sure that, one day, no one will have to turn to us for help. We’re here so no one has to fight bad housing or homelessness on their own. To find out more about the role and the benefits of working for Shelter please visit our website. Apply to be part of our team and be the change you want to see in society. Safeguarding is everyone's business. Shelter is committed to protecting the health, wellbeing and human rights of those we support, and enabling them to live free from harm, abuse and neglect. All our staff will be expected to observe professional standards of behaviour and conduct their work in line with our Safeguarding Policies. We are happy to talk about flexible working, personal growth, and to promote a workplace where you can be yourself and achieve success based only on your merit. Shelter does not accept unsolicited CVs from external recruitment agencies nor accept the fees associated with them.
