item.title: Key Relationships Manager
item.description: Job Title : Key Relationships Manager Salary: £46,000 per annum Location: Hybrid : London Office and Home Hours of work: Full-time (35 hours per week) Reporting to: Head of Key Relationships Premier, the UK’s largest Christian media agency, is seeking a Key Relationships Manager who shares our passion for helping people encounter God through media and experience renewal. Behind Premier’s ministry are generous supporters who make this work possible. Through thoughtful conversations, careful listening and a compelling invitation to give, you could help people connect their generosity with a mission close to their hearts — bringing the Gospel, encouragement and hope into everyday lives. Role Overview: You will build meaningful relationships with existing and prospective supporters, helping them discover how their giving can support Premier’s mission. Working with senior colleagues, you will guide relationships from first introduction through to a thoughtful invitation to give and ongoing care. Alongside warmth and conviction, you will need persistence, disciplined follow-through and the confidence to ask for significant financial support when relationships are ready — potentially including gifts of up to seven figures. You do not need to have made asks at this level before, but you must be willing to learn. Key responsibilities will include: Building lasting partnerships: Develop and care for a portfolio of supporters, securing major gifts and multi-year commitments towards your annual six-figure target. Opening new conversations: Research and approach potential supporters, including senior individuals in the City’s corporate community, and create proposals that connect their giving aspirations with Premier’s mission. Representing Premier: Communicate our mission at donor meetings and events, involving senior colleagues where appropriate. Following through with care: Maintain accurate records, timely follow-up and monthly reporting, treating supporters with respect and following the Code of Fundraising Practice. We are looking for someone with: A living Christian faith and a heart for the Gospel: A faith you can articulate clearly, commitment to Premier’s mission and a good understanding of the Christian community. A gift for relationships: Proven ability to build new professional connections and nurture trust, including with senior or influential people, through empathy, listening, tact and discretion. Purposeful communication: Excellent writing, presentation and conversational skills, with the confidence to represent Premier and a willingness to learn to ask directly for significant support. Initiative and accountability: Proven success against targets, resourcefulness in identifying opportunities, sound analytical judgement and a commitment to both personal responsibility and teamwork. Organisation and a learning mindset: Careful administration and follow-through, confident IT skills and the ability to learn new systems; degree-level education or equivalent knowledge and ability gained through professional experience. Ideally, you will understand the principles of the major donor journey, but previous experience managing major donors or securing large gifts is not essential. We are particularly interested in your commitment to Premier’s mission and your ability to build trust and turn conversations into lasting relationships. You might bring these strengths from account management, sales, fundraising or another relationship-focused role. We can help you develop the specialist fundraising skills – if you have empathy, initiative, sound judgement and a willingness to learn, this could be your next role! Location and availability: This is a primarily London-based role. You must live within daily commutable distance of the City of London and be able to attend London meetings and donor visits at least two days each week, with attendance at Premier’s London office as required. Additional travel and occasional evening and weekend work are also required. Please note that Premier is a Christian media agency and this role has a genuine occupational requirement for the post holder to have a personal Christian faith. For the full job description please click here: Key Relationships Manager | Premier Jobsearch Could God be calling you to use your relational gifts in this ministry? If this opportunity resonates with your faith, skills and sense of purpose, we would love to hear from you! Information for candidates Why Join Premier? Premier offers a great place to work, with people that support, encourage and look after one another. You will love coming into work, both in person and virtually! Competitive salary and benefits package: • Flexible working arrangements based on the requirements of the role • 25 days’ annual leave plus UK bank holidays • Additional leave on your birthday • Contributory pension scheme • Life Assurance scheme • Employee Assistance with online GP scheme • Eye care scheme • Enhanced Family leave and Pay In addition we offer: Mission-Driven Work : Take the opportunity to make a tangible impact by contributing to a mission that reaches millions of people. Dynamic Team Culture : Join a supportive, creative, and passionate team that values innovation and collaboration. Growth Opportunities : Benefit from ongoing professional development in a role where your contributions are truly valued. Application Process All applications need to be completed online using our recruitment system (linked from our adverts). You will be asked to answer a number of questions before submitting your application – please ensure you provide information on how your skills and experience meet the requirements for this role.

item.title: Head of Fundraising and Communications
item.description: Purpose of the role The Head of Fundraising and Communications is responsible for delivering our new 2026-2029 integrated fundraising and communications strategy that grows and diversifies DeafKidz International's income, raises our profile with key audiences, and ensures our storytelling authentically represents deaf children, young people and their communities. This is a hands-on leadership role, combining strategic direction with direct delivery. You will lead a small team of 1-2 direct reports and a network of freelancers/agencies, and work closely with the CEO, Trustees and programme teams to build a high-performing fundraising and communications function to deliver our new three-year strategy. As a member of the Senior Leadership Team, you will also contribute to organisation-wide strategy, planning and decision-making, and act as a champion for accessible and inclusive practice across the organisation. Key responsibilities 1. Strategic leadership • Develop and lead the implementation of a multi-year fundraising and communications strategy aligned to DeafKidz International's organisational strategy and growth ambitions. • Set annual income targets and communications objectives, and report regularly on progress to the CEO, Trustees and Board sub-committees. • As an SLT member, contribute to organisational planning, risk management, budgeting and culture, bringing an external, supporter-facing perspective to internal decisions. • Identify and evaluate new income opportunities, communications channels and partnerships that support long-term sustainability. • Support the CEO to drive proactive and strategic stakeholder engagement, coordinating and attending meetings and/or providing meetings briefs where required. 2. Income generation • Build and develop a multi-channel fundraising programme with definitive responsibility for trust & foundations, corporate and high-net-worth fundraising; whilst supporting colleagues and partners to build and deliver individual giving, events and community fundraising activities. • Lead on cultivating and securing minimum five figure gifts from trusts, foundations, corporate partners and high-net-worth individuals. • Oversee the development of compelling funding proposals, cases for support and impact reporting, working closely with programme teams to evidence outcomes. • Ensure excellent donor stewardship and supporter journeys across all income streams, treating every supporter interaction as an opportunity to deepen engagement. • Set, manage and report against the fundraising budget and income targets, ensuring robust forecasting and phasing. • Ensure all fundraising activity complies with the Fundraising Regulator's Code of Fundraising Practice, GDPR/data protection law and Charity Commission requirements. 3. Communications, brand and profile • Build DeafKidz International’s profile in the countries where we work and with new and prospective supporters • Lead the development and delivery of an integrated communications strategy covering digital, social media, PR, media relations and the organisation's website. • Ensure DeafKidz International's brand, messaging and storytelling are consistent, compelling and authentically centre the voices and experiences of deaf children, young people and their families. • Ensure communications activity is aligned with income generation and strategic priorities • Embed accessibility and inclusive communication practice across all channels and materials, including signed languages, captioning, Easy Read formats and deaf-led storytelling. • Oversee the planning and delivery of campaigns, appeals and content (including challenge events, awareness days and fundraising appeals) that build profile and drive income. • Manage relationships with media, PR support, ambassadors, influencers and patrons to extend reach and credibility. • Oversee internal communications, ensuring staff, volunteers and Trustees are well informed and engaged with fundraising and external messaging. 4. Team and resource management • Recruit, manage and develop a small fundraising and communications team as budget allows, building capability and resilience as the organisation grows. • Manage external suppliers, freelancers and agencies (e.g. design, video, web development, BSL interpretation/translation, PR) to extend the team's capacity cost-effectively. • Foster a collaborative, ambitious and supportive team culture, modelling DeafKidz International's values and commitment to deaf-led practice. 5. Governance and reporting • Prepare clear, accurate reports and presentations on fundraising and communications performance for the CEO, Senior Leadership Team and Board of Trustees. • Maintain oversight of donor and supporter data, ensuring CRM systems and data management practices are fit for purpose and compliant. • Carry out other duties commensurate with the role as reasonably required by the CEO. Person specification Experience • Significant senior-level fundraising experience within the charity sector, with a proven track record of securing five-figure and above gifts from trusts and foundations, corporate partners, and high-net-worth individuals. • Experience leading and managing teams to deliver successful individual giving, community fundraising, and events programmes, achieving agreed financial targets. • Demonstrable success in leading communications, marketing, digital engagement, or public relations activity within a purpose-driven organisation. • Experience operating at a strategic and senior leadership level, including budget management, target setting, organisational planning, and reporting to trustees or boards. • Experience managing and working effectively with freelancers, consultants, agencies, and external contractors. • Experience developing and growing fundraising and communications functions within a small or developing charity environment, demonstrating initiative, flexibility, and resourcefulness. • Experience of international development and/or working collaboratively with overseas partners and programmes. • Experience within the disability, deaf, or children's sectors, or a strong understanding of the challenges and barriers faced by deaf children and young people. Skills and abilities • Strong strategic thinking skills, with the ability to translate organisational ambitions into practical, measurable, and costed fundraising and communications plans. • Exceptional relationship-building and networking skills, with the confidence and credibility to engage trustees, major donors, corporate partners, and other senior stakeholders. • Outstanding written and verbal communication skills, with the ability to tailor messages and content for a wide range of audiences and channels. • Strong financial management skills, including budgeting, forecasting, income and expenditure monitoring, and performance reporting. • Proficiency in the use of fundraising databases, CRM systems, and digital marketing tools. • An inclusive and collaborative leadership style, with the ability to motivate, develop, and support a small team while fostering effective cross-organisational working. • A sound understanding of fundraising regulation and compliance, including the Fundraising Regulator Code of Fundraising Practice, GDPR, and Charity Commission requirements. Personal attributes • Passionate about the mission of DeafKidz International and committed to deaf-led, child-centred, and safeguarding-first approaches. Applicants with lived experience of deafness are particularly encouraged to apply. • Comfortable working within a small, ambitious, and fast-paced charity, balancing strategic leadership with hands-on delivery. • Creative, resilient, adaptable, and highly motivated to achieve results. • Committed to equality and accessibility in all aspects of their work. • Accountable, target-driven, and committed to delivering sustainable fundraising growth. Other requirements • Willingness to travel throughout the UK and internationally when required. • Willingness to learn and develop basic British Sign Language (BSL) skills. • Appointment to this role is subject to a satisfactory Enhanced DBS check due to the organisation's work with children and young people. Benefits • Generous annual leave entitlement, plus bank holidays. • Workplace pension scheme with employer contributions. • Remote working arrangements. • Learning and professional development opportunities. This role profile is intended to give a general indication of the scope of the role. It is not exhaustive and may be reviewed periodically in consultation with the postholder to reflect the changing needs of DeafKidz International.

item.title: Fundraising Partnerships Manager
item.description: Job Description Job title: Fundraising Partnerships Manager Location : Hackney Bridge , Queen Elizabeth Olympic Park, London (a canalside public destination less than five minutes from Hackney Wick station) Salary: £40,000-£45,000 FTE depending on experience, pro rata to £24,000-£27,000 Hours: 0.6 FTE (3 days/21 hours per week) with a view to the role expanding to full-time in the future. Office hours are 10am - 6pm with occasional evenings and weekends. Flexible working opportunities are available. Who are The Outrunners? The Outrunners are a running and movement charity based in Hackney, on a mission to empower young people through movement. Backed by an incredible crew of volunteers and partner brands like Nike and Moju, we help young people in East London to build confidence, wellbeing, health and leadership skills. We deliver free, fun, sociable, youth‑led running and movement sessions for 8–18 year olds every week - during term time and holidays. But we’re about more than just running. We also create space for young people to explore creativity and culture, go on exciting trips, access wraparound wellbeing support, and develop the skills and opportunities they need to shape the futures they want. Over the past five years, we’ve supported thousands of young people and helped push greater diversity within the running world. We like to do things differently - taking young people out of their everyday environments and into exciting new spaces, opening doors to opportunities they might not otherwise have access to. If that sounds like something you want to be part of…read on. Our achievements We’re a small charity but we pack a mighty punch. Our income has grown year-on-year since we became a charity 6 years ago - allowing us to expand our core team and move into office premises large enough to incorporate a Youth Hub. Last year we worked with over 1,150 young people through our school and communities programs, and this year we’re looking to expand our work even further! To give you a sense of the kinds of work that we do, over the last year we have: Hosted a free Girls’ Festival for 100+ ethnically diverse young girls, allowing them to try running sessions, creative classes and yoga experiences in a safe and empowering environment. Hosted free training Academies for ethnically diverse women and young people aged 16-21 to train for their very first half or full marathons! We offered physical, emotional and logistical support throughout their training journey and cheered on every single one of them as they ran either the Hackney Half or the London Marathon under The Outrunners name. Since programme launch, we have worked with over 250 people in our Academies. Took diverse groups of young people to races and events, such as Hackney School Run and Black to the Trails. Offered personalised mentoring to several of our young people who were struggling with school or life. Expanded the career horizons of young people by offering them free work experience opportunities with our partner brands. What do we want? We are looking for an experienced Fundraising Partnerships Manager to help drive the next stage of growth at The Outrunners (current annual income circa £350k). This growth will enable us to expand our after-school and holiday programmes reaching more young people where they are, building their confidence and skills. Reporting to the CEO, you will lead our brand and corporate partnerships fundraising strategy and delivery, securing and growing relationships with values-aligned brands and businesses who share our belief in the power of movement to transform young lives. This is a strategic and hands-on role. You will identify new partnership opportunities, develop compelling proposals, and build long-term relationships that generate income, opportunities and experiences for the young people we support. You will translate the lived experiences, energy and impact of our young people and programmes into compelling partnership opportunities that generate income, engagement and meaningful experiences for both our young people and partners. You'll be equally comfortable developing strategy, pitching to partners, nurturing relationships and rolling up your sleeves to make things happen. Does this sound like you? A driven, experienced partnerships and fundraising professional who enjoys generating income, building strategic relationships and taking ownership of growth. A natural networker and relationship-builder who is confident in engaging and influencing stakeholders at all levels. A strategic thinker who is also hands-on, happy researching prospects, developing proposals and nurturing relationships day-to-day. Someone who can translate impact, lived experience and data into compelling partnership propositions, sponsorship opportunities and cases for support. Commercially aware and confident identifying opportunities that create value for both The Outrunners and our partners. Highly motivated, resilient and persistent, comfortable managing multiple relationships, income streams and priorities in a fast-moving environment. Values-led and trustworthy, with a strong sense of integrity, accountability and ethical fundraising practice. Motivated by social impact and excited about the opportunity to connect brands, businesses and supporters with a youth-led organisation rooted in movement, equity and opportunity. Happy to occasionally work evenings or weekends to support partner events, networking opportunities and fundraising activity. Experience and skills we’re looking for Proven experience securing income through corporate partnerships (100k+), sponsorship, fundraising or business development. Strong track record of building and managing relationships with brands, businesses, funders or senior stakeholders. Experience identifying, developing and converting new partnership opportunities into income and impact. Experience delivering partnership benefits and activations, including events, volunteering opportunities, employee engagement initiatives, campaigns or sponsorship programmes. Ability to create compelling partnership proposals, presentations and cases for support, tailoring for specific audiences. Strong storytelling and communication skills, with the ability to translate impact data and lived experience into engaging partner propositions. Commercially minded, with an understanding of how to create mutually beneficial partnerships that align organisational and partner goals. Excellent organisation and project management skills, with the ability to manage multiple priorities and deadlines. Sound understanding of fundraising regulation, ethical partnerships and best practice. Collaborative and proactive, comfortable working in a small, ambitious and fast-moving organisation. Strong commitment to equality, diversity and inclusion, with confidence working across diverse communities. Desirable Experience working with sport, fitness, lifestyle or consumer brands. Experience fundraising for youth, wellbeing, sport or community-based organisations. Existing network of contacts within corporate partnerships, sponsorship, ESG or social impact teams. Key Responsibilities 1. New partnerships & business development Identify, research and secure new partnerships with values-aligned brands, businesses and organisations. Build relationships with decision-makers and key stakeholders across prospective partner organisations. Develop and deliver tailored partnership proposals, sponsorship decks and impact led presentations to attract partners. Lead partnership negotiations (with CEO) and onboarding, ensuring new partners have a positive experience from the outset. Represent The Outrunners externally through meetings, networking events and partnership opportunities to generate new leads and raise awareness of our work. 2. Partnership management & activation Act as the primary relationship manager for existing partners, building trusted, long-term relationships. Develop and deliver partnership plans, ensuring agreed activities, benefits and objectives are achieved. Work closely with colleagues to create engaging opportunities for partners to support and connect with young people through events, volunteering and other initiatives. Support the development of partnership content, case studies, presentations and storytelling assets that showcase the impact of The Outrunners' work. Provide regular updates, impact reports and partnership reviews that demonstrate value and outcomes. Identify opportunities to strengthen, renew and grow existing partnerships. 3. Partnerships strategy & growth Develop and deliver The Outrunners' partnerships strategy, aligned with our mission, values and organisational goals. Work with the CEO to identify and prioritise partnership opportunities that support organisational growth and impact. Build and manage a pipeline of prospective partners, monitoring performance against agreed partnership and income targets. Develop compelling partnership propositions that connect The Outrunners' work with the priorities of prospective partners. 4. Impact, Systems & Reporting Maintain accurate partnership records, reporting and pipeline management through CRM systems. Gather stories, outcomes and impact data to support partner communications and reporting. Produce partnership materials, presentations and case studies. Produce partnership performance reports. Stay informed about partnership, sponsorship and CSR trends to identify new opportunities for The Outrunners. What’s in it for you? Opportunity to make a meaningful difference in the lives of young people. Supportive and inclusive working environment. Professional development and training opportunities. 30 holiday days + all bank holidays (pro-rata) Self-development days Work-related travel reimbursement Learning and development opportunities to fit your aspirations, including with some of our partner businesses Working alongside aspirational brands Monthly wellness vo

item.title: Development Manager: Trusts & Foundations
item.description: Development Manager: Trusts & Foundations 28 hours per week (0.8 FTE), Monday to Thursday. c.£44,000 per annum (pro-rata), plus benefits 14 St James’s Square, London SW1Y 4LG (with some remote working possible) Applications to work full-time, 35 hours per week, Monday to Friday, will also be considered. About The London Library For 185 years, The London Library has stood as one of the UK's greatest literary institutions, inspiring creativity, and ideas. Our esteemed members, past and present, include literary giants like Charles Dickens, Charles Darwin, Virginia Woolf, and contemporary authors such as Kazuo Ishiguro and Sarah Waters. Our collection boasts around one million volumes, a vast eLibrary, and an invaluable postal loans service, making it a sanctuary for those who cherish the written word. We are championed by our President, Helena Bonham Carter CBE, and operate as a registered charity. We have over 7,500 members and charitable turnover of circa £5m per year. About the Role The London Library is an independently funded membership organisation. It has successfully achieved its goals to eliminate an operating deficit in recent years, which has included developing and growing its membership, the outreach and access programmes and the care of its collections and archive. Under an ambitious Executive Team and a strong board of Trustees, led by Chair Simon Godwin, the Library is in the middle of a £7 million capital campaign to transform some of its spaces and allow for a growth in membership and partnerships, underpinning its charitable purpose. Revenue fundraising is essential, and the team raises income through a patrons programme, grants from trusts and foundations, philanthropic gifts, legacies and a biannual appeal to members. The Library has developed a major giving strategy, which is attracting regular philanthropic gifts towards programming, collection projects, other revenue costs and the capital campaign. You will be supported by an active and supportive team and work alongside the Director of Development. A new CRM system, adopted in early 2024, enables enhanced prospect and donation management. Key Responsibilities · Manage two important strands of the Library’s Development operation: Trusts and Foundations, and Legacies · Oversee the Trusts and Foundations strategy and solicitation to maximise grants and income from grant giving bodies, including statutory funders · With the support of a Senior Development Officer, manage the Library’s Legacy programme, develop and implement strategies to promote legacy giving, steward legacy pledgers and grow the number of legacy pledgers About You · Previous trust fundraising experience or transferrable strong persuasive writing skills · Track record in relationship building externally (clients/donors) and internally (programme delivery staff) including customer or donor care experience · Track record in meeting income targets in a fundraising setting, or other transferrable setting · Experience of CRM systems · Ability to plan, prioritise and carry out work effectively to meet deadlines · Motivated, collaborative and able to work independently in a part-time role Why Join Us? The London Library offers a friendly, hardworking, and inclusive workplace where we strive to support the diverse needs of our team. We welcome applications from all sections of the community and are committed to equality and diversity. Specific adjustments and access needs can be discussed to make this role suitable for you. If you want to use your skills to help drive the success of The London Library, we would love to hear from you! Please note: All applicants will be considered on the basis of their merits and abilities for the post. We can only consider candidates with the current right to work in the UK. We reserve the right to shorten or extend the closing date of any position where a high or low volume of suitable applications are received. Therefore, if you are interested in this role, an early application would be encouraged. How to Apply To apply please visit our website and apply online. Closing date: 09 October 2026 @ 12:00pm Interviews: 15 October 2026

item.title: Brand Manager
item.description: Are you passionate about building brands that make a genuine difference? This is an exciting opportunity to join a well-known national charity at a time of significant ambition and growth. Working within a collaborative marketing team, you'll play a key role in shaping how the organisation is seen, understood and experienced by a wide range of audiences. As Brand & Insight Manager, you'll be responsible for driving brand excellence across the organisation, ensuring every campaign, communication and touchpoint reflects a clear and consistent identity. You'll champion best practice, support teams across the business and help bring the brand to life in a way that inspires action, builds trust and deepens engagement. Alongside brand management, you'll lead on audience insight, helping colleagues better understand their audiences and use insight to make smarter, more effective decisions. From developing brand assets and guidance to influencing strategic campaigns and supporting creative development, you'll be at the heart of some of the organisation's most important marketing activity. This is a fantastic opportunity for someone who enjoys combining creativity with strategic thinking and is passionate about creating meaningful connections between organisations and their audiences. What you'll be doing Acting as the guardian of a respected national brand, ensuring consistency across all channels and communications Supporting the ongoing development and evolution of the brand Building strong relationships with teams across the organisation to embed brand best practice Leading audience insight initiatives and championing data-led decision making Developing and maintaining brand assets, templates and guidelines Supporting the delivery of multi-channel campaigns and brand marketing activity Working closely with internal stakeholders, agencies and creative partners Leading brand reviews and identifying opportunities to strengthen impact and engagement Helping develop a culture of confident brand ambassadors across the organisation You'll bring: Experience in brand management and brand marketing Excellent stakeholder management and relationship-building skills Strong project management skills with the ability to juggle multiple priorities Outstanding written communication and proofreading skills Experience working with agencies and external suppliers A strong understanding of audience insight and how it can drive better marketing outcomes Excellent attention to detail and a passion for maintaining high brand standards A proactive and collaborative approach, with the confidence to influence and advise colleagues at all levels Closing date: 23rd September We want you to have every opportunity to demonstrate your skills, ability and potential; please contact us if you require any assistance or adjustment so that we can help with making the application process work for you.

item.title: Qualifications Marketing Manager
item.description: Are you an experienced marketing professional who thrives on creating impactful campaigns, building strong stakeholder relationships and driving audience growth through insight-led marketing? This is an exciting opportunity to join a respected professional membership organisation and educational charity at a time of significant development and growth. Working within a collaborative team, you'll lead the marketing strategy for a portfolio of professional qualifications, helping to attract future students, engage employers and strengthen the position of industry-leading qualifications. As Qualifications Marketing Manager, you'll be responsible for developing and delivering strategic marketing plans that increase awareness, generate engagement and grow the student pipeline. You'll use audience insight, research and performance data to shape campaigns, improve customer journeys and deliver measurable results. This role offers a unique blend of strategic marketing, stakeholder engagement and content development. You'll work closely with employers, training providers and internal teams to ensure marketing activity reaches the right audiences, communicates clear value and supports long-term growth objectives. What you'll be doing Leading the marketing strategy and delivery for professional qualifications, certifications and programmes • Driving student recruitment and awareness through targeted B2B and B2C campaigns • Leading the marketing activity for a major qualification launch and ongoing promotional campaigns • Using audience insight, market research and performance data to inform strategic decision-making • Mapping and improving customer journeys to increase engagement and conversion • Creating compelling content across websites, email marketing, social media and digital advertising • Developing marketing plans, creative briefs and campaign assets that align with brand guidelines • Building strong relationships with employers, training providers and key stakeholders • Managing agency relationships and external suppliers • Monitoring performance, analysing results and reporting on ROI and campaign effectiveness The appointed candidate will have: Proven experience delivering integrated marketing and campaign strategies • Experience of both B2B and B2C marketing • Strong analytical skills and experience using data and insight to drive decisions • Excellent stakeholder engagement and relationship-building skills • Strong project management skills and the ability to manage multiple priorities • Experience developing engaging content across digital channels • Confidence working with CRM systems, website platforms and marketing analytics tools • Excellent written and verbal communication skills, including presentation skills • A proactive and self-directed approach with excellent attention to detail • Experience within a membership body, professional education or qualifications environment would be highly desirable Closing date: 25 September 2026 We want you to have every opportunity to demonstrate your skills, ability and potential; please contact us if you require any assistance or adjustment so that we can help with making the application process work for you.

item.title: Head of Fundraising & Partnerships
item.description: Beder is looking for an ambitious, entrepreneurial and hands-on Head of Fundraising & Partnerships to lead the next stage of our growth. Beder was established in memory of Beder Mirjan, who sadly took his own life in 2017 at the age of 18. Since then, we have spent the past eight years working to raise awareness around mental health and suicide prevention, challenge stigma and, increasingly, provide tangible support to people who need it. The focus of our work is the Beder Therapy Voucher programme, through which we fund free therapy for people (18+) across the UK as we all need someone to talk to with demand for that support growing significantly. Until now, much of Beder's fundraising has been founder-led, supported by an incredible network of ambassadors, partners, businesses and individuals. We have built exciting partnerships across sport, business, entertainment and hospitality whilst creating a charity with an engaged community and an ambitious vision for the future. We are now ready to build a dedicated and sustainable fundraising function so we are looking for someone who can take ownership of that journey. This isn't a role for someone who simply wants to manage an existing fundraising programme as we are looking for someone who enjoys building one. Whilst working closely with our founder, trustees and wider team, you will develop and execute Beder's fundraising strategy, building sustainable income across corporate partnerships, major donors, trusts and foundations, individual giving, campaigns and events. You will inherit a compelling cause, an established brand, strong relationships and a growing pipeline of opportunities – but you will also have the freedom to shape how Beder approaches fundraising for the future. We are looking for someone who is equally comfortable developing a fundraising strategy, writing a compelling funding proposal, meeting a potential corporate partner and picking up the phone to a prospective supporter. Above all, we want someone who believes in what Beder is trying to achieve and wants to roll their sleeves up and help us build something special. Our immediate objective is to develop a diversified fundraising programme capable of sustaining our Beder Therapy Voucher service enabling Beder to meet the growing demand for free therapy while continuing to expand our wider mental health and suicide prevention work. The successful candidate will have significant autonomy to develop the strategy, partnerships and fundraising infrastructure required to achieve that. We are open to candidates from a range of fundraising backgrounds and would particularly welcome experience across corporate partnerships, philanthropy/major donors, trusts and foundations and strategic fundraising. Experience within mental health is welcome but is not essential. What matters most is that you are an outstanding relationship builder, an effective fundraiser and someone excited by the opportunity to help take a small, ambitious charity into its next chapter.

item.title: Support Coordinator
item.description: Support Coordinator This is an exciting opportunity to work with stroke survivors and their families to support them following stroke. We are looking for an innovative, passionate, and professional individual with excellent interpersonal and organisational skills to join our Stroke Recovery Service based in Macclesfield. Position: 000052 Stroke Association Support Coordinator Location: Home-based, Macclesfield, Cheshire. However, extensive travel will be required as part of this role (may include team meetings or other work-related meetings) Hours: Part-time, 28 hours per week Salary: Circa £22,600 per annum (FTE circa £28,300 per annum) Contract: Fixed term contract until 31 March 2027. Our services are contracted. We currently have funding for this contract until 31 March 2027. Benefits: 25 days’ annual leave plus bank holidays (this will increase with service up to 30 days, full time equivalent) cashback and discount scheme, employee assistance programme, learning and development, pension scheme, Life Assurance, Eye Care vouchers, Long Service Award, Health Cash Plan, flexible working opportunities available. Closing Date: Sunday 11 October 2026 Interview Date: First round interviews 16 October 2026. Second round interviews 22 October 2026. Interviews will be held via video conferencing. Please let us know if this will present any challenges when you email your application. The Role Reporting to the Service Delivery Coach, you will have the ability to support stroke survivors to identify their goals. Using strong assessment skills and a person-centred approach enabling them to maximise their recovery and improve communication. Key responsibilities will include: Supporting new stroke survivors and their carers from hospital discharge into the community. Provide personalised information, advice and support. Supporting stroke survivors to make informed lifestyle changes which will help them to prevent further strokes. Work collaboratively with NHS colleagues and other areas of the community to make a difference in the lives of people affected by stroke. About You You will have experience in: Experience/background in a caring profession, ideally supporting people with disabilities Excellent IT skills and an ability to maintain accurate records. An affinity with the values of the Stroke Association. A flexible approach and an ability to effectively manage a caseload. This role requires extensive travel across a large geographical locality to visit people at home and in community settings. Candidates must be able to demonstrate how they can meet this requirement of the role To fulfil the role, you must be a resident of the UK and have the right to work in the UK. Applications To apply you’ll be redirected to the organisation website where you can download the full role profile. You’ll need to submit a CV and cover letter demonstrating how you meet the person specification detailed in the role profile, and what you bring to the role in terms of your skills and experience. If you are applying under the Disability Confident scheme, please indicate this in your supporting statement when applying for the role. Stroke Association Finding strength through support The Stroke Association is the only charity in the UK providing lifelong support for all stroke survivors and their families. We provide tailored support to tens of thousands of stroke survivors each year. This support includes one-to-one and group support, funding vital scientific research into stroke prevention, acute treatment, recovery and long-term care, and campaigning to secure the best care for everyone affected by stroke. We’re here for stroke survivors and their loved ones, from the moment they enter the new and frightening post-stroke world, supporting them every step of the way as they find their strength and their way back to life. It’s only thanks to the generosity of our supporters and donors that we can provide vital support. Stroke Association is driven by our ambition to improve the lives of everyone affected by stroke. This means we’re determined to create an equitable and inclusive workplace that benefits from the difference, and thrives on the diversity, of our people. Guided by Our approach to solving inequity in stroke, we are prioritising listening to, and learning from, lived experience across our charity. We are working to improve the representation of this lived experience at all levels within the Stroke Association and we are eager to recruit applicants from a variety of communities and backgrounds. We are keen to receive applications from people affected by stroke, people of colour, members of LGBT+ communities, and disabled people because these identities and experiences are underrepresented and would add enormous value to how we work. We are a Disability Confident employer, and we are making great progress focusing on flexible working, reasonable adjustments and access to work. Our charity has a variety of staff network groups and we're committed to continuously improving our diversity and inclusion efforts. If you have questions, or access needs, we’re happy to discuss any support and adjustments we can make throughout the recruitment process so that you’re able to contribute your best in a way that meets your needs. You may also have experience in areas such as Engagement Officer, Community Engagement Officer, Peer Support, Health Support Officer, Community Support. Please note this role is advertised by the recruitment agency acting for the client, Not For Profit People. #INDNFP

item.title: RNCSF Springboard – North East Regional Coordinator
item.description: Seeking an enthusiastic, proactive individual with excellent communication skills and a commitment to improving outcomes for vulnerable children in the North East. We are delighted to share this role on behalf of Bradford Grammar School who we at the Royal National Children's Springboard Foundation (RNCSF) are working alongside. We are seeking a term time only, Regional Coordinator to support the relationship between RNCSF and local schools in the North East to secure independent day and boarding school bursary placements and access to partnership activities for care experienced children (CEVC). The post holder will be involved in engaging school stakeholders by attracting suitable school partners and being a powerful advocate for the programme. The successful candidate will need to use their excellent communication skills to influence stakeholders in Local Authorities and schools, ensuring the continued success of the “Broadening Educational Pathways” programme – a Department for Education programme delivered by RNCSF. As you will be responsible for all applications in your region it is also essential that you are organised and efficient, with superb time management skills. You will be joining a dynamic, vibrant team of 8 Regional Coordinators who operate all over the country but who work closely together, via Teams, to support CEVC into bursary places in independent day and boarding schools. Our regional coordinators work out of a local host school (with some remote working possible). This position will be based at Bradford Grammar School. The role is for 2 days per week, term time only. You will need to be available for up to 10 ‘in person’ days, and some travel may be required for this (for which you will be reimbursed). You will report into the Head of Bursary Activity as part of the Programmes Team at RNCSF. Please read more about the role in the Job Specification below. We look forward tor receiving your application!

item.title: Project Manager: Voices for Health Equity (Maternity Cover)
item.description: Project Manager: Voices for Health Equity (Maternity Cover) Job Description and Person Specification Job title Project Manager: Voices for Health Equity (Maternity Cover) Hours 35 hours per week Duration 11 months, ideally starting in mid November, with potential to extend to 15 months with mutual agreement Salary Between £37,000 - £43,750. Placement within the band will depend on skills and experience, with the upper end reflecting significant, directly relevant expertise. Location Hybrid work between home and our Vauxhall office, as well as regular travel to in-person events across England. Please read more about our approach to hybrid working in the relevant section below. Reports to Director of Evidence and Improvement National Voices Making what matters to people matter in health and care National Voices is the leading coalition of health and social care charities in England. We have more than 200 members covering a diverse range of health conditions and communities, connecting us with the experiences of millions of people. We work together to strengthen the voice of people: patients, service users, carers, their families, and the voluntary organisations that work for them. Our Vision: People shaping their health and care. Our Mission: We advocate for more inclusive and person centred health and care, shaped by the people who use and need it the most. We do this by: · Understanding and advocating for what matters to people especially those living with health conditions and groups who experience inequalities. · Finding common cause across communities and conditions by working with member charities and those they support. · Connecting and convening charities, decision makers and citizens to work together to change health and care for good. The Role In April 2026, National Voices was commissioned by the Care Quality Commission (CQC) to deliver their work with the CQC Public Engagement Network. The Public Engagement Network is a group of 50+ charities with reach into communities experiencing health inequalities across England. By engaging with these organisations, the CQC’s aim is to ensure that local health and care services meet the needs and preferences of the communities they serve. For both organisations this is much more than just another engagement contract, it is a new partnership designed to make the voices the CQC hears from more than the sum of its parts. In our work with the Public Engagement Network, we are committed to: 1. Ensuring meaningful participation of people and communities 2. Championing accessibility and inclusion 3. Valuing VCSE organisations as equal partners 4. Ensuring insights collected lead to impact and action 5. Investing in the long-term capacity and agency of VCSE organisations 6. Being brave and principled – acting with courage and not shying away from difficult conversations The Voices for Health Equity Project Manager role is to: - Lead the delivery of the Public Engagement Network contract from inception through to delivery, learning and evaluation, including co-ordinating an integrated management team including representatives of our two partner organisations. - Build, manage and sustain the Public Engagement Network, creating a range of opportunities for members to participate, and ensuring relationships are meaningful, inclusive and mutually beneficial. - Ensure high-quality insight is captured from the network, analysed and translated into learning, improvement and influence. - Provide day-to-day project governance, reporting, quality assurance and risk management. The role is delivery-focused and externally facing, with significant responsibility for programme management, partner relationships and ensuring National Voices’ values are embedded in how CQC uses the insights generated. Responsibilities Programme and client management · Lead the end-to-end delivery of the Public Engagement Network programme, including co-ordinating an integrated management team including representatives of our two partner organisations. · Manage individual project plans, budgets, risks and dependencies, escalating issues appropriately and ensuring delivery remains on track. · Oversee subcontracted work, including agreeing briefs, managing performance, quality assuring outputs and approving invoices. · Act as the main point of contact for the commissioners, and lead on regular reporting obligations and on programme evaluation. Building and managing the Public Engagement Network · Take lead responsibility for engaging, stewarding, supporting and retaining a network of VCSE organisations with reach into marginalised communities and those experience inequalities. · Design and deliver engagement approaches with the network and those they represent that prioritises trust, long-term relationships and mutual benefit. · Oversee the delivery of learning events, sense-making sessions and other opportunities that support members to build confidence, skills and influence. · Ensure participants are appropriately supported, reimbursed and recognised for their contribution. · Ambitiously grow the Network, through participating in outreach events, ongoing communication activities and more. Co-ordinate and support activities capturing insight, learning and impact · Co-ordinate and support colleagues with projects that capture qualitative and quantitative insight from people with lived experience, including insight capture events, focus groups, interviews, advisory groups etc. · When needed, support the analysis and synthesis of insight into clear themes, findings and recommendations. · Work with colleagues to ensure insight informs National Voices’ wider influencing, improvement and learning activity. · Support effective feedback loops, ensuring participants understand how their input has been used and what impact it has had. Governance, quality and risk management · Provide day-to-day programme governance for assigned projects, operating within agreed frameworks and reporting arrangements · Contribute to internal management groups and partnership meetings as required · Maintain and review risk registers and quality assurance processes. · Ensure safeguarding, data protection, accessibility and ethical considerations are embedded in all activity. · Support preparation of regular performance and impact reports for internal and external audiences. Partnership and stakeholder management · Work closely with partner organisations to deliver programmes collaboratively, modelling National Voices’ values and ways of working · Build effective relationships with senior stakeholders across the CQC, VCSE organisations and delivery partners. · Represent National Voices at external meetings, events and learning forums as required. Line management and internal leadership · Line-manage the Voices for Health Equity Project Officer including overseeing day-to-day work, quality assuring outputs, holding regular 1-2-1s as well as setting annual objectives and completing appraisals. · Provide matrix management for other National Voices of colleagues including other Manager roles and other officers, as and when work requires. · Work in sync with other managers across National Voices, contributing to a joined-up, supportive team culture · Deputise for the Director of Evidence and Improvement, or other senior colleagues, when required. General · Take a proactive approach to including people with lived experience and members in all areas of work · Support the development of funding bids and proposals, including shaping delivery models and costing activity. · Follow organisational processes to measure, monitor and communicate the impact of our work · Support good project, financial and data management · Contribute to team planning activities and undertake other relevant duties as appropriate · Be prepared to take part in full-day events and, with sufficient notice, events outside core working hours Person Specification Values, attitudes and behaviours Passionate about National Voices’ mission and the meaningful involvement of people with lived experience Strong commitment to equity, inclusion and reducing health inequalities Proactive, flexible and comfortable working in complexity Calm under pressure and able to manage multiple priorities while maintaining quality Confident in building relationships and constructively challenging where needed Comfortable working collaboratively and taking responsibility for delivery Energised by breadth and variety, able to work effectively across diverse topics and themes while spotting connections and opportunities for impact Skills and abilities Strong project or programme management skills, with experience delivering complex, multi-stakeholder work Demonstrable experience of working with people with lived experience and/or VCSE organisations in a meaningful and inclusive way Excellent communication skills, including the ability to translate complex insight into clear, accessible outputs Experience of managing partnerships, subcontractors or commissioned work Strong organisational skills, with the ability to prioritise, plan and manage risk Experience of quality assurance, reporting and working within governance frameworks Excellent people skills, with the ability to lead, support and motivate others Experience, knowledge and understanding · Demonstrable experience in leading insight generation projects which have led to real-world impact and improvements. · Experience in engaging with people experiencing inequalities in a safe and meaningful way. · Demonstrable experience in monitoring and reporting on KPIs and the impact of engagement work. · Experience of managing funder relationships and generating income. · Experience of facilitating and presenting at events and workshops. · Experience of managing and building coalitions or groups of VCSE or other membership organisations (desirable) · An understanding of qualitative and quantitative approaches to evidence generation and analysis (desirabl

item.title: Strategic Relationships and Events Manager
item.description: The Royal Institution (Ri) is an independent charity that has been connecting people with science of more than 225 years. Guided by our vision that Science is for Everyone, we have brought science to life through a vibrant programme of inspirational talks, education programmes and - with almost 1.8m YouTube subscribers - digital content that reaches audiences around the world We are now seeking an exceptional relationship builder and event manager to help drive the success of our ambitious £20 million Be the Spark campaign. this is an exciting opportunity to help shape a new approach to major donor engagement, creating meaningful experiences that strengthen relationships, increase giving and enhance the Ri's reputation among influential audiences. Your work will play an important role in the success of the Be the Spark campaign and help secure the future of the Ri, ensuring that future generations can continue to be inspired by science. About the Role Working closely with the Head of Fundraising, you will build and strengthen relationships with major donors, prospective supporters and influential advocates, developing engagement opportunities that inspire long-term giving. You will lead the planning and delivery of a programme of high-quality fundraising and cultivation events, from intimate donor gatherings to major campaign launches and prestigious VIP occasions. Working with senior stakeholders, trustees, ambassadors and supporters, you will ensure that every interaction strengthens relationships and creates meaningful opportunities for support. This is a varied and highly visible role that combines strategic relationship management, fundraising, event delivery and stakeholder engagement. What You'll Be Doing · Building and managing relationships with major donors, prospects and influential supporters. · Developing tailored cultivation and stewardship plans that deepen engagement and inspire giving. · Delivering exceptional fundraising, cultivation and VIP events from concept through to completion. · Supporting senior leaders, trustees and ambassadors to identify and develop donor engagement opportunities. About You You will be an experienced relationship manager with a talent for bringing people together around a compelling cause. Comfortable working with senior stakeholders and high-profile supporters, you will combine excellent interpersonal skills with strong organisational ability and attention to detail. We're particularly interested in hearing from candidates who have: · Experience managing high-value stakeholder or VIP relationships. · A track record of delivering successful fundraising, engagement or high-profile events. · Outstanding communication and relationship-building skills. · Strong judgement, discretion and stakeholder management skills. · The ability to manage multiple priorities and deliver results in a fast-paced environment. An interest in science, education or public engagement would be an advantage. Are you interested in joining our passionate team dedicated to inspiring people with science? If so, download the full job description and person specification and apply by uploading your CV and a supporting statement of no more than 500 words setting out why you want the job and how your skills and experience meet the criteria set out in the person spec Closing date for applications: midnight on Monday 28 September Interviews are scheduled for w/c 5 October - however we may interview as applications come in and may close the application process early if we receive a strong field of applicants.

item.title: Finance Manager
item.description: The role oversees financial planning, budgeting, forecasting, restricted fund management, audit and year end processes, investment oversight, HR administration, and operational workflows. It also supports the modernisation of financial systems and digital processes to ensure efficiency and good governance. The Finance Manager liaises with all areas of the Society and acts as the senior financial adviser to the Director, Treasurer, SMT and trustees. They attend and provide reports to the Finance, Audit and Risk Committee and Council, attend SMT meetings as required, and line manage the Finance and Operations Officer. Main Responsibilities Strategic Financial Leadership Lead financial strategy, reserves planning, long term forecasting and financial modelling. Embed financial insight into organisational decision making across all departments. Provide financial analysis and advice to SMT, Director, Treasurer and trustees. Support the modernisation of financial systems, digital workflows and reporting structures. Financial Governance and Compliance Ensure compliance with OSCR, HMRC, SORP, VAT, PAYE and statutory reporting requirements. Lead statutory submissions including OSCR returns, HMRC filings and annual compliance documentation. Maintain and strengthen internal controls, including segregation of duties, dual authorisation and documented procedures. Lead development and annual review of finance policies, SOPs and internal control frameworks. Audit and Year End Lead preparation of year end accounts and manage the audit process. Liaise with auditors, ensuring timely provision of information and implementation of post audit adjustments. Present audited accounts to Council and ensure compliance with statutory deadlines and reporting cycles. Investment Oversight Liaise with investment managers. Oversee investment reporting, reserve fund monitoring and alignment with financial strategy. Ensure investment movements and dividends are accurately recorded. Management Reporting Produce monthly management accounts, departmental reports, restricted fund reconciliations and projections. Provide quarterly financial reports to trustees, including trend analysis, variances and strategic indicators. Oversee accuracy and integrity of financial data within Sage and integrated systems. Budgeting and Forecasting Lead annual budgeting with SMT, Director and Treasurer. Provide monthly budget monitoring, variance analysis and recommendations for corrective action. Support project managers with financial planning for restricted fund applications and reporting. Restricted Fund Oversight Ensure accurate reconciliations, funder aligned reporting and compliance with donor conditions. Support fundraising staff with financial information for bids, stewardship and donor reporting. HR Oversight Oversee HR administration delivered by the Finance & Operations Officer. Ensure accurate timesheet collation, leave management, staff records and compliance with HR policies. Support SMT with HR-related financial planning including salary budgeting and workforce planning. Liaise with external HR providers as required. Operational Oversight Oversee procurement, supplier management and administrative workflows. Ensure operational systems support efficiency, compliance and digital working. Provide oversight of membership financial processes within S360 and ensure financial integration with Sage. Leadership Line manage the Finance & Operations Officer, providing direction, support and professional development. Provide financial guidance to SMT, trustees and project leads. Attend SMT, Finance, Audit & Risk Committee and other committees as required. Champion a culture of financial accountability, continuous improvement and organisational efficiency To apply visit our website for more information.

item.title: Philanthropy Manager
item.description: Who we are Nature is in crisis. People are destroying and consuming the natural world at a devastating rate, threatening the ecosystems on which all life depends. Birds are our early warning system, revealing the health of our planet and helping us understand the urgent action needed to protect it. BirdLife International is the world’s largest partnership for nature conservation, bringing together 125 national organisations across six continents to protect birds, biodiversity and the natural systems that sustain life. Through our unique local-to-global approach, we work at the intersection of science, policy and community action to tackle the global nature and climate crises. Using world-leading bird science, we collect and analyse data from across continents, landscapes and seascapes to identify the most effective and innovative conservation solutions. Our work conserves species, safeguards critical habitats and empowers communities to create lasting change for nature and people. At the heart of BirdLife is a powerful global movement. More than two million birders, scientists and local volunteers help track, study and protect birdlife around the world, generating the knowledge and action needed to drive conservation impact at scale. Together, we are giving nature a voice and building a future in which birds, wildlife and people can thrive. BirdLife International’s Development Team is in an exciting new phase of recruitment and growth and will be hiring for a number of roles to support growth and sustainability across the organisation – including this newly created role. About the role As Philanthropy Manager for the Europe and Central Asia (ECA) region of BirdLife International, you will play a key role in growing philanthropic income to support the RENATE initiative and wider ecological restoration programmes across the region. Working with conservation partners throughout Europe and Central Asia, you’ll help secure support for landscape-scale restoration projects in the Balkans, Türkiye and the Caucasus, while building relationships with donors and foundations across key philanthropic markets, including Switzerland, the Netherlands, Germany and the UK. Joining at an exciting stage of growth, you’ll help shape BirdLife ECA’s approach to philanthropy, develop new funding opportunities and build lasting partnerships that support some of the region’s most important restoration programmes. This is a newly created, highly external-facing role within a growing fundraising team, focused on engaging European foundations, major donors, family offices and donor-advised funds. You’ll play a leading role in establishing a sustainable pipeline of philanthropic support while helping to grow BirdLife ECA’s profile and fundraising reach across the region. Develop and implement a philanthropy fundraising strategy, including prospect cultivation and donor stewardship plans. Build a strong pipeline of prospective donors through research, networking and relationship development. Cultivate, solicit and steward new philanthropic relationships, securing first-time gifts, repeat support and multi-year partnerships. Create compelling funding propositions and tailored donor materials in collaboration with programme and development colleagues. Represent BirdLife International at donor meetings, conferences, networking events and cultivation activities across Europe. Who we are looking for We are looking for an entrepreneurial, relationship-driven fundraiser excited by the opportunity to create something new within an international conservation network spanning Europe and Central Asia. This could be the ideal next step for someone with experience in philanthropy, major donor fundraising or another relationship-led discipline who is ready to broaden their experience and take on a more strategic, internationally focused role. What matters most is your ability to build trust, spot opportunities, develop meaningful relationships and engage supporters around a compelling vision. You will bring sound knowledge of the European philanthropic landscape, excellent communication and influencing skills and the confidence to engage senior stakeholders with diplomacy, professionalism and discretion. Experience building and managing donor or stakeholder relationships, ideally within philanthropy, major giving, or another relationship-led fundraising environment. A proactive, self-starting approach with the confidence to help shape a newly created fundraising programme. Excellent communication skills, both written via strong proposals and verbal, with the ability to inspire, influence and negotiate with a range of audiences. A talent for networking, identifying opportunities and turning connections into long-term partnerships. The ability to work collaboratively and effectively with colleagues, partners and supporters across different countries, cultures and time zones. A willingness to travel across Europe and Central Asia to build relationships and represent BirdLife’s work. An interest in international conservation, nature restoration, climate action or sustainable development. Excellent written and verbal English; additional European languages are an advantage. Location: Remote, UK, with travel to the David Attenborough Building in Cambridge / Brussels Closing date: 9 a.m. Thursday 8th October

item.description: Who we are Nature is in crisis. People are destroying and consuming the natural world at a devastating rate, threatening the ecosystems on which all life depends. Birds are our early warning system, revealing the health of our planet and helping us understand the urgent action needed to protect it. BirdLife International is the world’s largest partnership for nature conservation, bringing together 125 national organisations across six continents to protect birds, biodiversity and the natural systems that sustain life. Through our unique local-to-global approach, we work at the intersection of science, policy and community action to tackle the global nature and climate crises. Together, we are giving nature a voice and building a future in which birds, wildlife and people can thrive. BirdLife International’s Development Team is in an exciting new phase of recruitment and growth and will be hiring for a number of roles to support growth and sustainability across the organisation – including this newly created role. About the role Reporting to the Chief Development Officer and working with colleagues worldwide, the Head of Major Gifts will lead the organisation’s major gifts programme, taking responsibility for both strategic development and frontline fundraising. The Head of Major Gifts will build pipeline, create new opportunities, strengthen fundraising discipline and embed a proactive new-business culture across the major gifts function. Seeking to grow and develop this area, the Head of Major Gifts will play both an operational and strategic role – personally winning and managing relationships at the £250k+ level, as well as developing the team and the strategy. It will also have the opportunity to partner with the Chief Development Officer on principal gifts at the £1m+ level. Key responsibilities: Develop and execute a major and principal gifts strategy to grow high-value individual giving across the UK, US and other global markets, in partnership with the CDO. Lead, coach and develop the Major Gifts team of 3, providing direct, hands-on role-modelling in cultivation and solicitation. Represent Major Gifts on the Development Management Team to steward the Development programme at BirdLife and collectively lead transformational change, especially the shared delivery of the Development strategy. Represent Major Gifts on the Principal Gifts Working Group. Identify opportunities to grow BirdLife’s donor base in key regions, particularly in the U.S. and Europe. Personally develop and manage a portfolio of £250k–£1m+ donors and prospects and provide direct, hands-on support to the CDO on principal-level (£1m+) relationships and proposals. Ensure each team member undertakes new business activity to build a robust pipeline within designated markets and giving levels, feeding future portfolio growth for the team. Set and monitor major gifts income targets and performance goals; track progress and pipeline health and provide regular reports to leadership on revenue generation and donor engagement and take corrective actions as needed. Manage the Major Gifts team budget, recruitment and resource allocation. Who we are looking for This role would suit a seasoned major gifts leader, ideally with experience in the conservation and/or international NGO space. We are looking for someone who enjoys being both hands-on and strategic, with experience securing and managing transformative (£250k+) gifts – and coaching others to maximise their own portfolios. A new-business mindset is crucial, as this role will continue BirdLife International’s major-giving growth trajectory. Experience personally raising six- and seven-figure gifts from individuals. Experience of successfully developing and delivering a major gifts/principal gifts strategy. Experience coaching or line-managing fundraisers to develop their own donor relationships. Experience working in an international, complex, not-for-profit environment. Experience managing a small major gifts team, including budgetary responsibility. Ability to work collaboratively across teams and with external stakeholders using a partnerships approach. Location: Remote, UK, with travel to the David Attenborough Building in Cambridge Closing date: 9 a.m. Monday 5th October

item.title: Associate Director (Investments)
item.description: Job description The Associate Director (Investments) role will design and lead a new mission-aligned strategy that puts racial justice and community power at its centre - redefining how our capital can be put to work to restore dignity and collective care within communities. This is not a conventional investment role. It will take all of us, including our grant partners to imagine, design and build. Your role is to hold this with bravery and humility, and a willingness to shift as we continue to learn and deepen our strategic ambitions. We are looking for someone who is as comfortable engaging with communities on the ground as they are with fund managers and wealth advisers - someone who understands that the way capital moves is itself an act of power, and who brings the vision, relationships and technical grounding to help Tudor use its assets in genuine service of our mission. You will sit on the Senior Leadership Team, serve as Tudor's primary investment adviser to the Board and Finance & Investment Committee, and lead a working group of trustees and partners as we chart this new course. item.title: Registered Manager
item.description: We are seeking an experienced Registered Manager to lead Trevi’s Jasmine Mother and Child Residential Family Centre, supporting women and children to build safer, more stable futures. Salary : £46,123 to £52,223 per annum, dependent on qualifications and experience Relocation Package : is available for the right candidate Location : Central Plymouth Hours : 37.5 hours per week, with flexible start and finish times, occasional home working and participation in an on-call rota Contract: Permanent About the role Jasmine Mother and Child Family Residential Centre is Trevi’s specialist residential service supporting women during pregnancy and mothers living with their children while addressing substance use, trauma, mental health needs and wider family pressures. As Registered Manager, you will lead the day-to-day delivery of this seven-bed residential family service, ensuring a safe, nurturing and trauma-responsive environment for women, children and staff. Working alongside the Head of Service, you will lead and develop a multidisciplinary team, maintain high standards of care and ensure the service meets Ofsted requirements and all relevant regulatory and safeguarding standards. Key responsibilities include: · Leading, supporting and developing the staff team · Ensuring the safe and effective day-to-day running of the service · Maintaining compliance with Ofsted requirements and relevant legislation · Overseeing safeguarding, risk management and quality assurance · Developing positive relationships with women, children and professionals · Ensuring individual care and support plans uphold families’ dignity, privacy and safety · Monitoring budgets, resources, staffing and service performance · Supporting continuous service development and improvement · Participating in the on-call rota, including scheduled weekends Trevi will provide support with the Ofsted registration and interview process. About you You will bring strong leadership experience within residential childcare alongside a sound understanding of Ofsted requirements, safeguarding and regulatory standards. You must have: · A minimum of two years’ residential childcare experience within the last five years, including at least one year in a supervisory capacity · An NVQ Level 5 Diploma in Leadership and Management for Residential Childcare, be working towards it or be prepared to work towards it within six months of appointment, or Social Work England registration · Experience of managing and developing an effective team · Experience of working with women and children · A strong understanding of safeguarding, risk assessment and person-centred support · Knowledge of trauma-informed practice · Excellent communication, organisational and leadership skills You will be compassionate, professional and non-judgemental, with the confidence to lead within a complex regulated service. About Trevi Trevi is an award-winning women’s charity that has supported women in Plymouth for more than 30 years. Through residential centres, a women’s centre and outreach programmes, Trevi provides specialist, gender-specific support to women experiencing some of life’s toughest challenges, helping them move from crisis towards safety, stability and independence. Benefits include 25 days’ holiday plus bank holidays, a day off for your birthday, enhanced sick pay, pension contributions, an Employee Assistance Programme, extensive learning and development opportunities and access to the Blue Light Card. This role is open to women only under Schedule 9, Part 1 of the Equality Act 2010. Employment is subject to an Enhanced DBS check, the cost of which will be reimbursed by Trevi. Applicants must already have the right to work in the UK as visa sponsorship is not available for this role. Closing date is 30th September 2026 at mid-day. Other roles you may have experience of could include: Residential Registered Manager, Children’s Registered Manager, Residential Childcare Manager, Residential Services Manager, Deputy Registered Manager, Children and Families Manager.
