item.description: Mind BLMK works across our communities to support positive mental health and wellbeing. Working closely with a range of partners, we offer a number of activities from our wellbeing centres and local venues to make a difference to the mental health and wellbeing of people in Bedfordshire, Luton and Milton Keynes , and our aim is to make sure that no-one has to face a mental health problem alone. Crisis Recovery Worker Post no: 670 Salary: £24,811.13 per annum FTE (£8,214.50 actual per annum for 2 shifts per week) Location: Milton Keynes Hours: 12.25 hours per week Working pattern: 2 x 6-hour shifts per week (Varied across 7-days) 5:00pm to 11:00pm, evenings and/or weekends (Pattern to be agreed) Contract: Permanent About our Community Crisis Cafés Our Community Crisis Cafes offer a safe, welcoming and non-judgmental environment outside of normal working hours for those who feel in mental distress or crisis. About the Role This will involve working with service users in a preventative way, assessing needs, deescalating crisis, offering coping strategies, signposting to other services and ensuring they feel supported, through the process of improving their mental health and wellbeing. Staff will work with a team of Crisis Recovery Workers. Service Delivery Deliver crisis focussed 1:1s and ensure outcomes which supports individuals experiencing a mental health crisis in Houghton Regis & Central Bedfordshire, in line with Mind BLMK’s agreed crisis service and requirements as well as contract requirements. Assessing need and suitability for the service in line with the access to service’s process and undertaking 1:1s. Contribute to maintaining an effective volunteer workforce for the service in line with Mind BLMK’s HR policies, procedures and guidance (workload planning and support). Carry out Cash Handling, Health and Safety and Data Collection responsibilities as directed by the Team Leader in line with Mind BLMK’s policies, procedures, requirements and guidance. Closedown: 5pm Friday 25th September 2026 Interview Date: Friday 2nd October 2026 Please note: We reserve the right to close this advert early if enough suitable applicants apply. Interested? If you would like to find out more, please click the apply button. You will be directed to our website to complete your application for this position. item.title: Head of Strategic Programmes
item.description: Head of Strategic Programmes Help shape the future of the Church across Sussex. We are seeking an experienced strategic leader to oversee an ambitious portfolio of programmes designed to help churches and communities flourish and grow. Position: Head of Strategic Programmes Location: Hove/Hybrid Salary: £61,149 per annum Contract: Fixed term until 31 December 2030, with the possibility of extension Closing Date: 11 October 2026 Interview Date: Hove on 30 October 2026 About the Role Working closely with the Diocesan Secretary, Bishops, Archdeacons and other senior leaders, you will lead the delivery and continued development of the Diocesan Growth Strategy. You will provide strategic oversight of major programmes and projects with a combined budget exceeding £10 million. This includes leading a multidisciplinary team, strengthening programme governance and ensuring investment delivers measurable mission impact. Key responsibilities include: Leading the delivery and development of a portfolio of strategic programmes and projects Translating diocesan priorities into achievable plans and measurable outcomes Overseeing programme governance, performance reporting, risk management and evaluation Managing programme budgets, resources and delivery Leading, supporting and developing the Strategic Programmes team Building effective relationships with parishes, clergy, diocesan boards, senior leaders and national church partners Providing clear analysis, reports and recommendations to support strategic decision-making About You You will be a wise, experienced and collaborative leader who can work strategically within a complex, faith-based organisation. You will have: Significant experience of leading large and complex programmes Experience of working with a diverse range of stakeholders Strong engagement and influencing skills at all levels Experience of managing budgets, resources and programme performance Excellent analytical, communication and report-writing skills The ability to turn strategic priorities into practical plans The confidence and judgement to work effectively with senior leaders The enthusiasm and self-motivation to lead and inspire others A Genuine Occupational Requirement applies under paragraph 1 of Schedule 9 of the Equality Act 2010, and the successful candidate must be a practising Christian. Full details can be found in the job description and person specification when you apply. About the Organisation The vision of the Diocese is to help people to know, love and follow Jesus. Based in Hove and serving the people of Sussex across more than 360 parishes and 154 church schools and the wider community, this is a great role for someone who supports the ethos, aims and objectives of the Diocese and the Church of England. As an employer, and as a team, the mutual values at work are to be Respectful, Professional, Flexible and Supportive. What is on offer: 28 days of annual leave, plus bank holidays and two privilege days per year Membership of the Church Worker’s Pension Scheme with a 15.1% employer contribution and an employee contribution between 0 and 6% Employee Assistance Programme with access to GP appointments, counselling and financial and legal support Flexible working, free parking, a ride to work scheme and development opportunities Our client is committed to safeguarding and promoting the welfare of children, young people and vulnerable adults. All post holders are expected to share this commitment and comply with the relevant safeguarding policy. This role is subject to an Enhanced DBS check and completion of the Church of England Confidential Declaration Form. Other roles you may have experience of could include Head of Programmes, Director of Programmes, Strategic Programmes Manager, Programme Director, Head of Strategy, Portfolio Director, Transformation Director or Head of Strategic Development. Please note this role is advertised by the recruitment agency acting for the client, Not For Profit People. #INDNFP

item.title: Data Compliance Officer
item.description: Contract: Permanent, hybrid 35 hours per week Salary: £35,426 - £38,093 per annum Location: Burford, Oxfordshire, OX18 4PF Closing date: Thursday 1st October 2026 We’re recruiting a Data Compliance Officer! You’ll be joining our Data & Insights team and be our data compliance subject matter expert (SME) in support of the successful delivery of the Blue Cross Data Strategy. In this position you will help us continue cultivating a data-driven culture across our organisation, building a charity-wide community focused on data. This is a hybrid role and you must be able to work from our Burford office in Oxfordshire twice a week. More about the role We are looking for a Data Compliance Officer to join our Data & Insights team within Information Services, working in close collaboration with our Head of Legal and Data Protection (DPO). In this role, you will be the day to day subject matter expert ensuring our data practices, marketing activities, and fundraising operations are compliant, robust, and aligned with current regulation. If you want to use your regulatory knowledge in a supportive, purpose-driven environment, this is a great opportunity to make a real impact. This role focuses on delivering clear, practical compliance guidance across the charity rather than taking a theoretical or box-ticking approach. You will act as the go to contact for advice on the Direct Marketing Association (DMA) code, PECR, and HMRC Gift Aid compliance, while supporting the DPO to maintain alignment with the UK GDPR, Data Protection Act 2018, and the Data (Use and Access) Act 2025. Your day to day work will range from assisting with Subject Access Requests and data incident responses to reviewing targeted communications, ensuring valid permission statements are in place, and auditing third-party supplier standards. You will collaborate closely with marketing, fundraising, and digital project teams to understand their goals and help them design compliant, effective processes from the start. Working alongside colleagues in Information Services, you will help develop data quality KPIs, establish standard operating procedures, and identify areas for automation and process improvement. You will also have the opportunity to advise on emerging challenges, including the responsible and transparent use of data in Artificial Intelligence, and deliver straightforward training and guidance that helps colleagues handle data with confidence. This is a hybrid role and you must be able to work from our Burford office in Oxfordshire twice a week. About you You have a solid foundation in data protection and direct marketing regulations, with a knack for translating complex legal rules into simple, practical advice that colleagues can readily apply. You take an analytical, considered approach to your work and feel comfortable balancing multiple projects, queries, and statutory deadlines without losing sight of detail. Collaboration is key to how you work. Rather than simply highlighting obstacles, you enjoy working alongside different teams to find workable solutions that achieve their objectives while keeping the organisation fully compliant. You bring sound judgment, the confidence to escalate risks when necessary, and strong communication skills that allow you to build positive working relationships across all levels of the charity. Essential Qualifications, Skills, and Experience In-depth working knowledge of Direct Marketing Association code (DMA) and Privacy and Electronic Communications Regulations (PECR) A good working knowledge of UK GDPR, experience in the practical application of UK GDPR principles and effective monitoring of compliance, including Subject Access Requests and Data Privacy Impact Assessments Excellent interpersonal skills, with the ability to explain complex issues clearly and calmly to non-experts Ability to work with diverse personalities and different perspectives to find common ground and influence positive outcomes Possess the confidence and integrity to highlight and escalate risks. Possess strong attention to detail. Ability to demonstrate understanding of and application of our Blue Cross values Desirable Qualifications, Skills, and Experience Practical experience of fundraising, marketing, and income generation Demonstrable awareness of Gift Aid and the requirements for HMRC compliance Experience of working in a not-for-profit environment Good working knowledge and understanding of risk management Experience of being part of a project team How to apply Click the apply button below and complete the online application process before the closing date. We reserve the right to close this vacancy early should we receive an overwhelming response. Blue Cross benefits Our people are the most important part of delivering our purpose. If it were not for their amazing efforts and commitment, we would not be able to make the difference that we do today. In return, Blue Cross wants to ensure we provide you with the best working environment we can. We want you to be happy working for us and will do everything we can to make sure you are. Our generous benefits package includes: Full time equivalent of 38 days holiday rising to 43 with service (including Bank Holidays) Programmes for physical and mental wellbeing support Free access to GP via MetLife- 24/7 GP services, private prescriptions and more for you and your family Health cash plan Unlimited access to an employee assistance programme Pension scheme with enhanced employer contribution Professional fees paid with Continuing Professional Development and personal development support. Life assurance 20% discount on Pet Plan pet insurance Enhanced family friendly policies Recognition scheme Annual volunteer days Charity worker discounts across a variety of retailers To read more about the benefits Blue Cross has to offer, please visit the 'why work for us' page on our website.

As the ideal candidate, your ability to connect with people experiencing homelessness and care leavers will help them build trust, resilience, and a sense of possibility for their future. Our Homeless Support Worker roles are support‑based, focused on guidance, encouragement, and empowering clients to achieve their goals. item.title: Residential Children & Young Peoples Worker
item.description: Are you looking for a new challenge? Do you enjoy working with families and children who have a range of complex needs? We have an exciting opportunity for a caring and compassionate individual to lead our Family Residential Centre as a Residential Support Worker, on a full-time permanent basis. Location of the post: Market Harborough, Leicestershire. Service Overview: Barnardo's, the UK's largest Children's Charity are currently on an exciting and innovative Journey alongside Leicestershire County Council to deliver a range of Children's homes for the most vulnerable children & young people in Leicestershire. Welland House has 3 self-contained flats with the capacity to house up to 3 families at any one time. Families utilising this type of service may include parents with moderate to high learning needs, those presenting with issues around domestic violence, and or substance/alcohol misuse. Additionally, they may have experienced mental ill health and/or trauma. During their stay, the parents will be supported in their parenting by Barnardo's staff, whilst being assessed by Leicestershire County Council Children's Service. The Welland House team is supportive in its approach, with our primary aim revolving around promoting best practices, through guidance, role modelling, key work sessions and practical advice on matters relating to concerns, risk, safety, routines, and boundaries. Some of the responsibilities of the role include but are not limited to: To build trust and develop nurturing relationships which promote the service user's independence, wellbeing, strengths, and capabilities. To work in partnership and build relationships with parents/carers and other professionals. To contribute to the upkeep of the home including cooking, cleaning etc. To document information accurately and ensure records are kept up to date. To ensure safeguarding policies and procedures are adhered to. To promote, monitor and maintain a safe environment at all times. Essential requirements to evidence in your written application: Must hold the Level 3 Diploma in Residential Childcare OR be willing to successfully achieve this within the required timeframe. Relevant experience working with families in a similar setting. Ability to demonstrate a good understanding of safeguarding and protection of children & young people. Flexibility to commit to shift work, including weekends and bank holidays. Excellent communication and interpersonal skills. Must hold a full driving license with access to own vehicle as travel across the locality is an essential part of the role. Whilst Welland House will be your base location, you must be flexible to travel throughout the locality to support our other homes should the need arise. These are located in Hinckley, Coalville, Mountsorrel and Syston. When completing your application please refer to your skills knowledge and experience in relation to the Person Specification, Job Description and Additional Information document. This should be done with an understanding of the context of the service described. Please note due to the high volume of applications for some posts, this advert might close before the displayed closing date. We recommend that you apply for this role as soon as possible

item.title: Solicitor/Cyfreithiwr
item.description: At The National Lottery Community Fund, we are driven by our strategy, ‘It starts with community’ and its four community-led missions, as well as our equity-based approach to tackling poverty, discrimination and disadvantage. We have an opportunity for a Solicitor to join a large team of thirteen, with no line management responsibilities. We are a fast paced in-house legal team which works on a very broad range of matters. Role Expectations The successful candidate will be required to provide legal advice across areas of law including but not limited to grant making, contracts, procurement, charity, litigation, insolvency, subsidy control, debt recovery and public law. In addition to providing substantive advice, the role requires a solicitor to be able to research and upskill on new areas of law very swiftly. It is also expected that the solicitor will use their legal knowledge to help improve the Fund’s internal processes and precedents, as well as ensuring that the Fund complies with statutory and regulatory frameworks at all times. The bulk of the solicitor’s workload will consist of autonomous matters and legal queries. These will need to be answered in a timely manner. Support and supervision is always available and the legal team works on a very collaborative basis. The solicitor will also work with colleagues on larger scale projects when the opportunity arises. Experience working in a busy in-house or private practice environment would be ideal, as would experience dealing with a range of clients, and experience with public law or public bodies. Knowledge of debt recovery/litigation and subsidy control law would be beneficial, as would experience gained in the UK. Interview Details: Interview Date: Week Commencing 5th October 2026 Format: Virtual Location: Can be based anywhere in the UK - We have a hybrid approach to working. Work pattern and location will be agreed with the successful candidate. The role can be based at any of our UK offices, these are Belfast, Birmingham, Cardiff, Exeter, Glasgow, Leeds, London, Manchester and Newcastle. Any questions about the recruitment process, please email the recruitment team. How to apply: Upload your CV in word format and write a supporting statement (1000 words) with the following criteria, we will use this to score your application. Essential criteria UK qualified solicitor, barrister or equivalent At least two years’ relevant experience in private practice or in-house legal in a medium/large sized organisation Excellent attention to detail and good drafting and negotiation skills Good communication and client management skills Ability to manage multiple demands and priorities with good organisational and time management skills Ability to quickly grasp new legal concepts Team player with excellent interpersonal skills Ability to use your initiative to proactively improve ways of working Equity, Diversity and Inclusion Communities in the UK come in all shapes and sizes. National Lottery funding is for everyone – therefore, we are committed to equity, diversity and inclusion and we work hard to ensure our funding reaches where it is needed. We also believe our people should represent the communities, organisations and individuals we work with. That’s why The National Lottery Community Fund is committed to being an inclusive employer and a great place to work. We recognise and celebrate the fact that our people come from diverse backgrounds. We positively welcome applications from people from ethnic minority backgrounds, people with disabilities or longstanding health conditions, people who are LGBTQ+, and people from different socio-economic and educational backgrounds, as well as people of all ages. As a Disability Confident Employer, we take a proactive approach in making reasonable adjustments, if needed, throughout the recruitment process and during employment. (This can be related to a physical and mental health condition.)

item.title: Research Assistant
item.description: Join a landmark study following 8,500 children across the UK Anna Freud is seeking 2 Research Assistants (6 and 12-month contracts) to join our world-leading mental health charity for children, young people and their families. Our mission is to close the gap in wellbeing and mental health by advancing, translating, delivering, and sharing the best science and practice with everyone who impacts the lives of children, young people and their families. More information about Anna Freud is available on our website. Our EDI commitment We are dedicated to fostering a diverse and inclusive workplace and being an equal opportunities employer, whereby equity, diversity, and inclusion (EDI) are core to our recruitment practices. All candidates who meet the job criteria will be considered for employment, regardless of ethnic origin, religion or belief, gender, sexual orientation, disability, age, socioeconomic background, caring responsibilities and care experience. We ask candidates to share their diversity dimensions with us to help us identify, tackle and prevent bias across the employee lifecycle. We believe a diverse workforce enhances our ability to support mental health and wellbeing, allowing us to better meet the needs of the children, young people and families we serve . As a Disability Confident employer, disabled candidates meeting our criteria are guaranteed an interview. Applications are submitted anonymously and assessed using a fair evaluation process based on the criteria set out in our job profiles. What we offer We offer a range of staff benefits, including wellbeing offers such as free counselling through our Employee Assistance Programme. We are proud to have staff-led Diversity Networks offering unique opportunities for learning, connection and impact. This unique opportunity will offer exposure to longitudinal studies and experience in how research interacts with policy. You will join a busy research team of 4-8 people working to tight deadlines with partners including University College London and Department for Education. What you’ll do Be part of a pioneering study following children born in the 2020s. You'll support research delivery through data management, study coordination and analysis activities. Your work will help improve understanding of children's development and wellbeing. What you’ll bring Essential skills and experience: Degree in Psychology (or related discipline) or significant research experience, ideally within child development. Experience of collecting, managing and working with quantitative research data, alongside a good understanding of research methods. Knowledge or experience of observing and coding parent-child interactions or working with similar observational research data. Effective written and verbal communication skills, with the ability to engage effectively with a range of stakeholders. Good organisational skills and the ability to coordinate research activities independently, while working collaboratively as part of a team. Key details Hours: Full-time (35 hours per week). Usual working hours are Monday to Friday, 09:00-17:00. Salary: £29,545 per annum FTE, plus 6% contributory pension scheme. Location: hybrid working (a mixture of onsite and home/remote working). Staff are working onsite for at least 40% of their working hours at our London office (4-8 Rodney Street, London N1 9JH). Contract type: Fixed-term, 6 months and 12 months - 2 posts available. Next steps Closing date for applications: midday (12pm), Wednesday 30 September 2026. Please note: we are expecting a high level of interest, so this vacancy is likely to close earlier than the advertised date. We encourage you to apply promptly and to keep an eye on our future vacancies for more opportunities. Notification of interview: shortlisted applicants will be notified no later than Monday 5 October 2026. During shortlisting, applicants are anonymously assessed using the criteria visible in the Job Profile. Please note: due to the high volume of applications received, we will not be able to provide feedback to unsuccessful applicants. Interviews: will be held remotely on Friday 9 October 2026. How to apply: click on the 'apply now’ button to apply online. We are unable to accept CVs and kindly request no contact from agencies. Questions? Please email Recruitment with any job enquiries, or if you require assistance or experience difficulties when applying. Please note that successful candidate(s) will be asked to evidence their Right to Work in the UK post-job offer – we do not hold a sponsor license therefore we are unable to provide Visa sponsorship.

item.title: Executive Director
item.description: The Executive Director will provide strategic, operational and financial leadership for East London Dance, working in close partnership with the Creative Director & CEO to deliver the organisation’s vision and business plan, strengthening its position as an Arts Council England National Portfolio Organisation. The role leads people, culture, finance, governance, risk, operations, fundraising and stakeholder engagement, ensuring the organisation remains financially sustainable, well-governed and equipped to deliver high-quality artistic and community programmes. As a senior ambassador, the Executive Director builds strong relationships with funders, partners, trustees and stakeholders, while fostering an inclusive, collaborative and values-led culture. The role creates the conditions for a thriving team, turning creative ambition into organisational reality and supporting East London Dance’s long-term success. We’re looking for someone who can help turn our ambition into a sustainable, thriving future – building the relationships and the funding that will carry us forward, and doing it alongside a team that already cares deeply about the organisation. If you’re someone who loves building things, who knows how to bring people and money together, and who wants to help shape what east London’s cultural life looks like for years to come – we’d love to hear from you. Job requirements: Must bring substantial senior leadership experience, ideally Director, Deputy CEO or equivalent level, with evidence of strategic planning, organisational growth and performance management. Must have a proven track record in fundraising, business development and income generation, including securing funding, managing funder relationships and identifying new commercial or partnership opportunities; experience leading high-performing teams, managing change and strengthening organisational culture; strong financial acumen, including understanding budgets, balance sheets and financial decision-making; knowledge of charity governance, safeguarding, health and safety, data protection and risk management frameworks; experience working with Boards of Trustees. Must demonstrate commitment to diversity, equity and inclusion, possess excellent written and verbal communication skills, be confident using Microsoft Suite, and have knowledge of ACE funding and reporting requirements. Job Responsibilities: Provides strategic, operational and financial leadership with Creative Director & CEO. The role translates the Business Plan into action, leads staff, freelancers and consultants, and develops an inclusive, high-performing culture. Key responsibilities include workforce planning, recruitment, HR compliance, performance management and staff wellbeing. The role oversees organisational systems, administration, IT and the operation of Talent House, including health and safety, compliance, venue hire and stakeholder relationships. They co-lead budgeting, forecasting, financial reporting, cash flow monitoring and audit processes, while driving fundraising and income generation across grants, trusts, partnerships, sponsorship and earned income. The role also leads governance, risk management and business continuity planning, supports the Board of Trustees, develops strategic partnerships, represents the organisation externally and strengthens its profile, impact and long-term sustainability. Apply via the East London Dance Website by Thursday 8 October, 12 Noon

item.title: South London Centre Manager
item.description: Smart Works is a dynamic, high profile and fast-growing UK charity that dresses and coaches unemployed women for success at their job interview. We empower each woman by giving her the clothes and the confidence she needs to succeed. After visiting Smart Works, 68% of clients secure a job, gaining financial independence and transforming their lives. The Smart Works service is delivered in London, Manchester, Edinburgh, Birmingham, Newcastle, Reading, Bristol and Leeds. Over the past ten years, Smart Works has helped over 50,000 women, and last year alone we reached 10,600 women. It is our mission that any woman who needs our service should be able to find her way to a Smart Works centre. In 2025 we launched our new 5-year strategy- we are aiming to build a future where every woman, at any stage of her career, can access trusted, personalised support to secure employment. We aspire to be local in feel, national in reach, shaped by the voices of women, valuing every story and every success. About the Role The South London Centre Manager will have overall responsibility for the day-to-day management, smooth running and development of the South London centre and Smart Works service in Croydon. They will oversee the delivery of a high-quality Smart Works service, to include managing centre operations, leading and supporting the volunteer community, and building strong relationships with local partners and stakeholders, to ensure that Smart Works is well-embedded in the South London community. The Centre Manager will be a highly organised and proactive individual who enjoys making things happen. They will be equally comfortable managing the practical running of a busy public-facing centre, supporting clients and volunteers, representing Smart Works externally and identifying opportunities to grow the service. They will be a natural relationship builder who is able to create a vibrant, friendly and inclusive environment where everyone feels welcome. The role would be based in the South London centre, and there will be occasional evening and weekend work for which staff are awarded TOIL. There will also be an expectation that this role may need to visit other Smart Works London centres or travel for outreach events and activities throughout the city. How to Apply Please submit a CV and a cover letter which answers the following questions by 29th September at 5pm. Your application should be addressed to Fiona Hollow, Head of London Service Delivery Why do you want to work for Smart Works? (Max 250 words) How will you create a positive atmosphere and environment for clients, volunteers and staff members in our South London centre? (Max 250 words) Tell us about a time you have worked effectively in a team to solve a problem. (Max 250 words) 1st round interviews will take place on Monday 5th October and will be virtual. If you are unable to attend a virtual interview for any reason, please let us know to discuss another arrangement.2nd round interviews will take place on Friday 9th October and will be in person in Croydon. If you require any reasonable adjustments or alterations for the application and recruitment processes, please reach out to us. Smart Works is committed to best practice employment practices, including reducing the burden for those seeking work. Smart Works will therefore reimburse reasonable costs of travel to interviews if required.
item.dc:creator: Smart Works

item.title: Digital Content & Community Lead
item.description: Job Title: Digital Content & Community Lead Location: London, Salford or Belfast, based from an RFF office with hybrid working arrangements and extensive travel across the UK and Ireland Salary: £30,000-£35,000 per annum, depending on experience Hours: 36 hours per week Reports to: Deputy CEO & Director of Development Job Description: You’ll lead RFF’s Instagram and TikTok presence, creating distinctive social-first content and building engaged digital communities around our work. This is a hands-on role. You’ll spend time with young people, staff, partners and ambassadors across the UK and Ireland, spotting, capturing and creating content that brings the Foundation to life. While Instagram and TikTok will be at the heart of the role, you’ll also support RFF’s wider digital and communications activity as required — including creating and adapting content for platforms such as LinkedIn, X and YouTube, supporting email communications and press activity, and helping strengthen RFF’s media presence around key events and opportunities. We’re open to emerging talent and care more about what you can create, your understanding of digital communities and your creative instincts than where you learned your skills. KEY DUTIES: Social Content & Community Take day-to-day ownership of RFF’s Instagram and TikTok channels, growing active and engaged communities around our work. Develop a forward content plan while responding creatively to trends, conversations and opportunities in real time. Listen to our audiences, engage actively with our communities and use insight and performance to continually improve our content. Content Creation & Production Proactively identify content opportunities across RFF’s work, partnerships and events, and plan, film, photograph, interview and edit high-quality social-first content across a range of formats. Create content specifically for digital platforms, particularly short-form video for Instagram Reels and TikTok, and maximise content captured by adapting it effectively across formats and channels. Use and advise on appropriate production equipment, software and tools, while maintaining an organised digital content and asset library for the Foundation. Young People & Youth-led Content Build positive and appropriate relationships with young people, creating content with them rather than simply about them and representing their personalities, perspectives, interests and achievements authentically. Create opportunities for young people to contribute as creators, presenters, interviewers and storytellers and, over time, help identify and develop aspiring young content creators from across RFF. Ensure all content involving young people is created, captured, stored and used in line with RFF’s safeguarding, consent and data-protection requirements. Partnerships, Ambassadors & Collaboration Work creatively with RFF’s corporate and industry partners, ambassadors and wider network to develop co-created content, campaigns and opportunities that benefit both RFF and its collaborators. Build strong relationships with partner communications and social teams, identifying opportunities for collaborative content, cross-platform amplification and reaching new communities and audiences. Work confidently across different environments - from community youth sessions to major corporate, media, sporting and cultural events - adapting your approach to different people, audiences and opportunities. Wider Digital Content Support the creation and adaptation of content across RFF’s wider digital ecosystem, including YouTube, LinkedIn, X and the Foundation’s website, while keeping Instagram and TikTok as the primary focus. Work collaboratively with colleagues to support wider communications activity, including email communications, press and media activity, campaigns, launches and events, and make effective use of strong content across channels. Bring ideas about new platforms, formats, technologies and approaches that could strengthen RFF’s digital presence and help our content reach and engage different audiences. Insight & Performance Monitor channel and content performance, using analytics to understand engagement, community growth, reach, audience behaviour and what content is creating meaningful interaction. Test new approaches and formats, learn from performance and audience response, and use those insights to continually develop RFF’s social content and community approach. Keep up to date with developments across social media, digital content, creator culture and platform changes, sharing clear insights and emerging opportunities with the Director of Development and wider team.

item.title: Digital Advertising Officer
item.description: Are you a digital marketing professional who loves dogs? We’re looking for a Digital Advertising Officer to deliver paid digital marketing campaigns, helping spread the word about Dogs Trust. What does this role do? As Digital Advertising Officer, you will: manage campaigns throughout the full lifecycle, from briefing with our media agency, to building and developing creative assets and copy, with a particular focus on paid social campaigns on Meta Ads and Google Ads, optimise and test campaigns, using platform data and Google Analytics 4 (GA4) to track KPIs, interpret performance, and provide actionable, data-driven recommendations to maximise impact, work closely with stakeholders across the charity to ensure campaigns are optimised, and all content reaches the appropriate audience. This role is a fixed term contract until 31st December 2026. Interviews for this role are provisionally scheduled for week commencing 25th to 29th September 2026, and will take place on Teams. Could this be you? To be successful in this role, you’ll need some experience of working with paid digital advertising campaigns, specifically Meta Ads and Google Ads, underpinned by a strong understanding of pay-per-click advertising and paid social. You’ll also have strong analytics skills, with the ability to interpret data and make decisions accordingly. You’ll need effective time management and prioritisation skills, as this role often juggles multiple, competing priorities. Creative copywriting skills are essential, as well as a passion for Dogs Trust and the work we do. What does this team do? The Digital Team is responsible for developing and maintaining Dogs Trust's digital presence, including its website and other online platforms and services. About Dogs Trust We love dogs. That’s why we do whatever we can to make sure every four-legged friend gets the love they deserve. We’ll never put a healthy dog down, so our work is focused on helping dogs in need, supporting owners every step of the walk, and creating a better world for dogs in the future. It’s what we’ve been doing since 1891 and how we’ve grown to become the UK’s leading dog charity, helping 12,000 loyal friends find their forever homes every year. To apply for this position please click the APPLY NOW button. Our application process requires you submit a personal statement explaining your interest and suitability for the role. Dogs are incredibly diverse, much like the humans that love them! At Dogs Trust we value diversity, and we're committed to fostering an inclusive culture. We actively encourage applications from people of all backgrounds, abilities, and cultures and believe that a diverse workforce helps us to achieve our mission. Our colleague networks give our people a voice, acting as vehicles for real and meaningful change within Dogs Trust. We truly want to see every candidate shine throughout the entire job application process, interview stages, and during their time with us. If there's anything on your mind or any adjustments you may need, don't hesitate to reach out to us. We're here to support you every step of the way.
item.dc:creator: Dogs Trust

item.title: Housing Contracts and Supplier Manager
item.description: The Housing Contracts & Supplier Manager is responsible for overseeing the procurement, performance, and management of contractors and suppliers that support the Church of England Pensions Board Housing Department working in collaboration with the NCIs procurement team. The role ensures services are delivered safely, compliantly, cost effectively and to a high standard, while supporting contract owners across the housing service and driving supplier performance and value for money. The Housing Contracts & Supplier Manager leads the management of supplier relationships, contract performance, procurement activity and service delivery across the Church of England Pensions Board Housing Department. The role plays a key part in ensuring that property maintenance, construction, specialist services and other housing-related contracts are effectively procured, managed, and monitored to deliver excellent outcomes for residents and the organisation. Working closely with internal stakeholders, contractors, suppliers, procurement colleagues and finance teams, the postholder is responsible for overseeing the full contract lifecycle, from procurement and mobilisation through to performance management, renewal and contract closure. They ensure compliance with regulatory, health and safety, governance and cyber security requirements, while maintaining accurate records and providing robust reporting and performance analysis. The role provides expert support and guidance to contract owners across the Housing Department, helping to deliver consistent contract management practices, effective supplier governance and best value outcomes. It also manages contractor performance through KPIs and SLAs, monitors budgets and expenditure, reviews invoices and contract variations, and identifies opportunities for service improvement and procurement efficiencies. As a commercial lead within the Housing Department, the Housing Contracts & Supplier Manager builds productive supplier partnerships, manages risks, supports compliance obligations, and contributes to the delivery of safe, high-quality housing services for retired clergy and their families across England. The closing date is 29th September at 23:55. Contract Management & Service Delivery Manage mobilisation and demobilisation of contracts with suppliers, including building relationships with suppliers and maintaining a register of specialists, suppliers and contractors in partnership with the central NCI procurement team. Responsibility for procurement and management of ad-hoc contractors and other suppliers across our housing portfolio. Support end to end contract management for all contract owners across the Housing Department Ensure services are delivered safely, on time, within budget, and in line with policies and regulatory requirements. Manage and maintain the list of approved property fixtures and fittings for residents to choose from Maintain accurate contract and supplier records, supporting audits and reporting. Oversee contract lifecycle administration, including renewals and variations, and ensuring ongoing compliance with NCI cyber security, ensuring up to date copies of insurances and compliance documentation for suppliers are on record and data management policies and best practice Support quality assurance processes and ensure compliance with relevant standards and legislation. Work with internal teams to manage risks, resolve issues, and meet statutory obligations. Champion the Board's Safeguarding policy and procedures because safeguarding is everyone's responsibility. Financial Oversight Monitor contract spend, supporting budgets and ensure value for money. Review and approve invoices, variations, and payments in line with finance and housing systems Systems & Reporting Monitor contractor performance against KPIs, SLAs, and contractual obligations, taking corrective action where required and considering if longer term arrangements would be beneficial. Maintain accurate data and produce performance reports including customer satisfaction surveys, benchmarking and trend analysis (type of works and expenditure) and provide insight to support decision making. Work collaboratively across Housing, Procurement, and Finance to support effective service delivery. You are a highly organised and commercially minded contracts professional with experience managing suppliers, contractors, and service delivery. You have strong stakeholder management skills, a keen eye for detail, and a proven ability to ensure contracts deliver high-quality, compliant, and cost-effective outcomes. You are a collaborative team player who can build positive relationships, solve problems proactively, and use data and insights to drive continuous improvement.

item.title: Campaign Communications Manager
item.description: I’m eager to speak to a Communications and Campaigns professional with experience developing and delivering integrated communications and public affairs strategies, ideally within the charity, education, or third sector, or in an agency environment. The opportunity is with a leading international children’s education charity, as their Campaign Communications Manager, based in London, working an innovative, 4 day week. In this role you will develop and deliver the communications strategy for a specific Education Campaign and Global Finance Summit, working closely with the Senior Campaigns Manager. You will manage communications with a global network of more than 200 businesses, NGOs, foundations, early childhood organisations and government partners, producing toolkits and campaign updates that enable effective advocacy. Your experience: Proven track record of managing external stakeholders, coordinating networks, and translating complex issues into content and stories that build public and political momentum. Led political insight and policy analysis across UK and devolved markets, identifying opportunities to influence Led communications and public affairs strategy Digital campaigning, overseen campaign communications across digital channels, including the website, social media and email Organised roundtables Drawing together evidence-based content for parliamentary and departmental audiences Secured national and regional media coverage Experience creating and/or overseeing the creation of social media assets Creation of Toolkits- creating communications assets for others to use and liaise with partners on communications. Events experience – desirable. Are you ready to play a central role in planning and delivering integrated communications that build momentum, engage partners and support advocacy? Salary £40,000 for 4 day week. 4 day working week (Monday-Thursday). item.title: Estate Worker
item.description: Estate Worker When registering to this job board you will be redirected to the online application form. Please ensure that this is completed in full in order that your application can be reviewed. Estate Worker Location West Midlands £26,760 per annum (pro rata for part time) Ref: 218REC Full time from 30-35 hours per week – we are happy to talk flexible working Base: Birmingham Contract: Permanent Disclosure: Basic DBS is not required for this position as the post holder will not (?)be working with school and community groups in the region. ABOUT THE ROLE Team: Estate Management As the Estate Worker, you will be playing a key role within the team, helping to maintain and enhance the condition, safety and accessibility of the Walk Wheel Cycle Trust estate. You will undertake a range of routine maintenance activities across National Cycle Network (NCN) routes, other paths, and associated land owned or managed by the Trust. What You’ll Be Doing Work as part of a small team undertaking planned and reactive maintenance work on Walk Wheel Cycle Trust owned and occupied estate. Identify issues during land inspections and take appropriate action to address them. Safely drive vehicles, tow trailers, and operate equipment and power tools, including chainsaws and strimmers. Support volunteering team or community engagement team with volunteer activities This role is ideal for someone with practical maintenance and groundcare skills who enjoys working outdoors both on their own and occasionally as part of a small team. ABOUT YOU We’re looking for someone who has experience and understanding in the areas listed below. Full clean driving licence and either hold, or be able to obtain, Category B and E for towing on driving licence. Hold relevant certificates of competence in chainsaw operation, brush cutter/strimmer use, PA1 and PA6 pesticide application, mobile plant operation (NPORS or equivalent), and ride-on mower operation. Experience of working outside in a paid or voluntary capacity. Understanding of countryside management principles. The ability to work in a way that promotes the safety and wellbeing of children, young people and adults at risk. LIVING OUR VALUES At the Walk Wheel Cycle Trust, we’re a values‑driven organisation. We’re looking for people who are: Always Learning – curious, open‑minded and committed to continuous improvement. Championing Equity – inclusive, respectful and focused on ensuring everyone has a voice and fair opportunity to succeed. Taking Ownership – proactive, responsible and empowered to make things better. Delivering Together – collaborative, transparent and motivated by shared success. Through our values we make it possible for more people to walk, wheel and cycle safely, healthily and joyfully. WHAT WE OFFER We want you to feel supported, valued, and empowered in your role. That’s why we offer flexible working, a positive team environment, and benefits designed to support your wellbeing, finances, and family life. Group Personal Pension scheme with a 6% or 7% of basic salary contribution being matched by Walk Wheel Cycle Trust Bike, computer and season ticket loans London Weighting Allowance of £4,530 per annum, pro rata for all those living within a London Borough (32 local authority districts plus the City of London). To apply, please complete our online application form. item.title: Facilities Manager
item.description: Harris Hill is delighted to be supporting a leading UK charity with the recruitment of a Facilities Manager to take responsibility for the facilities management and day-to-day operation of its purpose-built national training and conference centre. This is a varied role combining facilities management, health and safety, team leadership, contractor management and customer service, within an organisation with a strong social purpose. Key responsibilities include: Leading, managing and developing the on-site facilities team. Ensuring statutory, health and safety and facilities compliance is maintained. Managing contractors, suppliers and facilities contracts, ensuring value for money and agreed service standards. Overseeing preventative maintenance, building services and facilities improvements. Managing the facilities budget and procurement of goods and services. Supporting refurbishment, maintenance and capital works projects. Working closely with event and booking teams to ensure facilities are prepared to a high standard. Acting as a key point of contact for facilities and health and safety queries. You will ideally have: Experience managing facilities/buildings and a team. Operational management experience within a conference, hotel, leisure, hospitality or similar environment. Strong knowledge of health and safety, including risk assessments and audits. Experience managing contractors, suppliers and facilities contracts. Experience managing budgets and procurement. item.title: Programmes Manager
item.description: EASST is an international NGO promoting road safety and sustainable mobility across Eastern Europe and Central Asia. We believe local voices are essential to saving lives and bringing lasting change so we form long term partnerships with local civil society organisations, uniting their on-the-ground knowledge with national and international expertise to deliver evidence-based solutions that are grounded in the local reality. Across our region, fatality rates are more than twice the European average and can cost up to 4% GDP, yet road safety still doesn't get the priority or investment it needs. Today, rapidly escalating vehicle numbers are straining urban infrastructure, challenging existing road safety frameworks, and contributing to poor air quality and higher carbon emissions. Our projects are focused on long-term change, connecting the dots between road safety and sustainable mobility and supporting communities in the transition toward safer, more inclusive transport networks that reduce casualties, strengthen climate resilience, and support sustainable economic growth. EASST also operates EASST Expertise Ltd, an international road safety consultancy and wholly owned trading subsidiary. EASST Expertise draws on a wide network of specialists to support, advise and manage road safety projects across the world, with all surplus revenues returned to support EASST's charitable work. Why join EASST? EASST is a small organisation, and this is a varied role with significant responsibility. You will have the opportunity to work across the full project cycle, from developing new ideas and proposals through to delivery, evaluation and learning. You will work directly with our partners across the region, international experts and major funders, and have real scope to influence how our programmes develop. Working in a small team means being prepared to get involved across different areas of our work and to take responsibility when needed. In return, the role offers considerable autonomy and variety, and the opportunity to see the direct impact of your work. Role overview As Programmes Manager, you will play a central role in EASST’s small team, managing a varied portfolio of road safety and sustainable mobility projects across Eastern Europe and Central Asia. Reporting to the Director General, you will take responsibility for projects across their full lifecycle – from project development and planning through to delivery, monitoring, reporting and evaluation. Working closely with our network of local civil society partners, you will ensure projects are delivered on time, on budget and to a high technical standard. You will build strong, trusted relationships with our local civil society partners, support their organisational and technical development, and combine their on-the-ground knowledge with international technical expertise to influence policy and practice. This is a hands-on role in a small organisation. Alongside managing programmes, you will contribute to new business development, organisational strategy and wider EASST activities as needed. Key responsibilities Manage a portfolio of road safety and sustainable mobility projects across EASST's partner countries, ensuring high-quality delivery against agreed objectives, timelines and budgets. Oversee project planning, work plans and budgets, monitoring progress and flagging risks or delays early, with proposed solutions. Ensure projects are technically sound, evidence-based and aligned with international road safety good practice. Support the development of new project proposals and concept notes, including budgeting, log frames/theories of change, and donor-specific requirements. Build and maintain strong, trusted relationships with partner organisations, supporting them to strengthen organisational and technical capacity, including through monitoring visits and technical support missions. Develop and maintain project monitoring frameworks, tracking outputs, outcomes and impact, and capturing lessons learned to inform future programme design. Prepare high-quality narrative and financial reports for donors, ensuring accuracy and compliance with requirements and deadlines. Manage project budgets and financial compliance, working with the Director of Operations and Finance to monitor spend and forecast against donor rules. Identify and manage programmatic, financial, reputational and safeguarding risks, ensuring compliance with EASST's policies throughout. Collaborate with colleagues across EASST and represent EASST with donors, partners and other stakeholders, contributing to organisational strategy, business development, and communications outputs as needed. Person specification Essential Proven experience managing international development or NGO programmes. Experience managing project budgets and donor reporting, with a good understanding of donor compliance requirements (e.g. development banks, trusts, foundations or bilateral donors). Experience with monitoring and evaluation frameworks and tools. Experience working with and supporting local civil society or partner organisations. Strong project management skills, including planning, monitoring and risk management. Excellent written and verbal communication skills, with experience producing high-quality reports and proposals. Ability to manage multiple projects and priorities simultaneously, working independently and as part of a small team and taking responsibility when needed. Cultural sensitivity and experience working across diverse international contexts. Willingness and ability to travel internationally. Highly desirable Experience of road safety programmes and a strong understanding of road safety principles, data and evidence-based interventions. Experience of sustainable mobility programmes, including areas such as active travel, inclusive mobility, public transport or low-carbon transport. Experience working in Eastern Europe and Central Asia, or a comparable region. Experience of new business development or proposal writing for institutional donors. Desirable Russian and/or another regional language. Degree or professional qualification in a relevant field (e.g. transport, development, public health). Terms and Conditions Location: Based in the United Kingdom, with the right to work in the UK. The team currently works remotely with no office base. Travel: Travel may be required within the UK to Team meetings as well as within the region served by EASST and to conferences and other events. Hours: This is a full-time post. Some flexibility will be required to accommodate international travel and occasional meetings with partners and funders across different time zones. Salary: The salary offered for this post is £40–50K (depending on experience) plus 10% pension contribution and 30 days holiday per year. We recognise that excellent candidates may not meet every aspect of the person specification. If you have strong international programme management experience and believe your skills and experience could transfer well to EASST's road safety and sustainable mobility work, we would encourage you to apply.
item.dc:creator: EASST (Eastern Alliance for Safe and Sustainable Transport)

item.title: Independent Advocate
item.description: Are you passionate about making a difference in people's lives? Do you thrive in a dynamic, fast-paced environment? Are you ready to take on a role that impacts your community? We are currently seeking an enthusiastic and dedicated Independent Advocate to join our vibrant team in POhWER. As an Independent Advocate, you will provide crucial support to vulnerable adults facing significant health and social care challenges. Your role involves delivering persuasive verbal and written representations on behalf of clients, collaborating with public and voluntary organisations, and taking directed actions to address client issues. This role demands flexibility, excellent communication, and the ability to handle sensitive information confidently. Independent Advocate Requirements: Strong communication and time management skills to successfully work remotely. Excellent IT skills, including the use of Microsoft Outlook, Word, and Excel, and the ability to learn software packages such as client management databases. Attention to detail to ensure accurate recording of records and reporting to meet tight deadlines. Desirable: Previous experience in advocacy, information and advice, or a similar role within health, social care, or the voluntary sector. Demonstrable experience working with vulnerable adults. Working knowledge of public and voluntary organisations. Successful candidates must have a car and full drivers license. Expenses will be paid from the border of surrey for applicants outside of Surrey. Benefits: 25 days annual leave + Bank holiday (Rising to 30 days after 5 years’ service) with the option to buy or sell up to 5 days leave + your birthday off as an additional holiday day after 1 years’ service! Discretionary shutdown days at Christmas with up to 4 additional days leave. 1 Community Leave Day per annum. Cash Wellbeing Healthcare Plan which covers Optical/dental/alternative therapy and more! Auto enrolment Pension plan Death in service cover. Bike to work scheme. Meet the Organisation: Who We Are and What We Do At POhWER, we are committed to empowering individuals and enabling their voices to be heard. We provide advocacy and information services to support people in making effective decisions about their health and social care. Our team is dedicated to listening, exploring options, and taking action to meet our clients' best interests. We provide a full induction, training and equipment including a laptop and mobile phone. It is a contractual requirement that all advocates hold or are working towards an advocacy qualification. The most recognised qualification is the City and Guilds Level 4 Independent Advocacy Practice Qualification (IAP) for practising advocates, previously completed City and Guilds Level 3 National Advocacy Qualification (NAQ). If you do not already hold an NAQ certificate or diploma or IAP qualification or equivalent, the expectation will be that you will gain the City and Guilds IAP qualification following successful completion of probation and pre-enrolment process. POhWER will fully sponsor this and provide a reasonable amount of study time and in return expect advocates to manage their time and complete within 12 months of registration. Think you are the perfect fit for this Independent Advocate role? Don't wait! Apply Now! An Enhanced DBS check and National Offender Management Service vetting will be conducted for this position. We're proud to support our colleagues from the armed forces signing the Armed Forces Covenant in August 2024. Successful applicants will need to obtain business insurance for their own vehicle. POhWER is an equal opportunities employer, holder of the Investors in People Silver award, and a member of the MINDFUL EMPLOYER scheme. We are a level 2 Disability confidence scheme employer, and disabled applicants who meet all the essential criteria will be guaranteed an interview. POhWER is committed to equality, diversity, and inclusion. We encourage applications from all backgrounds, cultures, and abilities, and particularly welcome candidates from groups currently underrepresented in our workforce. Our goal is to foster an inclusive environment where everyone feels valued and empowered to contribute. This includes, but is not limited to, people with disabilities, women, men, Black, Asian and other racially minoritised people, LGBTQ+ who are currently under-represented in our workforce. To help embed inclusion for all, from day one, we offer a range of family friendly, inclusive employment policies, flexible working arrangements and employee networks to support people from different backgrounds.

item.title: Independent Advocate

(Applicants must live within the area and have the ability to travel to different Mersey Care sites) Starting Salary : £25,877.80 per annum. Contract type : Permanent Independent Advocate Requirements: Strong communication and time management skills Excellent IT skills, including the use of Microsoft Outlook, Word, and Excel, and the ability to learn software packages such as client management databases. item.title: Project & Transformation Manager
item.description: Reporting to: Chief Executive Contract: 12-month fixed-term contract Salary: £45,000–£48,000 per annum, depending on experience About the role This is an exciting opportunity to play a key role in an important period of development and transformation for West London Synagogue. Working closely with the executive team, the postholder will provide coordination and project management across a range of organisational priorities and will play a key role in supporting the delivery of the wider transformation programme. The role will bring together project management, organisational performance, impact measurement, reporting and continuous improvement . The successful candidate will help turn strategic priorities into practical plans, ensure projects remain on track, and provide clear information to senior leaders and the Board about progress, performance and impact. This is a broad and varied role for someone who enjoys working across an organisation, bringing structure to complexity and helping people turn good ideas into effective delivery. Key Responsibilities 1. Transformation and Organisational Priorities Play a key role in coordinating and supporting the organisation's transformation programme. Work with the Chief Executive, the finance and resources director and senior colleagues to translate strategic priorities into clear plans, actions, milestones and deliverables. Track progress against agreed priorities and identify risks, delays, dependencies and resource pressures. Identify connections and opportunities for collaboration between different projects and programmes. Support colleagues in embedding new processes, systems and ways of working arising from the transformation programme. Ensure that agreed decisions are translated into clear actions, ownership and follow-through. Support a culture of continuous improvement, learning and accountability. The postholder will not be expected to manage every change initiative directly. Their role will be to provide structure, coordination and visibility across the transformation programme , working with colleagues who own individual projects and areas of work. 2. Project Management Plan, coordinate and deliver a range of organisational projects in line with agreed priorities and timelines. Develop proportionate project plans setting out objectives, milestones, deliverables, responsibilities, dependencies and measures of success. Coordinate internal teams, volunteers, partners and external stakeholders where required. Facilitate project meetings, workshops and reviews. Maintain clear project documentation, actions and decision logs. Projects are likely to vary in scale and nature and may include organisational improvement, systems and process development, governance, member services, operational change, programme development and cross-team initiatives . 3. Organisational Performance and Data Collect, analyse and interpret data to understand project and organisational performance and impact Develop clear and proportionate dashboards and management information. Identify trends, gaps, risks and areas requiring attention. Work with colleagues to establish meaningful KPIs and measures of success. Ensure information is accurate, appropriately managed and compliant with relevant data protection requirements. 4. Board and Senior Leadership Reporting Coordinate the preparation of clear, concise and meaningful reports for the Board. Establish and maintain an effective reporting timetable. Track actions and decisions arising from Board and committee meetings and ensure appropriate follow-up. The emphasis will be on insight rather than simply reporting activity — helping leaders and trustees understand what is happening, why it matters and where action is required. 5. Governance, Compliance and Policies Maintain and regularly update the organisational compliance log, duties and mitigation plans. Monitor progress against compliance requirements and highlight emerging risks. Support colleagues to ensure compliance actions are followed through. Develop, review and update organisational policies and operational procedures. 6. Stakeholder Engagement and Coordination Build effective working relationships across the organisation. Work collaboratively with staff, volunteers, trustees, partners and external stakeholders. Bring people together where projects or priorities cross organisational boundaries. Facilitate meetings, workshops and project reviews where required. Communicate progress, challenges, risks and successes clearly and appropriately. Person Specification Essential Skills and Experience We are looking for someone who combines strong project management skills with excellent organisational judgement and the ability to work across different parts of an organisation. You will have: Proven experience managing projects and delivering organisational change or improvement initiatives. Experience managing several projects or workstreams simultaneously. Strong planning, prioritisation and organisational skills. The ability to take a project from initial idea and scoping through to implementation and evaluation. Strong analytical skills and experience working with data, KPIs and performance information. Experience producing high-quality reports Experience monitoring outcomes, performance or impact. Excellent written and verbal communication skills. Strong stakeholder management and relationship-building skills. The ability to influence and coordinate people without relying on formal authority. A practical, proactive and solutions-focused approach. Excellent attention to detail while retaining an understanding of the bigger picture. The ability to work independently, take ownership and use good judgement. Confidence working in an environment where priorities can change and not everything is fully defined. Desirable Experience supporting an organisational transformation or change programme. Experience working in a charity, synagogue, community organisation, social enterprise or other purpose-led organisation. Experience working with Boards, trustees or governance committees. Experience developing organisational dashboards or management information. Experience in impact measurement, monitoring and evaluation. Knowledge of project management methodologies such as PRINCE2 or Agile. Understanding of governance, compliance and data protection requirements, including GDPR. Experience developing policies and operational procedures. Why Join Us? This is an exciting time to join WLS. We are undertaking a significant programme of organisational development and transformation, creating an opportunity to improve how we work, strengthen our systems and processes and build an organisation that is well equipped for the future. The Project & Transformation Manager will have a central role in making this happen. You will work alongside senior leaders, colleagues and volunteers at all levels, with the opportunity to see your work have a direct and tangible impact. This is a role for someone who enjoys making things happen — someone who can take a complex problem, bring structure to it, bring people together and help turn an idea into something that works.
item.dc:creator: West London Synagogue

item.title: Volunteering Executive
item.description: ROLE OVERVIEW The Volunteering Executive is responsible for recruiting, managing, and coordinating RLSS UK volunteers. This role will require the candidate to interact with a wide variety of volunteers throughout the UK and Ireland, promoting volunteering opportunities and recruiting people to fulfil those roles; in particular but not limited to, supporting RLSS UK presence and voluntary lifeguarding at external events, and also the delivery of our schools education strategy and the Water Smart Schools programme. The Volunteering Executive will work closely with other colleagues who support RLSS UK’s volunteer-led community presence in the Volunteer and Events Team, as well as the Education Manager, and the Membership Team. As well as recruiting and organising individuals and teams of volunteers, the role will also play a key part in ensuring RLSS UK volunteers feel that their contribution and commitment is appreciated and properly recognised and it is recorded against their individual records on the RLSS UK system. KEY TASKS & RESPONSIBILTIES Volunteering To manage the recruitment, retention, and day-to-day recognition of RLSS UK Volunteers To maintain a robust and safe record of RLSS UK volunteers and their voluntary roles Working with the various directorates to identify and coordinate volunteering opportunities for RLSS UK volunteers To collate and manage William Henry hours in partnership with the Events Executive to recognise the contribution of individual RLSS UK volunteers through our Honours system To coordinate a cohort of RLSS UK Education Volunteers throughout the UK to deliver RLSS UK activity out in the community To assemble and coordinate the creation of teams of volunteer lifeguards for a variety of third-party water-based events To support RLSS UK volunteers and members with accessing and using our member led database To maintain accurate reports of volunteer activities, that can be used to look at the impact of their contribution to the Society’s objectives Manage partnerships with external event organisers to ensure: o Voluntary roles fulfilled by RLSS UK are clear, suitable, safe, and enjoyable o RLSS UK volunteers meet the requirements of external event organisers General To demonstrate and uphold the Society’s values and behavioural standards at all times Ensure compliance with UK GDPR and the Data Protection Act 2018 by complying with internal information governance policies and maintaining up to date documentation as part of RLSS UK’s compliance programme Proactively participate in the Society’s equality, diversity, and inclusion (EDI) initiatives and training, and to promote a culture of respect and inclusion for all staff and external stakeholders This job description is not to be regarded as exclusive or exhaustive. It is intended as an outline indication of areas of activity and responsibility and will be amended in the light of the changing needs of the organisation. PERSON SPECIFICATION Essential Relevant Skills and/or Aptitudes Excellent written and verbal communication skills, particularly when working with volunteers Strong planning and organisation skills and the ability to prioritise tasks Ability to multi-task and manage time effectively Ability to work effectively as part of a team and individually Good attention to detail Confidence using Microsoft Office (including Outlook, Excel, PowerPoint) Desirable Relevant Skills and/or Aptitudes Experience of volunteering or volunteer management would be an advantage Ability to work occasional weekends/evenings to support events Experience with a membership database WHAT RLSS UK CAN OFFER YOU Annual Leave based on 27 days + Bank Holidays + a discretionary day off for your birthday Private Healthcare Plan* Enhanced Society Sick Pay* Eye Care* Employee Assistance Programme Life Assurance Scheme Salary Sacrifice Pension Scheme* Discounts available including high street brands, entertainment, eating out and more Free RLSS UK Membership Free tea and coffee when working from HQ, including access to our wonderful Coffee Machine Free on-site parking when working from HQ Company events and socials *Subject to eligibility criteria YOUR APPLICATION Please send your CV and a Cover Letter outlining why you should join our Membership and Education team Closing Date – 12pm, Thursday 1st October 2026 Interview Date – Monday 12th October 2026, at our Worcester Head Office (subject to change) Should you wish to discuss the role, any adjustments you may require throughout the recruitment process, or have any questions, please get in touch where a member of the RLSS UK HR Department will be happy to help. RLSS UK are a Disability Confident Committed Employer and an INclusive Worcestershire Leader.

item.title: Creative Designer
item.description: About Starlight Starlight is the national charity for children's play in healthcare. We believe that healthcare should be a more humane and child-centred experience for every child. We work across the UK to champion the importance of play during treatment, care and recovery, supporting children, parents and carers, and healthcare professionals. Play is integral to children's wellbeing. It can help children experience greater agency, autonomy and control during healthcare, express thoughts and feelings, build resilience and make healthcare settings feel more welcoming and safe. But play is still too often overlooked or treated as an optional extra within children's healthcare. Our ambition is to end preventable trauma in children's healthcare. Our new strategy is taking Starlight into an important next phase. We want to build on the expertise, evidence, influence, partnerships and brand positioning we have developed over recent years and use them to create greater impact for children and families. That means becoming a stronger voice for change: increasing understanding of children's experiences of healthcare, influencing the systems and people who shape children's healthcare, strengthening our relationships with supporters and partners, and communicating with greater clarity, consistency and impact. Our brand and communications have an increasingly important and broad role to play. We need to tell powerful stories, challenge assumptions, engage people emotionally and intellectually, and make it clear why children's healthcare needs to change. This is an exciting time to join Starlight and help shape how our purpose, personality and ambition are experienced by the people who matter most. Our Strategy and the Creative Designer Our ambition is to influence how children's healthcare is understood and experienced. To do that successfully, we need communications and creative work that is distinctive, compelling and purposeful. We need to communicate with different audiences in ways that help them feel, understand and ultimately do something differently. As our Creative Designer, you will play an important role in making that happen. Working as part of the Influence, Insight & Communications team and reporting to the Communications & Brand Manager, you will develop ideas and produce high-quality work across campaigns, fundraising, influencing, digital communications, events and organisational communications. You will also help to evolve how Starlight looks, feels and expresses itself, ensuring that our creative work is distinctive, consistent and recognisably Starlight. You will work closely with our Digital Content Creator, who leads the production of channel-native video and social content. You will contribute visual concepts, campaign identities, graphics, storyboards and brand treatments to help this content feel coherent, distinctive and recognisably Starlight. You will help Starlight make effective use of new creative technologies, including AI, where they can improve efficiency, enable experimentation or extend our creative capability. We want to use technology to help us work smarter and create more, without compromising creative judgement, authenticity or quality. You will work with colleagues across Starlight and, where appropriate, with external creative specialists to ensure our communications are engaging, accessible, authentic and effective.
item.dc:creator: Starlight Children's Foundation

item.title: IT Coordinator
