A key priority will be leading Hft’s transition to PROACT-SCIPr-UK, ensuring this is embedded within our wider PBS and restrictive practice reduction approach and translates into meaningful improvements in frontline practice and the quality of life of the people we support. You’ll lead our PBS / Practice Team, provide expert oversight of complex situations and act as a trusted professional adviser to senior leaders on practice quality, risk, outcomes and improvement. What you’ll be doing You’ll: Develop and lead an organisation-wide Practice Strategy and Practice Standards Framework. Provide professional leadership, advice and constructive challenge to senior and operational leaders. Lead and develop the PBS / Practice Team and build sustainable specialist capability. Lead the implementation of PROACT-SCIPr-UK across the organisation. Drive our restrictive practice reduction strategy, using data and evidence to identify opportunities for improvement. Provide specialist leadership around complex and high-risk practice situations. Develop workforce capability through training, coaching, observation, modelling and reflective practice. Embed rights-based, person-centred and trauma-informed approaches across Hft. Lead or contribute to practice-related policies and professional guidance. Provide senior leadership with clear evidence of practice quality, risk, outcomes and improvement. What you’ll bring We’re looking for someone with: Significant senior experience within learning disability and/or autism services. Strong professional expertise in Positive Behaviour Support. Significant knowledge and practical experience of PROACT-SCIPr-UK, with the ability to lead organisational implementation. Experience of restrictive practice reduction and least restrictive approaches. Experience leading specialist practice or PBS teams. A strong track record of developing practice standards, frameworks and guidance. Experience building workforce capability through coaching, training and practice leadership. Strong knowledge of safeguarding, Mental Capacity Act principles and relevant health and social care requirements. The confidence to influence, advise and constructively challenge senior leaders. A relevant professional qualification and evidence of continued specialist development. A postgraduate qualification in PBS, Applied Behaviour Analysis, Psychology or a related discipline, relevant professional registration and PROACT-SCIPr-UK instructor or advanced implementation experience would be desirable. What success looks like Success in this role will mean better outcomes and quality of life for the people we support. You’ll help ensure that PBS is embedded in everyday practice, restrictive practices are reduced wherever safely possible, PROACT-SCIPr-UK is successfully implemented, and managers and frontline teams have the confidence and capability to deliver consistently excellent, rights-based support. Working arrangements This is a national hybrid role with regular travel to Hft services and other locations across the organisation. Why Hft? At Hft, our mission is simple: the best life possible. We believe people with learning disabilities should be able to live within their communities, with all the choice and support they need to live the best life possible. This is an exciting opportunity to influence practice at a national level and make a genuine difference to the lives of the people we support. Recruitment process Applications close on 11 October 2026. Interviews will take place on 27 October 2026 and will be held via Microsoft Teams.

item.title: Senior Hunger, Nutrition & Livelihoods Advocacy Advisor
item.description: Closing Date: 27 September 2026 Ref 7405 Save the Children UK is looking for an experienced policy and advocacy professional to join our Hunger, Nutrition & Livelihoods team as a Senior Hunger, Nutrition & Livelihoods Advocacy Advisor on a maternity cover basis, working three days per week. This is a unique opportunity to lead and shape Save the Children's global advocacy on child wasting and malnutrition, helping to drive progress on one of the most critical challenges facing children worldwide. You will strengthen our global leadership and visibility, influence policy and decision-makers, and build strategic relationships with partners including government, multilateral organisations, donors and civil society. You will also coordinate and influence key coalition activities, represent Save the Children in high-profile external forums and help strengthen policy and advocacy capability across the team. This role would suit someone with strong knowledge of the global nutrition policy landscape, particularly child wasting, together with experience of leading coalitions, building partnerships and delivering effective influencing strategies. About Us Save the Children UK believes every child deserves a future. In the UK and around the world, we work every day to give children a healthy start in life, the opportunity to learn and protection from harm. When crisis strikes, and children are most vulnerable, we are always among the first to respond and the last to leave. We ensure children's unique needs are met and their voices are heard. We deliver lasting results for millions of children, including those hardest to reach. About the Team Working as part of the Global Impact group, our Global Outcomes function catalyses positive change for children by driving influencing agendas and bringing knowledge, evidence, analysis and expertise to our partnerships, programmes and advocacy work. The Hunger, Nutrition & Livelihoods Team works as part of the Global Save the Children movement and the wider sector to drive long lasting systems changes at the global and country levels. We are committed to promoting inclusive and equitable solutions, amplifying the voices of children most affected by inequality, and prioritising locally led efforts for lasting change. About the role As Senior Hunger, Nutrition and Livelihoods Advocacy Advisor, you will provide global leadership in hunger, nutrition and livelihoods policy and advocacy, with a particular focus on child wasting and malnutritionto shape and drive shared advocacy and impact agendas across Save the Children and the wider sector. You will develop and deliver high-quality policy and influencing strategies, fostering innovation and inclusivity and contributing to systemic change. In this role, you will build strategic relationships with key decision-makers, lead capacity strengthening for colleagues and partners, and champion equality, inclusion and the shifting power agenda. Additionally, you will contribute to multi-disciplinary teams and drive thought leadership. In this role, you will: Provide global leadership in hunger, nutrition and livelihoods policy and advocacy, with a particular focus on child wasting and malnutrition, to shape and drive shared influencing and impact agendas within the Save the Children movement and the wider sector, maintaining up-to-date expertise and monitoring relevant external trends. Set and deliver outcome goals for your area of specialism by working collaboratively to implement strategies that contribute to systemic change, incorporating power analysis, policy, advocacy, research, partnerships and programme portfolios as relevant. Develop and deliver very high-quality policy, research and advocacy outputs with minimal supervision, ensuring inclusivity and excellence in implementation. Contribute to a strong learning culture through leading or supporting research, evaluation, innovation and knowledge sharing. Provide thought leadership in hunger, nutrition and livelihoods, particularly child wasting and malnutrition, including engaging in external debate and producing technical guidance, research briefs and analytical outputs to identify barriers and pragmatic but ambitious solutions for transformative change. Facilitate capacity strengthening through mentoring, coaching and training, providing formal and informal support to colleagues and partners to build expertise and effectiveness. Build and maintain strategic relationships with key high-level decision-makers and opinion leaders, including senior civil servants, academics, leaders in international organisations and civil society partners, to amplify the impact of our advocacy and programmes. Lead and coordinate coalition engagement and partnership working to advance shared advocacy objectives and strengthen collective impact on child wasting and malnutrition. Coordinate and contribute to high-level events, meetings and influencing opportunities, including preparing briefings and materials for senior leaders and representing Save the Children in external forums. Champion and role model equality, inclusion and impact across Save the Children's work and the broader sector, while actively shifting power and resources closer to the communities and children served. Identify and lead strategic partnerships with funders and other organisations in collaboration with partnership colleagues to advance child rights and increase impact. About you To be successful, it is important that you have/are: A strong track-record in designing and implementing successful influencing strategies with minimal supervision, drawing on analytical skills to identify political and other barriers to change and prioritise from a range of possible objectives and approaches. High-level expertise in the global international development and child rights policy landscape and institutions, coupled with deep expertise in hunger, nutrition and livelihoods policy and advocacy, including strong knowledge of the nutrition policy landscape and child wasting. A strong track-record in policy analysis and development, with the ability to draw on different sources of information and ideas from partners and children to generate relevant policy positions and solutions that resonate with target audiences. Experience working in and leading coalitions, partnerships and collaborative initiatives, bringing together diverse stakeholders to drive shared advocacy objectives and impact. Proven ability to build external relationships and partnerships, and to influence decision-makers and policy specialists, including politicians, donors, multilateral organisations, civil society actors and other key stakeholders globally. Very strong oral and written communication skills, with the ability to tailor messaging to resonate with and influence different audiences. The ability to network and represent Save the Children externally, including facilitating and speaking at high-level events and meetings, engaging with senior stakeholders and acting as a credible organisational representative. Experience coordinating or contributing to high-level events and influencing opportunities, including producing briefings and materials for senior leadership. Strong interpersonal skills, emotional intelligence and authenticity that enable effective communication and relationship-building with a wide range of audiences. Strong convening skills, creating synergy, fostering collaboration and bringing together diverse perspectives to achieve common goals. Experience supporting capacity strengthening through mentoring, coaching, training or knowledge-sharing activities. What we offer you We promote flexibility, inclusion, collaboration, and wellbeing both at work and beyond, and offer a wide range of benefits designed to reward your hard work and inspire you to help improve the lives of children every day. Some of the benefits you can expect include: Generous Annual Leave – Starting at 27 days per year (pro rata for part-time employees) increasing with service up to 32 days, plus public holidays and our annual 'Save the Children Day'. Family Leave – Up to 39 weeks of maternity/adoption pay (including up to 21 weeks full pay) and paternity/adoption leave of 10 weeks full pay (plus statutory entitlement). Special Leave – Up to 10 days paid leave per year (pro rata) for urgent or exceptional personal circumstances, without using annual leave. Volunteer Leave – Up to 3 days paid leave per year to support volunteering and give back. Pension & Life Assurance – Helping you plan for the future with up to 7% employer pension contributions. Employee Discounts – Access thousands of deals across groceries, retail, tech, travel, fitness, and more. Health & Wellbeing Support – Including access to a 24/7 Virtual GP and Employee Assistance Programme and Counselling, eye care support, and seasonal flu vaccinations. Please note: To avoid disappointment, you are advised to submit your application as soon as possible as we reserve the right to close the vacancy early if a high volume of applications are received. This is to ensure that we can manage application levels whilst maintaining a positive candidate experience. Unfortunately once a vacancy has closed, we are unable to consider further applications. Location & Ways of Working: The majority of our roles can be performed remotely in the UK, but at times you will be required to come to your contracted office (usually between 2–4 days per month, depending on the needs of your role, team, or service). For many roles, this is likely to be the minimum required to deliver impact. This will be discussed and agreed with your manager / team and we encourage candidates to discuss our ways of working in more detail at interview stage. Please note: travel costs to your contracted office will be at your own expense. Flexible Working - We are happy to discuss flexible working options at interview . Commitment to Diversity & Inclusion: Save the Children

item.title: Regional Fundraising Manager
item.description: Camphill Village Trust is a social care provider and charity rooted in nature and community, supporting adults with learning disabilities, autism, and mental health support needs to live healthier, more active and independent lives. For over 70 years we have pioneered a different kind of care – shaped by place, purpose, and the natural world. We believe care should do more than meet needs, it should create opportunity, belonging, and purpose. By rooting our support in meaningful work, relationships, and the natural environment, we help people to build skills, confidence, and independence. Do you want to make a difference and help us achieve our vision? The Regional Fundraising Manager (National Programme Development) will lead the creation, development and delivery of Camphill Village Trust’s community fundraising programme. You will establish community fundraising as a sustainable and growing income stream across the trust by creating a framework that can be scaled across Camphill Village Trust nationally. This role combines strategic planning, relationship building, and programme development but also encompasses hands-on delivery across our northern communities. You will play a key role in raising awareness of Camphill Village Trust, strengthening community connections and creating opportunities for supporters to help more people with learning disabilities and autism live extraordinary lives. Main Responsibilities: Create and deliver a community fundraising strategy that lays the foundations for long-term national growth. Develop and manage the community fundraising budget and forecasting processes. Design and launch engaging fundraising products including DIY fundraising, challenge events, in-house events, schools, community groups and local organisations. Create fundraising resources, toolkits and supporter materials that make it easy for people to get involved. Establish KPIs, reporting frameworks and performance measures to track success and inform future growth. Build strong relationships with supporters, volunteers, schools, community groups and local businesses. Identify regional corporate fundraising opportunities and partnerships and work with the Philanthropy Manager to develop these relationships. Work closely with Marketing and Communications colleagues to raise awareness of fundraising opportunities and campaigns. Act as a key link between fundraising and operational teams across Camphill Village Trust. Spend time within communities, building relationships with people we support, staff and families. Identify compelling fundraising stories and case studies. Support the involvement of people we support in fundraising activities where appropriate. Support fundraising volunteers and ambassadors. Line manage and develop the Regional Fundraising team – Initially 1 x Regional Fundraising Officer (Central/South) with a view to future expansion. Work collaboratively with colleagues across Supporter Care, Individual Giving, Philanthropy, Legacy and In-Memory fundraising. Ensure fundraising activity is delivered in line with relevant regulations, policies and best practice. Knowledge & Experience: Essential : At least three years' experience in community fundraising, supporter engagement or a related fundraising role. Experience developing and delivering fundraising campaigns, activities or products. Previous experience of developing fundraising strategy. Ability to build relationships with supporters, volunteers, community groups and local organisations. Experience using CRM systems and fundraising data. Experience recruiting, managing and developing staff. Experience setting KPIs, monitoring performance and reporting outcomes. Strong written and verbal communication skills. Ability to work collaboratively across teams and departments. Full UK driving licence and access to your own vehicle. Personal Attributes & Key Competencies: Strategic and commercially aware Entrepreneurial and comfortable with ambiguity Outstanding relationship builder and networker Creative and innovative thinker Strong project and programme management skills Confident communicator and influencer Collaborative and supportive leader Organised and able to manage multiple priorities Data-informed and results focused Resilient, adaptable and self-motivated Location & Travel: Hybrid. This is a hybrid role with a minimum of two days per week based within Camphill Village Trust communities. We are looking for someone who enjoys being out in the community. This is not a desk-based fundraising role. You will spend significant time building relationships, identifying opportunities, meeting supporters and representing Camphill Village Trust across the region. The successful candidate should live within reasonable commuting distance of our three communities in the north-east (based in North Yorkshire and Middlesbrough). Regular travel across the region and occasional travel to other Trust communities will be required, along with some overnight stays, evening and weekend work. Annual Leave and Benefits: 28 days paid annual leave plus statutory bank holidays The option to buy and sell annual leave Company sick pay after one month starting at 4 weeks and increasing to 12 weeks with service Life Cover for all employees Pension scheme Employee Assistance Program Blue Light Card

item.title: Corporate Partnerships Manager
item.description: Your Mission CALM’s Corporate Partnerships Team is scaling up and hunting for an ambitious and experienced Corporate Partnerships Manager who is motivated by results and a natural-born relationship builder. The role will be responsible for managing, growing and extending a portfolio of existing corporate partnerships, and, where appropriate, may be asked to support with new business by attending meetings, pitches and staff votes on an ad hoc basis. In this dynamic role, you will also take the reins of a brand-new, high-profile strategic partnership worth £250k+ per annum with a household-name brand, leading its strategic growth and turning ambitious plans into real-world impact. Because this nationwide partnership requires regular travel to various sites to deliver that impact face-to-face, you will need a full UK driving license and access to your own car. You will work hand-in-hand with our incredible Services team to ensure this flagship partnership directly supports, engages, and uplifts employees. Your profile Responsibilities Provide excellent relationship management to a portfolio of corporate partners, including, but not limited to, producing account management plans, setting partnership objectives, supporting fundraising initiatives and employee engagement, thereby significantly contributing to the corporate fundraising budget and strategy. Ensure partnership milestones and fundraising targets are monitored, met, reported on and celebrated with key internal and external stakeholders. Confidently represent CALM at key meetings and events, where public speaking and delivering presentations may be required. Work closely with the Services team to create bespoke support products for key corporate partner, as needed Work closely with the Services, Data and MarComms teams to build engaging, accurate and tailored impact reports for partners that encourage long-term support. Devise sustainable exit strategies for partners that leave behind a lasting legacy for CALM. Build strong working relationships and collaborate closely with colleagues across CALM to complement partnership activity. Support the Corporate Partnerships team as a whole to be more productive and efficient by identifying and making improvements to working practices and processes. Support the corporate partnerships team, where necessary, in securing new partnerships. This may involve (but not limited to) providing quotes or case studies, attending meetings or pitches, and canvassing for staff votes. Adhere to GDPR, fundraising regulator legislation and guidelines. Understand and adhere to the CALM values. Competencies A full UK driving license and access to your own car. A demonstrable track record of delivering financial results against agreed targets and timescales. Excellent relationship management skills, with ability to engage effectively with a range of audiences both internal and external. Ability to direct client facing meetings, getting to the core of what motivates a partner to take action, and present a case for support convincingly. Confidence in managing partner expectations and having difficult conversations where necessary, keeping the charity’s best interests at heart. Excellent verbal and written communication skills, with a keen eye for detail and the ability to develop tailored and compelling presentations, reports and communications to a high standard. Proven ability to prioritise and manage a varied workload, taking initiative and often working to conflicting deadlines. Ability to collaborate and positively contribute to team culture. Willingness to work hard and attend, where necessary, events outside of office hours. Passion for the cause and delivering CALM’s mission. Experience 5-7 years experience of successfully managing multi-layered, five or six figure corporate partnerships, ideally within the third sector - from the onboarding of a partnership to delivering exit strategies. Experience of growing and extending partnerships in line with organisational objectives. Experience of working in a fast paced environment with conflicting priorities and deadlines. Why work for us? Reports to: Senior Corporate Partnerships Manager Contract: Benefits: Nine day fortnight & unlimited annual leave, Healthcare cash plan, 6% pension contribution, therapeutic services (after completion of probation), hybrid working. Based: London Waterloo twice a week (Wednesdays and Thursdays) / Remote Working (Mon, Tues & Fri), 9.30am - 5.30pm. Salary: £38-42k A work environment that values creativity, personal growth and collaboration. About us Hi. We’re Campaign Against Living Miserably, or CALM to our mates. We’re a suicide prevention charity, on a mission to help people end their misery, not their lives. We run stigma-smashing campaigns, offer loads of digital tools and resources, and run a life-saving helpline - all designed to help people find hope and way forward. We are - united against suicide. We’re Campaign Against Living Miserably (CALM), and we’re united against suicide. We’re a suicide prevention charity, on a mission to help people end their misery, not their lives. We run stigma-smashing campaigns, offer loads of digital tools and resources, and run a life-saving helpline - all designed to help people find hope and a way forward. We are - united against suicide. Don't meet every requirement? We’re still interested. Research shows that people from marginalised groups – including women, LGBTQ+ people, people from global majority backgrounds, disabled people, and those from lower socioeconomic backgrounds – are less likely to apply for a role unless they meet the full criteria. At CALM, we know that skills and potential come in many forms, and that diverse perspectives and lived experience of mental health or suicide can be just as valuable as formal qualifications. If you're passionate about our mission but your experience doesn't tick every box, we'd still love to hear from you. You could be exactly who we're looking for. Safeguarding We are committed to safeguarding children and adults at risk in both physical and digital environments. We expect all staff and volunteers to share this commitment and adhere to our safeguarding policies. Any appointment is subject to satisfactory references and a DBS check at the appropriate level. Successful candidates will be required to complete mandatory safeguarding training.

item.title: Programme Manager
item.description: The Opportunity This is an opportunity to take a key management role within Happy Healthy You, a community-rooted organisation delivering culturally grounded health and wellbeing activity across Bradford, while playing a significant role in the delivery of the five-year Bradford Health Inequities Programme (Bhip). You will work across HHU’s established programmes and community activity while helping to develop and strengthen the organisation as it grows. Alongside this, you will have a significant role in Bhip, supporting an ambitious programme that brings together communities, the VCSE sector and health and care systems to address health inequities driven by structural racism and discrimination. The role offers a distinctive opportunity to connect strong community-based delivery with wider change, helping ensure that what is learned through HHU’s trusted relationships and Bhip’s work leads to better practice, stronger services, and demonstrable outcomes for communities. You will join at a crucial point in the development of both HHU and Bhip, with genuine scope to shape how programmes are delivered, developed, evaluated, and improved as the work grows. About you / The Role You will be an experienced and capable programme manager with a strong track record of managing community-based programmes, activities, services, and teams, with the ability to design, develop and implement plans and projects that achieve effective delivery and measurable outcomes. You will understand the realities of delivering culturally grounded health and wellbeing activity alongside Global Majority communities and be committed to addressing health inequities, structural racism, and discrimination. You will be equally comfortable supporting the Bhip Programme Lead, HHU’s CEO and senior management with organisational priorities, managing staff and resources, and working alongside community teams to ensure delivery is well coordinated, responsive and of a consistently high standard. You will have a strong focus on evaluation, ensuring HHU and the Bhip programme can demonstrate the outcomes, impact, and value of its work. As a key member of the Bhip team, you will lead the operational management of HHU’s contribution, ensuring its community engagement, co-design, Insight to Action and related activity is effectively planned, delivered, monitored, evaluated, and continuously improved. You will understand how HHU’s existing trusted community activity provides an important route through which communities can engage with and shape Bhip’s aims and work. HHU’s established community delivery footprint will provide a key route for Bhip’s structural literacy, listening, story capture and co-design work, enabling community insight and stories to be translated into action and system change. You will bring strong people management, organisation, and judgement, with the ability to manage competing priorities, solve problems and maintain effective relationships across HHU, Bhip, communities and partner organisations

item.title: Supported Housing - Core Coordinator (MOUP)
item.description: Supported Housing - Core Coordinator (MOUP) Salford, Manchester £29,471.62 per annum Permanent, Full Time (35 hours per week) Closing date: 29th September 2026 Interview date: 5th October 2026 Interview location: Oaklands House, Suite 2, Second Floor, Oaklands House, 34 Washway Road, Sale, M33 6FS MOUP Hours: 35 hours per week, with services operating between 7:45am and 8:10pm, Monday to Sunday worked on a shift rota including 2 on 2 off weekends and shifts across the week. Shifts are either 7:45am to 4:45pm (Early), 10:00am to 6:00pm (Flexi) or 11:10am to 8:10pm (Late). Our organisation is all about people – the people who live in our homes, the communities we serve, and those we work with. So, it’s no surprise that we recruit for attitude and behaviour which are central to us building relationships and delivering great experiences for these people. We employ colleagues who are passionate about making a difference who will take responsibility to get things done. As a not-for-profit housing association, providing affordable homes and services to more than 20,000 people across Greater Manchester. We have a strong social purpose and make it our mission to enable people to live well in their home and community. This role will help us achieve our ambition by working as part of a team within supported housing and outreach services in Greater Manchester, providing high-quality, personalised housing-related support and enablement support to young adult clients. In this role, you will be responsible for Using coaching and strengths-based approaches to enable clients to develop emotional resilience, overcome barriers, promote independent living and take control of their lives. Taking a lead on liaising with external agencies and raising safeguarding concerns in an appropriate and timely manner. Completing Positive Behaviour Plans, Support Plans, Essential Profiles and Risk Assessments. Managing a caseload of clients, with workloads determined by client needs and service demand. Supporting the Project Manager to ensure all aspects of housing management, housing-related support and enablement support are delivered to a high standard. Working as part of a supported housing team to provide high-quality personalised support to young adults with ADHD and ASD, alongside clients with substance misuse support needs. Working with young people and their extended families. Delivering individualised support packages. We need people who have Knowledge of relevant legislation, policy and developments relating to vulnerable adults, including people with ADHD, ASD and substance misuse issues. Knowledge of issues affecting clients, including behaviour management, mental health, leaving care and neurodiversity. Understanding of safeguarding, health and safety procedures, risk management and tenancy management. Experience of working within a supported housing environment or relevant social care setting. Experience of supporting people with complex support needs. Experience of working with statutory agencies and partner organisations. Strong communication, recording, report-writing and IT skills. The ability to build positive working relationships with clients, families, colleagues and partner agencies. The ability to work independently, use initiative and prioritise a demanding workload. It would be advantageous if you have: Experience of working within supported housing services. Knowledge of legislation and best practice relating to housing support, safeguarding, ADHD, ASD, learning disabilities and substance misuse. A qualification in Health and Social Care or a related subject. Please note that an Enhanced DBS check is required for this role and you must be able to work shifts, including evenings, weekends and bank holidays where required. The successful candidate will be flexible, reliable, resilient, professional and passionate about making a positive difference to the lives of vulnerable adults and young people. We want to hear from you! You may use AI tools to support your application, but any content submitted must accurately reflect your own skills, experience, qualifications and suitability for the role. During the recruitment process, you may be asked to discuss and provide evidence of the information contained within your application. Everyone’s welcome here. Our culture is inclusive, and we are committed to increasing diversity. We enable everyone to be themselves at work, so that they feel at home with us. And we trust and support people to do their best, in a role that is fulfilling and rewarding because we know that this helps us to deliver better outcomes for our customers and our colleagues. If you want to be part of our team and help us make a difference, we’d love to hear from you. # SupportWorker #YouthWorker #ProjectWorker #HousingSupportJobs #SupportedHousing #housingjobs #recruiting #Manchesterjobs

item.title: Community Wellbeing Coordinator – Housing Advocacy
item.description: Housing is one of the biggest factors affecting people's health and wellbeing. We are looking for two Community Wellbeing Coordinators to join our Community Connect Social Prescribing Service, with a specific focus on housing advocacy and support. This is an exciting opportunity to work at the intersection of health, housing and community support, helping residents navigate complex systems, understand their options and access the support they need. You will support residents whose wellbeing is affected by issues such as: Housing insecurity Risk of homelessness Overcrowding Disrepair Temporary accommodation Digital exclusion Difficulties understanding housing processes and evidence requirements The role is about practical support, advocacy and navigation. You will work alongside residents to understand their circumstances, explore options, gather evidence, complete applications where appropriate and connect them with relevant services. We're looking for someone who: Has experience supporting people in health, social care, housing, advice, voluntary sector or community settings. Can build trusting relationships with residents facing difficult circumstances. Understands how housing and other wider determinants impact health and wellbeing. Is confident working with multiple agencies and coordinating support. Can manage expectations sensitively whilst maintaining hope and motivation. Has strong organisational and case management skills. Understands safeguarding and person-centred practice If you're passionate about reducing inequalities, empowering residents and finding practical solutions to complex challenges, we'd love to hear from you. Please note, a member of the housing team will be on the interview panel therefore CV’s & supporting statements will be shared with them. Interviews are likely to be held Friday 23rd October 2026. Why Work for Us: • Hybrid working • Additional Birthday Day off • Flexitime and TOIL • Pension employer contribution 6% • Two volunteering days (pro rata) • 25 days annual leave plus bank holidays (pro rata) • Access to the Blue Light Card • Ongoing training and professional development opportunities • A positive, inclusive team culture where your ideas are valued • Enhanced maternity/paternity pay • Employee Assistance Programme

item.title: Finance Manager
item.description: Job description Every year, Seaview Project works alongside over 1,200 people across Hastings and St Leonards to build stability out of complexity. We need a Finance Manager who wants their expertise to make that possible. Role details Responsible to: Chief Officer and Treasurer Salary: £13,497 per annum Hours: 12 hours per week (Monday–Friday, hours negotiable) Holidays: 25 days per year plus statutory days, pro rata Pension: NEST Pension Plan, with a 4% contribution from Seaview About us Seaview Project has been delivering practical services for complex lives since 1985, supporting people across Hastings and St Leonards who are facing homelessness, poverty and related challenges, helping them build on their strengths and move towards greater stability and independence. About the role We're looking for an experienced Finance Manager to take responsibility for Seaview's overall financial management, ensuring our transactions, procedures and records meet internal, charity and legal requirements. You'll work closely with our Service Managers, Honorary Treasurer and Board of Trustees on financial forecasting, business planning and grant applications, and you'll lead the development of budgeting and finance awareness across the organisation. Key responsibilities Advise trustees on financial policy and prepare annual budgets, costings and appraisals Monitor income and expenditure against budget and produce regular management reports Liaise with bankers and investment managers and manage cash flow Oversee invoicing, fee and grant claims, and Gift Aid submissions Manage payroll, PAYE, NI and pension administration Maintain fixed asset and balance code schedules Review financial systems to minimise the risk of error or fraud and ensure statutory compliance Prepare draft statutory accounts in line with the Charities SORP, liaising with our Independent Examiner or auditor Provide financial information to support contracts and funding applications Line manage and support our Finance Officer, including supervision and appraisals Act as Charity Commission correspondent and company secretary for compliance purposes What we're looking for Essential: Proven experience of budget setting and budget management Proven experience producing statutory accounts for charities to a high standard A relevant accountancy qualification, or significant experience in management, finance or the voluntary sector A genuine understanding of, and commitment to, the culture and ethos in which Seaview operates Proven ability to lead a team to achieve outcomes, targets and deadlines High levels of motivation and a commitment to improving service provision for people with complex needs Excellent verbal and written communication skills with people who use our services, professionals and colleagues Self-motivated, well organised, and flexible in approach Desirable: Experience working in a small charity, in any sector Experience managing social housing rental accounts Experience of homelessness — lived, voluntary, professional or otherwise Posted on: 16 September 2026 Closing date: 07 October 2026 at 10:55 Tags: Finance, Governance / Management

item.title: Head of Data & Digital (Fixed Term)
item.description: The National Biodiversity Network Trust is the UK charity dedicated to making biodiversity data accessible and useful. We co-ordinate the National Biodiversity Network, develop the NBN Atlas, support iNaturalistUK and are developing the NBN Record Manager. Our work connects biological recording, digital infrastructure and better decisions for nature across the UK. Our vision is Nature thriving everywhere, in all its diversity. Our mission is Making data work for nature. We are looking for an experienced leader to undertake a newly-created Head of Data & Digital role reporting to the Chief Executive Officer on a full-time fixed-term contract of 24 months. Purpose of Job Lead the NBN Trust’s data and digital function, providing strategic and functional leadership across the NBN Atlas, related digital products and services, and the Trust’s wider data and digital portfolio. Line manages the Trust’s data and technical team managers, ensuring clear priorities, strong performance, proportionate governance, and effective delivery across business as usual, funded projects, and strategic development. Ensure the Trust’s data and digital work is led in a way that is inclusive, accessible, and supportive of a diverse range of staff, partners, and users. Deliver the Trust’s 2-year National Lottery Heritage Fund’s organisational sustainability project, “Building a Sustainable Future for the UK’s Biodiversity Data Heritage”, including the development and testing of value-added data and digital services, hosted products, and support offers that strengthen financial resilience without compromising the Trust’s public good role. Support the strategic direction, stewardship, and future sustainability of the NBN Atlas, related digital products and services, and the Trust’s wider technical delivery, ensuring that risks, opportunities, and investment choices are well managed. Play an active role in the NBN Trust’s Executive Team, contributing to organisational planning, funding development, cross Trust collaboration, and external engagement where this supports delivery and the Trust’s wider strategic objectives. The role provides strategic and functional leadership across the Trust’s data and digital work, working closely with the Principal Software Engineer as the Trust’s senior software engineering lead. Main Responsibilities Strategic Leadership and Function Management · Lead the Trust’s data and digital function, aligning work with organisational priorities, the NBN Atlas strategy, and the wider Operating Plan. · Provide strategic advice to the CEO and senior colleagues on delivery priorities, service development, digital risk, technical resilience, and future investment needs. · Translate complex technical, delivery, and service development issues into clear options, trade-offs, and recommendations for the CEO, Executive Team, Board, and relevant committees. · Lead, line manage, and develop the Trust’s data and technical managers, and relevant technical project staff, ensuring clear objectives, strong management practice, accountability, wellbeing support, and effective performance management. · Build leadership capacity within the function, supporting managers to develop their teams, handle performance issues well, and contribute positively to the Trust’s culture and ways of working. · Assess capacity, sequencing, and resource pressures across the data and digital portfolio, working with team managers to identify priorities, trade-offs, and resourcing needs and advise the CEO accordingly. · Work across the Trust to improve prioritisation, sequencing, decision making, and resource allocation across data and digital activity. · Champion inclusive leadership and equality, diversity and inclusion in team management, service design, recruitment, and ways of working, helping ensure the Trust’s data and digital function is accessible, supportive, and well-led. Data Infrastructure, Services, and Innovation · Provide strategic leadership for the stewardship, prioritisation, development, and continuous improvement of the NBN Atlas and related data and digital products and services, working with the relevant data, technical, and programme leads. · Ensure data and digital activity support the long-term accessibility, usability, quality, and public value of biodiversity records and related digital services. · Lead diagnostic work, market testing, and service development to identify viable value-added data and digital offers, working with relevant data, technical, programme, and commercial colleagues to shape propositions. · Oversee the selection, development, and testing of pilot services, hosted products, training, or support offers, working with the relevant delivery leads and refining propositions in light of evidence, demand, legal advice, licensing constraints, and delivery capacity. Governance, Risk and Project Delivery · Lead delivery of the organisational resilience project within agreed scope, time, and budget, with support from colleagues and external consultants as required. · Ensure major data and digital programmes have proportionate project governance, reporting, stakeholder, and advisory arrangements in place, working with relevant programme and project leads and identifying additional project support where required. · Commission and manage consultants and contractors, ensuring briefs are clear, outputs are practical, and learning is embedded in delivery, working with relevant technical or data leads where specialist assessment or oversight is required. · Act as the senior staff lead for the Data and Technology Committee, working in partnership with its Trustee Chair and relevant data and technical leads to support effective oversight of the Trust’s data and digital infrastructure, strategic development, risk, and associated governance. · Oversee function-level risks relating to data and digital resilience, data governance, licensing, delivery capacity, and service sustainability, working with the relevant technical and data leads to ensure specialist risks are identified, managed, and escalated appropriately. · Balance governance, assurance, and innovation so that data and digital systems support delivery, resilience, and public value without creating unnecessary burden. · Work with finance and programme colleagues to ensure accurate budgeting, reporting, monitoring, and evidence of impact. Partnerships, Income Development and External Engagement · Build and manage relationships with key partners, data providers, heritage and conservation organisations, public bodies, consultancies, funders, and prospective service users. · Help shape and test future income opportunities, including service offers, hosted portals, training, funded programmes, and strategic partnerships. · Develop and support fundable and deliverable future propositions arising from the work, ensuring the Trust is better positioned for long term resilience. · Act as the Trust’s UK Node Manager for GBIF, leading relationships, coordination, and representation linked to the UK Node function, and ensuring this role supports the Trust’s wider strategic, technical, and partnership objectives. · Represent the Trust externally on biodiversity data infrastructure, digital leadership, service development, standards, and innovation, working alongside relevant technical and data leads where specialist expertise is required Trust Wide Contribution · Play an active role in the Executive Team, contributing to organisational planning, business improvement, and wider strategic discussions. · Keep the wider NBN Trust team up to date with, and involved in, relevant data and digital activity as appropriate. · Contribute to Trust wide initiatives, events, business planning, and other activities as needed. · Share ideas, lessons learned, and opportunities openly to improve organisational performance. General Responsibilities Attend any required learning and development opportunities. Collaborate effectively with other departments. Contribute to a respectful and inclusive working environment. Ensure commitment to continuous professional development. Follow organisational policies including Health & Safety, Cybersecurity, IT, Finance, and EDI. The ability to travel occasionally is required, including international travel. Candidates must also be based in and have the right to work in the UK, and be able to work effectively from home. These are the criteria we will be looking for in your application. If you don't meet all of them in full, but can offer something else that would help you excel in the role, we'd still encourage you to apply. Essential Experience and Qualities · Strong leadership experience in data, digital, technical, product, or programme roles, ideally with responsibility for teams, delivery, and strategic planning. · Ability to operate at both strategic and practical levels, moving between organisational leadership, service design, risk management, and delivery oversight. · Experience of commissioning and managing consultants, contractors, or specialist external support to deliver clear and practical outputs. · Experience of developing partnerships, shaping propositions, or securing income through funded programmes, service offers, or strategic collaboration. · Good judgement, with the ability to assess trade-offs, challenge assumptions, and make proportionate decisions in a resource-constrained environment. · Strong communication and relationship management skills, including confidence with senior stakeholders, funders, partners, and technical specialists. · Knowledge of biodiversity data infrastructure, environmental data, heritage data, or closely related fields would be beneficial, but is not essential if the candidate can learn quickly and lead credibly. · Experience of working with Boards, committees, or governance groups, including presenting complex issues clearly and supporting effective decision-making.

item.title: Senior Life Sciences Partnership Lead
item.description: This role We are seeking a commercially minded senior leader to establish and lead a new Life Sciences Partnership Function for the South West Secure Data Environment (SWSDE). Serving more than five million people across six Integrated Care Board areas, the SWSDE enables approved researchers to securely access and analyse health and care data to support research and innovation that benefits patients and populations. This is an opportunity to shape how the South West works with the life sciences sector to develop research, innovation and commercial partnerships. Working across the NHS, academia and industry, you will build and lead a pipeline of partnership opportunities, taking them from initial engagement through to agreed programmes that deliver clear value for partners and the health and care system. You will play a key role in developing the frameworks, commercial models and ways of working needed to support effective collaboration between the NHS, academia and industry, while maintaining high standards of privacy, security, ethics and public trust. As Secure Data Environments continue to evolve across the UK, you will help define how organisations work with life sciences partners to use health data safely and responsibly to support research and innovation. The role forms part of the SWSDE leadership and delivery model and is hosted by Health Innovation South West on behalf of the SWSDE, working closely with Health Innovation West of England and regional NHS and academic partners. Role profile: Key success factors · The Senior Life Sciences Partnership Lead will lead the development and delivery of the Life Sciences Partnership Function for the SWSDE. The postholder will originate, develop and convert high impact partnerships between the SWSDE, NHS organisations and the life science sector that utilise the functionality and capability of the SWSDE safely, ethically and efficiently to deliver benefit for partners and the population of the South West region. · The role will act as a key interface between the SWSDE and external partners, ensuring opportunities for partnership working between the SWSDE and the life science sector are translated into deliverable, governance-ready programmes that create measurable research, innovation and economic benefits. This will include providing NHS organisations involved in the SWSDE to develop effective partnership working with the life science sector, including pricing approaches, contract development and commercial operating models that enable sustainable collaboration with industry partners. · This role reflects emerging functions being developed across other SDEs, Trusted Research Environments (TREs) and regional data innovation ecosystems, where specialist life science sector leadership expertise is required to complement technical, governance and academic routes. · The postholder will develop commercially and operationally viable proposals for consideration through SWSDE governance. The role will not determine access to data. All projects will remain subject to feasibility assessment, information-governance requirements, demonstration of public benefit and independent Data Access Committee approval. Responsibilities 1. Leading strategic partnership development Build trusted relationships with SWSDE partner organisations, including Integrated Care Boards (ICBs) and NHS providers, supporting partners to develop effective partnership working with the life science sector and the SWSDE. 2. Leading partnership pipeline generation Lead the management, and delivery of the partnership pipeline, ensuring effective planning and oversight to deliver agreed partnership pipeline, revenue targets and KPIs. 3. Leading partnership opportunity development and conversion Translate external opportunities with the life science sector into scoped programmes, studies or service offers, working with technical, IG, governance and delivery teams to assess feasibility of proposals and progress opportunities from concept to approval. Support NHS organisations and SWSDE partners to develop and adopt effective and sustainable models of partnership working with the life science sector and the SWSDE, including providing expert advice on contracting mechanisms, commercial frameworks and partnership agreements. Work with SWSDE finance, legal, information governance and operational colleagues to develop robust partnership agreements, contractual documentation and commercial propositions that support scalable and repeatable approaches to partnership delivery. 5. Leading effective governance and assurance Ensure all partnership activity aligns with SafeGUARDs, information governance, ethics and NHS standards, working closely with SWSDE governance and operational leads to maintain public trust and transparency. 6. Leading people and partners in a matrix management structure Person specification Experience we’re looking for · Experience leading partnership working between the NHS and life science sector. · Track record leading commercial growth and business development. · Experience leading commercial negotiation and contract development, contract development and partnership agreement design across complex multi-organisational environments. · Experience operating in environments with complex and rigorous information governance and data sharing requirements. · Understanding of the UK health, innovation and research landscape. Desirable experience required: · Experience leading partnership working with universities and research partners. · Experience working with health and care data or in trusted research data environments, including NHS data policy, SafeGUARDs or data governance frameworks. · Experience working with NHS governance structures and decision making. Abilities and attributes · Strategic Vision – opportunity-focused, creates new customer markets and develops new revenue streams that balance strategic ambition with attention to risk. · Customer Orientation – builds trust, anticipates partner needs, works with agility, delivers value to partners. · Commercial Acumen – skilled in complex negotiations, high levels of financially literacy, focused on sustainable commercial growth. · Execution excellence – translate partnership opportunities into actionable plans that deliver measurable results, with a strong attention to detail. · Leadership & Influence – motivates, provides clear direction and build effective working relationships in a matrix managed, partnership structured operating model. · Communication – translates complexity into clear narrative, compelling storyteller, adapts style to target audiences. Reporting to: Executive Director of Innovation & Commercial Partnerships, Health Innovation South West

item.title: Membership Officer
item.description: Job description We are looking for a part-time Membership Officer, who will be working alongside our existing part-time Membership Officer. Together, you will lead on administrative support of our membership functions. Reporting to our Operations Manager, the post holder will be responsible for the administrative functions that support the smooth running and ongoing success of the organisation around membership. This role will work Tuesdays, Thursdays and Fridays and will work one day a week in our office in Archway, London (Tuesdays). This is an interesting and varied role that acts as a first 'point of contact’ for the people we work with (such as Member Institutions, Registrants and queries from members of the public), as well as managing the administrative aspect of memberships, such as setting up new Registrants on our CRM system. The role also involves longer term project work such as overseeing the CPD audit and improving and growing membership processes. We are looking for a committed and highly motivated individual with previous similar experience who is keen to join our small and friendly team. It’s important to us that the successful candidate will be in post for a substantial period. Occasionally this role would be asked to support at evening committee meetings or on Saturdays. If you think you may have the relevant skills and experience, we look forward to hearing from you. item.title: Head of Community Services
item.description: Head of Community Services £54,961 PA 37.5 hours per week Working days: Predominately Monday-Friday with On Call requirements Benefits 5 weeks’ holiday plus Bank Holidays Pension Scheme, Staff referral scheme (earn extra each time you successfully refer someone), Employee Assistance Programme, including private GP access, Blue Light Card discount scheme, Free DBS check, Free parking and uniform Closing date: Mid-day 9 October Interview date: 19 October Make a genuine difference, every day At Nottinghamshire Hospice, we’re proud to lead the way in delivering compassionate, community-based palliative care for people living with a terminal or life limiting illness across Nottingham and Nottinghamshire. Our values—Compassion, Trust and Ambition—guide everything we do, for the people we support and for each other. About the Role The Head of Community Services is a senior leadership role responsible for the operational, and clinical delivery of Nottinghamshire Hospice’s community-based services. You will ensure the provision of high-quality, safe, and compassionate palliative and end-of-life care, supporting people to live as well as possible in the place they call home. As a key member of the Hospice Leadership Team, you will provide visible and inspiring leadership, driving excellence in care delivery, service performance, and workforce development. This role combines strong operational management with professional clinical leadership, requiring an experienced registered healthcare professional with a sound understanding of palliative and end-of-life care. You will lead and develop our Hospice in Your Home (24-hour service) and Wellbeing Day Services, ensuring they are responsive, sustainable, and patient-centred. The role involves regular travel across Nottinghamshire and participation in the clinical on-call rota (approximately one week in every five weeks). What we’re looking for We are seeking a compassionate and experienced leader to drive excellence in our community palliative care services. You will champion equity, inclusion, diversity and belonging, while fostering a positive, high-performing culture where staff feel supported and empowered. With strong experience in service delivery, you will manage performance, resources, and workforce planning to meet the needs of our patients and families. You will build effective partnerships with healthcare and community stakeholders, helping to improve access and patient pathways. A commitment to quality, governance, and continuous improvement is essential, alongside the ability to lead confidently in complex situations. Above all, you will embody our values of Compassion, Trust, and Ambition, helping us deliver outstanding care and shape the future of hospice services. You don’t need to meet every desirable criteria — we recruit based on values . If you’re compassionate, reliable and eager to learn, we’d love to hear from you. Equity, Diversity, Inclusion and Belonging We want Nottinghamshire Hospice to be a place where everyone feels they belong. We warmly welcome applicants from all backgrounds and value the different perspectives and experiences that help us provide better care. We particularly encourage applications from people who are currently under‑represented in our workforce, including individuals from minoritised ethnic communities, people with disabilities, and men. Registered Charity No: 509759

item.title: Programme Lead – Bradford Health Inequities Programme (Bhip)
item.description: The Opportunity This is an opportunity for an exceptional Programme Leader whose strengths combine strong operational delivery, strategic thinking, partnership development and a sound understanding of health inequities and the factors that drive them. You will thrive on building and leading a new, nationally significant programme, working alongside communities and partners to address structural racism and discrimination, strengthen shared power and translate community insight into meaningful action and community stories into lasting system change. You will lead an evolving programme that generates learning, evidence and evaluation to inform local policy and practice across Bradford District while contributing to the National Lottery Community Fund’s National Collective, helping shape learning and action that extends beyond Bradford. About you/ The Role You will be an experienced, motivational and credible leader with a proven track record of successfully leading complex programmes, partnerships or services that improve health equity and deliver meaningful system change. You will relish an opportunity to establish and lead a new, fast-paced programme from the ground up. You will demonstrate an understanding of REN’s anti-racist purpose, HHU’s community-led approach, and a commitment to addressing structural racism, discrimination and health inequities.You will be equally comfortable working across communities, grassroots and VCSE organisations, stakeholder and partner organisations, multidisciplinary teams and with senior system leaders. You will be able to inspire and develop others, contribute to effective governance and deliver programme management arrangements, confidently managing people, budgets, performance and outputs. You will be motivated by addressing racism and improving health equity and understand the importance of working alongside communities to support shared power, enabling communities to influence services, decision-making, commissioning and wider system change. Importantly, you will be someone who motivates people and brings them together around a shared purpose, builds strong partnerships and a well-supported, effective team, and brings resilience and sound judgement to complex environments. You will be comfortable navigating ambiguity, adapting to emerging learning and opportunities, and maintaining momentum in a programme designed to learn, evolve and influence change.

item.title: Programme Development Manager - Bradford Health Inequities Programme (Bhip)
item.description: About You You will be a highly organised, proactive and values-led programme professional with experience of coordinating and delivering complex programmes, partnerships or community-based work involving multiple organisations, communities and stakeholders. You will be confident turning plans into practical action, coordinating people, workstreams, developing and delivering training, community leadership, networks and system-facing activity, and ensuring commitments are delivered and followed through. You will understand REN’s anti-racist purpose, Happy Healthy You’s work and remit as programme partners and Bhip’s approach to turning lived experience and community insight into action and system change, with experience of working alongside Global Majority communities, VCSE organisations, community leaders and system partners. You will understand the importance of data, evidence and evaluation in demonstrating impact and be committed to embedding consistent use of agreed programme systems and ways of working across REN’s delivery. As a key member of the Bhip team, you will work with the Programme Lead and closely with the HHU Programme Manager to ensure REN and HHU delivery is joined up and complementary, sharing learning, coordinating interdependent activity and working together to contribute to Bhip’s outcomes. You will be a practical, people-focused team player who builds strong working relationships and a positive, collaborative team culture. You will bring resilience, adaptability and strong problem-solving skills, with the confidence to get involved, make things happen and respond constructively as the programme develops and evolves. The Opportunity This is an opportunity to take a hands-on role at the heart of Bhip, helping turn an ambitious five-year programme into practical activity across communities, organisations and systems in Bradford. You will coordinate and deliver a diverse portfolio of REN-led work that will evolve, innovate and create meaningful change, from developing and delivering anti-racism and structural discrimination training, supporting community leaders and mobilising REN’s VCSE network, to strengthening the Health Policy Forum and supporting wider influencing activity. Working alongside the Programme Lead and wider Bhip team, you will help support and build a genuinely joined-up programme, with scope to shape new approaches and contribute learning that helps change how health and care services, organisations and systems respond to structural racism, discrimination and health inequity, locally and nationally.

item.title: Communications Officer (Maternity Cover)
item.description: About Global Canopy Global Canopy is a data-driven not for profit delivering real transparency and accountability for market impacts on nature and people. Our special focus is on ending deforestation – an essential step in achieving urgent global goals on climate, nature and human rights. Our platforms, data and insights are relied upon by Fortune 500 companies, major financial institutions, national and regional governments, and some of the most effective campaigning organisations worldwide. We work globally, with a focus on both forested regions (particularly across Latin America and South East Asia), and major consumer and financial markets (with a focus on Europe, the US, Singapore and China). About Corporate Performance A growing number of companies and financial institutions are seeking to mitigate their impacts on nature. But many have made commitments that are not being met, and others are failing to take any action at all. We hold the most exposed companies and financial institutions to account through our Forest 500 project, by assessing their policies and performance. With our suite of Deforestation-free Finance Guidance and a forthcoming new tool, DEFT Pathway, we provide tools and data for financial institutions and investors to support effective engagement with high-risk companies. We support the finance sector, policy makers and other stakeholders by providing market-leading data on deforestation and ESG metrics through Forest IQ. About the Role This is an exciting opportunity for an individual with experience in communications and/or marketing to become part of an accomplished and proactive team at the heart of the fight against market-driven deforestation and nature loss. The Communications Officer will support the Communications Lead to deliver communications activity across the Corporate Performance programme, with responsibility for the day-to-day delivery and coordination of digital communications, including website content, newsletters, social media, webinars and media monitoring. The role will work closely with programme colleagues, subject-matter experts and the wider Communications team to develop accurate, engaging and audience-focused content, and to ensure communications activity is delivered effectively, consistently and on time. Finally – as we ask of all colleagues – you will contribute to a culture of kindness, collaboration, rigour and accountability in equal measure. You will share our conviction that it is not just what we do that matters in our working life, but how we do it too. Ideally the successful candidate will be available to start in the first week of December. Responsibilities Manage and publish content across Global Canopy’s websites, keeping content accurate, up to date, accessible and aligned with programme and organisational objectives. Coordinate and deliver newsletters and email communications, including drafting, building and sending Mailchimp campaigns, advising on email tactics and best practice, and monitoring campaign performance. Draft, edit and proofread communications content, including website copy, newsletter content, social media copy, webinar materials and other digital communications, working with subject-matter experts to translate technical information into clear and engaging content. Coordinate and support external Communications webinars, including publicity, invitations, communications materials, technical hosting, moderator and housekeeping materials, liaison with speakers and interpreters, and preparation and publication of webinar recordings. Monitor relevant communications, digital and sustainability trends and the external news landscape, identifying opportunities and recommending approaches that could strengthen Global Canopy’s communications. Support social media communications, including drafting copy, creating social share kits and maintaining communications resources, in collaboration with Communications Leads and the Digital Communications Designer. Conduct monthly and quarterly monitoring across media coverage, webinar engagement and Mailchimp analytics – maintaining media records, evaluating coverage and actively contributing as part of the Monitoring, Evaluation and Learning (MEL) working group. Support the management of journalist lists, undertaking research for media outreach, and logging and evaluating media coverage. Maintain communications resources, including relevant website content and image banks, ensuring content is well organised and consistent with Global Canopy’s brand. Work collaboratively across the Communications and programme teams, providing communications support and expertise as required. About You To be successful in this role , these are the things that will matter the most: Strong editorial judgement and a good eye for design and visual presentation Excellent writing, editing and proofreading skills, with the ability to translate complex or technical information into clear, accurate and engaging content tailored for specific audiences Strong organisational and project coordination skills, with the ability to manage multiple deadlines and priorities. Good understanding of digital communications and social media Essential behavioural competencies: Good interpersonal skills, with the ability to build effective working relationships with colleagues across different teams Ability to work independently, take initiative and manage day-to-day communications activity while knowing when to seek advice or approval Excellent attention to detail and accuracy Skills and experience: At least three years’ experience working in a communications, marketing, digital communications or related role or equivalent experience Experience working with technical or complex subject matter and translating it for non-specialist audiences. Experience managing and publishing content through a website content management system and using email marketing platforms such as Mailchimp Experience supporting webinars, online events or other external-facing events Desirable Interest in how data can illuminate stories and change minds Knowledge of the external news and media landscape, especially on sustainability, deforestation and the finance sector Experience and/or interest in working with a global team Knowledge of languages spoken in forest-rich regions (e.g. Brazilian Portuguese, Bahasa Indonesia, Spanish, French) Salary & Benefits Salary : £33,000 full time equivalent. This role sits within Band E on Global Canopy’s remuneration framework. Nature of contract : Full-time, 14-month maternity cover. Our office is in Oxford, with flexible home-working arrangements in place. Attendance at the office would be required once a month at minimum, with additional attendance for Corporate Performance quarterly meetings. Holidays : 36 days (including bank/public holidays) for discretionary use across the annual leave year. Option to purchase up to an additional 5 days or equivalent of one week’s leave. Pension : Employer pension contribution of 8%. Healthcare cashback plan : Covering dental fees, eye-care, wellbeing, physiotherapy, chiropody and much more – for you and any children. Employee Assistance Programme : Which provides free, confidential advice on personal and legal matters. Other : Huge range of discounts and cashback deals at gyms, restaurants, holidays, and much more. How to Apply To apply for the position, please use follow the link below and submit an up-to date CV and a cover letter explaining your interest in and suitability for the role (please no more than one side of A4). The closing date for applications is Tuesday, 29 September at 9am BST . Early application encouraged. We may close applications early if enough suitable candidates are identified. The recruitment process for this position is intended to be as follows: 1. First-round interview of 30 mins (to be held 5-7 Oct) 2. Written assessment to complete in your own time 3. Final interview of 1 hour (to be held 20 & 21 Oct) Applicants are required to disclose if and how they have used AI in their application. Right-to-work in the UK is required for this position. This recruitment process will take place online via video. The entire process is likely to take 4 weeks to complete from the closing date of this advert. Due to the volume of interest, we are unable to provide all applicants with individual feedback.

item.title: Supporter Experience Coordinator
item.description: We offer more than just a career, we offer the opportunity to support our global movement in a dynamic and inclusive environment with a real focus on personal development. As the first point of contact for supporters, the Supporter Experience Coordinator handles enquiries, processes and reconciles donations, and maintains accurate records using our CRM system. Supporting the delivery of supporter communications, materials and platforms, and contributing to a positive supporter experience that reflects the heart of Mary’s Meals is all key to the role. The Supporter Experience Coordinator works side-by-side with colleagues from across the Supporter Experience and Communications directorate ensuring a joined-up approach to all activities, through the integration of strong storytelling, marketing expertise and supporter engagement. Key responsibilities include Act as the first point of contact for donors, supporters, and volunteers across all channels (in person, phone, email, social media) Take donations and thank donors promptly and warmly, meeting response time KPIs. Collate and provide supporter feedback to the Supporter Experience and Communications team to shape help shape and deliver supporter communications and marketing across all channels, leading to income growth and greater supporter retention. Maintain accurate supporter records, donation data and back up documentation in the CRM system. Ensure data handling complies with GDPR and information is retained and used in compliance with data protection policy and procedures and in line with retention periods. Process, reconcile, and manage all incoming donations received online and via post and telephone. Provide admin support to the Supporter Experience & Communications and Development directorates, to support income generation. Manage incoming and outgoing digital and posted mail. Manage inventory and communicate stock requirements of supporter materials and online shop items. About you Excellent ‘customer service’ skills - warm, friendly, clear, and professional across phone, email, social media, and in person. Experience of data entry or donation processing. Meticulous attention to detail - accurate data entry, record-keeping, and donation processing. Strong computer skills including Microsoft Office, Excel, Outlook and database applications. Excellent written and verbal communication skills. Ability to manage a diverse workload and juggle multiple priorities, ensuring deadlines are met. Sound experience of working ‘hands on’ as part of a team, in a supportive, flexible and friendly manner. Strong organisational and planning skills - able to manage multiple tasks, prioritise effectively, and meet deadlines. Excellent interpersonal skills with the ability to liaise at all levels within the organisation and externally. Passion for working in a values-centred charity that deeply values every supporter. Able to build strong internal collaborative relationships with colleagues across different teams. How to apply To apply for the role of Supporter Experience Coordinator based at Mary’s Meals UK, please click the APPLY button for all information. Applicants must hold full right to work in the UK. We welcome applications from candidates of all different backgrounds and identities to apply. We are committed to building an inclusive and diverse charity providing a supportive place for you to do the best and most rewarding work of your career. Closing date for applications is Monday, 5 October We reserve the right to close this vacancy early if we receive sufficient applications for the role. Therefore, if you are interested, please submit your application as early as possible. Please note: If you have any special requirements or adjustments before an interview, please let us know.
