item.title: Advice Hub and Sexual Violence Helpline Practitioner x2 (Female Applicants Only)
item.description: About the role This role sits within Women and Girls Network’s Intake Service and provides high-quality, trauma-informed and survivor-led support to women and girls affected by Violence Against Women and Girls (VAWG). As an Advice Hub & Sexual Violence Helpline Practitioner, you will be a key first point of contact for survivors, providing one-off and short-term support through WGN’s Advice Hub and Sexual Violence Helpline. You will offer practical advice, advocacy, emotional support, risk and needs assessment, and safety planning via telephone and webchat. You will also contribute to WGN’s Emotional Support & Resiliency programme, provide specialist guidance to professionals, and help ensure the continued development of accessible, survivor-centred services. Job description As the Advice Hub & Sexual Violence Helpline Practitioner, you will: Deliver one-off and short-term support, advocacy, information and safety planning to survivors via telephone and webchat. Undertake risk and needs assessments and respond appropriately to safeguarding concerns. Deliver structured emotional support sessions for survivors of sexual violence. Provide specialist advice and consultation to professionals supporting survivors of VAWG. Support survivors to understand their rights, options and available services. Work within an intersectional, feminist, anti-oppressive and trauma-informed framework. Contribute to the effective delivery, development and promotion of the Advice Hub and Sexual Violence Helpline services. Maintain accurate records, monitoring information and partnership relationships to support high-quality service delivery. Closing date and interviews This vacancy will close at 23:59pm on Thursday 8 October 2026 . Interviews will take place shortly thereafter, and shortlisted candidates will be notified of the arrangements. We encourage early applications, as we reserve the right to close the vacancy before the advertised closing date should we receive a high volume of applications or identify a suitable candidate. Interviews may be conducted either in person or remotely, depending on panel availability and logistical requirements. About us Women and Girls Network (WGN) is a pan-London organisation that supports women and girls affected by all forms of gendered-based violence. Our overall aim is to promote, preserve and restore the mental health and well-being of women and girls who have experienced, or are at risk of, gendered-based violence, whilst working towards a society free of gendered-based violence. We do this by: Providing women-only holistic and seamless therapeutic services, which meet women and girls’ needs and contribute to total and sustainable recovery from the experiences of violence. Evidencing the impact of gendered-based violence and presenting this information in appropriate forums to affect social change in attitudes towards, and responses to, gendered-based violence. Developing good practice in the sector by providing training and guidance on specialist service provision and the development of culturally appropriate service delivery. WGN is proud to be an accredited Living Wage Employer and a member of The London VAWG Consortium, Halo Code, and Helplines Partnership. Join us and be part of a team that values your well-being, growth, and contribution. Commitment to Equity and Inclusion We are deeply committed to building a workforce that reflects the diversity, resilience and strength of the women and girls we serve. We strongly encourage applications from Black and Global Majority women and applicants with Lived Experience, including those who may not meet every criterion. WGN is an equal opportunities employer. Exemption This post is exempt under the Equality Act 2010, Schedule 9, Part 1 , and is open to female applicants only , due to the nature of the role.

item.title: Chief Operating Officer
item.description: Who we are We are OUTpatients, the UK’s LGBTIQ+ cancer charity. Proudly led by and for our community, we are here to shake up the system, advocate for equity, and stand up for every LGBTIQ+ person affected by cancer. Our passion to support others is born out of personal experience; we understand what it’s like to not see yourself reflected in the services you use, and feel like you are left in the margins at a time when you most need personalised support. That is why we host peer support, educate healthcare professionals and help to shape national policy so that nobody has to go through cancer alone. The position The Chief Operating Officer is one of three new senior leadership roles we're creating alongside our CEO, the first time OUTpatients has built a leadership team of this kind. It's a genuine opportunity to shape how a fast-growing charity operates, not simply maintain what already exists. You'll be the CEO's key partner in turning our five-year strategy into a well-run, sustainable organisation: leading a team of six, taking ownership of our finances, risk and governance, and building the systems and structures that let our small, passionate team deliver more, safely and well. Working closely with our incoming Head of Fundraising & Business Development and Chief Medical Officer, and deputising for the CEO when needed, your work will directly shape how many more LGBTIQ+ people affected by cancer we're able to reach. To learn more about the role, please read the attached Job Description.

item.title: Chief Medical Officer
item.description: Who we are We are OUTpatients, the UK’s LGBTIQ+ cancer charity. Proudly led by and for our community, we are here to shake up the system, advocate for equity, and stand up for every LGBTIQ+ person affected by cancer. Our passion to support others is born out of personal experience; we understand what it’s like to not see yourself reflected in the services you use, and feel like you are left in the margins at a time when you most need personalised support. That is why we host peer support, educate healthcare professionals and help to shape national policy so that nobody has to go through cancer alone. The position The Chief Medical Officer is one of three new senior leadership roles we're creating alongside our CEO, the first time OUTpatients has built a leadership team of this kind. Although the role is part-time, just one day a week, its influence is not: you'll be the clinical conscience of everything we produce, and a trusted voice for LGBTIQ+ people affected by cancer within the NHS and medical sector. Working at the intersection of oncology and LGBTIQ+ health equity, you'll ensure our resources, training and peer support are always backed by rigorous clinical evidence and safe, reliable quality standards, giving our small team the confidence to support people safely. Beyond quality assurance, you'll act as a trusted spokesperson and policy voice, opening doors within the NHS and cancer sector that a patient-led charity alone cannot. Working closely with our incoming Chief Operating Officer and Head of Fundraising & Business Development, and reporting directly to our CEO, your clinical judgement will directly shape how safely and credibly we're able to grow. To learn more about the role, please read the attached Job Description.

item.title: Charity Development Manager
item.description: About the Royal School for the Blind Charity The Royal School for the Blind Charity Liverpool is a charity that runs both a School for young people aged 2-19 years old and an adult day service for young adults over the age of 19 with vision impairment, sensory, or additional needs. Although our funding comes from a variety of sources, we are starting to fundraise to support our income and make our work more sustainable for the future. Income generated will support the development of our pupils and young adults, prepare them for the opportunities, responsibilities and experiences of adult life and encourage their independence, communication and mobility. Why this role matters We have ambitious plans for the future including building a new Centre to provide opportunities for therapies and independent growth for young people, and we know that developing sustainable voluntary income will be critical to achieving them. That's why we're investing in fundraising and creating this new role. As our first Development Manager, you'll have the opportunity to build our fundraising approach from the ground up, developing new relationships with individuals, businesses, communities and charitable funders and helping us tell the story of our work to new audiences. Role Overview and Application Process Job Title: Charity Development Manager Hours: Full Time (37 hours per week) Location: This role can be either office-based at the Royal School for the Blind Charity, or hybrid. Responsible to: Charity Leadership Group and managed by Head of Central Services Pay Scale: £35k - £40k, depending on experience (NJC 26-30) Term: Two-year fixed term in the first instance, with the ambition to establish fundraising as a sustainable long-term function within the charity. This is a rare opportunity to build and shape a new fundraising operation from the ground up, playing a pivotal role in the long-term growth and sustainability of the Royal School for the Blind Charity. As the function develops, there will be scope to expand its reach and impact, offering excellent potential for career progression. The Charity Development Manager will lead efforts to secure vital income that underpins the charity’s vision and purpose, driving support through donor engagement, targeted campaigns, and strategic fundraising initiatives. Our long-term ambition is to build a diversified fundraising programme capable of generating approximately £400,000 annually. This role will be instrumental in developing and delivering a growing, high-performing fundraising portfolio. We are looking for an experienced fundraising professional who can design and deliver a robust, evidence-based fundraising strategy. This will involve gaining a deep understanding of the charity’s mission, stakeholders, and audiences, as well as the broader funding landscape, creating a diversified and effective approach that maximizes income and long-term sustainability. This is an exciting time for the Charity as we become much more outward-looking. Alongside our existing work, we have begun a capital building project to enhance our resources. When completed, the new Rushton Centre will house facilities which are open to the public, including a hydrotherapy pool and a café. At the heart of this is a wish to make the Royal School for the Blind Charity part of the fabric of the City. In this new post we are looking for someone who can help open up our work to the wider public: the role is well suited to an experienced fundraiser looking for autonomy and the opportunity to help shape the next chapter in the charity’s history. Although this is a new standalone fundraising role, you won't be building the function in isolation. The post sits within a well-established and supportive team and will be strategically led by the Charity Leadership group and Board of Trustees. In addition, you will have access to colleagues across our services to help bring our impact to life, and support to develop campaigns and engage new audiences. Alongside this, the Charity is currently fundraising for a capital project for a significant new building to resource our activities and reach out into the wider community. Whilst this is a separate project, in the future there will be exciting opportunities to link the new building into the core fundraising strategy. For full roles and responsibilities please see the application pack. Applications close: 9am on Wednesday 21st October Shortlisting: Thursday 22nd October Interviews: Wednesday 4th November Preferred start date: January 2027 (or as soon as possible) Safeguarding The Charity considers safeguarding as its highest priority and fosters an active safeguarding culture. The post will be subject to a range of pre-employment checks, including collection of 3 references, online checks and an Enhanced Disclosure and Barring Service check.

item.title: Head of Integrated Children and Family Services
item.description: Scope and senior accountability Hold delegated senior responsibility for the performance, quality, workforce, safeguarding and development of the children and family services portfolio. Lead EHWP+ as a key commissioned programme, ensuring that delivery remains aligned with contract requirements, local need, agreed outcomes and Spring North’s values. Hold senior accountability for the effective management and delivery of counselling and therapeutic services within the portfolio, including service quality, practitioner practice, professional standards, supervision arrangements and continuous improvement. Balance strategic direction with strong operational grip, intervening early where delivery, safety, quality, finance or partnership performance is at risk. Contribute to whole-organisation leadership, growth, resilience and culture as an active member of the Senior Leadership Team. 4. Key accountabilities 4.1 Strategic leadership of children and family services Develop and implement a clear strategic direction for EHWP+ and the wider children and family services portfolio, aligned with Spring North’s organisational strategy and local commissioning priorities. Maintain a strong understanding of the changing needs of children, young people, parents and carers, using data, lived experience, professional insight and community intelligence to shape priorities. Create a more connected portfolio by linking existing services, clarifying pathways and reducing gaps, duplication and avoidable hand-offs for families. Promote early help, prevention, relationship-based and strengths-based approaches that improve emotional health, wellbeing, resilience and family outcomes. Keep abreast of policy, legislation, evidence and emerging practice affecting children, young people and families, translating these into proportionate action. 4.2 EHWP+ programme leadership and delivery Provide senior leadership and direction to the EHWP+ team, creating a shared focus on access, quality, outcomes, partnership delivery and continuous improvement. Lead the operational delivery of counselling and therapeutic provision, ensuring clear service models, referral and allocation arrangements, appropriate caseload management, safe thresholds, effective practitioner deployment and consistent therapeutic practice across employed teams and delivery partners. Ensure counselling and therapeutic interventions are delivered by appropriately qualified and competent practitioners, with suitable induction, supervision, continuing professional development and access to specialist or clinical advice where required. Ensure that service plans, capacity, resources and delivery arrangements are sufficient to meet contractual commitments and respond appropriately to local need. Establish clear management arrangements, decision-making routes and performance expectations across employed teams and delivery partners. Review delivery data, caseload or activity information, outcomes, waiting times, feedback and emerging risks; agree and monitor corrective action where required. Ensure that the voice of children, young people, parents and carers is visible in-service design, review and improvement. Support effective mobilisation, change and service redesign when contracts, need or evidence require a different delivery response.

item.title: DiSSCo UK Head of the Technical Innovation Centre
item.description: About Us We are a world-class visitor attraction and leading science research centre. We use the Museum's unique collections and our unrivalled expertise to tackle the biggest challenges facing the world today. We care for more than 80 million objects spanning billions of years and welcome more than five million visitors annually and 16 million visits to our website. Today the Museum is more relevant and influential than ever. By attracting people from a range of backgrounds to work for us, we can continue to look at the world with fresh eyes and find new ways of doing things. We employ 1100 staff in a variety of roles, all united by our vision of a future where people and planet thrive. We need everyone to have the passion and drive to help us with our mission to create advocates for our planet and inspire millions to care about the natural world. Diversity and inclusion matter to us. Our vision is of a future where both people and the planet thrive. Diversity is one of our core values and we strive to build a workplace where everyone feels a sense of belonging. All new staff who join us learn about the importance of diversity and inclusion to the Museum and how to contribute to creating an inclusive environment. We know we have more to do, but we are committed to ensuring that everyone who works at the Museum feels they can thrive and feel valued and respected. About the role This is an opportunity to lead a new national centre, as part of the DiSSCo UK programme, using AI, robotics, data and digital technologies to transform access to the UK’s natural science collections. As Head of the DiSSCo UK Technical Innovation unit, (known internally as the Catalysis centre) you will establish and lead a specialist team developing new ways to digitise collections faster and turn collections data into useful tools and services for research, policy and industry. You will set the Centre’s direction, build and lead a multidisciplinary technical team, and take promising ideas from early testing through to practical use. Initially, the focus will be on technologies such as AI-assisted transcription, computer vision, automated imaging and robotics to improve the speed and quality of digitisation. Reporting to the DiSSCo UK Programme Director, and working closely with the Head of Digitisation and Head of Engineering, within the Natural History Museum's Department of Digital Data and Informatics, you will ensure new approaches can be adopted across the national programme. You will also develop partnerships with universities, government and industry, and identify opportunities for further investment and commercial development. This is a fixed term role until 31 March 2029. About you You will be an experienced technology, innovation or digital leader who has successfully turned new technologies into practical products, services or ways of working. Your background might be in AI, data, research infrastructure, digital transformation or a technology business. You will have strong technical understanding in one or more areas such as AI and machine learning, robotics, automation, data engineering or digital platforms, together with experience of leading multidisciplinary teams and delivering complex programmes. You will be a collaborative leader who can work across organisational boundaries, build strong partnerships and explain complex technical ideas clearly. You should also be comfortable getting close to the technical work when needed. Experience of developing partnerships, attracting investment or turning technology and research into sustainable services would be an advantage. Above all, you will be motivated by using technology to accelerate scientific discovery and increase the value and use of the UK’s natural science collections. Thriving at the Museum: the way we work We are proud to work at the Museum and have identified the qualities we all need to embody to reach our shared ambition. This sits alongside the Museum’s values and forms the framework for the way we work. Find out more on our website. What we offer 27.5 days holiday plus 8 bank holidays (full time equivalent) Generous defined contribution Natural History Museum Pension Scheme (employer contribution 4 - 10%) Season ticket, bicycle and rental loan Life insurance Free admission to our exhibitions and many other paid exhibitions at museums, galleries and institutions across London and the UK. Staff discount at our Museum shops and cafes We offer a wide variety of training initiatives and opportunities to build skills. Investing in staff development is important to us, and we are ambitious about helping staff to grow and fulfil their potential. Affordable membership to the Civil Service Sports Council which offers a range of benefits including an extensive list of special offers and reduced entry fees at a selection of cinema chains, theme parks, theatres, retailers and supermarkets. It also provides entry to up to 300 English Heritage sites and other national treasures. Membership to our Sports and Social Association (for a small fee), which includes access to our in-house gym and clubs such as football, softball, table tennis and tennis and classes in Middle Eastern dance, yoga and Tai Chi Hybrid working We are working towards a vision where both people and planet thrive, and nothing gives a greater connection with this, than seeing first-hand, the visitors, scientific research and collections that all of our work is inspired by and working side by side with the teams delivering the visitor experience and events. We also recognise the benefits and flexibility that hybrid working brings. We operate a hybrid working model that requires regular, weekly attendance for this role, with the precise pattern of days on site and worked from home to be agreed with your manager. How to apply If this sounds like you, please apply on our website. Please note that as part of our commitment to anonymised shortlisting, panels do not view CVs during the recruitment process. If you choose to upload your CV, our system will automatically pull information from your CV into our application form. We advise you to double-check your application form data before submitting as the tool may interpret CVs differently. Closing date: 23:59 on 14 October Interviews expected: w/c 26 October Please note that this role does not qualify for Museum sponsorship so the successful postholder will need to have a valid right to work in the UK at the point of offer.

item.title: Data & Tech Lead
item.description: Are you looking for a rewarding role working for an intersectional feminist organisation? If so, we have an incredible opportunity for you to join our team as a Data & Technology Project Lead at Solace Women's Aid. You will be joining a team of committed and inspiring individuals whose dedication has saved the lives of thousands of women, men and children in the capital. We are looking for friendly and diligent individuals to join our services and help us make a difference. Our core values reflect our history and were developed in consultation with staff and service users. Feminism and intersectionality are key to our work, and we are committed to the principles of being survivor-led, trauma-informed, empowering, diverse, anti-racist and anti-discriminatory. About the Service Solace are one of seven members of the Enhanced Mental Health Pathfinder (EMHP) Alliance. The EMHP Alliance aims to improve care for adult victims and survivors of sexual assault and abuse with multiple complex trauma-related mental health needs, enabling recovery, healing and long-term wellbeing. To achieve this, the Pathfinder will strengthen collaboration between statutory and voluntary sector services, improve identification of complex trauma-related needs and develop the capacity and pathways required to deliver timely, sustained and trauma informed support. About the Role We are seeking a highly capable Data & Technology Project Lead to establish and manage the data and technology infrastructure for an innovative multi-agency programme involving charities and NHS Trusts, known as the Enhanced Mental Health Pathfinders Alliance. The postholder will lead the commissioning, procurement, and implementation of digital solutions, such as referral, triage and screening tools, and ensure these are embedded effectively across partners to reduce waiting times and improve access. This role requires a strategic yet hands-on professional who can bridge service delivery goals with digital implementation, enabling collaborative, secure, and user-led systems that support programme growth. About You We are looking for an experienced and proactive professional to lead and support our digital, data, and systems development. You will combine strategic leadership with practical implementation skills, bringing experience of designing and embedding systems in low-resource or start-up settings. You have a strong knowledge of information governance, NHS digital frameworks, data protection and compliance requirements, alongside the ability to establish effective data-sharing systems and governance protocols. Confident in managing projects and programmes, you will be able to coordinate stakeholders across complex partnerships and translate technical requirements into practical, safe and joined-up service solutions. You’ll hold a degree in an IT, Data Manager, Health Informatics, Project Management or related field, or qualified by experience. What we can offer you We provide a comprehensive benefits package to all our employees, including: Flexible working Focus on learning and development (internal career progression and training) Generous holiday entitlement Employer pension contribution Family-friendly leave and enhanced maternity pay Access to Inclusion Networks Daily clinical debriefing Employee Assistance Programme providing free 24/7 support and advice Employee Benefits Platform offering staff discounts, benefits and savings Flow & Restore yoga classes Meditation sessions Cycle to Work Scheme How to apply Please submit your CV and Supporting Statement through the recruitment portal. When applying for this role, kindly highlight in your Supporting Statement how your values, knowledge, transferable skills, and experience align with each point within the following sections of the Job Profile Document: Values, Behaviours & Competencies Knowledge, Experience and Skills Solace Women's Aid values diversity, promotes equity, and challenges discrimination. We encourage and welcome applications from candidates of diverse cultures, abilities, perspectives, and lived experiences. We have policies and processes in place to ensure that all employees are offered an equal opportunity in recruitment and selection, promotion, training, pay, and benefits. Our Inclusion Networks support staff with protected characteristics and offer inclusive spaces to connect. We anticipate and provide reasonable adjustments as needed and support employees who acquire a disability or long-term health condition, enabling them to stay in work. As part of safer recruitment practices, we carry out pre-employment checks including references, Disclosure and Barring Service (DBS) and right to work in the UK checks. No agencies.

item.title: Domestic Abuse Outreach Worker (Home Security Specialist)
item.description: Stop Domestic Abuse is a trauma informed organisation; the work we do to support those effected by domestic abuse may be triggering for those with past trauma. Please only apply if you are living free from abuse. If you’d like to talk to us about this, please get in touch. Location: Southampton Salary: £25,750 - £26,383 Hours per week: 37.5 Contract Type: Permanent Reference Number: STOPDA837 Main Purpose and Scope of the Job: Co-Ordinate an individual package of target hardening for clients using Stop Domestic Abuse services which is informed by a full risk assessment, the type and condition of the property and the needs and circumstances of the individual household. Working collaboratively with existing target hardening schemes within the city including Southampton City Council’s Dove scheme and similar offers from other social landlords and The Blue Lamp Trust. Participating and contributing in awareness-raising campaigns of domestic abuse issues locally in liaison with local multi agency partnerships, and to participate in training events. Remaining up-to-date and compliant with all organisational procedures policies and professional codes of conduct and uphold standards of best practice. Maintaining accurate and confidential records using our secure web-based case management database and contribute to monitoring information for the service by ensuring that evaluation information is properly recorded What We Offer: Time off and Flexibility: - 25 days’ annual leave plus bank holidays (Increasing with service) - Birthday day off - Child’s first day of school off - Option to purchase up to 10 additional days’ leave per year - Flexible and hybrid working - Protected time of up to one hour each month Family-Friendly Benefits: - Enhanced Maternity, Paternity, Shared Parental and Adoption leave - IVF Leave Health and Wellbeing: - Westfield Health Healthcare Cashback Plan (after probation) - Westfield Health Personal Health Insurance (after 2 years’ service) - Employee Assistance Programme - Eye care vouchers - Cycle to Work Scheme About Stop Domestic Abuse: Stop Domestic Abuse is a proud women-led organisation supporting victims and survivors of domestic violence and abuse across Portsmouth and Hampshire. Our vision is a world without domestic abuse, and we work to ensure that it’s ‘everyone’s business.’ We provide refuge and community-based support, delivering in a trauma-informed way for adults, children and young people, tailored to individual needs. Our 19 refuges offer safe, welcoming homes, and across our services we provide one-to-one support and group activities to help improve their safety and to meet others with similar experiences. We support children process their experiences and help regain a sense of safety. Our UP2U programmes support those seeking to change abusive behaviours, and we also offer specialist support for victims of stalking. We also deliver training to professionals, including the hair and beauty industry, to recognise domestic abuse and connect people to specialist support services. Our Values: Equality, Openness, Honesty, Respect for individual dignity and diversity, Empowering women and children, and Care and Compassion – are at the heart of everything we do. By committing to these values, we aim to significantly improve the lives of those we support and work towards our vision of a world without domestic abuse.

item.title: Evidence and Insight Lead
item.description: Job Title: Evidence & Insight Lead Location: Hybrid with 1 day per week in the London Office Hours: 35 hours per week Contract type: Permanent Salary: £50,430 per annum (hybrid) What we do: We help young people through cancer How we work: We’re Determined, United, Spirited and Kind What we’re looking for: We’re looking for a strategic and creative Evidence & Insight Lead to shape Teenage Cancer Trust’s approach to evidence, insight and learning. You’ll set up this new function, identify the charity’s insight needs and develop a forward-looking plan to deliver against them. Acting as the charity’s expert on research and insight, you’ll ensure existing knowledge and learning is consolidated, interpreted and shared to maximise its value. Drawing on well-honed relationship skills, you’ll work across multiple teams and forge new partnerships externally. How to apply: You’ll need to register on our portal, complete a short application form and answer questions about your skills and experience in relation to the role. Key dates: Applications by Sunday 27th September, 1st Stage Interviews Monday 19th October ( online ) and 2nd Stage Interviews on Thursday 22nd October potentially in person. What we offer: Leave: 25 days of annual leave, which increases with service, in addition to bank holidays and a 3 or 4 day closure over the Christmas period. We also have finish early Fridays in August and quarterly reset days to step away from day to day work and refocus. Flexible bank holidays: the option to swap five UK public holidays (except 25th, 26th December, and 1st January or any substitute bank holidays for these dates) for other dates off. Paid Carer and Compassionate Leave: paid time off to care for family members or dependants. Paid Parental Leave: enhanced pay for parental leave such as maternity leave, paternity leave or adoption leave. Paid Volunteering Leave: support your community by taking paid leave for volunteering activities. Health Cashback Plan: access a health cashback plan to cover medical expenses. Life assurance and Income Protection: financial support if you’re unable to work due to illness or injury. Discount scheme: access exclusive savings at various high street retailers and gyms. Flexible Working: we care about your wellbeing and encourage flexible work arrangements to promote work-life balance. Our commitment to inclusion and accessibility: At Teenage Cancer Trust one of our key focuses is around equity and making sure our services are accessible and inclusive to all young people with cancer, with no-one left behind. We have the same goal for people working with us. Teenage Cancer Trust is committed to recognising and valuing individual differences and the contributions of all people. Should you require any assistance or adjustments to support your interview process, such as additional time for tasks, meeting the panellists beforehand, information in another format or a different interview format (online/offline/in person), please don’t hesitate to get in touch with the HR Team and we will do our best to accommodate your request. We are a Disability Confident employer which means we have committed to offering interviews to disabled candidates who meet the essential criteria for the role listed under the 'What you'll bring to the team' section of the job description and shortlisting questions. To opt into this scheme, please enter ‘yes’ in the appropriate question on the application form. Please note that in recruitment campaigns with a high volume of candidates opting into the scheme, interview offers will be made only to those who best meet the essential criteria and provide the strongest responses to the shortlisting questions. We are unable to offer individual feedback at the shortlisting stage. Privacy and Safeguarding: At Teenage Cancer Trust we take our commitment to safeguarding seriously and work to protect and promote the rights of the young people who we support.Our safeguarding responsibilities extendto the children and adults who work to support the charity, who we also have a duty of care to protect.Safeguarding isat the forefront of each activity we carry out.In line with our approach, this role issubject to a DBS check(Disclosure and Barring Service). For information on how we collect, store and process personal data please contact the HR Team We anonymise applications until interview stage to ensure an equitable hiring process. We understand that some applicants may choose to use AI tools such as ChatGPT to support their application. If you do, please make sure your responses reflect your own voice, experience and motivation for joining us. We’re looking to get to know you, so the strongest applications are those that are authentic, personal and demonstrate your unique skills, experience, and knowledge. Relying heavily on AI-generated content can sometimes overlook key requirements in the job description and may reduce how effectively your application comes across.

item.title: Executive Assistant
item.description: A varied, practical support role at the heart of Cheshire Wildlife Trust. Executive Assistant Salary: Starting in the region of £25,526 per annum, pro rata for part time Salary band: Rank 5 (£25,526 - £28,978 per annum FTE) Contract type: Permanent Working hours: Full time or Part Time Location: Bickley Hall Farm, Malpas, SY14 8EF – Hybrid Working About Us Cheshire Wildlife Trust is the region’s leading independent wildlife charity working across Cheshire, Halton, Stockport, Tameside, Trafford, Warrington and Wirral for over 60 years. Wildlife is in decline and the climate crisis is accelerating — but change is possible. At Cheshire Wildlife Trust, we’re working towards a bold vision: by 2030, nature is in recovery and more people are taking action for wildlife. About You and the Role At Cheshire Wildlife Trust, we’re working for a wilder future across Cheshire. We’re looking for a capable, conscientious Executive Assistant to help our CEO, Senior Leadership Team and Board of Trustees stay organised, informed and on track. This is a hands-on administrative role in a small, friendly charity. You’ll help arrange meetings, share papers, track actions, maintain records, support communications and make sure the right people have what they need at the right time. The role will suit someone organised, dependable and detail-focused: a practical all-rounder who takes pride in accuracy, follows through on tasks and enjoys keeping things running smoothly. You may have experience as an administrator, team assistant, office coordinator, secretary, governance assistant or similar. You’ll be confident using common office systems, communicating clearly and warmly, and handling confidential information with care. In return, you’ll join a welcoming organisation with varied work, great benefits, flexible full or part-time hours and the chance to support work that helps nature recover across Cheshire. At Cheshire Wildlife Trust we embrace agile working with a focus on supporting you to achieve your objectives alongside a healthy work-life balance. We operate a hybrid working policy with most staff working at least part of the week from home and/or out on site. We are open to both full-time and part-time applicants. We’re happy to discuss working patterns with candidates. Closing date: Sunday 4 October 2026 Interested? If you would like to find out more, please click the apply button. You will be directed to our website to complete your application for this position. You may be required to carry out a DBS check for this role. Applicants must have the right to work in the UK. Sorry, we are unable to offer sponsorship for this position No agencies please.

Through our two‑year Impact Programme, we help build a joined‑up network of support around each child and family, working in partnership with schools, local services and community organisations. item.title: Senior Programme Manager
item.description: Lumos is looking for an experienced and solutions-focused Senior Programme Manager to coordinate the successful delivery of complex, multi-country programmes, including a major, multi-country and multi-year programme. This is a pivotal role for an accomplished programme-management professional who can bring people, plans, budgets and evidence together to keep ambitious projects moving forward. Working across countries, disciplines and organisational functions, you will help ensure that our programmes are delivered to a high standard, on time, within budget and in accordance with donor requirements. You do not need to be a specialist in childcare reform. What matters most is your strong track record of managing large, restricted-funded international programmes and your ability to navigate complexity with clarity, sound judgement and a collaborative approach. About Lumos Lumos works to realise every child’s right to a family by transforming care systems around the world. Our vision is a world in which all children grow up in safe and loving families, supported by their communities. Working alongside governments, civil society organisations and young people with lived experience, we help families stay together or reunite and support the transition from institutional to family- and community-based care. Over the next 10 years, Lumos aims to enable 500,000 children in care to return to family-based care and help prevent 10 million children from experiencing family breakdown and separation. Achieving this ambition requires pace, collaboration and excellent programme delivery—and this role will make an important contribution. The role Reporting to the Director of Programme Delivery, you will provide day-to-day coordination, monitoring and support across a portfolio of international projects. Your principal focus will be coordinating a major multi-country, multi-year programme across multiple participating countries. You will work closely with Country Directors, project teams, technical and MEAL colleagues, Fundraising, Finance and People teams, as well as donors and delivery partners. Your responsibilities will include: Coordinating multi-country project delivery against agreed workplans, budgets, results frameworks and donor requirements Maintaining clear project plans, risk registers, dashboards, logframes and delivery trackers Identifying risks, delays and bottlenecks early and helping teams find practical solutions Managing budgets, forecasts and expenditure, including donor financial reporting and budget realignments Supporting country teams and partners to strengthen their project and financial-management capacity Managing or matrix-managing project colleagues across different countries and disciplines Coordinating monitoring, evaluation, accountability and learning activities, ensuring that reliable evidence informs delivery Supporting high-quality narrative and results reporting in collaboration with grant-management colleagues Monitoring sub-awards, sub-grants and partner compliance Supporting donor monitoring visits, audits, procurement and grant-compliance processes Contributing to proposals and concept notes for future institutional funding Ensuring safeguarding is embedded effectively across the projects you coordinate Travelling internationally when required to support programme delivery As projects begin, evolve and close, you will work flexibly across the wider portfolio, providing dependable coordination wherever it is most needed. About you You will bring significant experience coordinating large, restricted-funded international programmes, ideally valued at more than £1 million per year. This may have been gained within international development, child protection, education, health, WASH or another related field. You will also bring: A recognised project-management qualification and strong practical expertise in work planning, risk management and multi-stakeholder coordination Experience delivering single- or multi-country projects funded by institutional donors such as USAID, FCDO, the Dutch Government or major foundations Strong financial-management skills, including budgeting, forecasting, expenditure monitoring and donor compliance Experience of complex institutional-donor grant requirements, or the ability to apply closely related experience Experience managing or matrix-managing multidisciplinary and geographically dispersed teams Strong knowledge of results frameworks, indicators, monitoring and donor reporting Experience overseeing sub-awards, sub-grants, consortium partners or other delivery partners Excellent organisation, analysis and problem-solving skills The ability to remain calm, make sound decisions and manage competing priorities Excellent written and spoken English; Spanish, Romanian, Ukrainian or Arabic would be an advantage A genuine commitment to children’s rights and to Lumos’ mission and values You will be a collaborative and culturally sensitive communicator who builds trusted relationships across teams, countries and professional disciplines. You will combine close attention to detail with the ability to see the wider picture and will be comfortable creating structure and momentum in a complex international environment. Why join Lumos? This is an opportunity to apply your programme-management expertise to work with meaningful, lasting impact. You will collaborate with committed colleagues and partners around the world, helping to strengthen programmes designed to ensure that children can grow up in safe, loving families. Closing date: 11 October 2026 Interview dates: week commencing 19 October 2026 Applicants must have the right to work in the UK Only shortlisted candidates will be contacted Lumos is committed to safeguarding and promoting the welfare of children. The successful candidate will be required to complete safeguarding checks appropriate to the role, including references from previous employers and a relevant DBS check. We are committed to equality, diversity and inclusion and welcome applications from candidates of all backgrounds.
item.dc:creator: Lumos

You'll be confident leading projects and working collaboratively across teams to deliver impactful campaigns through social media, email and paid media, bringing creativity, innovation and new ideas to help secure and grow all forms of voluntary income and raise the profile of Birmingham Hospice. What you’ll bring A background in a fundraising and/or communications environment A proven track record creating multimedia communications campaigns, including social media, email and paid digital advertising (e.g. Meta, Google, TikTok ads) Experience of developing and managing digital channels, including websites and a variety of social media platforms Some experience of line managing, mentoring or developing team members Excellent organisational skills, with the ability to manage a complex workload and prioritise effectively Creative thinking skills with the ability to spot opportunities for innovation and growth What we offer Join a supportive, creative and collaborative team where your ideas are valued A varied and interesting role leading fundraising marketing, digital and campaigns activity Autonomy to try new things and bring innovation to your work Work that makes a genuine difference for people living with terminal illness and their families Recognition of prior NHS or hospice service (including pension and annual leave entitlements) Generous annual leave, wellbeing programmes and access to employee benefit platforms such as Stream and Engage

item.title: Communications Assistant
item.description: About parkrun parkrun is a health and wellbeing charity and our vision is to create a healthier and happier planet. Since our conception in 2004, parkrun has evolved into a global social movement with a vibrant and inclusive community at its core. As of 2026, we have recorded over 160-million instances of walking, jogging, running, and volunteering. Our mission is to transform lives by empowering people to be active, together, outdoors in their local community; and to protect parkrun for the generations to come. Each and every weekend, we deliver free, weekly timed events that people of all ages and backgrounds can join in. By tackling barriers to participation, we encourage communities to come together and embrace regular physical activity Now in its 22nd year, parkrun spans over 2,900 locations in 23 countries with more than 12 million people registered, and counting. And we have really only just begun. Brief role description: The Communications Assistant provides creative and administrative support across parkrun’s internal and external communications. The role contributes to the planning, production, and delivery of content that reflects parkrun’s values and engages its global community. Responsibilities include managing the content schedule, designing and preparing communication assets, and ensuring that online spaces remain welcoming, inclusive, and safe. The post requires strong organisational skills, attention to detail, creativity, and a collaborative approach to working with colleagues across teams Main responsibilities: Content creation, storytelling, and media: Research, draft, and produce highly engaging blogs and case studies that capture the imagination of our community. Actively spot powerful individual stories and manage them - either as standalone features, as part of broader media moments, or fundraising campaigns - obtaining appropriate permissions and working closely with our press agency. Content and channel management, and optimisation: Maintain our central communications grid. Manage the production, design, and distribution of our newsletters, retail and fundraising emails and other internal/external emails as required. Monitor and report on performance metrics (opens, clicks, visits etc) to continuously improve engagement. Social media management and community building: Support the management of our social media channels (including scheduling and content creation) to build a vibrant, welcoming online presence. Actively monitor and respond to comments and messages, ensuring our digital spaces are warm, supportive, and inclusive for existing parkrunners, volunteers, and prospective newcomers alike. Basic asset design: Create visually appealing, on-brand graphics (using tools like Canva). Community safeguarding and media management: Ensure all external communications, particularly case studies involving community members, strictly adhere to our safeguarding, consent, and data protection policies. Oversee and organise our image and media library. Ensure all photos and videos used across our communications celebrate the diversity of our community, adhere strictly to safeguarding standards and photography policies. Internal communications and adaptable team support : Assist in sharing internal updates to keep staff, volunteers, and key stakeholders aligned and informed. Provide flexible communications support across different projects and team objectives as organisational priorities evolve.

Our vision is a world without domestic abuse, and we work to ensure that it’s ‘everyone’s business.’ We provide refuge and community-based support, delivering in a trauma-informed way for adults, children and young people, tailored to individual needs. Our 19 refuges offer safe, welcoming homes, and across our services we provide one-to-one support and group activities to help improve their safety and to meet others with similar experiences. We support children process their experiences and help regain a sense of safety. We also deliver training to professionals, including the hair and beauty industry, to recognise domestic abuse and connect people to specialist support services. Our Values: Equality, Openness, Honesty, Respect for individual dignity and diversity, Empowering women and children, and Care and Compassion – are at the heart of everything we do. By committing to these values, we aim to significantly improve the lives of those we support and work towards our vision of a world without domestic abuse.
item.dc:creator: Stop Domestic Abuse

item.title: Philanthropic Partnerships Lead – Trusts and Foundations (Parental Leave Cover)
item.description: Philanthropic Partnerships Lead – Trusts and Foundations (parental leave cover) Application Closing Date: 9th October 2026 Location: Remote or hybrid working within the UK; individuals will be required to attend episodic in-person office days in London as needed and prescribed by the organisation. This role requires applicants to be able to show that they have the right to work in the UK. Term: full time - 35 hours a week. This is a fixed term contract for a period of 12 months covering parental leave. Ideally looking for a candidate to commence the role from November 2026. Organisation: Global Greengrants Fund UK Salary: Salaries at Global Greengrants Fund UK (GGF UK) are dependent on applicable salary scales, internal pay policies including equity considerations and budget. Due to the ways in which salary negotiations perpetuate existing structural inequities, GGF UK has moved away from salary negotiation processes for any candidate. Our best offer for this position is £70,600 per annum. Benefits: We have improved our benefits package and we now offer 10% employer’s pension contribution, remote and flexible remote working, generous family and sick leave, employee assistance programme, health and life insurances, 28 days annual leave plus all UK bank holidays. About Global Greengrants Fund Global Greengrants Fund (GGF) supports grassroots activists and civil society organisations around the world working to address environmental and social justice in over 160 countries. GGF applies a participatory and decentralised model in making grants to grassroots groups through regional and thematic boards of advisors, global partner networks and independent funds, to support grassroots environmental and social justice action. Global Greengrants Fund comprises two organisations: one located in the USA, Global Greengrants Fund Inc (established in 1993), and Global Greengrants Fund UK (established in 2012). The two organisations work closely together with a shared grantmaking programme and strategic collaboration at the senior leadership level. GGF UK consists of sixteen staff members working on fundraising and influencing philanthropy; finance; communications; and operations, with all of these functions operating autonomously but in close collaboration with their US counterpart functions. Global Greengrants Fund has experienced tremendous growth over the past two years and we are thoughtfully, yet rapidly, growing our annual grantmaking, our philanthropic advocacy, and our global partnerships and collaborations to new levels as part of our ongoing transformative journey. The Role The Philanthropic Partnerships Lead – Trusts & Foundations will contribute to Global Greengrants Fund UK’s fundraising and partnership objectives by stewarding a portfolio of existing and new Trust & Foundation supporters to secure significant restricted and unrestricted grants and donations for the organisation. Working as part of the Philanthropic Partnerships team and reporting to the Director of Philanthropic Partnerships, the postholder will also collaborate closely with colleagues across the global organisation Global Greengrants Fund, particularly within the Programmes, External Relations and Finance functions. The Candidate Profile The post holder will be an experienced, senior-level fundraising leader with a track record of securing and developing successful collaborations with trusts, foundations and partner organisations to achieve ambitious income goals; extensive experience in developing pitches, proposals, and fundraising products; and a strong interest in environmental justice, international development or human rights issues. They will have an extensive knowledge of the funding and philanthropy sectors in the UK and Europe; excellent written and verbal communication skills; and be confident in engaging a wide range of internal and external stakeholders, including at senior levels. The candidate will excel in relationship building and interpersonal skills, capable of managing complex relationships and politics. With excellent written and verbal communication skills in English, they will be adept at developing compelling proposals, presentations, reports, and other fundraising materials. Additionally, they will demonstrate strategic, innovative, and analytical thinking, with a strong capacity for complex problem-solving and decision-making. The right candidate will understand Global Greengrants Fund’s core values and be committed to the guiding principles and mission of Global Greengrants Fund and ensure they uphold them in the way they take up the responsibilities of the role. They will value transparency and accountability, demonstrating strong critical thinking, strategic risk management, and the ability to influence and resolve differences across boundaries. With a high degree of self-awareness and insight, the candidate will excel in building strong interpersonal relationships, both within and outside the organisation, and possess outstanding communication and collaboration skills. How to Apply Please review the full job description and person specification on our website and submit your application via email. Please note that the email address to address your application is listed in the job advert on our website. In your application, please send a copy of your current CV and covering letter by 9th October 2026 at 23:00 GMT. You will need to submit these in English. If you’re intrigued by this position but feel like you don’t fit the profile precisely, please still apply. You can ask questions or seek further information to feel able to apply by emailing us. We thank all those who apply, but only shortlisted candidates will be contacted. Global Greengrants Fund UK is an equal opportunities employer. We strongly encourage applicants from all backgrounds and walks of life. We believe that diversity and inclusion among our team is critical to our success. We seek to recruit, develop and retain the most talented people from a diverse candidate pool and welcome applications from all qualified candidates. We do not discriminate on the basis of race, colour, religion, ethnicity, gender, disability, sexual orientation or gender identity.

item.title: Lead MHST Supervisor (Mental Health Support Teams)
item.description: About the role West London Mind is looking for an experienced and compassionate Lead MHST Supervisor to join our long-standing Mental Health Support Team (MHST). You will provide senior clinical supervision and line management to a team of Education Mental Health Practitioners (EMHPs), Child Wellbeing Practitioners (CWPs), Schools Mental Health Practitioners (SMHPs) and trainee/newly qualified supervisors. You will facilitate group supervision of supervisors as well as the wider MHST team. Working closely with schools across Hammersmith & Fulham, you will help ensure our service is safe, effective and responsive to the needs of children and young people. Alongside your leadership and supervision responsibilities, you will maintain a small caseload and deliver evidence-based CBT interventions, including group and 1:1 work. This is an opportunity to play a key role in developing our MHST, supporting practitioners to deliver high-quality interventions and helping us reach children and young people who may face additional barriers to accessing mental health support. What you’ll be doing You will: Work directly with the Clinical Lead to provide clinical supervision, case management and line management to practitioners and supervisors. Act as the senior supervisor within the MHST, overseeing a group of supervisors, working closely with the Clinical Lead and Head of Mental Health Support and Inclusion. Support high-quality, evidence-based delivery of CBT interventions within schools. Monitor clinical quality, safeguarding, risk and outcomes across the team. Hold a small caseload, including more complex cases, deliver 1:1 and group interventions and oversee the delivery of team projects. Support the development of workshops, resources and interventions for children, young people, families and school staff. Work collaboratively with schools and colleagues to develop and expand the service. Take part in the Duty Manager rota and support staff to manage clinical risk effectively. Contribute to training, reflective practice and continuous professional development. About you We’re looking for an experienced children and young people’s mental health professional who is passionate about developing others and improving outcomes for young people. You will have: A relevant professional qualification and registration, such as EMHP, CWP, SWP A PG Certificate in Supervision for Children and Young People’s Mental Health, or equivalent supervisory qualification. At least 3 years’ experience working in children and young people’s mental health. At least 2 years’ experience supervising and case-managing practitioners, including line management experience. At least two years’ experience of delivering evidence-based CBT interventions to children and young people, in line with CYP psychological training supervision. Knowledge and experience of the MHST model and CBT manualised approach. Experience of managing clinical risk and safeguarding within a child and young people’s setting. Excellent communication, organisation and relationship-building skills. A commitment to equality, diversity and delivering culturally appropriate support. You must be registered with the relevant UK professional body, such as BPS, BABCP, HCPC, UKCP, NMC or BACP, as appropriate to your profession. Why join West London Mind? At West London Mind, we believe every young person should have access to the mental health support they need. As one of a small number of third-sector providers of MHSTs, we are proud to work closely with schools and communities to make a meaningful difference. You’ll join a supportive and experienced team where your clinical expertise, leadership and ideas will be valued. You’ll also have opportunities for supervision, training and ongoing professional development. If you are an experienced mental health professional who enjoys supporting and developing others, working collaboratively with schools and delivering high-quality interventions, we’d love to hear from you. Post is subject to an enhanced DBS check.

item.title: Major Gifts Officer
item.description: Who we are Nature is in crisis. People are destroying and consuming the natural world at a devastating rate, threatening the ecosystems on which all life depends. Birds are our early warning system, revealing the health of our planet and helping us understand the urgent action needed to protect it. BirdLife International is the world’s largest partnership for nature conservation, bringing together 125 national organisations across six continents to protect birds, biodiversity and the natural systems that sustain life. Through our unique local-to-global approach, we work at the intersection of science, policy and community action to tackle the global nature and climate crises. Using world-leading bird science, we collect and analyse data from across continents, landscapes and seascapes to identify the most effective and innovative conservation solutions. Our work conserves species, safeguards critical habitats and empowers communities to create lasting change for nature and people. At the heart of BirdLife is a powerful global movement. More than two million birders, scientists and local volunteers help track, study and protect birdlife around the world, generating the knowledge and action needed to drive conservation impact at scale. Together, we are giving nature a voice and building a future in which birds, wildlife and people can thrive. BirdLife International’s Development Team is in an exciting new phase of recruitment and growth and will be hiring for a number of roles to support growth and sustainability across the organisation – including this newly created role. About the role BirdLife International has created the role of Major Gifts Officer to provide dedicated focus to cultivating, stewarding and growing the pool of donors in the £10k-£50k giving range – helping supporters move through the pipeline while providing outstanding stewardship and donor care. Working closely with the Head of Major Gifts and the wider team, the postholder will have the opportunity to learn from experienced major donor fundraisers while developing their own portfolio and solicitation skills. Key responsibilities: Personally manage a portfolio of donors and prospects in the £10k–£50k range, developing appropriate cultivation, solicitation and stewardship plans Cultivate and steward relationships with donors and prospects in the portfolio Conduct prospect research to inform cultivation strategies, working closely with the Prospect Research & Insights Manager. Work with conservation, regional, science, policy, communications and finance colleagues to gather information for donor proposals, impact updates, reports and other cultivation or stewardship materials. Draft donor reports, proposals and stewardship materials to support the Major Gifts team in cultivating and reporting to donors. Support the Events Coordinator in the planning and delivery of cultivation and fundraising events Support the Major Gifts team across research, stewardship, administration, compliance and CRM management. Who we are looking for Experience in fundraising, donor relationship management, or a related client- or relationship-facing role Ability to build rapport with donors and colleagues and to communicate donor and pipeline information clearly Good knowledge of major gifts fundraising practice and prospect research techniques Highly organised, evidence-based, results-focused self-starter Excellent verbal and written communication skills, with the ability to draft clear donor-facing correspondence, reports, proposals and stewardship materials Ability to work collaboratively across teams and with external stakeholders Location: Remote, UK, with travel to the David Attenborough Building in Cambridge Closing date: 9 a.m. Monday 19th October

item.title: Adviser (Scotland)
item.description: Please note - this role is homebased in Scotland, with some travel througout Scotland and to London required. Independent Age is the national charity working towards ending financial hardship in later life. Our Helpline and expert advisers offer free information and advice to older people without enough money to live on, while our external training equips professionals with the information they need to support older people on low incomes. Through our grants programme, we fund and support hundreds of local charities working with older people across the UK. We use the knowledge and insight gained from our support services and partnerships to highlight the issues experienced by older people in poverty and campaign for change. We believe no one should face financial hardship in later life. We would love to find individuals from all walks of life and diverse backgrounds to join us on this journey. Responsibilities and Person Specification: This new role is an integral part of the day-to-day delivery of our Advice and Support Service. The service is targeted at older people in or facing financial hardship, and provides information, advice and follow up support relating to a range of issues, including Welfare Benefits, Social Care and Housing. As an Adviser (Scotland) you will be responsible for providing specialist support to older people, their families and carers through our advice service with their enquiries relating to housing and welfare benefits in Scotland as well as providing generalist level support on a range of issues through our duty service. You should have in depth, specialist level knowledge of Housing or Welfare Benefits in Scotland as they relate to older people. Experience of working within a high-volume advice setting and advice supervision framework such as the AQS framework. We plan to further develop our advice offer in Scotland to cover advice around charging for Social Care, so whilst not essential, knowledge of this area, or a desire to develop will be beneficial. For full details on the role and requirements, please review the job description and person specification. If your experience doesn’t align perfectly with all the criteria in the person specification but you do meet most of them and are excited about the role, we encourage you to apply anyway. This is a full-time role, 35 hours per week, which you can choose to work over five days or a 9-day fortnight. We also are open to this role being worked on a part-time basis on a minimum of 21 hours per week. What it’s like to work at Independent Age: We celebrate diversity at Independent Age and champion the differences that make each of us unique. We actively support and encourage people from a variety of backgrounds, experiences and skill sets to join us and help shape what we do. We aim to attract and retain a wide range of talent and create an environment where everyone can feel safe, protected, welcome and included. We offer great benefits including 28 days annual leave plus public holidays, a generous pension scheme with life assurance, and fantastic learning and development opportunities. We also offer a number of enhanced leave provisions and benefits. We know that a good work life balance helps us perform at our best and supports wellbeing. Flexible working hours and hybrid working is standard for all. But if you need a different form of flexibility, we are always happy to talk flexible working. With an employee engagement score of 98%, colleagues say Independent Age is a great place to work. You can find out more about what it’s like to work at Independent Age by visiting the Careers page on our website. Application Process: To apply, please visit our website to submit a CV and a Supporting Statement, detailing how your skills and experience meet the criteria within the Job Description and Person Specification. We are committed to ensuring our recruitment process is inclusive and accessible to all. If you require any specific arrangements or adjustments to enable you to fully participate in the recruitment process, such as having the job description in a larger text format or to apply in an alternative format, please get in touch with us via the email address on the ‘Contact Us’ page on our jobs site. To support our commitment to equity, diversity and inclusion our hiring managers use anonymous shortlisting. Please don’t include your name, photo, or any information that could indicate your gender or age in your CV and supporting statement, and don’t include your name in the title of any documents that you upload. However, please do include all dates of employment. Independent Age is committed to safeguarding and follows Safer Recruitment practices to ensure we are safeguarding those we work with. We therefore ask that you supply your full work history with explanations for any gaps in the application documents you submit and, if offered the post, we will require a minimum of two employment references including your current or most recent employer. A Level 1 (Basic) Disclosure check will be carried out for the successful candidate. Closing Date: Sunday 4th October 2026 11:59pm Interview Dates: First round of interviews will take place online on Tuesday 13th & Wednesday 14th October Second round of interviews will be held in person, in Glasgow, on Wednesday 21st October
